```tern
# with Result: res = http.try_get(url)?   Err only when there's no response at all ("http:
# request failed: connect: Connection refused"); 4xx / 5xx responses are Ok
fn try_fetch(cr: ClientRequest) Result[Response, str]:
    res = fetch(cr)
    if res.status == 0:
        return Err("http: request failed: " + res.body)
    return Ok(res)

fn try_get(url: str) Result[Response, str]:
    return try_fetch(ClientRequest("GET", url, "", "", 30000, 5))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- for middleware

fn now_us() int:
    return _now_us()

fn log(line: str):
    _log(line)

# Token buckets by key (a client IP, an API key), refilled at per_second tokens a second up
# to burst, shared by every thread; idle ones are forgotten.
fn limiter(per_second: float, burst: int) Limiter:
    return Limiter(_rl_new(per_second, float(burst)))

# use a token from key's bucket: 0.0, or (none left) the seconds until one is there
fn consume(l: Limiter, key: str) float:
    return _rl_take(l.id, key)

fn request_id() str:
    lo = -9223372036854775807 - 1
    a = (random.int(lo, 9223372036854775807) & ~0xF000) | 0x4000          # version 4
    b = (random.int(lo, 9223372036854775807) & 0x3FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF) | lo    # variant 10
    out = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
    binary.set_u64be(&out, 0, _hex8(a >> 32))
    h = _hex8(a)
    binary.set_u32be(&out, 9, h >> 32)
    binary.set_u32be(&out, 14, h)
    h = _hex8(b >> 32)
    binary.set_u32be(&out, 19, h >> 32)
    binary.set_u32be(&out, 24, h)
    binary.set_u64be(&out, 28, _hex8(b))
    return out

# x's low 32 bits as 8 lowercase hex digits in a word, the first in its high byte
fn _hex8(x: int) int:
    v = x & 0xffffffff
    v = (v | v << 16) & 0x0000FFFF0000FFFF
    v = (v | v << 8) & 0x00FF00FF00FF00FF
    v = (v | v << 4) & 0x0F0F0F0F0F0F0F0F
    return v + 0x3030303030303030 + (((v + 0x0606060606060606) >> 4) & 0x0101010101010101) * 0x27

# a == b, in time that depends only on the lengths (for comparing secrets)
fn secure_equal(a: str, b: str) bool:
    return _ct_eq(a, b)

fn gzip(data: str) str:
    return _gzip(data)

# count requests from now on (every server in the program), for metrics_text
fn enable_metrics():
    _metrics_enable()

fn metrics_text() str:
    return _metrics_text()
```

## library/std/http/text.tn

```tern
# http: lookups in a request's raw text (headers, query strings and forms, cookies, path
# parameters), url_encode, and a constant-time compare. They read the text where it is and
# copy only the result.

import binary
import simd

# c lowercased (ASCII letters only)
fn _lc(c: int) int:
    return c | 32 if c >= 65 and c <= 90 else c

# does s[at..] start with name, ignoring ASCII case?
fn _ieq_at(s: str, at: int, name: str) bool:
    for k in 0..len(name):
        if _lc(s.byte(at + k)) != _lc(name.byte(k)):
            return false
    return true

# the value of header `name` (in any case) in "Name: value\r\n" lines, without the spaces
# around it; "" if there's none. The newlines are found 16 bytes at a time, and a line is
# looked at only when a `:` comes right after len(name) bytes.
fn _header(head: str, name: str) str:
    n = len(name)
    end = len(head)
    p = 0                                   # the line being looked at starts here
    i = 0
    while i < end:
        m = simd.eq(simd.load_upto(head, i), simd.splat(10))
        if simd.any(m):
            bits = simd.bits(m)
            while bits != 0:
                le = i + simd.first(bits)
                if le - p > n and head.byte(p + n) == 58 and _ieq_at(head, p, name):
                    return _hval(head, p + n + 1, le)
                p = le + 1
                bits &= bits - 1
        i += 16
    if end - p > n and head.byte(p + n) == 58 and _ieq_at(head, p, name):
        return _hval(head, p + n + 1, end)
    return ""

# head[v..ve] without spaces and tabs before it, or spaces, tabs and a CR after it
fn _hval(head: str, v0: int, ve0: int) str:
    v = v0
    ve = ve0
    while v < ve and (head.byte(v) == 32 or head.byte(v) == 9):
        v += 1
    while ve > v and (head.byte(ve - 1) == 13 or head.byte(ve - 1) == 32 or head.byte(ve - 1) == 9):
        ve -= 1
    return head[v..ve]

fn _hexv(c: int) int:
    if c >= 48 and c <= 57:
        return c - 48
    if c >= 97 and c <= 102:
        return c - 87
    if c >= 65 and c <= 70:
        return c - 55
    return -1

# does s[a..b] have a % (or, with plus, a +)?
fn _escaped(s: str, a: int, b: int, plus: bool) bool:
    for i in a..b:
        c = s.byte(i)
        if c == 37 or (plus and c == 43):
            return true
    return false

# s[a..b] with %XX undone (and, with plus, + as a space); a % without two hex digits stays
fn _decode(s: str, a: int, b: int, plus: bool) str:
    if not _escaped(s, a, b, plus):
        return s[a..b]
    o = ""
    o.reserve(b - a)
    run = a
    i = a
    while i < b:
        c = s.byte(i)
        if c == 43 and plus:
            o += s[run..i] + " "
            run = i + 1
        elif c == 37 and i + 2 < b and _hexv(s.byte(i + 1)) >= 0 and _hexv(s.byte(i + 2)) >= 0:
            o += s[run..i] + chr(_hexv(s.byte(i + 1)) * 16 + _hexv(s.byte(i + 2)))
            i += 2
            run = i + 1
        i += 1
    o += s[run..b]
    return o

# the value for key `name` in "a=1&b=2" (url-decoded, the key too); "" if absent. The & = % +
# bytes are found 16 bytes at a time; each & ends a pair, and a pair is compared only there.
fn _form(q: str, name: str) str:
    end = len(q)
    p = 0                                   # the pair being read starts here
    eq = -1                                 # its first =
    esc = false                             # a % or + in its key
    i = 0
    while i < end:
        v = simd.load_upto(q, i)
        m = simd.eq(v, simd.splat(38)) | simd.eq(v, simd.splat(61)) | simd.eq(v, simd.splat(37)) | simd.eq(v, simd.splat(43))
        if simd.any(m):
            bits = simd.bits(m)
            while bits != 0:
                k = i + simd.first(bits)
                c = q.byte(k)
                if c == 38:
                    if _form_hit(q, p, k, eq, esc, name):
                        return _decode(q, eq + 1, k, true) if eq >= 0 else ""
                    p = k + 1
                    eq = -1
                    esc = false
                elif eq < 0:
                    if c == 61:
                        eq = k
                    else:
                        esc = true
                bits &= bits - 1
        i += 16
    if p < end and _form_hit(q, p, end, eq, esc, name):
        return _decode(q, eq + 1, end, true) if eq >= 0 else ""
    return ""

# is the key of the pair q[p..e] (its first = at eq, or -1; esc: % or + in the key) name?
fn _form_hit(q: str, p: int, e: int, eq: int, esc: bool, name: str) bool:
    ke = eq if eq >= 0 else e
    if esc:
        return _decode(q, p, ke, true) == name
    return ke - p == len(name) and q[p..ke] == name

# every key and value of "a=1&b=2", decoded (a later key replaces an earlier one; empty keys
# are left out)
fn _pairs(q: str) {str: str}:
    out: {str: str} = {}
    end = len(q)
    if end == 0:
        return out
    p = 0
    while true:
        e = q.find_from("&", p)
        if e < 0:
            e = end
        eq = q[p..e].find("=")
        ke = p + eq if eq >= 0 else e
        k = _decode(q, p, ke, true)
        if k != "":
            out[k] = _decode(q, ke + 1, e, true) if eq >= 0 else ""
        if e == end:
            break
        p = e + 1
    return out

# a cookie's value in a Cookie header ("a=1; b=2"), without quotes around it. The ; and =
# bytes are found 16 bytes at a time; a cookie is compared only at the ; after it.
fn _cookie(h: str, name: str) str:
    end = len(h)
    p = _cookie_start(h, 0)                 # the cookie being read starts here
    eq = -1                                 # its first =
    i = 0
    while i < end:
        v = simd.load_upto(h, i)
        m = simd.eq(v, simd.splat(59)) | simd.eq(v, simd.splat(61))
        if simd.any(m):
            bits = simd.bits(m)
            while bits != 0:
                k = i + simd.first(bits)
                if k >= p:
                    if h.byte(k) == 61:
                        if eq < 0:
                            eq = k
                    else:
                        if eq >= 0 and eq - p == len(name) and h[p..eq] == name:
                            return _cookie_value(h, eq + 1, k)
                        p = _cookie_start(h, k)
                        eq = -1
                bits &= bits - 1
        i += 16
    if p < end and eq >= 0 and eq - p == len(name) and h[p..eq] == name:
        return _cookie_value(h, eq + 1, end)
    return ""

# past the spaces and ;s at p
fn _cookie_start(h: str, p0: int) int:
    p = p0
    while p < len(h) and (h.byte(p) == 32 or h.byte(p) == 59):
        p += 1
    return p

# h[v..ve] without spaces after it, and without the quotes around it if it has them
fn _cookie_value(h: str, v0: int, ve0: int) str:
    v = v0
    ve = ve0
    while ve > v and h.byte(ve - 1) == 32:
        ve -= 1
    if ve - v >= 2 and h.byte(v) == 34 and h.byte(ve - 1) == 34:
        v += 1
        ve -= 1
    return h[v..ve]

# Path parameters come packed in one str (the engine's web_pack_params): per parameter, a
# 1-byte name length, the name, a 4-byte (little-endian) value length, the decoded value.
fn _param(packed: str, name: str) str:
    p = 0
    while p < len(packed):
        nl = packed.byte(p)
        nm = p + 1
        vl = binary.u32le(packed, nm + nl)
        v = nm + nl + 4
        if nl == len(name) and packed[nm..nm + nl] == name:
            return packed[v..v + vl]
        p = v + vl
    return ""

fn _params(packed: str) {str: str}:
    out: {str: str} = {}
    p = 0
    while p < len(packed):
        nl = packed.byte(p)
        nm = p + 1
        vl = binary.u32le(packed, nm + nl)
        v = nm + nl + 4
        out[packed[nm..nm + nl]] = packed[v..v + vl]
        p = v + vl
    return out

# a letter, digit, - _ . or ~: what url_encode leaves as it is
fn _unreserved(c: int) bool:
    return (c >= 97 and c <= 122) or (c >= 65 and c <= 90) or (c >= 48 and c <= 57) or c == 45 or c == 95 or c == 46 or c == 126

const _HEX = "0123456789ABCDEF"

# s with every byte but A-Z a-z 0-9 - _ . ~ as %XX (for a query string or a path segment)
fn url_encode(s: str) str:
    o = ""
    o.reserve(len(s))
    run = 0
    for i in 0..len(s):
        c = s.byte(i)
        if not _unreserved(c):
            o += s[run..i] + "%" + chr(_HEX.byte(c >> 4)) + chr(_HEX.byte(c & 15))
            run = i + 1
    o += s[run..len(s)]
    return o

# a == b, in time that depends only on the lengths
fn _ct_eq(a: str, b: str) bool:
    if len(a) != len(b):
        return false
    d = 0
    for i in 0..len(a):
        d |= a.byte(i) ^ b.byte(i)
    return d == 0
```

## library/std/json/codec.tn

```tern
# json: the encoders and decoders the compiler puts together for each type. _enc[T] / _dec[T]
# (json.tn) become, by T's kind:
#   int byte float f32 bool str      _enc_int ... / _dec_int ...
#   [E]                              _enc_arr[E] / _dec_arr[E]
#   {str: V} {int: V}                _enc_map_s[V] _enc_map_i[V] / _dec_map_s[V] _dec_map_i[V]
#   Option[T]                        _enc_opt[T] / _dec_opt[T]     (null is None)
#   a struct or an enum              made from its fields (compiler/checker/json_codec.tn)
# A decoder that needs fresh values (an array's elements, a map's values) is handed one: z.

import simd

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- encoding

# bytes a string can't hold as they are: control bytes, " and \ (and non-ASCII, checked)
fn _esc16(v: bytes16) bytes16:
    return simd.lt(v, simd.splat(32)) | simd.eq(v, simd.splat(34)) | simd.eq(v, simd.splat(92)) | simd.lt(simd.splat(127), v)

# the length of the UTF-8 sequence at s[i..n] (2 to 4 bytes), 0 if it isn't a well-formed one
fn _utf8_seq(s: str, i: int, n: int) int:
    c = s.byte(i)
    if c >= 0xc2 and c <= 0xdf:
        if i + 1 < n and (s.byte(i + 1) & 0xc0) == 0x80:
            return 2
        return 0
    if c >= 0xe0 and c <= 0xef:
        if i + 2 >= n:
            return 0
        c1 = s.byte(i + 1)
        if (c1 & 0xc0) != 0x80 or (s.byte(i + 2) & 0xc0) != 0x80:
            return 0
        if c == 0xe0 and c1 < 0xa0:        # overlong
            return 0
        if c == 0xed and c1 >= 0xa0:       # a surrogate
            return 0
        return 3
    if c >= 0xf0 and c <= 0xf4:
        if i + 3 >= n:
            return 0
        c1 = s.byte(i + 1)
        if (c1 & 0xc0) != 0x80 or (s.byte(i + 2) & 0xc0) != 0x80 or (s.byte(i + 3) & 0xc0) != 0x80:
            return 0
        if c == 0xf0 and c1 < 0x90:        # overlong
            return 0
        if c == 0xf4 and c1 >= 0x90:       # past U+10FFFF
            return 0
        return 4
    return 0

fn _hexd(d: int) str:
    return "0123456789abcdef"[d..d + 1]

# s as a JSON string: " \ and control bytes escaped, a byte that isn't well-formed UTF-8 as
# U+FFFD (as Go's encoder does), so the output is always valid JSON
fn _enc_str(o: mut str, v: str):
    n = len(v)
    o.reserve(n + 2)
    o += "\""
    run = 0
    i = 0
    while i < n:
        m = _esc16(simd.load_upto(v, i)) & simd.lt(_lanes(), simd.splat(min(n - i, 16)))
        if not simd.any(m):
            i += 16
            continue
        i += simd.first_lane(m)
        c = v.byte(i)
        if c >= 128:
            k = _utf8_seq(v, i, n)
            if k > 0:
                i += k
                continue
            o += v[run..i] + "\xef\xbf\xbd"
            i += 1
            run = i
            continue
        o += v[run..i]
        if c == 34:
            o += "\\\""
        elif c == 92:
            o += "\\\\"
        elif c == 10:
            o += "\\n"
        elif c == 13:
            o += "\\r"
        elif c == 9:
            o += "\\t"
        else:
            o += "\\u00" + _hexd(c >> 4) + _hexd(c & 15)
        i += 1
        run = i
    o += v[run..n] + "\""

fn _enc_int(o: mut str, v: int):
    o += str(v)

fn _enc_byte(o: mut str, v: byte):
    o += str(v)

# infinities and NaN have no JSON: null
fn _enc_float(o: mut str, v: float):
    if v - v == 0.0:
        o += str(v)
    else:
        o += "null"

fn _enc_f32(o: mut str, v: f32):
    if float(v) - float(v) == 0.0:
        o += str(v)
    else:
        o += "null"

fn _enc_bool(o: mut str, v: bool):
    o += "true" if v else "false"

fn _enc_arr[E](o: mut str, v: [E]):
    o += "["
    for i, x in v:
        if i > 0:
            o += ","
        _enc[E](&o, x)
    o += "]"

fn _enc_map_s[V](o: mut str, v: {str: V}):
    o += "{"
    first = true
    for k, x in v:
        if not first:
            o += ","
        first = false
        _enc_str(&o, k)
        o += ":"
        _enc[V](&o, x)
    o += "}"

# int keys are written as strings ({"1": ...}), as JSON's keys are strings
fn _enc_map_i[V](o: mut str, v: {int: V}):
    o += "{"
    first = true
    for k, x in v:
        if not first:
            o += ","
        first = false
        o += "\""
        o += str(k)
        o += "\":"
        _enc[V](&o, x)
    o += "}"

fn _enc_opt[T](o: mut str, v: Option[T]):
    match v:
        Some(x):
            _enc[T](&o, x)
        None:
            o += "null"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- decoding

fn _dec_byte(p: mut _P, out: mut byte) bool:
    n = 0
    if not _dec_int(&p, &n) or n < 0 or n > 255:
        return false
    out = byte(n)
    return true

fn _dec_f32(p: mut _P, out: mut f32) bool:
    x = 0.0
    if not _dec_float(&p, &x):
        return false
    out = f32(x)
    return true

# an array: the first four elements wait in locals, so a short array (most are) is made once
# at its size
fn _dec_arr[E](p: mut _P, out: mut [E], z: E) bool:
    if not _eat(&p, 91):
        return false
    if _eat(&p, 93):
        out = []
        return true
    e0 = z
    if not _dec[E](&p, &e0):
        return false
    if not _eat(&p, 44):
        if not _eat(&p, 93):
            return false
        out = [e0]
        return true
    e1 = z
    if not _dec[E](&p, &e1):
        return false
    if not _eat(&p, 44):
        if not _eat(&p, 93):
            return false
        out = [e0, e1]
        return true
    e2 = z
    if not _dec[E](&p, &e2):
        return false
    if not _eat(&p, 44):
        if not _eat(&p, 93):
            return false
        out = [e0, e1, e2]
        return true
    e3 = z
    if not _dec[E](&p, &e3):
        return false
    if not _eat(&p, 44):
        if not _eat(&p, 93):
            return false
        out = [e0, e1, e2, e3]
        return true
    a = [e0, e1, e2, e3]
    while true:
        e = z
        if not _dec[E](&p, &e):
            return false
        a.push(e)
        if not _eat(&p, 44):
            break
    if not _eat(&p, 93):
        return false
    out = a
    return true

fn _dec_map_s[V](p: mut _P, out: mut {str: V}, z: V) bool:
    if not _eat(&p, 123):
        return false
    m: {str: V} = {}
    if not _eat(&p, 125):
        while true:
            k = ""
            if not _dec_str(&p, &k) or not _eat(&p, 58):
                return false
            x = z
            if not _dec[V](&p, &x):
                return false
            m[k] = x
            if not _eat(&p, 44):
                break
        if not _eat(&p, 125):
            return false
    out = m
    return true

# int keys: written as strings of digits ("12", "-3"); anything else fails
fn _dec_map_i[V](p: mut _P, out: mut {int: V}, z: V) bool:
    if not _eat(&p, 123):
        return false
    m: {int: V} = {}
    if not _eat(&p, 125):
        while true:
            k = ""
            if not _dec_str(&p, &k) or not _eat(&p, 58):
                return false
            n = k.to_int(-9223372036854775807 - 1)
            if n == -9223372036854775807 - 1:
                return false
            x = z
            if not _dec[V](&p, &x):
                return false
            m[n] = x
            if not _eat(&p, 44):
                break
        if not _eat(&p, 125):
            return false
    out = m
    return true

fn _dec_opt[T](p: mut _P, out: mut Option[T], z: T) bool:
    if _null(&p):
        out = None
        return true
    x = z
    if not _dec[T](&p, &x):
        return false
    out = Some(x)
    return true
```

## library/std/json/json.tn

```tern
# json: encode and decode any Tern value.
#
#   import json
#   text = json.encode(user)                 # structs, arrays, maps, str, int, float, bool
#   ok = json.decode(req.body, &user)        # fills user; false (and no change) if invalid
#   s = json.schema[User]()                  # User's JSON Schema (2020-12), as text
#
# Each type gets its own encoder and decoder, made while compiling (no reflection; see
# codec.tn and the compiler's checker/json_codec.tn). Struct fields map to JSON object keys by name; missing
# keys keep their current value; unknown keys are ignored; null keeps the value.
# To tell a missing key from an empty value, make the field an Option and start it at None:
# a missing key (or null) leaves None, "" gives Some("").
#   struct LinkReq:  url: str   slug: Option[str]      ... if r.slug is Some(s): ...
# Map keys may be str or int (int keys are written as JSON strings).
#
# JSON whose shape isn't known ahead of time: parse it into a Value and look inside.
#
#   v = json.parse(text)?                    # Result[json.Value, str]
#   v.field("user").field("name").str_or("")     # a missing key or wrong kind gives Null,
#   v.field("tags").at(0).str_or("none")         # so lookups chain; the *_or default ends it
#   n = v.field("count").int_or(0)   x = v.field("ratio").float_or(0.0)   b = v.field("ok").bool_or(false)
#   for k in v.fields(): ...       for x in v.elems(): ...       v.size()
#   m = v.to_map()                           # {str: Value}: field() scans the keys, so for many
#                                            # lookups in a big object, index it once
#   match v: Obj(keys, vals) / Arr(items) / Str(s) / Num(x, text) / Bool(b) / Null
#   json.dump(v) str                         back to JSON text
#
# Objects keep their keys in order (and repeated keys, as written); numbers keep their text
# too, so int_or reads integers beyond float's 2^53 exactly.

import simd

fn encode[T](value: T) str:
    o = ""
    _enc[T](&o, value)
    return o

fn decode[T](text: str, out: mut T) bool:
    p = _P(text, 0, 0, 0, simd.splat(0), 0, "")
    d = out                                 # into a copy: bad input leaves out as it was
    if not _dec[T](&p, &d):
        return false
    _ws_p(&p)
    if p.i != len(text):
        return false
    out = d
    return true

# T's encoder and decoder: the compiler makes each one for its T (by kind, from codec.tn's
# templates, or for a struct or an enum from its fields), so these bodies are never used
fn _enc[T](o: mut str, v: T):
    pass

fn _dec[T](p: mut _P, out: mut T) bool:
    return false

enum Value:
    Null
    Bool(b: bool)
    Num(x: float, text: str)
    Str(s: str)
    Arr(items: [Value])
    Obj(keys: [str], vals: [Value])

fn _ws(s: str, pos: mut int):
    while pos < len(s):
        c = s.byte(pos)
        if c != 32 and c != 10 and c != 13 and c != 9:
            return
        pos += 1

fn _hexval(c: int) int:
    if c >= 48 and c <= 57:
        return c - 48
    if c >= 97 and c <= 102:
        return c - 87
    if c >= 65 and c <= 70:
        return c - 55
    return -1

fn _utf8(cp: int) str:
    if cp < 0x80:
        return chr(cp)
    if cp < 0x800:
        return chr(0xc0 | (cp >> 6)) + chr(0x80 | (cp & 0x3f))
    if cp < 0x10000:
        return chr(0xe0 | (cp >> 12)) + chr(0x80 | ((cp >> 6) & 0x3f)) + chr(0x80 | (cp & 0x3f))
    return chr(0xf0 | (cp >> 18)) + chr(0x80 | ((cp >> 12) & 0x3f)) + chr(0x80 | ((cp >> 6) & 0x3f)) + chr(0x80 | (cp & 0x3f))

fn _hex4(s: str, pos: int, err: mut str) int:
    if pos + 4 > len(s):
        err = "truncated \\u escape"
        return 0
    v = 0
    for i in 0..4:
        h = _hexval(s.byte(pos + i))
        if h < 0:
            err = "bad \\u escape"
            return 0
        v = v * 16 + h
    return v

fn _string(s: str, pos: mut int, err: mut str) str:
    pos += 1
    out = ""
    start = pos
    while pos < len(s):
        c = s.byte(pos)
        if c == 34:
            out += s[start..pos]
            pos += 1
            return out
        if c < 32:
            err = "control character in a string"
            return out
        if c == 92:
            out += s[start..pos]
            if pos + 1 >= len(s):
                break
            e = s.byte(pos + 1)
            pos += 2
            match e:
                110:
                    out += "\n"
                116:
                    out += "\t"
                114:
                    out += "\r"
                98:
                    out += chr(8)
                102:
                    out += chr(12)
                34:
                    out += "\""
                92:
                    out += "\\"
                47:
                    out += "/"
                117:
                    cp = _hex4(s, pos, &err)
                    pos += 4
                    if cp >= 0xd800 and cp < 0xdc00 and pos + 6 <= len(s) and s.byte(pos) == 92 and s.byte(pos + 1) == 117:
                        lo = _hex4(s, pos + 2, &err)
                        if lo >= 0xdc00 and lo < 0xe000:
                            cp = 0x10000 + ((cp - 0xd800) << 10) + (lo - 0xdc00)
                            pos += 6
                    out += _utf8(cp)
                _:
                    err = "bad escape \\" + chr(e)
                    return out
            start = pos
        else:
            pos += 1
    err = "unterminated string"
    return out

fn _value(s: str, pos: mut int, err: mut str, depth: int) Value:
    _ws(s, &pos)
    if pos >= len(s):
        err = "unexpected end"
        return Value.Null
    if depth > 512:
        err = "nested too deeply"
        return Value.Null
    c = s.byte(pos)
    if c == 34:
        return Value.Str(_string(s, &pos, &err))
    if c == 123:
        pos += 1
        keys: [str] = []
        vals: [Value] = []
        _ws(s, &pos)
        if pos < len(s) and s.byte(pos) == 125:
            pos += 1
            return Value.Obj(keys, vals)
        while err == "":
            _ws(s, &pos)
            if pos >= len(s) or s.byte(pos) != 34:
                err = "expected a key string"
                break
            keys.push(_string(s, &pos, &err))
            _ws(s, &pos)
            if pos >= len(s) or s.byte(pos) != 58:
                err = "expected `:` after a key"
                break
            pos += 1
            vals.push(_value(s, &pos, &err, depth + 1))
            _ws(s, &pos)
            if pos < len(s) and s.byte(pos) == 44:
                pos += 1
            elif pos < len(s) and s.byte(pos) == 125:
                pos += 1
                break
            else:
                err = "expected `,` or `}`"
        return Value.Obj(keys, vals)
    if c == 91:
        pos += 1
        items: [Value] = []
        _ws(s, &pos)
        if pos < len(s) and s.byte(pos) == 93:
            pos += 1
            return Value.Arr(items)
        while err == "":
            items.push(_value(s, &pos, &err, depth + 1))
            _ws(s, &pos)
            if pos < len(s) and s.byte(pos) == 44:
                pos += 1
            elif pos < len(s) and s.byte(pos) == 93:
                pos += 1
                break
            else:
                err = "expected `,` or `]`"
        return Value.Arr(items)
    if s[pos..pos + 4] == "true":
        pos += 4
        return Value.Bool(true)
    if s[pos..pos + 5] == "false":
        pos += 5
        return Value.Bool(false)
    if s[pos..pos + 4] == "null":
        pos += 4
        return Value.Null
    start = pos
    while pos < len(s):
        d = s.byte(pos)
        if (d >= 48 and d <= 57) or d == 45 or d == 43 or d == 46 or d == 101 or d == 69:
            pos += 1
        else:
            break
    text = s[start..pos]
    x = text.to_float(0.0)
    if pos == start or (x == 0.0 and not _zeroish(text)):
        err = "unexpected character"
        return Value.Null
    return Value.Num(x, text)

fn _zeroish(t: str) bool:
    for i in 0..len(t):
        c = t.byte(i)
        if c >= 49 and c <= 57:
            return false
    return len(t) > 0 and t != "-" and t != "."

# parse JSON text into a Value (Err says what's wrong and at which byte)
fn parse(text: str) Result[Value, str]:
    err = ""
    pos = 0
    v = _value(text, &pos, &err, 0)
    if err == "":
        _ws(text, &pos)
        if pos != len(text):
            err = "extra text after the value"
    if err != "":
        return Err(f"json: {err} at byte {pos}")
    return Ok(v)

# the value under key in an object (the last one, if repeated), or Null
fn field(v: Value, key: str) Value:
    match v:
        Obj(keys, vals):
            i = len(keys) - 1
            while i >= 0:
                if keys[i] == key:
                    return vals[i]
                i -= 1
        _:
            pass
    return Value.Null

# element i of an array, or Null
fn at(v: Value, i: int) Value:
    match v:
        Arr(items):
            if i >= 0 and i < len(items):
                return items[i]
        _:
            pass
    return Value.Null

fn str_or(v: Value, default: str) str:
    match v:
        Str(s):
            return s
        _:
            return default

fn float_or(v: Value, default: float) float:
    match v:
        Num(x, t):
            return x
        _:
            return default

fn int_or(v: Value, default: int) int:
    match v:
        Num(x, t):
            if not (t.contains(".") or t.contains("e") or t.contains("E")):
                return t.to_int(default)
            if x >= -9.2e18 and x <= 9.2e18:
                return int(x)
            return default
        _:
            return default

fn bool_or(v: Value, default: bool) bool:
    match v:
        Bool(b):
            return b
        _:
            return default

# an object's keys in order ([] for anything else)
fn fields(v: Value) [str]:
    match v:
        Obj(keys, vals):
            return keys
        _:
            return []

# an object as a map (a repeated key keeps its last value, as field() does; {} for anything else)
fn to_map(v: Value) {str: Value}:
    m: {str: Value} = {}
    match v:
        Obj(keys, vals):
            for i, k in keys:
                m[k] = vals[i]
        _:
            pass
    return m

# an array's elements ([] for anything else)
fn elems(v: Value) [Value]:
    match v:
        Arr(items):
            return items
        _:
            return []

# how many elements or keys (0 for anything else)
fn size(v: Value) int:
    match v:
        Arr(items):
            return len(items)
        Obj(keys, vals):
            return len(keys)
        _:
            return 0

# the value as compact JSON text
fn dump(v: Value) str:
    match v:
        Null:
            return "null"
        Bool(b):
            return "true" if b else "false"
        Num(x, t):
            return t
        Str(s):
            return json_quote(s)
        Arr(items):
            parts: [str] = []
            for x in items:
                parts.push(dump(x))
            return "[" + ",".join(parts) + "]"
        Obj(keys, vals):
            parts: [str] = []
            for i, k in keys:
                parts.push(json_quote(k) + ":" + dump(vals[i]))
            return "{" + ",".join(parts) + "}"
```

## library/std/json/scan.tn

```tern
# json: the scanner the decoders read with. JSON as json.decode has always taken it:
# whitespace (space, tab, CR, LF) before any token; a number is what C's strtod reads whole
# from a sign and then a run of 0-9 . e E + -; strings undo \n \t \r \b \f \uXXXX (a surrogate
# pair as one character) and take any other escaped byte as itself.

import simd

struct _P:
    s: str
    i: int
    depth: int          # values _skip is inside
    kl: int             # the last key's length (-1: it had escapes; it's in kbuf)
    kv: bytes16         # ... its first 16 bytes (zeros past its end)
    ka: int             # ... where it starts in s
    kbuf: str

fn _lanes() bytes16:
    return simd.of("\x00\x01\x02\x03\x04\x05\x06\x07\x08\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x0e\x0f")

fn _ws_p(p: mut _P):
    if p.i < len(p.s) and p.s.byte(p.i) > 32:     # (the usual case: nothing to skip)
        return
    _ws_run(&p)

fn _ws_run(p: mut _P):
    s = p.s
    n = len(s)
    i = p.i
    while i < n:
        c = s.byte(i)
        if c > 32 or (c != 32 and c != 10 and c != 13 and c != 9):
            break
        i += 1
    p.i = i

# the byte c next (after whitespace): taken
fn _eat(p: mut _P, c: int) bool:
    if p.i < len(p.s) and p.s.byte(p.i) == c:
        p.i += 1
        return true
    _ws_p(&p)
    if p.i < len(p.s) and p.s.byte(p.i) == c:
        p.i += 1
        return true
    return false

# is the next byte c? (no whitespace skipped)
fn _peek(p: _P, c: int) bool:
    return p.i < len(p.s) and p.s.byte(p.i) == c

# null next: taken
fn _null(p: mut _P) bool:
    s = p.s
    i = p.i
    if i < len(s) and s.byte(i) > 32 and s.byte(i) != 110:
        return false
    _ws_p(&p)
    i = p.i
    if i + 4 <= len(s) and s.byte(i) == 110 and s.byte(i + 1) == 117 and s.byte(i + 2) == 108 and s.byte(i + 3) == 108:
        p.i = i + 4
        return true
    return false

# the first " or \ in s[i0..n] (n if none)
fn _quote_or_bs(s: str, i0: int, n: int) int:
    i = i0
    while i < n:
        v = simd.load_upto(s, i)
        k = simd.first_lane(simd.eq(v, simd.splat(34)) | simd.eq(v, simd.splat(92)))
        if k < 16:
            return min(i + k, n)
        i += 16
    return n

fn _hx(c: int) int:
    if c >= 48 and c <= 57:
        return c - 48
    d = c | 32
    if d >= 97 and d <= 102:
        return d - 87
    return -1

fn _hex4p(s: str, i: int) int:
    v = 0
    for k in 0..4:
        h = _hx(s.byte(i + k))
        if h < 0:
            return -1
        v = v * 16 + h
    return v

# cp as UTF-8 (a lone surrogate too, as 3 bytes)
fn _utf8_to(o: mut str, cp: int):
    if cp < 0x80:
        o += chr(cp)
    elif cp < 0x800:
        o += chr(0xc0 | (cp >> 6)) + chr(0x80 | (cp & 63))
    elif cp < 0x10000:
        o += chr(0xe0 | (cp >> 12)) + chr(0x80 | ((cp >> 6) & 63)) + chr(0x80 | (cp & 63))
    else:
        o += chr(0xf0 | (cp >> 18)) + chr(0x80 | ((cp >> 12) & 63)) + chr(0x80 | ((cp >> 6) & 63)) + chr(0x80 | (cp & 63))

# a string's text with its escapes undone, from just after its opening " (at p.i)
fn _str_body(p: mut _P, out: mut str) bool:
    s = p.s
    n = len(s)
    a = p.i
    q = _quote_or_bs(s, a, n)
    if q < n and s.byte(q) == 34:          # no escapes: one copy
        out = s[a..q]
        p.i = q + 1
        return true
    o = s[a..q]
    i = q
    while i < n:
        c = s.byte(i)
        if c == 34:
            p.i = i + 1
            out = o
            return true
        if c != 92:
            t = _quote_or_bs(s, i, n)
            o += s[i..t]
            i = t
            continue
        i += 1
        if i >= n:
            break
        e = s.byte(i)
        i += 1
        if e == 117:
            if n - i < 4:
                break
            cp = _hex4p(s, i)
            i += 4
            if cp < 0:
                break
            if cp >= 0xd800 and cp < 0xdc00 and n - i >= 6 and s.byte(i) == 92 and s.byte(i + 1) == 117:
                lo = _hex4p(s, i + 2)
                if lo >= 0xdc00 and lo < 0xe000:
                    cp = 0x10000 + ((cp - 0xd800) << 10) + (lo - 0xdc00)
                    i += 6
            _utf8_to(&o, cp)
        elif e == 110:
            o += "\n"
        elif e == 116:
            o += "\t"
        elif e == 114:
            o += "\r"
        elif e == 98:
            o += "\x08"
        elif e == 102:
            o += "\x0c"
        else:
            o += chr(e)
    return false

# an object's key and the `:` after it. The key stays where it is in the text (kl, kv, ka),
# unless it has escapes (then kbuf, kl -1).
fn _key(p: mut _P) bool:
    if not _eat(&p, 34):
        return false
    s = p.s
    a = p.i
    v = simd.load_upto(s, a)
    kq = simd.first_lane(simd.eq(v, simd.splat(34)) | simd.eq(v, simd.splat(92)))
    q = a + kq if kq < 16 else _quote_or_bs(s, a + 16, len(s))
    if q < len(s) and s.byte(q) == 34:
        p.kl = q - a
        p.ka = a
        p.kv = v & simd.lt(_lanes(), simd.splat(kq))
        p.i = q + 1
    else:
        k = ""
        if not _str_body(&p, &k):
            return false
        p.kl = -1
        p.kbuf = k
    if p.i < len(s) and s.byte(p.i) == 58:
        p.i += 1
        return true
    return _eat(&p, 58)

# is the last key `name` (n bytes long, its first 16 bytes v, zeros after)?
fn _key_is(p: _P, n: int, v: bytes16, name: str) bool:
    if p.kl == n:
        return p.kv == v and (n <= 16 or p.s[p.ka..p.ka + n] == name)
    return p.kl < 0 and p.kbuf == name

# the last key as a string
fn _key_str(p: _P) str:
    if p.kl < 0:
        return p.kbuf
    return p.s[p.ka..p.ka + p.kl]

# a byte that can be part of a number: 0-9 . e E - +
fn _numch(c: int) bool:
    return (c >= 48 and c <= 57) or c == 46 or c == 101 or c == 69 or c == 45 or c == 43

# the number at p.i (after whitespace): [+-] then a run of _numch bytes; its end, or -1
# (an empty run, or more than 60 bytes)
fn _numtok(p: mut _P) int:
    _ws_p(&p)
    s = p.s
    n = len(s)
    i = p.i
    if i < n and (s.byte(i) == 45 or s.byte(i) == 43):
        i += 1
    d = i
    while i < n and _numch(s.byte(i)):
        i += 1
    if i == d or i - p.i > 60:
        return -1
    return i

# is s[a0..e] one whole decimal number as strtod reads it ([+-] digits [. digits] [e [+-] digits],
# a digit somewhere before the e)?
fn _numok(s: str, a0: int, e: int) bool:
    a = a0
    if s.byte(a) == 45 or s.byte(a) == 43:
        a += 1
    digits = 0
    while a < e and s.byte(a) >= 48 and s.byte(a) <= 57:
        a += 1
        digits += 1
    if a < e and s.byte(a) == 46:
        a += 1
        while a < e and s.byte(a) >= 48 and s.byte(a) <= 57:
            a += 1
            digits += 1
    if digits == 0:
        return false
    if a < e and (s.byte(a) == 101 or s.byte(a) == 69):
        a += 1
        if a < e and (s.byte(a) == 45 or s.byte(a) == 43):
            a += 1
        ed = a
        while a < e and s.byte(a) >= 48 and s.byte(a) <= 57:
            a += 1
        if a == ed:
            return false
    return a == e

# 10^k for k in 0..22 (each exact as a float)
fn _pow10(k: int) float:
    if k < 8:
        if k < 4:
            return [1.0, 10.0, 100.0, 1000.0][k]
        return [1e4, 1e5, 1e6, 1e7][k - 4]
    if k < 16:
        if k < 12:
            return [1e8, 1e9, 1e10, 1e11][k - 8]
        return [1e12, 1e13, 1e14, 1e15][k - 12]
    if k < 20:
        return [1e16, 1e17, 1e18, 1e19][k - 16]
    return [1e20, 1e21, 1e22][k - 20]

# s[a0..e] (checked by _numok) as strtod reads it: worked out here when the digits fit in 2^53
# and the power of ten is exact (one rounding, so the same float), else by strtod
fn _numval(s: str, a0: int, e: int) float:
    a = a0
    neg = s.byte(a) == 45
    if neg or s.byte(a) == 43:
        a += 1
    w = 0
    nd = 0
    scale = 0
    frac = false
    i = a
    while i < e:
        c = s.byte(i)
        if c == 46:
            frac = true
        elif c >= 48 and c <= 57:
            if nd >= 15:
                return s[a0..e].to_float(0.0)
            w = w * 10 + (c - 48)
            if w != 0:
                nd += 1
            if frac:
                scale -= 1
        else:
            break
        i += 1
    if i < e:
        i += 1
        eneg = false
        if s.byte(i) == 45 or s.byte(i) == 43:
            eneg = s.byte(i) == 45
            i += 1
        x = 0
        while i < e:
            if x < 100000:
                x = x * 10 + (s.byte(i) - 48)
            i += 1
        scale += -x if eneg else x
    if scale < -22 or scale > 22:
        return s[a0..e].to_float(0.0)
    v = float(w)
    if scale < 0:
        v = v / _pow10(-scale)
    else:
        v = v * _pow10(scale)
    return -v if neg else v

fn _dec_float(p: mut _P, out: mut float) bool:
    _ws_p(&p)
    s = p.s
    n = len(s)
    i = p.i
    neg = false
    if i < n and s.byte(i) == 45:
        neg = true
        i += 1
    w = 0
    nd = 0
    scale = 0
    d = i
    while i < n and nd < 16:               # the plain case first: [-] digits [. digits]
        c = s.byte(i) - 48
        if c < 0 or c > 9:
            break
        w = w * 10 + c
        if w != 0:
            nd += 1
        i += 1
    if i > d and i < n and s.byte(i) == 46 and nd < 16:
        i += 1
        f = i
        while i < n and nd < 16:
            c = s.byte(i) - 48
            if c < 0 or c > 9:
                break
            w = w * 10 + c
            if w != 0:
                nd += 1
            i += 1
        scale = f - i
        if i == f and i < n and _numch(s.byte(i)):
            return _dec_float_slow(&p, &out)
    if i > d and nd < 16 and scale >= -22 and (i == n or not _numch(s.byte(i))) and i - p.i <= 60:
        v = float(w)
        if scale < 0:
            v = v / _pow10(-scale)
        out = -v if neg else v
        p.i = i
        return true
    return _dec_float_slow(&p, &out)

fn _dec_float_slow(p: mut _P, out: mut float) bool:
    e = _numtok(&p)
    if e < 0 or not _numok(p.s, p.i, e):
        return false
    out = _numval(p.s, p.i, e)
    p.i = e
    return true

fn _dec_int(p: mut _P, out: mut int) bool:
    _ws_p(&p)
    s = p.s
    n = len(s)
    i = p.i
    neg = false
    if i < n and s.byte(i) == 45:
        neg = true
        i += 1
    d = i
    u = 0
    while i < n:                           # the plain case first: [-] digits
        c = s.byte(i) - 48
        if c < 0 or c > 9:
            break
        if u < 0 or u > 922337203685477580 or (u == 922337203685477580 and c > (8 if neg else 7)):     # (u < 0: already -2^63)
            u = -1
            break
        u = u * 10 + c
        i += 1
    if u >= 0 and i > d and i - p.i <= 60 and (i == n or not _numch(s.byte(i))):
        out = -u if neg else u
        p.i = i
        return true
    return _dec_int_slow(&p, &out)

# an integer as strtoll reads it (past int64 is an error); else a number that is a whole
# float inside the int range (3.0 or 1e2, not 3.5)
fn _dec_int_slow(p: mut _P, out: mut int) bool:
    e = _numtok(&p)
    if e < 0:
        return false
    s = p.s
    a = p.i
    neg = s.byte(a) == 45
    if neg or s.byte(a) == 43:
        a += 1
    u = 0
    i = a
    while i < e:
        c = s.byte(i) - 48
        if c < 0 or c > 9:
            break
        if u < 0 or u > 922337203685477580 or (u == 922337203685477580 and c > (8 if neg else 7)):     # (u < 0: already -2^63)
            return false
        u = u * 10 + c
        i += 1
    if i == e and i > a:
        out = -u if neg else u
        p.i = e
        return true
    if not _numok(s, p.i, e):
        return false
    v = _numval(s, p.i, e)
    if not (v > -9.2e18 and v < 9.2e18) or v != float(int(v)):
        return false
    out = int(v)
    p.i = e
    return true

fn _dec_bool(p: mut _P, out: mut bool) bool:
    _ws_p(&p)
    s = p.s
    i = p.i
    if i + 4 <= len(s) and s.byte(i) == 116 and s.byte(i + 1) == 114 and s.byte(i + 2) == 117 and s.byte(i + 3) == 101:
        p.i = i + 4
        out = true
        return true
    if i + 5 <= len(s) and s.byte(i) == 102 and s.byte(i + 1) == 97 and s.byte(i + 2) == 108 and s.byte(i + 3) == 115 and s.byte(i + 4) == 101:
        p.i = i + 5
        out = false
        return true
    return false

fn _dec_str(p: mut _P, out: mut str) bool:
    if not _eat(&p, 34):
        return false
    return _str_body(&p, &out)

# past any one value (nested at most 256 deep)
fn _skip(p: mut _P) bool:
    _ws_p(&p)
    if p.i >= len(p.s):
        return false
    p.depth += 1
    if p.depth > 256:
        return false
    ok = true
    c = p.s.byte(p.i)
    if c == 34:
        t = ""
        ok = _dec_str(&p, &t)
    elif c == 123 or c == 91:
        close = 125 if c == 123 else 93
        p.i += 1
        if not _eat(&p, close):
            while true:
                if c == 123 and not _key(&p):
                    ok = false
                    break
                if not _skip(&p):
                    ok = false
                    break
                if not _eat(&p, 44):
                    break
            ok = ok and _eat(&p, close)
    elif c == 116 or c == 102:
        b = false
        ok = _dec_bool(&p, &b)
    elif c == 110:
        ok = _null(&p)
    else:
        x = 0.0
        ok = _dec_float(&p, &x)
    p.depth -= 1
    return ok

# does s name an enum variant loosely: ignoring case and _ - and spaces? ("in_progress",
# "IN-PROGRESS" and "in progress" all name InProgress)
fn _loose(s: str, name: str) bool:
    i = 0
    j = 0
    while true:
        while i < len(s) and (s.byte(i) == 95 or s.byte(i) == 45 or s.byte(i) == 32):
            i += 1
        while j < len(name) and name.byte(j) == 95:
            j += 1
        if i == len(s) or j == len(name):
            return i == len(s) and j == len(name)
        a = s.byte(i)
        b = name.byte(j)
        if a >= 65 and a <= 90:
            a += 32
        if b >= 65 and b <= 90:
            b += 32
        if a != b:
            return false
        i += 1
        j += 1
    return false
```

## library/std/log.tn

```tern
# log: leveled, structured logging to stderr, one line per call.
#
#   import log
#   log.info("server started")
#   log.info_with("user logged in", {"user": name, "id": str(id)})
#   log.warn("slow query")      log.error_with("payment failed", {"order": oid, "err": msg})
#   log.debug("cache miss")     (hidden unless the level is debug)
#
# Output (logfmt, the default):
#   time=2026-09-28T06:45:12.345Z level=info msg="user logged in" user=ada id=7
# log.set_format("json"):
#   {"time":"2026-09-28T06:45:12.345Z","level":"info","msg":"user logged in","user":"ada","id":"7"}
# log.set_format("text"), for people:
#   2026-09-28 06:45:12.345 INFO  user logged in user=ada id=7
#
#   log.debug(msg str)  log.info(msg str)  log.warn(msg str)  log.error(msg str)
#   log.debug_with(msg str, fields {str: str})  ... info_with, warn_with, error_with
#   log.set_level(name str) bool      "debug", "info" (default), "warn", "error", "off"
#   log.set_format(name str) bool     "logfmt" (default), "json", "text"
#   Or set them from the environment: TERN_LOG_LEVEL=debug, TERN_LOG_FORMAT=json.
#
# Times are UTC. Each line is one write(2), so lines from different threads never mix;
# a call below the level costs almost nothing (the fields aren't formatted).
#
# The last 100 records at warn and above are also kept in memory, whatever the level, for
# error reporters (Sentry breadcrumbs, a crash page):
#   log.recent(n int) [Record]        the newest n, oldest first (Record: time, level, msg, fields)
#   log.keep(name str) bool           keep records from this level up instead ("info", "off", ...)

import os
import task
import time

struct Record:
    time: float                 # seconds since 1970
    level: str
    msg: str
    fields: {str: str}

const _NAMES = ["debug", "info", "warn", "error"]
const _LEVEL = task.atomic(-1)          # -1 until read from the environment (TERN_LOG_LEVEL)
const _FORMAT = task.atomic(0)          # 0 logfmt, 1 json, 2 text
const _KEEP = task.atomic(2)            # log.recent keeps records from this level up (warn)
const _RING = task.shared(_Ring([], 0))

struct _Ring:
    recs: [Record]              # up to _RING_N, the oldest at next once it's full
    next: int

const _RING_N = 100

fn _level_of(s: str) int:
    l = s.lower()
    for i, nm in _NAMES:
        if l == nm:
            return i
    if l == "warning":
        return 2
    if l == "off" or l == "none":
        return 4
    return -1

fn _init():
    if _LEVEL.load() >= 0:
        return
    f = os.env("TERN_LOG_FORMAT", "").lower()
    _FORMAT.store(1 if f == "json" else 2 if f == "text" else 0)
    lv = _level_of(os.env("TERN_LOG_LEVEL", ""))
    _LEVEL.store(lv if lv >= 0 else 1)

# "debug", "info" (default), "warn", "error", "off"; false (and no change) for another name
fn set_level(name: str) bool:
    lv = _level_of(name)
    _init()
    if lv < 0:
        return false
    _LEVEL.store(lv)
    return true

# "logfmt" (default), "json", "text"; false (and no change) for another name
fn set_format(name: str) bool:
    f = 0 if name == "logfmt" else 1 if name == "json" else 2 if name == "text" else -1
    _init()
    if f < 0:
        return false
    _FORMAT.store(f)
    return true

# log.recent keeps records from this level up instead ("off": none); false for another name
fn keep(name: str) bool:
    lv = _level_of(name)
    if lv < 0:
        return false
    _KEEP.store(lv)
    return true

fn recent(n: int) [Record]:
    fn newest(r: mut _Ring) [Record]:
        out: [Record] = []
        k = len(r.recs)
        m = min(n, k)
        for i in 0..m:
            out.push(r.recs[(r.next - m + i + k) % k])
        return out
    return _RING.update(newest)

fn _remember(level: int, msg: str, fields: {str: str}):
    rec = Record(time.now(), _NAMES[level], msg, fields)
    fn add(r: mut _Ring) int:
        if len(r.recs) < _RING_N:
            r.recs.push(rec)
            r.next = len(r.recs) % _RING_N
        else:
            r.recs[r.next] = rec
            r.next = (r.next + 1) % _RING_N
        return 0
    _RING.update(add)

# logfmt's value: as it is, or quoted (JSON's escapes) if it's empty or has a space, a quote,
# =, \, a control character or a non-ASCII one
fn _logfmt_val(o: mut str, v: str):
    quote = len(v) == 0
    for i in 0..len(v):
        b = v.byte(i)
        if b <= 32 or b == 34 or b == 61 or b == 92 or b >= 128:
            quote = true
            break
    if quote:
        o += json_quote(v)
    else:
        o += v

fn _log(level: int, msg: str, fields: {str: str}):
    _init()
    keep = _KEEP.load()
    if level >= keep and keep < 4:
        _remember(level, msg, fields)
    if level < _LEVEL.load():
        return
    now = time.now()
    lv = _NAMES[level]
    f = _FORMAT.load()
    o = ""
    o.reserve(64 + len(msg) + len(fields) * 24)
    if f == 1:
        o += "{\"time\":\"" + time.format(now, "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%LZ") + "\",\"level\":\"" + lv + "\",\"msg\":" + json_quote(msg)
        for k, v in fields:
            o += "," + json_quote(k) + ":" + json_quote(v)
        o += "}\n"
    elif f == 2:
        o += time.format(now, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%L") + " " + ["DEBUG", "INFO ", "WARN ", "ERROR"][level] + " " + msg
        for k, v in fields:
            o += " " + k + "="
            _logfmt_val(&o, v)
        o += "\n"
    else:
        o += "time=" + time.format(now, "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%LZ") + " level=" + lv + " msg="
        _logfmt_val(&o, msg)
        for k, v in fields:
            o += " " + k + "="
            _logfmt_val(&o, v)
        o += "\n"
    _out(o)

fn debug(msg: str):
    _log(0, msg, {})

fn info(msg: str):
    _log(1, msg, {})

fn warn(msg: str):
    _log(2, msg, {})

fn error(msg: str):
    _log(3, msg, {})

fn debug_with(msg: str, fields: {str: str}):
    _log(0, msg, fields)

fn info_with(msg: str, fields: {str: str}):
    _log(1, msg, fields)

fn warn_with(msg: str, fields: {str: str}):
    _log(2, msg, fields)

fn error_with(msg: str, fields: {str: str}):
    _log(3, msg, fields)
```

## library/std/math.tn

```tern
# math: floating-point functions.
#   math.sqrt floor ceil round log exp sin cos tan (float) float
#   math.pow(x, y) float    math.pi() float
#   math.popcount(x) int    the bits set in x's 64 (the CPU's popcount: one instruction)
```

## library/std/net.tn

```tern
# net: TCP connections for tasks. Reads and writes look blocking, but only the task
# waits (the other tasks keep running). Also works outside tasks (the thread waits).
#
#   import net
#   import task
#   fn serve_one(c: net.Conn):
#       line = c.read_line()                  # "hello\n"; "" when the peer closes
#       c.write("echo: " + line)
#       c.close()
#   fn main():
#       l = net.listen(9000)                  # every address; net.listen_on("127.0.0.1", 9000)
#       while true:
#           c = l.accept()
#           task.spawn(fn() serve_one(c))
#
#   c = net.connect("example.com", 80)        # check c.ok(); net.error() says why it failed
#
# net.listen(port int) Listener               net.listen_on(host str, port int) Listener
# net.port(l Listener) int  (after listen(0))  net.accept(l Listener) Conn   net.stop(l Listener)
# net.connect(host str, port int) Conn        net.ok(c Conn) bool           net.error() str
# net.read(c Conn, max int) str   ("" at end) net.read_line(c Conn) str  (with its "\n"; "" at end)
# net.read_exact(c Conn, n int) str           net.write(c Conn, data str) bool (false: peer gone)
# net.close(c Conn)                           net.peer(c Conn) str  ("1.2.3.4:5678")
# net.starttls(c Conn, host str, verify bool) bool   TLS on an open connection (needs `import tls`)
# net.starttls_within(c Conn, host str, verify bool, ms int) bool   the same, the handshake within ms
# net.tls_linked() bool                       did the program import tls (so TLS works)?
# net.write_within(c Conn, data str, ms int) bool    write; false once ms pass without room for the rest
# net.pending(c Conn) bool                    a read wouldn't wait (data, or the end, is there)
# net.refill(c Conn, buf mut str, used int, max int) int    drop buf[..used], read onto buf's end
# net.refill_within(c Conn, buf mut str, used int, max int, ms int) int   the same; -1 if nothing came in ms
# net.connect_within(host str, port int, ms int) Conn   connect (resolving too) within ms
# net.wait_read(c Conn, ms int) bool          true once a read won't wait; false after ms
# net.read_line_within(c Conn, ms int) str    a whole line, or "" if none came within ms (or the end)
# net.dns_query(name str, qtype int, ms int) str   one DNS question's raw answer ("" if none)
# net.lookup_mx(domain str, ms int) Result[[Mx], str]   mail servers, most preferred first
#
# A Conn is its socket: copies refer to the same connection, and close() closes it for
# all of them (close it when you're done; the program's end closes the rest).
# Not available on wasm.

struct Conn:
    fd: int

struct Listener:
    fd: int

# with Result: c = net.dial("example.com", 80)?   (Err: "net: connect: Connection refused")
fn dial(host: str, port: int) Result[Conn, str]:
    c = connect(host, port)
    if not c.ok():
        return Err("net: " + error())
    return Ok(c)

# TLS on a connection that is already open, when the protocol says so first (PostgreSQL's
# SSLRequest, SMTP's STARTTLS). verify: check the certificate and the host name. Needs
# `import tls` in the program; without it (and when the handshake fails) false, and
# net.error() says why.
fn starttls(c: Conn, host: str, verify: bool) bool:
    return _starttls(c.fd, host, verify)

fn starttls_within(c: Conn, host: str, verify: bool, ms: int) bool:
    return _starttls_ms(c.fd, host, verify, ms)

fn tls_linked() bool:
    return _tls_linked()

# all of data, or false (net.error() says why) once ms pass with the peer not taking the rest
fn write_within(c: Conn, data: str, ms: int) bool:
    return _write_ms(c.fd, data, ms)

# Would a read return at once (data, or the end, is waiting)? A look without waiting: an idle
# connection the other side closed says so here (a connection pool's health check).
fn pending(c: Conn) bool:
    return _pending(c.fd)

# A buffered reader's step, for protocols: drops buf[..used] (what's been read), then reads up
# to max more bytes onto the end of buf, in place: no new string per read. Returns the bytes
# read (0: the end, or an error: net.error()).
#   n = c.refill(&buf, at, 65536)     # (then at = 0: what was at buf[at] is at buf[0])
fn refill(c: Conn, buf: mut str, used: int, max: int) int:
    return _refill(c.fd, &buf, used, max)

# refill, waiting at most ms for bytes: -1 when none came in time
fn refill_within(c: Conn, buf: mut str, used: int, max: int, ms: int) int:
    return _refill_ms(c.fd, &buf, used, max, ms)

# connect, the whole attempt (resolving included) within ms milliseconds; check c.ok()
fn connect_within(host: str, port: int, ms: int) Conn:
    return Conn(_connect_ms(host, port, ms))

# Wait (only the task) until a read would return at once: data, or the end. false after ms
# milliseconds without either: a protocol's read timeout.
#   if not c.wait_read(10000): ...       # the server said nothing for 10 s
fn wait_read(c: Conn, ms: int) bool:
    return _readable(c.fd, ms)

# the next line (with its "\n"), or "" when no whole line came within ms or the peer closed
# (a part of one stays buffered for the next read)
fn read_line_within(c: Conn, ms: int) str:
    return _read_line_ms(c.fd, ms)

# One DNS question (qtype: 1 A, 15 MX, 16 TXT, 28 AAAA, ...) over UDP to the servers in
# TERN_DNS_SERVERS, else /etc/resolv.conf's: the answer's raw bytes (RFC 1035), "" if none
# came within ms. lookup_mx reads one; use this for the record types it doesn't.
fn dns_query(name: str, qtype: int, ms: int) str:
    return _dns(name, qtype, ms)

struct Mx:
    pref: int       # lower is preferred
    host: str

fn _u16(b: str, o: int) int:
    return b.byte(o) * 256 + b.byte(o + 1)

# the name at o in a DNS message (compression pointers followed) and where it ends
fn _dns_name(b: str, o0: int) (str, int):
    out = ""
    o = o0
    end = -1
    hops = 0
    while o < len(b) and hops < 64:
        c = b.byte(o)
        if c == 0:
            if end < 0:
                end = o + 1
            return (out, end)
        if c >= 192:
            if o + 1 >= len(b):
                return ("", -1)
            if end < 0:
                end = o + 2
            o = (c - 192) * 256 + b.byte(o + 1)
            hops += 1
            continue
        if o + 1 + c > len(b):
            return ("", -1)
        if out != "":
            out += "."
        out += b[o + 1..o + 1 + c]
        o += 1 + c
    return ("", -1)

# A domain's mail servers (MX records), most preferred first. Ok([]) when the domain exists
# but has none (mail then goes to its A record, RFC 5321); Err when it doesn't exist or no
# answer came within ms.
fn lookup_mx(domain: str, ms: int) Result[[Mx], str]:
    b = _dns(domain, 15, ms)
    if len(b) < 12:
        return Err("no answer for " + domain)
    rcode = b.byte(3) % 16
    if rcode == 3:
        return Err("no such domain: " + domain)
    if rcode != 0:
        return Err("name server failed for " + domain + " (rcode " + str(rcode) + ")")
    qd = _u16(b, 4)
    an = _u16(b, 6)
    o = 12
    for _ in 0..qd:
        o = _dns_name(b, o).1
        if o < 0:
            return Err("bad answer for " + domain)
        o += 4
    out: [Mx] = []
    for _ in 0..an:
        n = _dns_name(b, o)
        o = n.1
        if o < 0 or o + 10 > len(b):
            return Err("bad answer for " + domain)
        kind = _u16(b, o)
        size = _u16(b, o + 8)
        o += 10
        if o + size > len(b):
            return Err("bad answer for " + domain)
        if kind == 15 and size >= 3:
            h = _dns_name(b, o + 2)
            if h.1 >= 0:
                out.push(Mx(_u16(b, o), h.0.lower()))
        o += size
    return Ok(out.sort_by(fn(m) m.pref))
```

## library/std/os.tn

```tern
# os: the process: arguments, environment, exit, stderr, stdin, subprocesses, signals.
#   os.env(name str, default str) str       os.args() [str]  (args()[0] is the program)
#   os.exit(code int)                       (stdout is flushed first)
#   os.eprint(s str)                        a line to stderr
#   os.flush()                              write out buffered stdout now (print is buffered when
#                                           stdout isn't a terminal)
#   os.cpu_count() int                      the cores this process may use (Linux: its affinity mask)
#   os.load_avg() float                     the 1-minute load average (-1.0 where there's none)
#   os.getpid() int                         this process's id
#   os.executable() str                     the running program's absolute path ("" if unknown)
#   os.read_line() str                      the next line of stdin, with its "\n" ("" at the end)
#   os.read_all() str                       the rest of stdin
#   os.run(cmd str, args [str]) Output      run a program (PATH is searched) and wait for it
#   os.run_input(cmd str, args [str], input str) Output     ... with input as its stdin
#       Output fields: status (exit code; 128+n if killed by signal n; -1 if it couldn't be
#       started, and then err says why), out (its stdout), err (its stderr)
#   os.wait_signal() str                    wait for SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGHUP, SIGUSR1 or SIGUSR2 and
#                                           return its name; the first call makes those signals
#                                           events instead of ending the program. Each signal goes
#                                           to one waiter. (roost.serve drains and returns on
#                                           SIGINT / SIGTERM by itself.)
#   os.spawn(cmd str, args [str]) Process   start a program and keep going; its stdin and stdout
#                                           are pipes, its stderr is ours
#   os.spawn_with(cmd, args, ProcOpts) Process    ... with ProcOpts fields: dir (where it runs; ""
#       here), env (["NAME=value", ...] added to ours), out ("pipe", "inherit", "null", or a
#       file path), err ("inherit", "out" (into its stdout), "null", or a file path)
#   p.ok() bool                             false if it couldn't be started (os.error() says why)
#   p.write(text) bool   p.close_input()    to its stdin (false once it stopped reading)
#   p.out_line() str                        the next line of its stdout, with its "\n" ("" at the end)
#   p.out_bytes(n) str                      the next n bytes of its stdout (fewer at the end)
#   p.out_all() str                         the rest of its stdout (waits for it to close it)
#   p.wait() int                            its exit status (128+n if killed by signal n)
#   p.wait_ms(ms) int                       ... or -1 if it's still running after ms milliseconds
#   p.kill(sig) bool                        send signal sig (15 TERM, 9 KILL, 2 INT) to it and to
#                                           the processes it started (it has its own process group)
#   p.pid() int
#   os.cwd() str   os.chdir(dir) bool   os.setenv(name, value)  (value "" removes it)
#   os.error() str                          why the last spawn / chdir on this thread failed
#   os.on_error(f fn(ErrorReport))          call f with a report of every runtime error from now on,
#                                           caught ones too (a failed task, a web handler's 500):
#                                           message, file, line, function, frames [Frame{function,
#                                           pc}], image_base, slide, build_id, task_id, thread_id,
#                                           time (ns), locals (the failing task's task-locals).
#                                           f runs on a thread of its own, one report at a
#                                           time; its own errors are dropped. Stack overflows aren't
#                                           reported. (For error trackers like Sentry.)
#   os.last_error_report() ErrorReport      the most recent report (message "" if none); recording
#                                           starts with the first on_error or last_error_report call
#   os.at_exit(f fn())                      call f when the program ends (main returns, os.exit, or a
#                                           runtime error; not a signal), the last one added first
# Reading stdin or waiting for a subprocess or a signal parks only the task (in a task).
#
#   r = os.run("git", ["rev-parse", "HEAD"])
#   if r.status == 0:
#       print(r.out.trim())
#   else:
#       os.eprint("git failed: " + r.err)
#
#   server = os.spawn("./server", ["--port", "8080"])
#   line = server.out_line()                 # e.g. wait until it says it's listening
#   ...
#   server.kill(15)
#   server.wait()

struct Output:
    status: int
    out: str
    err: str

fn run(cmd: str, args: [str]) Output:
    return run_input(cmd, args, "")

struct Process:
    h: int

struct ProcOpts:
    dir: str
    env: [str]
    out: str
    err: str

fn spawn(cmd: str, args: [str]) Process:
    return spawn_with(cmd, args, ProcOpts("", [], "pipe", "inherit"))

fn spawn_with(cmd: str, args: [str], o: ProcOpts) Process:
    return Process(_spawn(cmd, args, o.dir, o.env, o.out, o.err))

fn ok(p: Process) bool:
    return p.h >= 0

fn pid(p: Process) int:
    return _pid(p.h)

fn write(p: Process, text: str) bool:
    return _write(p.h, text)

fn close_input(p: Process):
    _close_input(p.h)

fn out_line(p: Process) str:
    return _out_line(p.h)

fn out_bytes(p: Process, n: int) str:
    return _out_bytes(p.h, n)

fn out_all(p: Process) str:
    return _out_all(p.h)

fn wait(p: Process) int:
    return _wait_ms(p.h, -1)

fn wait_ms(p: Process, ms: int) int:
    return _wait_ms(p.h, ms)

fn kill(p: Process, sig: int) bool:
    return _kill(p.h, sig)

# ---- error reports
struct Frame:
    function: str          # the Tern function (or the C symbol; "" if unknown)
    pc: int

struct ErrorReport:
    message: str           # "runtime error (...): ..." as printed
    file: str              # the source file ("" if unknown)
    line: int
    function: str          # the Tern function the error happened in ("" if unknown)
    frames: [Frame]        # innermost first
    image_base: int        # where the executable is loaded, and its ASLR slide
    slide: int
    build_id: str          # Mach-O LC_UUID / ELF GNU build id, in hex (for symbolicating)
    task_id: int           # 0 outside tasks
    thread_id: int
    time: int              # nanoseconds since the Unix epoch
    locals: {str: str}     # the failing task's task-locals (task.local_set), up to about 4KB

# f runs when the program ends: main returns, os.exit, or a runtime error ends it (a signal
# like SIGKILL doesn't run it). The last one added runs first; a runtime error in one is
# printed and the others still run. For final writes: a queue to commit, a buffer to send.
fn at_exit(f: fn()):
    _at_exit(f)

fn on_error(f: fn(ErrorReport)):
    _on_error(fn(s: str) f(_decode_report(s)))

fn last_error_report() ErrorReport:
    return _decode_report(_last_report())

fn _decode_report(s: str) ErrorReport:
    p = s.split(chr(31))
    locals: {str: str} = {}
    if len(p) < 11:
        return ErrorReport("", "", 0, "", [], 0, 0, "", 0, 0, 0, locals)
    kv = p[10].split(chr(30))
    j = 0
    while j + 1 < len(kv):
        locals[kv[j]] = kv[j + 1]
        j += 2
    frames: [Frame] = []
    i = 11
    while i + 1 < len(p):
        frames.push(Frame(p[i + 1], p[i].to_int(0)))
        i += 2
    return ErrorReport(p[0], p[1], p[2].to_int(0), p[3], frames, p[4].to_int(0), p[5].to_int(0), p[6], p[7].to_int(0), p[8].to_int(0), p[9].to_int(0), locals)
```

## library/std/path/glob.tn

```tern
# path: shell-style patterns (matches) and finding the files that match them (glob).

import fs

fn matches(pattern: str, name: str) bool:
    return _match(pattern, 0, name, 0)

# Iterative * with one backtrack point (linear for patterns with a single *, and never
# exponential: a later * replaces the earlier backtrack point).
fn _match(pat: str, p0: int, s: str, s0: int) bool:
    p = p0
    i = s0
    star_p = -1
    star_i = 0
    np = len(pat)
    ns = len(s)
    while true:
        if p < np:
            c = pat.byte(p)
            if c == 42:
                star_p = p
                star_i = i
                p += 1
                continue
            if i < ns:
                ch = s.byte(i)
                if c == 63:
                    if ch != 47:
                        p += 1
                        i += 1
                        continue
                elif c == 91:
                    end = _class_end(pat, p)
                    if end < 0:
                        return false
                    if ch != 47 and _in_class(pat, p + 1, end, ch):
                        p = end + 1
                        i += 1
                        continue
                elif c == 92:
                    if p + 1 >= np:
                        return false
                    if pat.byte(p + 1) == ch:
                        p += 2
                        i += 1
                        continue
                elif c == ch:
                    p += 1
                    i += 1
                    continue
            elif c == 91 and _class_end(pat, p) < 0:
                return false
        elif i == ns:
            return true
        # mismatch: let the last * take one more byte (never a "/")
        if star_p < 0 or star_i >= ns or s.byte(star_i) == 47:
            return false
        star_i += 1
        p = star_p + 1
        i = star_i
    return false

# Index of the "]" closing the class that starts at pat[p] == "[", or -1.
fn _class_end(pat: str, p: int) int:
    j = p + 1
    n = len(pat)
    if j < n and (pat.byte(j) == 33 or pat.byte(j) == 94):
        j += 1
    if j < n and pat.byte(j) == 93:          # "]" first is a member
        j += 1
    while j < n:
        c = pat.byte(j)
        if c == 92:
            j += 2
            continue
        if c == 93:
            return j
        j += 1
    return -1

fn _in_class(pat: str, a: int, end: int, ch: int) bool:
    neg = false
    j = a
    if j < end and (pat.byte(j) == 33 or pat.byte(j) == 94):
        neg = true
        j += 1
    found = false
    first = true
    while j < end:
        lo = pat.byte(j)
        if lo == 92 and j + 1 < end:
            j += 1
            lo = pat.byte(j)
        elif lo == 93 and not first:
            break
        first = false
        j += 1
        hi = lo
        if j + 1 < end and pat.byte(j) == 45:
            j += 1
            hi = pat.byte(j)
            if hi == 92 and j + 1 < end:
                j += 1
                hi = pat.byte(j)
            j += 1
        if ch >= lo and ch <= hi:
            found = true
    return found != neg

fn _has_meta(s: str) bool:
    for i in 0..len(s):
        c = s.byte(i)
        if c == 42 or c == 63 or c == 91 or c == 92:
            return true
    return false

# The piece with its "\" escapes removed (a piece with no * ? [ is a plain name).
fn _unescape(s: str) str:
    if not s.contains("\\"):
        return s
    out = ""
    i = 0
    while i < len(s):
        if s.byte(i) == 92 and i + 1 < len(s):
            i += 1
        out += s[i]
        i += 1
    return out

fn glob(pattern: str) [str]:
    out: [str] = []
    if pattern == "":
        return out
    pieces: [str] = []
    for piece in pattern.split("/"):
        if piece != "" and piece != ".":
            pieces.push(piece)
    start = "."
    if pattern.starts_with("/"):
        start = "/"
    _glob(start, pieces, 0, &out)
    out = out.sort_by(fn(x) x)
    if pattern.find_from("**", pattern.find("**") + 2) < 0:
        return out
    # two ** can reach a path more than one way
    once: [str] = []
    for p in out:
        if len(once) == 0 or once[len(once) - 1] != p:
            once.push(p)
    return once

fn _child(d: str, name: str) str:
    if d == ".":
        return name
    if d == "/":
        return "/" + name
    return d + "/" + name

# names in list_marked(d) end in "/" for a directory
fn _glob(d: str, pieces: [str], k: int, out: mut [str]):
    if k == len(pieces):
        if d != "." and d != "/":
            out.push(d)
        return
    piece = pieces[k]
    last = k + 1 == len(pieces)
    if piece == "**":
        if k + 1 < len(pieces) and pieces[k + 1] != "**" and pieces[k + 1] != ".." and _has_meta(pieces[k + 1]):
            _glob_star_star(d, pieces, k, &out)
            return
        _glob(d, pieces, k + 1, &out)
        for name in fs.list_marked(d):
            if name.byte(len(name) - 1) == 47 and name.byte(0) != 46:
                _glob(_child(d, name[..len(name) - 1]), pieces, k, &out)
        return
    if piece == ".." or not _has_meta(piece):
        c = _child(d, _unescape(piece))
        info = fs.stat(c)
        if info.exists and (last or info.is_dir):
            _glob(c, pieces, k + 1, &out)
        return
    dot_ok = piece.byte(0) == 46
    for name in fs.list_marked(d):
        if name.byte(0) == 46 and not dot_ok:
            continue
        is_dir = name.byte(len(name) - 1) == 47
        if not last and not is_dir:
            continue
        nm = name
        if is_dir:
            nm = name[..len(name) - 1]
        if matches(piece, nm):
            _glob(_child(d, nm), pieces, k + 1, &out)

# "**" followed by a pattern piece: one listing of d serves both (the next piece matched here,
# and the directories ** goes down into)
fn _glob_star_star(d: str, pieces: [str], k: int, out: mut [str]):
    piece = pieces[k + 1]
    dot_ok = piece.byte(0) == 46
    last = k + 2 == len(pieces)
    for name in fs.list_marked(d):
        is_dir = name.byte(len(name) - 1) == 47
        nm = name
        if is_dir:
            nm = name[..len(name) - 1]
        hidden = name.byte(0) == 46
        if (last or is_dir) and (dot_ok or not hidden) and matches(piece, nm):
            _glob(_child(d, nm), pieces, k + 2, &out)
        if is_dir and not hidden:
            _glob_star_star(_child(d, nm), pieces, k, &out)
```

## library/std/path/path.tn

```tern
# path: file paths as text (joining, splitting, cleaning, extensions, relative paths, globs).
# Paths use "/" (as on Linux, macOS and WebAssembly); nothing here touches the disk except
# path.abs (the working directory) and path.glob (lists directories).
#
#   import path
#   p = path.join("assets", "img/logo.png")       # "assets/img/logo.png"
#   path.dir(p)  path.base(p)  path.ext(p)         # "assets/img"  "logo.png"  ".png"
#   path.stem(p)  path.with_ext(p, ".webp")        # "logo"  "assets/img/logo.webp"
#   path.clean("a//b/./c/../d/")                   # "a/b/d"
#   path.rel("/srv/app", "/srv/app/static/x.css")? # "static/x.css"
#   for f in path.glob("src/**/*.tn"): ...         # every .tn file below src, sorted
#
#   path.join(a, b) str          a and b with one "/" between, cleaned ("" parts are skipped);
#                                like Go's filepath.Join: join("/a", "/b") is "/a/b"
#   path.join_all(parts) str     the same for any number of parts
#   path.resolve(base, p) str    p if it's absolute, else join(base, p) (like Python's
#                                os.path.join and Node's path.resolve with two arguments)
#   path.clean(p) str            the shortest equal path: one "/" between names, no "." names,
#                                "a/.." removed, no trailing "/"; "" becomes "."; ".." that go
#                                above the start stay ("../x"), above "/" are dropped ("/x")
#   path.dir(p) str              everything before the last name, cleaned: "a/b" -> "a",
#                                "a" -> ".", "/a" -> "/"
#   path.base(p) str             the last name, trailing "/" ignored: "a/b/" -> "b", "" -> ".",
#                                "/" -> "/"
#   path.split(p) (str, str)     (everything up to and including the last "/", the rest):
#                                "a/b.txt" -> ("a/", "b.txt"); joined back they are p
#   path.ext(p) str              the extension of the last name, with its dot: ".gz" for
#                                "x.tar.gz"; "" when there is none (".bashrc" has none)
#   path.stem(p) str             the last name without its extension: "x.tar" for "x.tar.gz"
#   path.with_ext(p, ext) str    p with its extension replaced (or added): with_ext("a/b.md",
#                                ".html") == "a/b.html"; ext "" removes it
#   path.parts(p) [str]          the names in clean(p): "/a/b" -> ["/", "a", "b"], "." -> []
#   path.is_abs(p) bool          starts with "/"
#   path.abs(p) str              resolve(os.cwd(), p), cleaned
#   path.rel(base, target) Result[str, str]
#                                a path that is target when joined to base: rel("a/b", "a/c/d")
#                                == Ok("../c/d"); Err when one is absolute and the other isn't
#                                (or base climbs out with ".." where target doesn't)
#   path.matches(pattern, name) bool
#                                shell-style match of the whole name: * (any run of bytes but
#                                "/"), ? (one byte but "/"), [abc] [a-z] [!a-z] (one byte in /
#                                not in the set), \x (x itself); a malformed pattern is false
#   path.glob(pattern) [str]     the existing paths that match, sorted; each "/"-separated piece
#                                is a matches() pattern, and a piece that is just ** matches any
#                                number of directories (zero included). Names starting with "."
#                                match only a piece that starts with "." (so ** skips .git).
#                                "src/**/*.tn", "/etc/*.conf", "docs/[a-c]*.md"

import os

fn join(a: str, b: str) str:
    if a == "":
        return clean(b)
    if b == "":
        return clean(a)
    return clean(a + "/" + b)

fn join_all(parts: [str]) str:
    s = ""
    for p in parts:
        if p != "":
            if s == "":
                s = p
            else:
                s += "/" + p
    return clean(s)

fn resolve(base: str, p: str) str:
    if p.starts_with("/"):
        return clean(p)
    return join(base, p)

fn is_abs(p: str) bool:
    return p.starts_with("/")

fn abs(p: str) str:
    return resolve(os.cwd(), p)

# clean in C (runtime/strings.h): an already-clean p comes back as it is
fn clean(p: str) str:
    return _clean(p, len(p))

fn _last_slash(p: str) int:
    i = len(p) - 1
    while i >= 0 and p.byte(i) != 47:
        i -= 1
    return i

fn split(p: str) (str, str):
    i = _last_slash(p)
    return (p[..i + 1], p[i + 1..])

fn dir(p: str) str:
    return _dir(p)

fn base(p: str) str:
    return _name(p, false)

# Where the extension's dot is in p (-1 if none): after the last "/", not the name's first byte.
fn _ext_at(p: str) int:
    i = len(p) - 1
    while i >= 0:
        c = p.byte(i)
        if c == 47:
            return -1
        if c == 46:
            if i == 0 or p.byte(i - 1) == 47:
                return -1
            return i
        i -= 1
    return -1

fn ext(p: str) str:
    i = _ext_at(p)
    if i < 0:
        return ""
    return p[i..]

fn stem(p: str) str:
    return _name(p, true)

fn with_ext(p: str, e: str) str:
    i = _ext_at(p)
    if i < 0:
        return p + e
    return p[..i] + e

fn parts(p: str) [str]:
    c = clean(p)
    out: [str] = []
    if c == ".":
        return out
    if c.starts_with("/"):
        out.push("/")
        c = c[1..]
        if c == "":
            return out
    for name in c.split("/"):
        out.push(name)
    return out

fn rel(base_path: str, target: str) Result[str, str]:
    b = clean(base_path)
    t = clean(target)
    if b == t:
        return Ok(".")
    if is_abs(b) != is_abs(t):
        return Err(f"path: can't make {target} relative to {base_path}")
    if b == ".":
        b = ""
    if t == ".":
        t = ""
    # skip the names they share, one at a time (Go's filepath.Rel)
    bl = len(b)
    tl = len(t)
    b0 = 0
    bi = 0
    t0 = 0
    ti = 0
    while true:
        while bi < bl and b.byte(bi) != 47:
            bi += 1
        while ti < tl and t.byte(ti) != 47:
            ti += 1
        if not _same(b, b0, bi, t, t0, ti):
            break
        if bi < bl:
            bi += 1
        if ti < tl:
            ti += 1
        b0 = bi
        t0 = ti
        if b0 >= bl and t0 >= tl:
            break
    if bi - b0 == 2 and b.byte(b0) == 46 and b.byte(b0 + 1) == 46:
        return Err(f"path: can't make {target} relative to {base_path}")
    if b0 < bl:
        out = ".."
        for k in b0..bl:
            if b.byte(k) == 47:
                out += "/.."
        if t0 < tl:
            out += "/" + t[t0..]
        return Ok(out)
    return Ok(t[t0..])

fn _same(a: str, a0: int, a1: int, b: str, b0: int, b1: int) bool:
    if a1 - a0 != b1 - b0:
        return false
    for k in 0..a1 - a0:
        if a.byte(a0 + k) != b.byte(b0 + k):
            return false
    return true
```

## library/std/pqueue.tn

```tern
# pqueue: values of any type, taken out in order of a priority (an int, float or str) given
# with each: lowest first (queue) or highest first (queue_max). For Dijkstra, schedulers,
# event loops. The priority comes first, as in Python's heapq tuples. Values with the same
# priority come out in no particular order.
#
#   import pqueue
#   q = pqueue.queue[int, str]()             # priorities int, values str
#   q.push(3, "deploy")
#   q.push(1, "build")
#   q.pop()                                  # Some("build")
#
#   pqueue.queue[P, T]() PriorityQueue[P, T]    pqueue.queue_max[P, T]()
#   q.push(priority, value)    q.pop() Option[T]    q.peek() Option[T]
#   q.peek_priority() Option[P]    q.len()    q.is_empty()

struct PriorityQueue[P, T]:
    prios: [P]
    vals: [T]
    max: bool
```
