```tern
fn _lscore(c: [str]) int:
    m = 1 << 20
    for x in c:
        if len(x) < m:
            m = len(x)
    return m * 64 - len(c)

fn _lbest(cnf: [[str]], n: int) [[str]]:
    s = cnf.sort_by(fn(c) -_lscore(c))
    out: [[str]] = []
    for c in s:
        if len(out) < n:
            out.push(c)
    return out

# (a1 and a2 ...) or (b1 and b2 ...) = and of every (ai or bj)
fn _lor(a: [[str]], b: [[str]]) [[str]]:
    out: [[str]] = []
    if len(a) == 0 or len(b) == 0:
        return out
    for x in _lbest(a, LIT_KEEP):
        for y in _lbest(b, LIT_KEEP):
            u = x
            for s in y:
                if not _lhas(u, s):
                    u.push(s)
            if len(u) <= LIT_OR:
                _land(&out, u)
    return out

fn _lcat(x: _LInfo, y: _LInfo, min: int) _LInfo:
    if x.known and y.known:
        p = _lcross(x.exact, y.exact)
        if p.1:
            return _lexact(p.0)
        cnf = x.cnf
        _land_all(&cnf, y.cnf)
        _land(&cnf, _lclause(x.exact, min))
        _land(&cnf, _lclause(y.exact, min))
        return _LInfo(false, [], x.exact, y.exact, cnf)
    cnf = x.cnf
    _land_all(&cnf, y.cnf)
    xs = x.exact if x.known else x.suf
    yp = y.exact if y.known else y.pre
    j = _lcross(xs, yp)                               # across the join: "ab" then "cd" holds "abcd"
    if j.1:
        _land(&cnf, _lclause(j.0, min))
    else:
        _land(&cnf, _lclause(xs, min))
        _land(&cnf, _lclause(yp, min))
    pre = x.pre
    if x.known:
        p = _lcross(x.exact, y.pre)
        pre = p.0 if p.1 else x.exact
    suf = y.suf
    if y.known:
        p = _lcross(x.suf, y.exact)
        suf = p.0 if p.1 else y.exact
    return _LInfo(false, [], pre, suf, cnf)

fn _lalt(x: _LInfo, y: _LInfo, min: int) _LInfo:
    if x.known and y.known:
        u = _lunion(x.exact, y.exact)
        if u.1:
            return _lexact(u.0)
    xp = x.exact if x.known else x.pre
    yp = y.exact if y.known else y.pre
    xs = x.exact if x.known else x.suf
    ys = y.exact if y.known else y.suf
    p = _lunion(xp, yp)
    s = _lunion(xs, ys)
    return _LInfo(false, [], p.0 if p.1 else [""], s.0 if s.1 else [""], _lor(_lfull(x, min), _lfull(y, min)))

fn _linfo(t: Tree, i: int, min: int) _LInfo:
    n = t.nodes[i]
    if n.kind == N_EMPTY or n.kind == N_ASSERT:
        return _lexact([""])
    if n.kind == N_CHAR:
        if n.c == 0xFFFD or (n.fold and n.c >= 0x80):      # (U+FFFD also stands for a bad byte)
            return _lany()
        return _lexact([_lascii_lower(encode(n.c))])
    if n.kind == N_CLASS:
        c = t.classes[n.cls]
        if c.neg:
            return _lany()
        total = 0
        for k in 0..len(c.lo):
            if c.hi[k] >= 0x80:
                return _lany()
            total += c.hi[k] - c.lo[k] + 1
        if total > 2 * 10:
            return _lany()
        out: [str] = []
        for k in 0..len(c.lo):
            for x in c.lo[k]..c.hi[k] + 1:
                s = _lascii_lower(chr(x))
                if not _lhas(out, s):
                    out.push(s)
        return _lexact(out) if len(out) <= 10 else _lany()
    if n.kind == N_GROUP:
        return _linfo(t, n.kids[0], min)
    if n.kind == N_CAT:
        acc = _lexact([""])
        for k in n.kids:
            acc = _lcat(acc, _linfo(t, k, min), min)
        return acc
    if n.kind == N_ALT:
        acc = _linfo(t, n.kids[0], min)
        for k in 1..len(n.kids):
            acc = _lalt(acc, _linfo(t, n.kids[k], min), min)
        return acc
    if n.kind == N_REP:
        if n.max == 0:
            return _lexact([""])
        x = _linfo(t, n.kids[0], min)
        if n.min == 0:
            if n.max == 1 and x.known:
                u = _lunion(x.exact, [""])
                if u.1:
                    return _lexact(u.0)
            return _lany()
        if x.known and n.max == n.min:
            acc = _lexact([""])
            for k in 0..n.min:
                acc = _lcat(acc, x, min)
            return acc
        cnf = x.cnf
        if x.known:
            _land(&cnf, _lclause(x.exact, min))
            return _LInfo(false, [], x.exact, x.exact, cnf)
        return _LInfo(false, [], x.pre, x.suf, cnf)
    return _lany()                                       # N_ANY

# does every literal of a contain one of b's (then b says nothing a doesn't)
fn _limplies(a: [str], b: [str]) bool:
    for x in a:
        found = false
        for y in b:
            if x.contains(y):
                found = true
                break
        if not found:
            return false
    return true

# The clauses of tree t (see literals in re.tn).
fn tree_literals(t: Tree, min: int) [[str]]:
    all = _lfull(_linfo(t, t.root, min), min)
    out: [[str]] = []
    for i, c in all:
        implied = false
        for j, d in all:
            if j != i and _limplies(d, c) and (not _limplies(c, d) or j < i):
                implied = true
                break
        if not implied:
            out.push(c)
    return out.sort_by(fn(c) -_lscore(c))
```

## library/std/re/parse.tn

```tern
# re: the parser. A pattern becomes a tree of nodes in one array (Tree.nodes; a node's kids
# are indexes into it), and its character classes a table (Tree.classes). The syntax and the
# error messages are RE2's subset described in re.tn.

const N_EMPTY = 0
const N_CHAR = 1
const N_ANY = 2
const N_CLASS = 3
const N_CAT = 4
const N_ALT = 5
const N_REP = 6
const N_GROUP = 7
const N_ASSERT = 8

const A_BOT = 0       # \A, or ^ without (?m)
const A_EOT = 1       # \z, or $ without (?m)
const A_BOL = 2
const A_EOL = 3
const A_WORD = 4      # \b
const A_NWORD = 5     # \B

struct Node:
    kind: int
    c: int            # N_CHAR: the character (a code point)
    fold: bool        # N_CHAR: case-insensitive (and it has another case)
    dotnl: bool       # N_ANY: matches \n too
    cls: int          # N_CLASS: index into Tree.classes
    min: int          # N_REP
    max: int          # N_REP: -1 for no limit
    greedy: bool      # N_REP
    group: int        # N_GROUP: its index, or -1 (non-capturing)
    at: int           # N_ASSERT: A_*
    kids: [int]

# a set of characters: sorted, merged ranges [lo[i], hi[i]], and whether it's negated;
# ascii0/ascii1: the ranges' members below 64 and 64..127, as bits (before negation)
struct Class:
    lo: [int]
    hi: [int]
    neg: bool
    ascii0: int
    ascii1: int

struct Tree:
    nodes: [Node]
    classes: [Class]
    root: int
    names: [str]      # each group's name ("" if unnamed); [0] is the whole match

struct _P:
    s: str
    p: int
    fi: bool
    fm: bool
    fs: bool
    fx: bool
    depth: int
    err: str
    t: Tree

# one character of s at i: (code point, bytes). A byte that doesn't start a valid UTF-8
# sequence (overlong forms, surrogates and past U+10FFFF too) reads as U+FFFD, one byte wide.
fn decode(s: str, i: int) (int, int):
    c = s.byte(i)
    if c < 0x80:
        return (c, 1)
    n = 0
    lo = 0x80
    hi = 0xBF
    if c >= 0xC2 and c <= 0xDF:
        n = 2
    elif c >= 0xE0 and c <= 0xEF:
        n = 3
        if c == 0xE0:
            lo = 0xA0
        elif c == 0xED:
            hi = 0x9F
    elif c >= 0xF0 and c <= 0xF4:
        n = 4
        if c == 0xF0:
            lo = 0x90
        elif c == 0xF4:
            hi = 0x8F
    else:
        return (0xFFFD, 1)
    if i + n > len(s) or s.byte(i + 1) < lo or s.byte(i + 1) > hi:
        return (0xFFFD, 1)
    v = c & (0x3F >> (n - 1))
    for k in 1..n:
        b = s.byte(i + k)
        if k > 1 and (b & 0xC0) != 0x80:
            return (0xFFFD, 1)
        v = (v << 6) | (b & 0x3F)
    return (v, n)

fn encode(cp: int) str:
    if cp < 0x80:
        return chr(cp)
    out = ""
    if cp < 0x800:
        out += chr(0xC0 | cp >> 6)
    elif cp < 0x10000:
        out += chr(0xE0 | cp >> 12)
        out += chr(0x80 | (cp >> 6 & 63))
        out += chr(0x80 | (cp & 63))
        return out
    else:
        out += chr(0xF0 | cp >> 18)
        out += chr(0x80 | (cp >> 12 & 63))
        out += chr(0x80 | (cp >> 6 & 63))
    out += chr(0x80 | (cp & 63))
    return out

# simple case folding: ASCII, Latin-1, Greek, Cyrillic
fn lower(c: int) int:
    if c >= 65 and c <= 90:
        return c + 32
    if c < 0xC0:
        return c
    if (c >= 0xC0 and c <= 0xDE and c != 0xD7) or (c >= 0x391 and c <= 0x3A9 and c != 0x3A2) or (c >= 0x410 and c <= 0x42F):
        return c + 32
    if c >= 0x400 and c <= 0x40F:
        return c + 80
    return c

fn upper(c: int) int:
    if c >= 97 and c <= 122:
        return c - 32
    if c < 0xE0:
        return c
    if (c >= 0xE0 and c <= 0xFE and c != 0xF7) or (c >= 0x3B1 and c <= 0x3C9 and c != 0x3C2) or (c >= 0x430 and c <= 0x44F):
        return c - 32
    if c >= 0x450 and c <= 0x45F:
        return c - 80
    return c

fn is_word(c: int) bool:
    return (c >= 48 and c <= 57) or (c >= 97 and c <= 122) or (c >= 65 and c <= 90) or c == 95

fn _node(kind: int) Node:
    return Node(kind, 0, false, false, -1, 0, 0, true, -1, 0, [])

fn _add(ps: mut _P, n: Node) int:
    ps.t.nodes.push(n)
    return len(ps.t.nodes) - 1

fn _fail(ps: mut _P, msg: str) int:
    if ps.err == "":
        ps.err = f"re: {msg} (at byte {ps.p} of the pattern)"
    return -1

fn _more(ps: _P) bool:
    return ps.p < len(ps.s)

fn _at(ps: _P) int:
    return ps.s.byte(ps.p) if ps.p < len(ps.s) else -1

# classes
fn _class_add(c: mut Class, lo: int, hi: int):
    c.lo.push(lo)
    c.hi.push(hi)

fn _class_add_fold(c: mut Class, lo: int, hi: int, fold: bool):
    _class_add(&c, lo, hi)
    if not fold:
        return
    x = lo
    while x <= hi and x < 0x460:                 # the cased letters lower() knows
        l = lower(x)
        u = upper(x)
        if l != x:
            _class_add(&c, l, l)
        if u != x:
            _class_add(&c, u, u)
        x += 1

# sorts and merges the ranges, and fills the ASCII bitmaps
fn class_done(c: mut Class):
    if len(c.lo) > 1:
        idx: [int] = []
        for i in 0..len(c.lo):
            idx.push(i)
        los = c.lo
        order = idx.sort_by(fn(i) los[i])
        lo: [int] = []
        hi: [int] = []
        for i in order:
            if len(lo) > 0 and c.lo[i] <= hi[len(hi) - 1] + 1:
                if c.hi[i] > hi[len(hi) - 1]:
                    hi[len(hi) - 1] = c.hi[i]
            else:
                lo.push(c.lo[i])
                hi.push(c.hi[i])
        c.lo = lo
        c.hi = hi
    c.ascii0 = 0
    c.ascii1 = 0
    for i in 0..len(c.lo):
        x = c.lo[i]
        while x <= c.hi[i] and x < 128:
            if x < 64:
                c.ascii0 |= 1 << x
            else:
                c.ascii1 |= 1 << (x - 64)
            x += 1

fn class_has(c: Class, x: int) bool:
    inside = false
    if x < 64:
        inside = ((c.ascii0 >> x) & 1) != 0
    elif x < 128:
        inside = ((c.ascii1 >> (x - 64)) & 1) != 0
    else:
        lo = 0
        hi = len(c.lo) - 1
        while lo <= hi:
            m = (lo + hi) / 2
            if x < c.lo[m]:
                hi = m - 1
            elif x > c.hi[m]:
                lo = m + 1
            else:
                inside = true
                break
    return inside != c.neg

# \d \w \s and their negations (as ranges of the complement)
fn _perl(c: mut Class, k: int):
    r: [int] = [32, 32]
    if k == 100 or k == 68:
        r = [48, 57]
    elif k == 119 or k == 87:
        r = [48, 57, 65, 90, 95, 95, 97, 122]
    else:
        r = [9, 13, 32, 32]
    if k >= 97:
        for i in 0..len(r) / 2:
            _class_add(&c, r[2 * i], r[2 * i + 1])
        return
    lo = 0
    for i in 0..len(r) / 2:
        if r[2 * i] > lo:
            _class_add(&c, lo, r[2 * i] - 1)
        lo = r[2 * i + 1] + 1
    _class_add(&c, lo, 0x10FFFF)

fn _posix(c: mut Class, name: str, fold: bool) bool:
    t = [("alpha", "AZaz"), ("digit", "09"), ("alnum", "09AZaz"), ("upper", "AZ"), ("lower", "az"), ("space", "\t\r  "), ("xdigit", "09AFaf"), ("punct", "!/:@[`{~"), ("word", "09AZ__az"), ("blank", "\t\t  "), ("cntrl", "\x01\x1f\x7f\x7f"), ("print", " ~"), ("graph", "!~")]
    for e in t:
        if e.0 == name:
            for i in 0..len(e.1) / 2:
                _class_add_fold(&c, e.1.byte(2 * i), e.1.byte(2 * i + 1), fold)
            if name == "cntrl":
                _class_add(&c, 0, 0)
            return true
    return false

fn _hexval(b: int) int:
    if b >= 48 and b <= 57:
        return b - 48
    if b >= 97 and b <= 102:
        return b - 87
    if b >= 65 and b <= 70:
        return b - 55
    return -1

# after \x: HH or {H..}; -1 on an error
fn _hex(ps: mut _P) int:
    v = 0
    n = 0
    if _at(ps) == 123:
        ps.p += 1
        while _more(ps) and _at(ps) != 125:
            d = _hexval(_at(ps))
            n += 1
            if d < 0 or n > 6:
                return _fail(&ps, "bad \\x{...}: write 1 to 6 hex digits")
            v = v * 16 + d
            ps.p += 1
        if not _more(ps) or n == 0:
            return _fail(&ps, "bad \\x{...}: write 1 to 6 hex digits")
        ps.p += 1
    else:
        while n < 2:
            d = _hexval(_at(ps))
            if d < 0:
                return _fail(&ps, "bad \\x: write two hex digits (\\x41) or \\x{263a}")
            v = v * 16 + d
            ps.p += 1
            n += 1
    if v > 0x10FFFF:
        return _fail(&ps, "\\x{...} is past the last Unicode character")
    return v

# an escape after `\`: (kind, value): kind 0 a character, 1 a class (value: its index), 2 an
# assertion (value: A_*); kind -1 on an error
fn _escape(ps: mut _P, in_class: bool) (int, int):
    if not _more(ps):
        _fail(&ps, "the pattern ends with a lone \\")
        return (-1, 0)
    k = _at(ps)
    ps.p += 1
    if k == 110:
        return (0, 10)
    if k == 116:
        return (0, 9)
    if k == 114:
        return (0, 13)
    if k == 102:
        return (0, 12)
    if k == 118:
        return (0, 11)
    if k == 97:
        return (0, 7)
    if k == 120:
        v = _hex(&ps)
        return (-1, 0) if v < 0 else (0, v)
    if k == 100 or k == 68 or k == 119 or k == 87 or k == 115 or k == 83:
        c = Class([], [], false, 0, 0)
        _perl(&c, k)
        class_done(&c)
        ps.t.classes.push(c)
        return (1, len(ps.t.classes) - 1)
    if not in_class:
        if k == 98:
            return (2, A_WORD)
        if k == 66:
            return (2, A_NWORD)
        if k == 65:
            return (2, A_BOT)
        if k == 122:
            return (2, A_EOT)
    if k == 112 or k == 80:
        _fail(&ps, "\\p{...} Unicode classes aren't supported: use a class like [a-zA-Z\\x{c0}-\\x{24f}]")
        return (-1, 0)
    if k == 90:
        _fail(&ps, "\\Z isn't supported: use \\z (the end of the text)")
        return (-1, 0)
    if k >= 49 and k <= 57:
        _fail(&ps, "backreferences (\\1) aren't supported: they need backtracking, which can take exponential time")
        return (-1, 0)
    alnum = (k >= 48 and k <= 57) or (k >= 65 and k <= 90) or (k >= 97 and k <= 122)
    if k < 128 and not alnum:
        return (0, k)                               # \. \* \\ \( ...
    _fail(&ps, "unknown escape \\" + chr(k))
    return (-1, 0)

# after `[`
fn _class_node(ps: mut _P) int:
    c = Class([], [], false, 0, 0)
    if _at(ps) == 94:
        c.neg = true
        ps.p += 1
    first = true
    while _more(ps) and (_at(ps) != 93 or first):
        first = false
        lo = 0
        if _at(ps) == 91 and ps.p + 1 < len(ps.s) and ps.s.byte(ps.p + 1) == 58:       # [:alpha:]
            nm = ps.p + 2
            e = nm
            while e + 1 < len(ps.s) and not (ps.s.byte(e) == 58 and ps.s.byte(e + 1) == 93):
                e += 1
            if e + 1 >= len(ps.s) or not _posix(&c, ps.s[nm..e], ps.fi):
                return _fail(&ps, "unknown [:class:] (alpha, digit, alnum, upper, lower, space, xdigit, punct, word, blank, cntrl, print, graph)")
            ps.p = e + 2
            continue
        if _at(ps) == 92:
            ps.p += 1
            esc = _escape(&ps, true)
            if esc.0 < 0:
                return -1
            if esc.0 == 1:                            # \d inside a class: its ranges
                sub = ps.t.classes[esc.1]
                for i in 0..len(sub.lo):
                    _class_add(&c, sub.lo[i], sub.hi[i])
                continue
            lo = esc.1
        else:
            d = decode(ps.s, ps.p)
            lo = d.0
            ps.p += d.1
        hi = lo
        if ps.p + 1 < len(ps.s) and _at(ps) == 45 and ps.s.byte(ps.p + 1) != 93:
            ps.p += 1
            if _at(ps) == 92:
                ps.p += 1
                esc = _escape(&ps, true)
                if esc.0 < 0:
                    return -1
                if esc.0 == 1:
                    return _fail(&ps, "a class can't be the end of a range")
                hi = esc.1
            else:
                d = decode(ps.s, ps.p)
                hi = d.0
                ps.p += d.1
            if hi < lo:
                return _fail(&ps, "a range's end comes before its start (like z-a)")
        _class_add_fold(&c, lo, hi, ps.fi)
    if not _more(ps):
        return _fail(&ps, "missing ] to close a [class]")
    ps.p += 1
    class_done(&c)
    ps.t.classes.push(c)
    n = _node(N_CLASS)
    n.cls = len(ps.t.classes) - 1
    return _add(&ps, n)

fn _skip_x(ps: mut _P):
    if not ps.fx:
        return
    while _more(ps):
        b = _at(ps)
        if b == 32 or b == 9 or b == 10 or b == 13:
            ps.p += 1
        elif b == 35:
            while _more(ps) and _at(ps) != 10:
                ps.p += 1
        else:
            break

# (?flags) or (?flags:  -- 1 for a scoped group, 0 for flags alone, -1 on an error
fn _flags(ps: mut _P) int:
    on = true
    while _more(ps) and _at(ps) != 41 and _at(ps) != 58:
        b = _at(ps)
        if b == 45:
            on = false
        elif b == 105:
            ps.fi = on
        elif b == 109:
            ps.fm = on
        elif b == 115:
            ps.fs = on
        elif b == 120:
            ps.fx = on
        elif b == 85:
            return _fail(&ps, "the U flag isn't supported: write lazy quantifiers (*?) where you want them")
        else:
            return _fail(&ps, "unknown flag in (?...): use i, m, s or x")
        ps.p += 1
    if not _more(ps):
        return _fail(&ps, "missing ) after (?flags")
    scoped = _at(ps) == 58
    ps.p += 1
    return 1 if scoped else 0

fn _char_node(ps: mut _P, ch: int) int:
    n = _node(N_CHAR)
    n.c = ch
    n.fold = ps.fi and lower(ch) != upper(ch)
    return _add(&ps, n)

fn _atom(ps: mut _P) int:
    c = _at(ps)
    if c == 40:                                         # (
        ps.p += 1
        ps.depth += 1
        if ps.depth > 500:
            return _fail(&ps, "groups nested too deeply")
        group = -1
        fi = ps.fi
        fm = ps.fm
        fs = ps.fs
        fx = ps.fx
        if _at(ps) == 63:
            ps.p += 1
            if _at(ps) == 61 or _at(ps) == 33:
                return _fail(&ps, "lookahead (?= ...) isn't supported (it needs backtracking)")
            if ps.p + 1 < len(ps.s) and _at(ps) == 60 and (ps.s.byte(ps.p + 1) == 61 or ps.s.byte(ps.p + 1) == 33):
                return _fail(&ps, "lookbehind (?<= ...) isn't supported (it needs backtracking)")
            if _at(ps) == 80 or _at(ps) == 60:              # a named group
                if _at(ps) == 80:
                    ps.p += 1
                if _at(ps) != 60:
                    return _fail(&ps, "a named group is (?P<name>...) or (?<name>...)")
                ps.p += 1
                nm = ps.p
                while _more(ps) and (is_word(_at(ps))):
                    ps.p += 1
                if _at(ps) != 62 or ps.p == nm:
                    return _fail(&ps, "a group name is letters, digits and _, then >")
                name = ps.s[nm..ps.p]
                for g in 1..len(ps.t.names):
                    if ps.t.names[g] == name:
                        return _fail(&ps, "two groups have the same name")
                ps.p += 1
                group = len(ps.t.names)
                ps.t.names.push(name)
            else:
                f = _flags(&ps)
                if f < 0:
                    return -1
                if f == 0:                                  # (?i): the rest of this group
                    ps.depth -= 1
                    return _add(&ps, _node(N_EMPTY))
        else:
            group = len(ps.t.names)
            ps.t.names.push("")
        sub = _alt(&ps)
        if sub < 0:
            return -1
        if _at(ps) != 41:
            return _fail(&ps, "missing ) to close a group")
        ps.p += 1
        ps.depth -= 1
        ps.fi = fi
        ps.fm = fm
        ps.fs = fs
        ps.fx = fx
        g = _node(N_GROUP)
        g.group = group
        g.kids.push(sub)
        return _add(&ps, g)
    if c == 91:
        ps.p += 1
        return _class_node(&ps)
    if c == 46:
        ps.p += 1
        n = _node(N_ANY)
        n.dotnl = ps.fs
        return _add(&ps, n)
    if c == 94 or c == 36:
        ps.p += 1
        n = _node(N_ASSERT)
        if c == 94:
            n.at = A_BOL if ps.fm else A_BOT
        else:
            n.at = A_EOL if ps.fm else A_EOT
        return _add(&ps, n)
    if c == 42 or c == 43 or c == 63:
        return _fail(&ps, "a quantifier (* + ?) with nothing before it: write \\* for the character")
    if c == 92:
        ps.p += 1
        esc = _escape(&ps, false)
        if esc.0 < 0:
            return -1
        if esc.0 == 1:
            n = _node(N_CLASS)
            n.cls = esc.1
            return _add(&ps, n)
        if esc.0 == 2:
            n = _node(N_ASSERT)
            n.at = esc.1
            return _add(&ps, n)
        return _char_node(&ps, esc.1)
    d = decode(ps.s, ps.p)
    ps.p += d.1
    return _char_node(&ps, d.0)

# digits for {n,m}: the value, or -1 if there are none or more than 4
fn _pcount(ps: mut _P) int:
    v = 0
    n = 0
    while _more(ps) and _at(ps) >= 48 and _at(ps) <= 57:
        v = v * 10 + _at(ps) - 48
        ps.p += 1
        n += 1
        if n > 4:
            return -1
    return v if n > 0 else -1

fn _repeat(ps: mut _P) int:
    a = _atom(&ps)
    if a < 0:
        return -1
    while true:
        _skip_x(&ps)
        if not _more(ps):
            return a
        min = 0
        max = 0
        c = _at(ps)
        if c == 42:
            max = -1
            ps.p += 1
        elif c == 43:
            min = 1
            max = -1
            ps.p += 1
        elif c == 63:
            max = 1
            ps.p += 1
        elif c == 123:
            save = ps.p
            ps.p += 1
            min = _pcount(&ps)
            if min < 0:
                ps.p = save                                 # a literal {
                return a
            max = min
            if _at(ps) == 44:
                ps.p += 1
                if _at(ps) == 125:
                    max = -1
                else:
                    max = _pcount(&ps)
                    if max < 0:
                        return _fail(&ps, "bad {n,m}")
            if _at(ps) != 125:
                return _fail(&ps, "missing } in {n,m}")
            ps.p += 1
            if min > 1000 or max > 1000:
                return _fail(&ps, "a count in {n,m} is over 1000")
            if max >= 0 and max < min:
                return _fail(&ps, "{n,m} with m smaller than n")
        else:
            return a
        k = ps.t.nodes[a].kind
        if k == N_ASSERT or k == N_EMPTY:
            return _fail(&ps, "nothing to repeat before a quantifier")
        if k == N_REP:
            return _fail(&ps, "two quantifiers in a row (like a**): group the first one, (a*)*")
        r = _node(N_REP)
        r.min = min
        r.max = max
        if _at(ps) == 63:
            r.greedy = false
            ps.p += 1
        r.kids.push(a)
        a = _add(&ps, r)
    return a

fn _concat(ps: mut _P) int:
    kids: [int] = []
    while true:
        _skip_x(&ps)
        if not _more(ps) or _at(ps) == 124 or _at(ps) == 41:
            break
        k = _repeat(&ps)
        if k < 0:
            return -1
        kids.push(k)
    n = _node(N_CAT)
    n.kids = kids
    return _add(&ps, n)

fn _alt(ps: mut _P) int:
    first = _concat(&ps)
    if first < 0:
        return -1
    if _at(ps) != 124:
        return first
    kids = [first]
    while _at(ps) == 124:
        ps.p += 1
        k = _concat(&ps)
        if k < 0:
            return -1
        kids.push(k)
    n = _node(N_ALT)
    n.kids = kids
    return _add(&ps, n)

# The tree of pattern, or the reason it isn't a valid pattern.
fn parse(pattern: str) Result[Tree, str]:
    ps = _P(pattern, 0, false, false, false, false, 0, "", Tree([], [], -1, [""]))
    root = _alt(&ps)
    if root >= 0 and ps.p < len(pattern):
        _fail(&ps, "unmatched ) (write \\) for the character)")
    if ps.err != "":
        return Err(ps.err)
    ps.t.root = root
    return Ok(ps.t)
```

## library/std/re/re.tn

```tern
# re: regular expressions that run in linear time (no catastrophic backtracking).
#
#   import re
#   r = re.compile("(\\w+)@(\\w+)\\.com")?      # Result[re.Regex, str]; or re.must(pattern)
#   r.test(s) bool                              is there a match anywhere in s
#   r.full(s) bool                              does the whole of s match
#   r.search(s) Option[re.Match]                the first match
#   r.search_at(s, at) Option[re.Match]         the first match at or after byte `at`
#   r.find_all(s) [re.Match]                    every match, left to right, not overlapping
#                                               (`for m in r.find_all(s):` takes them one at a
#                                               time, without an array of all of them)
#   r.count(s) int                              how many matches
#   r.search_reach(s) ([int], int)              the first match as slots (each group's start
#                                               and end, -1 if it didn't take part; [] for no
#                                               match) and how many of s's first bytes the search
#                                               read: any text with those bytes first (and at
#                                               least as long) gets the same slots; len(s) + 1
#                                               when the rest mattered. For many texts sharing
#                                               prefixes (a sorted list), one search can stand
#                                               for the next
#   r.replace_all(s, repl) str                  every match replaced; repl may use $1, ${name},
#                                               $0 (the whole match), $$ (a dollar sign)
#   r.replace_first(s, repl) str                only the first match
#   r.replace_with(s, f) str                    each match replaced by f(m) (f: fn(re.Match) str)
#   r.split_all(s) [str]                        the text between matches
#   r.names() [str]                             each group's name ("" if unnamed; [0] is the match)
#   re.escape(s) str                            s with every special character escaped
#   re.error() str                              why the last compile failed
#   re.literals(pattern, min) Result[[[str]], str]   for searching an index before running the
#                                               pattern: groups of literals such that every match
#                                               contains at least one literal of each group
#                                               (literals are lowercase and compare ASCII letters
#                                               without case; none shorter than min bytes; [] if
#                                               nothing is certain, like for \w+). Sorted most
#                                               selective first. `cdn\.(shopify|wix)\.com` gives
#                                               [["cdn.shopify.com", "cdn.wix.com"]]
#
# A Match: start, end (byte offsets: s[m.start..m.end] is m.text), text, groups ([0] is the
# whole match, [i] group i, "" if it didn't take part), starts (each group's start, -1 if it
# didn't take part), and named ({name: text} for named groups). m.group("name") reads one.
#
# Syntax (RE2's, shared by Go, Rust, Python and JavaScript):
#   .  [abc]  [^a-z]  [[:alpha:]]  \d \w \s  \D \W \S       (\d \w \s are ASCII)
#   ^ $ (text start / end; with (?m) line start / end)  \A \z  \b \B (ASCII word boundary)
#   (x) (?:x) (?P<name>x) (?<name>x)   x|y   x* x+ x? x{n} x{n,} x{n,m}, and x*? etc. (lazy)
#   (?i) case-insensitive, (?m) multi-line, (?s) . matches \n, (?x) spaces and # comments
#   ignored; (?i:x) for part of a pattern. \x41 \x{1F600} \n \t, and \. \* \( ... for the
#   characters themselves.
# Not supported, because they need backtracking: backreferences (\1), lookahead and
# lookbehind ((?=x), (?<=x)). \p{...} Unicode classes aren't supported either.
#
# Matching is by character on UTF-8 text: `.` is one character, however many bytes. Offsets
# (start, end, starts) are in bytes, like everything else on str. Time is linear in the
# text's length. A pattern is compiled once per program (the last 1000 are kept, so
# re.must(p) in a loop is cheap) and shared by every thread; its DFA's states are kept per
# thread, so threads searching with one pattern at once don't wait on each other.
# The engine is in this directory: parse.tn (syntax), compile.tn (programs), vm.tn (Pike
# VM, backtracker, one-pass), dfa.tn (lazy DFA), find.tn (searching, prefilters with simd).

import task

struct Regex:
    pattern: str
    group_names: [str]      # each group's name ("" if unnamed); [0] is the whole match
    named_groups: bool      # any of them has a name
    e: Engine

struct Match:
    start: int
    end: int
    text: str
    groups: [str]
    starts: [int]
    named: {str: str}

# compiled patterns, by pattern (cleared when it holds CACHE_MAX)
struct _Cache:
    regs: {str: Regex}

const CACHE_MAX = 1000
const _CACHE = task.shared(_Cache({}))

fn _look(c: mut _Cache, pattern: str) Option[Regex]:
    if pattern in c.regs:
        return Some(c.regs[pattern])
    return None

fn _keep(c: mut _Cache, r: Regex) int:
    if len(c.regs) >= CACHE_MAX:
        c.regs = {}
    c.regs[r.pattern] = r
    return 0

fn _any_named(names: [str]) bool:
    for nm in names:
        if nm != "":
            return true
    return false

# with Result: r = re.compile("[0-9]+")?   (Err: "re: missing ) to close a group (at byte 3 of the pattern)")
fn compile(pattern: str) Result[Regex, str]:
    found = _CACHE.update(fn(c) _look(&c, pattern))
    match found:
        Some(r):
            return Ok(r)
        None:
            pass
    match engine(pattern):
        Ok(e):
            names = e.ps[0].names
            r = Regex(pattern, names, _any_named(names), e)
            _CACHE.update(fn(c) _keep(&c, r))
            task.local_set("re.error", "")
            return Ok(r)
        Err(msg):
            task.local_set("re.error", msg)
            return Err(msg)

# for a pattern written in the program: a bad one is a runtime error with the reason
fn must(pattern: str) Regex:
    match compile(pattern):
        Ok(r):
            return r
        Err(msg):
            panic(msg + ": " + pattern)
    return must(pattern)

# why the last compile on this task failed ("" if it didn't)
fn error() str:
    return task.local_get("re.error")

fn test(r: Regex, s: str) bool:
    return e_test(r.e, s)

fn full(r: Regex, s: str) bool:
    return e_full(r.e, s)

# the match of slots[base..base + 2 * groups]
fn _match_of(r: Regex, s: str, slots: [int], base: int) Match:
    n = len(r.group_names)
    groups: [str] = []
    starts: [int] = []
    named: {str: str} = {}
    for i in 0..n:
        a = slots[base + 2 * i]
        b = slots[base + 2 * i + 1]
        if a >= 0 and b >= a:
            groups.push(s[a..b])
            starts.push(a)
        else:
            groups.push("")
            starts.push(-1)
    if r.named_groups:
        for i, nm in r.group_names:
            if nm != "":
                named[nm] = groups[i]
    return Match(starts[0], starts[0] + len(groups[0]), groups[0], groups, starts, named)

fn search_at(r: Regex, s: str, at: int) Option[Match]:
    sl = e_search(r.e, s, at)
    if len(sl) == 0:
        return None
    return Some(_match_of(r, s, sl, 0))

fn search(r: Regex, s: str) Option[Match]:
    return search_at(r, s, 0)

fn search_reach(r: Regex, s: str) ([int], int):
    return e_search_reach(r.e, s)

# the matches one at a time (`for m in r.find_all(s)` runs on this: codegen find_all_foreach)
struct _Iter:
    sr: [Search]
    w: Walk
    out: [int]

fn _iter(r: Regex, s: str) _Iter:
    return _Iter(_search(r.e, s), walk(), [0] * (2 * len(r.group_names)))

fn _iter_next(r: Regex, s: str, it: mut _Iter) bool:
    if len(it.sr) == 0:
        return false
    if walk_next(r.e.ps[0], &it.sr[0], s, &it.w, true, false, &it.out):
        return true
    _done(r.e, it.sr)
    it.sr = []
    return false

fn _iter_match(r: Regex, s: str, it: _Iter) Match:
    return _match_of(r, s, it.out, 0)

fn find_all(r: Regex, s: str) [Match]:
    it = _iter(r, s)
    out: [Match] = []
    while _iter_next(r, s, &it):
        out.push(_iter_match(r, s, it))
    return out

fn count(r: Regex, s: str) int:
    return e_count(r.e, s)

fn replace_all(r: Regex, s: str, repl: str) str:
    return e_replace(r.e, s, repl, -1)

fn replace_first(r: Regex, s: str, repl: str) str:
    return e_replace(r.e, s, repl, 1)

fn replace_with(r: Regex, s: str, f: fn(Match) str) str:
    out = ""
    last = 0
    for m in find_all(r, s):
        out += s[last..m.start] + f(m)
        last = m.end
    return out + s[last..]

fn split_all(r: Regex, s: str) [str]:
    sl = e_find_all(r.e, s)
    per = 2 * len(r.group_names)
    out: [str] = []
    last = 0
    for i in 0..len(sl) / per:
        a = sl[i * per]
        b = sl[i * per + 1]
        if a == 0 and b == 0:
            continue
        out.push(s[last..a])
        last = b
    out.push(s[last..])
    return out

fn names(r: Regex) [str]:
    return copy(r.group_names)

# a named group's text ("" if the pattern has no such group or it didn't take part)
fn group(m: Match, name: str) str:
    return m.named.get(name, "")

fn escape(s: str) str:
    out = ""
    for i in 0..len(s):
        c = s[i..i + 1]
        if "\\.+*?()|[]{}^$#&-~ \t\n".contains(c):
            if c == "\n":
                out += "\\n"
            elif c == "\t":
                out += "\\t"
            else:
                out += "\\" + c
        else:
            out += c
    return out

fn literals(pattern: str, min: int) Result[[[str]], str]:
    t = parse(pattern)?
    return Ok(tree_literals(t, min))
```

## library/std/re/vm.tn

```tern
# re: the matchers that know groups. The Pike VM runs every possible match together, one
# character at a time (linear in the text); the bounded backtracker fills in the groups of a
# match already known to span s[st..e) by trying paths depth first without visiting an
# (instruction, position) twice; the one-pass walk does it with no choices at all when the
# next byte always says which branch to tk2.

# where to keep threads and captures (made once per search, sized for the program)
struct Scratch:
    apc: [int]
    acaps: [int]
    an: int
    bpc: [int]
    bcaps: [int]
    bn: int
    seen: [int]
    stamp: int
    stack: [int]
    best: [int]
    caps: [int]
    btseen: [int]
    jobs: [int]               # the backtracker's stack
    reach: int                # how much of the text the last backtrack read (see _backtrack)

# (the VM's thread lists are made when it first runs: most searches only backtrack)
fn scratch(p: Prog) Scratch:
    ns = 2 * p.ngroups
    return Scratch([], [], 0, [], [], 0, [], 0, [], [0] * ns, [0] * ns, [], [], 0)

fn _vm_scratch(p: Prog, sc: mut Scratch):
    nc = len(p.code.op)
    ns = 2 * p.ngroups
    sc.apc = [0] * nc
    sc.acaps = [0] * (nc * ns)
    sc.bpc = [0] * nc
    sc.bcaps = [0] * (nc * ns)
    sc.seen = [0] * nc

fn _assert(kind: int, s: str, pos: int) bool:
    n = len(s)
    if kind == A_BOT:
        return pos == 0
    if kind == A_EOT:
        return pos == n
    if kind == A_BOL:
        return pos == 0 or s.byte(pos - 1) == 10
    if kind == A_EOL:
        return pos == n or s.byte(pos) == 10
    a = pos > 0 and is_word(s.byte(pos - 1))
    b = pos < n and is_word(s.byte(pos))
    return a != b if kind == A_WORD else a == b

fn _char_ok(p: Prog, pc: int, cp: int) bool:
    op = p.code.op[pc]
    if op == I_CHAR:
        return (lower(cp) if p.code.fold[pc] else cp) == p.code.x[pc]
    if op == I_ANY:
        return cp != 10
    if op == I_ANYNL:
        return true
    return class_has(p.classes[p.code.x[pc]], cp)

# _char_ok for instruction op at pc, with ASCII classes inline (the backtracker's hot path)
fn _cok(p: Prog, op: int, pc: int, cp: int) bool:
    if op == I_ANY:
        return cp != 10
    if op == I_CLASS:
        ci = p.code.x[pc]
        if cp < 64:
            return (((p.classes[ci].ascii0 >> cp) & 1) != 0) != p.classes[ci].neg
        if cp < 128:
            return (((p.classes[ci].ascii1 >> (cp - 64)) & 1) != 0) != p.classes[ci].neg
        return class_has(p.classes[ci], cp)
    if op == I_CHAR:
        return (lower(cp) if p.code.fold[pc] else cp) == p.code.x[pc]
    return true

# add the thread at pc (and everything it reaches without reading a character) to list b
# (into_b) or a; caps (the thread's slots) is scratch, restored on the way back
fn _addthread(p: Prog, sc: mut Scratch, into_b: bool, pc0: int, ns: int, s: str, pos: int):
    st = [pc0, -1]
    while len(st) > 0:
        b = st.pop()
        a = st.pop()
        if b >= 0:                                    # restore a capture slot
            sc.caps[a] = b
            continue
        if b == -2:                                   # (restore to "unset")
            sc.caps[a] = -1
            continue
        pc = a
        if sc.seen[pc] == sc.stamp:
            continue
        sc.seen[pc] = sc.stamp
        op = p.code.op[pc]
        if op == I_JMP:
            st.push(p.code.x[pc])
            st.push(-1)
        elif op == I_SPLIT:
            st.push(p.code.y[pc])
            st.push(-1)
            st.push(p.code.x[pc])
            st.push(-1)
        elif op == I_SAVE:
            x = p.code.x[pc]
            if x < ns:
                old = sc.caps[x]
                st.push(x)
                st.push(old if old >= 0 else -2)
                sc.caps[x] = pos
            st.push(pc + 1)
            st.push(-1)
        elif op == I_ASSERT:
            if _assert(p.code.x[pc], s, pos):
                st.push(pc + 1)
                st.push(-1)
        elif into_b:
            sc.bpc[sc.bn] = pc
            for k in 0..ns:
                sc.bcaps[sc.bn * ns + k] = sc.caps[k]
            sc.bn += 1
        else:
            sc.apc[sc.an] = pc
            for k in 0..ns:
                sc.acaps[sc.an * ns + k] = sc.caps[k]
            sc.an += 1

fn _swap(sc: mut Scratch):
    t = sc.apc
    sc.apc = sc.bpc
    sc.bpc = t
    tc = sc.acaps
    sc.acaps = sc.bcaps
    sc.bcaps = tc
    sc.an = sc.bn
    sc.bn = 0

# mode 0: the leftmost-first match at or after `at` (its slots in sc.best); 1: the same but
# only one that starts at `at` and ends at the end of the text (full); 2: just whether one
# exists; 3: only one that starts at `at`
fn run_vm(p: Prog, sc: mut Scratch, s: str, at: int, mode: int, ns: int) bool:
    if len(sc.seen) == 0:
        _vm_scratch(p, &sc)
    n = len(s)
    sc.an = 0
    sc.bn = 0
    matched = false
    only_start = mode == 1 or mode == 3 or p.anchored
    sc.stamp += 1
    pos = at
    while true:
        if not matched and (pos == at or not only_start):
            if sc.an == 0 and not only_start:         # nothing running: skip to a possible start
                if len(p.prefix) > 1 or (len(p.prefix) == 1 and p.has_first):
                    f = s.find_from(p.prefix, pos) if pos < n else -1
                    if f < 0:
                        return false
                    pos = f
                elif p.has_first:
                    while pos < n and not p.first[s.byte(pos)]:
                        pos += 1
                    if pos >= n:
                        return false
            if sc.an == 0:
                sc.stamp += 1
            for k in 0..ns:
                sc.caps[k] = -1
            _addthread(p, &sc, false, 0, ns, s, pos)
        if sc.an == 0:                                # nothing can match from here: the next start
            if matched or only_start or pos >= n:
                break
            pos += decode(s, pos).1
            continue
        cp = -1
        w = 0
        if pos < n:
            d = decode(s, pos)
            cp = d.0
            w = d.1
        sc.stamp += 1
        sc.bn = 0
        i = 0
        while i < sc.an:
            pc = sc.apc[i]
            op = p.code.op[pc]
            if op == I_MATCH:
                if mode == 1 and pos != n:
                    i += 1
                    continue
                if mode == 2:
                    return true
                for k in 0..ns:
                    sc.best[k] = sc.acaps[i * ns + k]
                matched = true
                break                                 # lower-priority threads lose
            if cp >= 0 and _char_ok(p, pc, cp):
                for k in 0..ns:
                    sc.caps[k] = sc.acaps[i * ns + k]
                _addthread(p, &sc, true, pc + 1, ns, s, pos + w)
            i += 1
        _swap(&sc)
        if pos >= n:                                  # (MATCHes at the end were seen this round)
            break
        pos += w
        if sc.an == 0 and (matched or only_start):
            break
    return matched

const BT_MAX_BITS = 256 * 1024

# (apart: the backtracker's stack doubles, rarely)
fn _more_jobs(js: mut [int]):
    n = [0] * (len(js) * 2 + 48)
    for i, x in js:
        n[i] = x
    js = n

# groups for a match known to span s[st..e), depth first in priority order (e: the end of
# the text when the match's end isn't known: the first MATCH reached is the match). Leaves in
# sc.reach how far it read: every text that starts with s[..reach] (and runs past it) gets
# the same answer; e + 1 when where the text ends mattered.
fn _backtrack(p: Prog, sc: mut Scratch, s: str, st: int, e: int, ns: int, out: mut [int]) bool:
    width = e - st + 1
    words = (len(p.code.op) * width + 63) / 64
    if len(sc.btseen) < words:
        sc.btseen = [0] * words
    else:
        for k in 0..words:
            sc.btseen[k] = 0
    for k in 0..ns:
        sc.caps[k] = -1
    # jobs: (pc, pos, -1): explore; (slot, value, -2): restore; kept in sc, `top` long
    if len(sc.jobs) < 3 * width + 48:                # (a job a position is the usual most)
        sc.jobs = [0] * (3 * width + 48)
    sc.jobs[0] = 0
    sc.jobs[1] = st
    sc.jobs[2] = -1
    top = 3
    reach = st
    while top > 0:
        top -= 3
        a = sc.jobs[top]
        b = sc.jobs[top + 1]
        kind = sc.jobs[top + 2]
        if kind == -2:
            sc.caps[a] = b
            continue
        pc = a
        pos = b
        while true:
            bit = pc * width + (pos - st)
            if ((sc.btseen[bit >> 6] >> (bit & 63)) & 1) != 0:
                break
            sc.btseen[bit >> 6] |= 1 << (bit & 63)
            op = p.code.op[pc]
            if op <= I_CLASS:                         # CHAR ANY ANYNL CLASS
                if pos >= e:
                    reach = e + 1
                    break
                cp = s.byte(pos)
                w = 1
                if pos >= reach:
                    reach = pos + 1
                if cp < 64:                           # (ASCII: the instruction's bits)
                    if ((p.am0[pc] >> cp) & 1) == 0:
                        break
                elif cp < 0x80:
                    if ((p.am1[pc] >> (cp - 64)) & 1) == 0:
                        break
                else:
                    reach = max(reach, e + 1 if pos + 4 > e else pos + 4)    # (decode reads up to 4)
                    d = decode(s, pos)
                    cp = d.0
                    w = d.1
                    if pos + w > e or not (p.ahi[pc] or _cok(p, op, pc, cp)):
                        break
                pc += 1
                pos += w
                continue
            if op == I_SPLIT:
                bpc = p.code.x[pc]
                bop = p.code.op[bpc]
                if bop <= I_CLASS and (bpc == pc - 1 or (bpc == pc + 1 and p.code.op[pc + 2] == I_JMP and p.code.x[pc + 2] == pc)):
                    # a greedy loop over one character (k+: k; SPLIT k,out. k*: SPLIT k,out; k;
                    # JMP): run it here, a job (leave the loop) and a visited bit at each
                    # position, not three instructions' worth. (The body and the JMP are only
                    # reached through this SPLIT, so they needn't be marked.)
                    # (possessive, when what follows the loop can't start with a character the
                    # loop takes: leaving it early can't match, so only its end is tried)
                    out_pc = p.code.y[pc]
                    poss = p.poss[pc]
                    last = pos
                    while true:
                        last = pos
                        if not poss:
                            if top + 3 > len(sc.jobs):
                                _more_jobs(&sc.jobs)
                            sc.jobs[top] = out_pc
                            sc.jobs[top + 1] = pos
                            sc.jobs[top + 2] = -1
                            top += 3
                        if pos >= e:
                            reach = e + 1
                            break
                        cp = s.byte(pos)
                        w = 1
                        if pos >= reach:
                            reach = pos + 1
                        if cp < 64:
                            if ((p.am0[bpc] >> cp) & 1) == 0:
                                break
                        elif cp < 0x80:
                            if ((p.am1[bpc] >> (cp - 64)) & 1) == 0:
                                break
                        else:
                            reach = max(reach, e + 1 if pos + 4 > e else pos + 4)
                            d = decode(s, pos)
                            cp = d.0
                            w = d.1
                            if pos + w > e or not (p.ahi[bpc] or _cok(p, bop, bpc, cp)):
                                break
                        pos += w
                        bit = pc * width + (pos - st)
                        if ((sc.btseen[bit >> 6] >> (bit & 63)) & 1) != 0:
                            break
                        sc.btseen[bit >> 6] |= 1 << (bit & 63)
                    if poss:
                        pc = out_pc
                        pos = last
                        continue
                    break
                if top + 3 > len(sc.jobs):
                    _more_jobs(&sc.jobs)
                sc.jobs[top] = p.code.y[pc]
                sc.jobs[top + 1] = pos
                sc.jobs[top + 2] = -1
                top += 3
                pc = p.code.x[pc]
                continue
            if op == I_JMP:
                pc = p.code.x[pc]
                continue
            if op == I_SAVE:
                x = p.code.x[pc]
                if x < ns:
                    if top + 3 > len(sc.jobs):
                        _more_jobs(&sc.jobs)
                    sc.jobs[top] = x
                    sc.jobs[top + 1] = sc.caps[x]
                    sc.jobs[top + 2] = -2
                    top += 3
                    sc.caps[x] = pos
                pc += 1
                continue
            if op == I_ASSERT:
                # (an assertion reads the bytes around pos, or that the text ends at pos)
                reach = max(reach, e + 1 if pos >= e else pos + 1)
                if not _assert(p.code.x[pc], s, pos):
                    break
                pc += 1
                continue
            for k in 0..ns:                           # MATCH: the first reached wins
                out[k] = sc.caps[k]
            sc.reach = reach
            return true
    sc.reach = reach
    return false

# groups for a match known to span s[st..e) when the program is one-pass; false: it didn't
# get there (the caller falls back to the backtracker)
fn _onepass(p: Prog, s: str, st: int, e: int, ns: int, out: mut [int]) bool:
    if len(p.fixoff) > 0:
        if e - st != p.fixlen:
            return false
        for k in 0..ns:
            out[k] = -1 if p.fixoff[k] < 0 else st + p.fixoff[k]
        return true
    for k in 0..ns:
        out[k] = -1
    pc = 0
    idle = 0                                          # steps since the last character
    pos = st
    n = len(s)
    nc = len(p.code.op)
    while true:
        op = p.code.op[pc]
        if op == I_SAVE:
            x = p.code.x[pc]
            if x < ns:
                out[x] = pos
            pc += 1
        elif op == I_JMP:
            pc = p.code.x[pc]
        elif op == I_SPLIT:
            b = s.byte(pos) if pos < e else 256
            tk2 = (p.onepass[5 * pc + (b >> 6)] >> (b & 63)) & 1
            pc = p.code.x[pc] if tk2 != 0 else p.code.y[pc]
        elif op == I_ASSERT:
            if not _assert(p.code.x[pc], s, pos):
                return false
            pc += 1
        elif op == I_MATCH:
            return pos == e
        else:
            if pos >= e:
                return false
            c = s.byte(pos)
            cp = c
            w = 1
            if c >= 0x80:
                d = decode(s, pos)
                cp = d.0
                w = d.1
            if pos + w > e or not _char_ok(p, pc, cp):
                return false
            pc += 1
            pos += w
            idle = -1
        idle += 1
        if idle > nc:                                 # (a loop that reads nothing)
            return false
    return false

# the groups of a match known to span s[st..e): one walk if the program is one-pass, else the
# backtracker if the match is short, else the VM
fn groups(p: Prog, sc: mut Scratch, s: str, st: int, e: int, ns: int, out: mut [int]) bool:
    if len(p.onepass) > 0 and _onepass(p, s, st, e, ns, &out):
        return true
    if len(p.code.op) * (e - st + 1) <= BT_MAX_BITS:
        if _backtrack(p, &sc, s, st, e, ns, &out):
            return true
    if run_vm(p, &sc, s, st, 3, ns):
        for k in 0..ns:
            out[k] = sc.best[k]
        return true
    return false
```

## library/std/simd.tn

```tern
# simd: 16 bytes worked on at once. A bytes16 is a value like an int (no allocation), and
# each operation is one instruction on ARM (NEON), x86 (SSE2/SSSE3) and wasm (SIMD128), or a
# short loop elsewhere: for scanning text, parsing, checksums, byte tables.
#
#   import simd
#   v = simd.load(s, i)            # bytes16: s[i..i+16] (a runtime error past the end)
#   simd.load_upto(s, i)           # the same, with zeros past the end (i up to len(s)): a
#                                  # string's last few bytes, or a short string, in one load
#   simd.of(t) bytes16             # a 16-byte string as a bytes16 (a table for lookup)
#   simd.splat(b) bytes16          # every lane b (0 to 255)
#   simd.to_str(v) str             # the 16 bytes as a string
#   a & b, a | b, a ^ b, ~a        # lane by lane
#   a + b, a - b                   # lane by lane, wrapping (250 + 10 is 4)
#   a << n, a >> n                 # every lane shifted by n (0 to 7), zeros shifted in
#   a == b, a != b                 # all 16 lanes equal (bool)
#   simd.eq(a, b) bytes16          # 255 in the lanes where a == b, else 0
#   simd.lt(a, b), simd.le(a, b)   # ... where a < b / a <= b (as bytes: 0 to 255)
#   simd.min(a, b), simd.max(a, b) # lane by lane
#   simd.lookup(t, i) bytes16      # lane k is t's lane i[k] (0 if i[k] >= 16): a table lookup
#   simd.bits(v) int               # bit k set when lane k isn't 0 (16 bits)
#   simd.any(v) bool               # a lane isn't 0
#   simd.first_lane(v) int         # the first lane that isn't 0 (16 if none): cheaper than bits
#   simd.lane(v, k) int            # lane k (0 to 15)
#   simd.popcount(v) bytes16       # lane k is the number of bits set in lane k (0 to 8)
#   simd.sum(v) int                # the 16 lanes added up
#   simd.first(m) int              # the lowest set bit of m (64 if none): a bits mask's first lane
#
# f32x4: four f32s at once, a value like a bytes16 (dot products and distances over [f32]):
#   simd.load_f32(xs, i) f32x4     # xs[i..i+4] of an [f32]   simd.store_f32(&xs, i, v)
#   simd.splat_f32(x) f32x4        # every lane x             simd.f32x4(a, b, c, d) f32x4
#   a + b, a - b, a * b, a / b, -a # lane by lane (b may be an f32: every lane)
#   a == b, a != b                 # all four lanes equal (bool)
#   simd.fma(a, b, c) f32x4        # a * b + c, rounded once
#   simd.sum_f32(v) f32            # the four lanes added up
#   simd.min_f32(a, b), simd.max_f32(a, b), simd.abs_f32(v), simd.sqrt_f32(v)   # lane by lane
#   simd.lane_f32(v, k) f32        # lane k (0 to 3)
#
# Finding the first digit, 16 bytes a step:
#
#   fn first_digit(s: str) int:
#       zero = simd.splat(48)
#       nine = simd.splat(9)
#       i = 0
#       while i + 16 <= len(s):
#           k = simd.first_lane(simd.le(simd.load(s, i) - zero, nine))   # '0'..'9': 0..9 after - '0'
#           if k < 16:
#               return i + k
#           i += 16
#       ...                                                         # the last few bytes one at a time
```

## library/std/sql.tn

```tern
# sql: what database drivers share, like Go's database/sql: rows read straight into structs.
# A driver (the pg and sqlite packages, or your own) hands its rows over in the format below;
# sql.decode_rows reads them into your struct type with code the compiler writes for it
# (columns matched to fields by name, each value read by the field's type, no JSON between).
#
#   import sql
#   b = sql.rows(["id", "name", "email"])
#   b.row(3)                      # a row of 3 values, in column order
#   b.put_int(7)
#   b.put_text("Ada")
#   b.put_null()
#   users: [User] = []
#   n = sql.decode_rows(b.bytes(), &users)      # the rows read; -1 if a value doesn't fit
#   if n < 0:
#       print(sql.decode_error())               # the value "x" doesn't fit id: int
#
#   sql.decode_rows(raw str, out: mut T or [T]) int
#       Into a [T]: the rows replace its contents. Into a T: the first row fills the fields it
#       has a column for (the others keep their values); the result counts every row. Fields
#       may be int, float, bool, str, an enum without payloads (read from its label), [int]
#       [float] [bool] [str] (a PostgreSQL array, or JSON), any type json.decode reads (from
#       JSON text), or an Option of one (NULL is None; elsewhere NULL leaves the field zero).
#       -1: a value doesn't fit its field (sql.decode_error() says which), or raw is malformed
#       (decode_error() is "").
#   sql.decode_error() str           why the last decode_rows on this thread returned -1
#   sql.rows_from(head str) Rows     rows(columns) again from b.head() (the header alone, taken
#                                    before the first row): no names to write
#   sql.rows(columns [str]) Rows     builds raw rows: r.row(n), then n values, each one of
#                                    r.put_int(v) put_float put_bool put_text put_null;
#                                    r.bytes() str. Any column may hold any kind of value.
#
# The format (for a driver that forwards a server's bytes, as pg does with PostgreSQL's):
#   header   u32 little-endian column count, then per column: u32le format, u32le name
#            length, the name's bytes
#   rows     each one 'D', u32 big-endian length (of what follows, counting itself), u16be
#            field count, then per field: i32be length (-1: NULL) and that many bytes
#   formats  sql.TEXT    the value as text ("42", "t", "2026-10-11 12:00:00+00", JSON)
#            sql.INT     a signed big-endian integer of 1, 2, 4 or 8 bytes
#            sql.FLOAT   a big-endian IEEE float of 4 or 8 bytes
#            sql.BOOL    one byte, 0 or not
#            sql.UINT    an unsigned big-endian integer of 1, 2, 4 or 8 bytes
#            sql.TAGGED  each value starts with a byte giving its own format (one of the above)
# (These rows are PostgreSQL's DataRow messages, so its rows need no copying.)

import binary
import json                     # (JSON columns decode with json.decode's decoders)

const TEXT = 0
const INT = 1
const FLOAT = 2
const BOOL = 3
const UINT = 4
const TAGGED = 5

struct Rows:
    w: binary.Writer
    _at: int                    # where the row being written starts (-1: none yet)

fn rows(columns: [str]) Rows:
    r = Rows(binary.writer(), -1)
    r.w.put_u32le(len(columns))
    for c in columns:
        r.w.put_u32le(TAGGED)
        r.w.put_u32le(len(c))
        r.w.put_bytes(c)
    return r

# For a driver that already has the values in hand (no rows string to build and read back):
# the first row of a result into a struct. row_field gives the number of the field a column
# is for (-1: the struct has none), once per statement and struct (row_id says which struct,
# a number for its type; 0 when out is an array: use decode_rows). Then per column set_int,
# set_float, set_text or set_null (NULL zeroes the field, or makes an Option None) read the
# value the way decode_rows reads it: true, or false when it doesn't fit the field
# (decode_error() says which).
fn row_id[T](out: mut T) int:
    return _tid(&out)

fn row_field[T](out: mut T, name: str) int:
    return _field(&out, name)

fn set_int[T](out: mut T, field: int, v: int) bool:
    return _put(&out, field, 0, v, 0.0, "")

fn set_float[T](out: mut T, field: int, v: float) bool:
    return _put(&out, field, 1, 0, v, "")

fn set_text[T](out: mut T, field: int, s: str) bool:
    return _put(&out, field, 2, 0, 0.0, s)

fn set_null[T](out: mut T, field: int) bool:
    return _put(&out, field, 3, 0, 0.0, "")

# The same, from the header bytes of an earlier one (head: r.head() of a Rows made by rows(columns)
# with no row yet): a driver that runs the same statement again skips writing the names.
fn rows_from(head: str) Rows:
    r = Rows(binary.writer(), -1)
    r.w.put_bytes(head)
    return r

# The header written so far (the bytes rows(columns) wrote: call before the first row)
fn head(r: mut Rows) str:
    return r.w.bytes()

fn _end_row(r: mut Rows):
    if r._at >= 0:
        r.w.patch_u32be(r._at + 1, r.w.len() - r._at - 1)

# Starts a row of n values (the ones after n are ignored; a row may have fewer than the columns)
fn row(r: mut Rows, n: int):
    _end_row(&r)
    r._at = r.w.len()
    r.w.put_u8(68)                       # 'D'
    r.w.put_u32be(0)                     # (its length, once it's written)
    r.w.put_u16be(n)

fn put_null(r: mut Rows):
    r.w.put_u32be(-1)

fn put_int(r: mut Rows, v: int):
    r.w.put_u32be(9)
    r.w.put_u8(INT)
    r.w.put_u64be(v)

fn put_float(r: mut Rows, v: float):
    r.w.put_u32be(9)
    r.w.put_u8(FLOAT)
    r.w.put_f64be(v)

fn put_bool(r: mut Rows, v: bool):
    r.w.put_u32be(2)
    r.w.put_u8(BOOL)
    r.w.put_u8(1 if v else 0)

fn put_text(r: mut Rows, s: str):
    r.w.put_u32be(len(s) + 1)
    r.w.put_u8(TEXT)
    r.w.put_bytes(s)

# The rows written so far (r can go on)
fn bytes(r: mut Rows) str:
    _end_row(&r)
    return r.w.bytes()
```

## library/std/task.tn

```tern
# task: tasks (green threads), channels, and shared values. Like Go's goroutines, or
# tokio without async/await: code in a task looks blocking, but only the task waits.
#
#   import task
#   h = task.spawn(fn() fetch(url))      # h: task[str]; runs on any core
#   body = h.join()                      # waits; a runtime error in the task is raised here
#
#   ch: chan[int] = task.channel(100)    # holds up to 100 values (0: unbounded)
#   task.spawn(fn() produce(ch))
#   for x in ch:                         # until the channel is closed and empty
#       print(x)
#
#   hits = task.shared(0)                # shared[int]: one value many tasks change
#   fn bump(n: mut int):
#       n += 1
#   hits.update(bump)                    # runs under a lock; tasks (not threads) wait for it
#   print(hits.get())                    # a snapshot (O(1): values are copy-on-write)
#
# Channels:  ch.send(v)  ch.recv()  ch.next(&x) bool (false: closed)  ch.try_recv(&x) bool
#            ch.recv_timeout(&x, ms) bool  ch.close()  len(ch)
#            task.select(chans, &x, ms) int: receive from whichever of chans ([chan[T]]) has a
#            value first; returns its index, -1 after ms milliseconds (ms < 0: no limit), -2
#            when all are closed and empty. Like Go's select / tokio's select!.
# Tasks:     task.spawn(f) task[T]  h.join() T  h.done() bool  h.cancel()
#            task.sleep(ms)  task.yield_now()      (time.sleep(ms) also parks just the task)
#            task.blocking(f) T: run f (fn() T) on a pool of extra threads and wait for it;
#            for work that would stall this core (fsync, SQLite, big files), like tokio's
#            spawn_blocking. Only the calling task waits.
# Groups:    task.all(fs) [T]   task.try_all(fs) Result[[T], E]   task.try_all_limit(fs, n): run the
#            functions at once, results in order; the first Err cancels the rest (Go's errgroup;
#            see the end of this file)
# Shared:    task.shared(v) shared[T]  s.get() T  s.set(v)  s.update(f) (f: fn(mut T) R, returns R)
#            task.atomic(v) Atomic: a.load() a.store(v) a.add(n) int a.cas(old, new) bool
#            task.shared_map() SharedMap: m.put(k, v) m.get_or(k, default) str m.has(k) m.remove(k)
#              m.count() m.add_int(k, n) int m.get_int(k) int
#            (counters and caches without a task lock: far faster than shared under contention)
# Locals:    task.local_set(key, value)  task.local_get(key) str ("" if unset)  task.local_clear():
#            strings that belong to the running task (request ids, tracing context); a spawned
#            task starts with a copy of its spawner's, and they're freed with the task. Outside
#            tasks there's one set per thread.
# Id:        task.id() int: the running task's (0 outside tasks)
#            task.thread_slot() int: the running thread's slot in the scheduler (0 ... cores),
#            for a cache per thread that no other thread contends for
#            task.workers() int: the scheduler's threads (how many `parallel` iterations run
#            at once), for sizing batches of work
#
# Copying a chan / task / shared value shares it (they're handles). Values sent through
# a channel are copied (copy-on-write, so O(1)). One worker per core (TERN_ASYNC_THREADS
# to change); a task stays on the core that first runs it. Tasks share their core's
# 64MB stack, and a waiting task's frames are copied aside (usually well under 1KB), so
# deep recursion works in any task and a million waiting tasks are fine.
# Code inside `parallel:` may use channels; there it waits like a thread.
# Not available on wasm.

fn local_set(key: str, value: str):
    _local_set(key, value)

fn local_get(key: str) str:
    return _local_get(key)

fn local_clear():
    _local_clear()

# The running task's id: the same number for as long as the task runs (0 outside tasks).
# For keeping things per task, like the connection a task's database transaction is on.
fn id() int:
    return _id()

# The running thread's slot in the scheduler: a small number (0 ... cores) no other thread
# running at the same time has (threads outside the scheduler share 0). For keeping a cache
# per thread, as re does with its DFA states. A task may move to another thread when it
# waits, so read it again after a wait.
fn thread_slot() int:
    return _wid()

# The threads the scheduler runs tasks on (TERN_THREADS, or the cores this process may use):
# how many `parallel` iterations run at once. For sizing work batches to the machine.
fn workers() int:
    return _workers()

# ---- groups (like Go's errgroup)
#   task.all(fs) [T]                     run every f (fn() T) at once; their results in order.
#                                        A runtime error in one is raised here.
#   task.try_all(fs) Result[[T], E]      every f (fn() Result[T, E]) at once: Ok with the values in
#                                        order, or the first Err to arrive; the ones still
#                                        running are cancelled
#   task.try_all_limit(fs, n) Result[[T], E]     the same, at most n running at a time
#
#   pages = task.try_all([fn() fetch(a), fn() fetch(b), fn() fetch(c)])?

fn all[T](fs: [fn() T]) [T]:
    hs: [task[T]] = []
    for f in fs:
        hs.push(spawn(f))
    out: [T] = []
    for h in hs:
        out.push(h.join())
    return out

fn try_all[T, E](fs: [fn() Result[T, E]]) Result[[T], E]:
    return try_all_limit(fs, 0)

struct _Done[T, E]:
    i: int
    r: Option[Result[T, E]]

fn _run_one[T, E](ch: chan[_Done[T, E]], i: int, f: fn() Result[T, E]) int:
    ch.send(_Done(i, Some(f())))
    return i

fn try_all_limit[T, E](fs: [fn() Result[T, E]], limit: int) Result[[T], E]:
    n = len(fs)
    ch: chan[_Done[T, E]] = channel(0)
    hs: [task[int]] = []
    vals: [Option[T]] = []
    for k in 0..n:
        vals.push(None)
    started = 0
    got = 0
    while got < n:
        while started < n and (limit <= 0 or started - got < limit):
            i = started
            f = fs[i]
            hs.push(spawn(fn() _run_one(ch, i, f)))
            started += 1
        none: Option[Result[T, E]] = None
        d = _Done(0, none)
        if not ch.recv_timeout(&d, 10):
            for h in hs:                           # one that failed never sends: raise its error
                if h.done():
                    h.join()
            continue
        got += 1
        match d.r.unwrap():
            Ok(v):
                vals[d.i] = Some(v)
            Err(e):
                for h in hs:
                    if h.done():
                        h.join()
                    else:
                        h.cancel()
                while ch.try_recv(&d):             # (results that arrived meanwhile)
                    pass
                return Err(e)
    out: [T] = []
    for v in vals:
        out.push(v.unwrap())
    return Ok(out)

# ---- shared state without task locks (runtime/cells.h)
# shared[T] takes a lock that parks tasks on every get / update: right for a value that
# changes as a whole, slow for a counter or a cache that every request touches. These don't:
#   a = task.atomic(0)          task.Atomic: an int changed by atomic instructions
#   a.load() int   a.store(v)   a.add(n) int (the new value)   a.cas(old, new) bool (store if it was old)
#   m = task.shared_map()       task.SharedMap: str -> str, safe from any task or thread
#   m.put(k, v)   m.get_or(k, default) str   m.has(k) bool   m.remove(k) bool   m.count() int
#   m.add_int(k, n) int   m.get_int(k) int   a per-key int, for counting (0 until added to)
# Copies share the same one (like channels), and the last copy gone frees it: a cache may start
# again with a fresh map.

struct Atomic:
    _h: shared[int]

fn atomic(v: int) Atomic:
    return Atomic(_atomic_new(v))

fn load(a: Atomic) int:
    return _atomic_get(a._h)

fn store(a: Atomic, v: int):
    _atomic_set(a._h, v)

fn add(a: Atomic, n: int) int:
    return _atomic_add(a._h, n)

fn cas(a: Atomic, old: int, v: int) bool:
    return _atomic_cas(a._h, old, v)

struct SharedMap:
    _h: shared[int]

fn shared_map() SharedMap:
    return SharedMap(_smap_new())

fn put(m: SharedMap, k: str, v: str):
    _smap_put(m._h, k, v)

fn get_or(m: SharedMap, k: str, dflt: str) str:
    return _smap_get_or(m._h, k, dflt)

fn has(m: SharedMap, k: str) bool:
    return _smap_has(m._h, k)

fn remove(m: SharedMap, k: str) bool:
    return _smap_remove(m._h, k)

fn count(m: SharedMap) int:
    return _smap_len(m._h)

fn add_int(m: SharedMap, k: str, n: int) int:
    return _smap_add(m._h, k, n)

fn get_int(m: SharedMap, k: str) int:
    return _smap_get_int(m._h, k)
```

## library/std/term.tn

```tern
# term: the terminal: whether output goes to one, its size, colors that switch themselves off
# when they shouldn't show, aligned tables, a progress line, and reading a password.
#
#   import term
#   print(term.green("ok"), term.bold("3 files"))     # plain text when piped, NO_COLOR, ...
#   print(term.table([["NAME", "SIZE"], ["a.txt", "12"], ["notes.md", "3401"]]))
#   for i in 0..n:
#       term.progress(i + 1, n, "copying")             # one line on stderr, redrawn
#   pw = term.secret("password: ")                     # typed without echo
#
#   term.is_tty() bool          stdout is a terminal (stderr_is_tty, stdin_is_tty for the others)
#   term.width() int  term.height() int   the terminal's size ($COLUMNS / $LINES, else 80 x 24)
#   term.color() bool           whether the color functions add color: stdout is a terminal,
#                               NO_COLOR is unset and TERM isn't "dumb" (FORCE_COLOR=1 forces it)
#   term.set_color(on bool)     decide it yourself (a --color flag)
#   term.red(s) green yellow blue magenta cyan gray  bold dim italic underline  (s str) str
#   term.strip_ansi(s) str      s without escape sequences (colors, cursor moves, links)
#   term.display_width(s) int   the columns s takes: escapes take none, a character one
#   term.pad(s, width) str      s and spaces to width columns (escape sequences don't count)
#   term.table(rows [[str]]) str   columns lined up, two spaces apart, a line per row
#   term.progress(done, total, label)   "label [#####-----]  50% 5/10" on stderr, redrawn in
#                               place; a line end once done == total; nothing if stderr isn't
#                               a terminal
#   term.clear_line() str       goes to the start of the line and clears it ("\r\x1b[2K")
#   term.secret(prompt) str     prompt on stderr, then a line from stdin without echoing it
#   term.read_line(prompt) str  prompt on stderr, then a line from stdin with its "\n" ("" at the
#                               end of input), like os.read_line; on a terminal it can be edited
#                               (arrows, Home/End, Ctrl-A/E/K/U/W) and Up/Down bring back the lines
#                               read before. Ctrl-C returns "\x03"

import os
import simd
import task

fn is_tty() bool:
    return _isatty(1)

fn stderr_is_tty() bool:
    return _isatty(2)

fn stdin_is_tty() bool:
    return _isatty(0)

# rows << 16 | columns of the terminal on stdout (else stderr, else stdin), or -1
fn _size() int:
    s = _winsize(1)
    if s < 0:
        s = _winsize(2)
    if s < 0:
        s = _winsize(0)
    return s

fn width() int:
    s = _size()
    if s > 0:
        return s & 0xffff
    return max(os.env("COLUMNS", "").to_int(80), 1)

fn height() int:
    s = _size()
    if s > 0 and s >> 16 > 0:
        return s >> 16
    return max(os.env("LINES", "").to_int(24), 1)

# -1 until decided: once, on first use (a terminal, NO_COLOR unset, TERM not "dumb";
# FORCE_COLOR wins), or by set_color
const _COLOR = task.atomic(-1)

fn color() bool:
    c = _COLOR.load()
    if c < 0:
        force = os.env("FORCE_COLOR", "")
        if force != "" and force != "0":
            c = 1
        elif os.env("NO_COLOR", "") != "" or os.env("TERM", "") == "dumb" or not _isatty(1):
            c = 0
        else:
            c = 1
        _COLOR.store(c)
    return c == 1

fn set_color(on: bool):
    _COLOR.store(1 if on else 0)

fn _paint(s: str, code: str) str:
    if not color():
        return s
    return "\x1b[" + code + "m" + s + "\x1b[0m"

fn red(s: str) str:
    return _paint(s, "31")

fn green(s: str) str:
    return _paint(s, "32")

fn yellow(s: str) str:
    return _paint(s, "33")

fn blue(s: str) str:
    return _paint(s, "34")

fn magenta(s: str) str:
    return _paint(s, "35")

fn cyan(s: str) str:
    return _paint(s, "36")

fn gray(s: str) str:
    return _paint(s, "90")

fn bold(s: str) str:
    return _paint(s, "1")

fn dim(s: str) str:
    return _paint(s, "2")

fn italic(s: str) str:
    return _paint(s, "3")

fn underline(s: str) str:
    return _paint(s, "4")

fn clear_line() str:
    return "\r\x1b[2K"

# bit k set when s[base + k] is ESC (16 bits)
fn _escs(s: str, base: int) int:
    return simd.bits(simd.eq(simd.load_upto(s, base), simd.splat(0x1b)))

# where the escape sequence at i ends (its last byte, or len(s)): CSI "ESC [ ... final byte",
# OSC "ESC ] ... BEL or ESC \\", and two-byte ones (ESC c, ESC 7, ...)
fn _esc_end(s: str, at: int) int:
    n = len(s)
    i = at
    if i + 1 < n and s.byte(i + 1) == 0x5b:
        i += 2
        while i < n and (s.byte(i) < 0x40 or s.byte(i) > 0x7e):
            i += 1
    elif i + 1 < n and s.byte(i + 1) == 0x5d:
        i += 2
        while i < n and s.byte(i) != 7 and not (s.byte(i) == 0x1b and i + 1 < n and s.byte(i + 1) == 0x5c):
            i += 1
        if i < n and s.byte(i) == 0x1b:
            i += 1
    elif i + 1 < n:
        i += 1
    return i

# s without ANSI escape sequences. The ESCs are found 16 bytes at a time, as a bit mask.
fn strip_ansi(s: str) str:
    n = len(s)
    base = 0
    m = _escs(s, 0)
    if m == 0:
        if n <= 16:
            return s
        first = s.find_from("\x1b", 16)
        if first < 0:
            return s
        base = first & -16
        m = _escs(s, base) & (-1 << (first - base))
    out = ""
    out.reserve(n)
    lo = 0
    while lo < n:
        if m == 0:
            base += 16
            if base >= n:
                break
            m = _escs(s, base)
            continue
        i = base + simd.first(m)
        out += s[lo..i]
        lo = min(_esc_end(s, i) + 1, n)
        if lo < n:
            if lo >= base + 16:
                base = lo & -16
                m = _escs(s, base)
            m = m & (-1 << (lo - base))
    out += s[lo..]
    return out

# characters (bytes that don't continue one) in s[lo..hi]
fn _chars(s: str, lo: int, hi: int) int:
    c = 0
    for i in lo..hi:
        if s.byte(i) & 0xc0 != 0x80:
            c += 1
    return c

# columns: escape sequences take none, and each character (not byte) one
fn display_width(s: str) int:
    n = len(s)
    i = s.find("\x1b")
    if i < 0:
        return _chars(s, 0, n)
    w = _chars(s, 0, i)
    while i < n:
        c = s.byte(i)
        if c == 0x1b:
            i = _esc_end(s, i)
        elif c & 0xc0 != 0x80:
            w += 1
        i += 1
    return w

fn pad(s: str, width: int) str:
    w = display_width(s)
    if w >= width:
        return s
    return s + " ".repeat(width - w)

fn table(rows: [[str]]) str:
    widths: [int] = []
    for row in rows:
        for k, cell in row:
            w = display_width(cell)
            if k >= len(widths):
                widths.push(w)
            elif w > widths[k]:
                widths[k] = w
    out = ""
    for row in rows:
        line = ""
        for k, cell in row:
            if k == len(row) - 1:
                line += cell
            else:
                line += pad(cell, widths[k]) + "  "
        e = len(line)
        while e > 0 and line.byte(e - 1) == 32:
            e -= 1
        out += line[..e] + "\n"
    return out

fn progress(done: int, total: int, label: str):
    if not _isatty(2):
        return
    t = max(total, 1)
    d = min(max(done, 0), t)
    bar = 30
    fill = d * bar / t
    pct = str(d * 100 / t)
    line = f"\r\x1b[2K{label} [" + "#".repeat(fill) + "-".repeat(bar - fill) + "] " + " ".repeat(3 - len(pct)) + f"{pct}% {d}/{t}"
    if d == t:
        line += "\n"
    _ewrite(line)

# prompt on stderr, then a line from stdin with echo off (if stdin is a terminal), without its
# line end; "" at the end of input
fn secret(prompt: str) str:
    _ewrite(prompt)
    quiet = _mode(1)
    line = os.read_line()
    if quiet:
        _mode(0)
        _ewrite("\n")
    return line.strip_suffix("\n").strip_suffix("\r")

fn read_line(prompt: str) str:
    os.flush()
    if _isatty(0) and _isatty(2) and _mode(2):
        return _edit(prompt)
    _ewrite(prompt)
    return os.read_line()

# the lines read_line returned, oldest first (kept for the process)
struct _Hist:
    lines: [str]

const _HIST = task.shared(_Hist([]))

fn _remember(h: mut _Hist, line: str) int:
    if len(h.lines) == 0 or h.lines[len(h.lines) - 1] != line:
        h.lines.push(line)
    return 0

fn _cont(c: int) bool:
    return c & 0xc0 == 0x80

fn _prev(b: str, i: int) int:
    j = i
    while j > 0:
        j -= 1
        if not _cont(b.byte(j)):
            return j
    return j

fn _next(b: str, i: int) int:
    j = i
    if j < len(b):
        j += 1
    while j < len(b) and _cont(b.byte(j)):
        j += 1
    return j

# columns: characters, not bytes; CSI escapes take none
fn _cols(p: str) int:
    c = 0
    n = len(p)
    i = 0
    while i < n:
        if p.byte(i) == 0x1b and i + 1 < n and p.byte(i + 1) == 0x5b:
            i += 2
            while i < n and (p.byte(i) < 0x40 or p.byte(i) > 0x7e):
                i += 1
        elif not _cont(p.byte(i)):
            c += 1
        i += 1
    return c

# The line is redrawn whole after each key; when it is wider than the terminal, the part
# around the cursor is shown.
fn _draw(prompt: str, b: str, pos: int):
    w = _winsize(2)
    width = w & 0xffff if w > 0 else 80
    pc = _cols(prompt)
    room = width - pc - 1 if width > pc + 1 else 1
    start = 0
    while _cols(b[start..pos]) >= room:
        start = _next(b, start)
    end = start
    shown = 0
    while end < len(b) and shown < room:
        end = _next(b, end)
        shown += 1
    at = pc + _cols(b[start..pos])
    out = "\r" + prompt + b[start..end] + "\x1b[K\r"
    if at > 0:
        out += f"\x1b[{at}C"
    _ewrite(out)

# the editor, with stdin in raw mode; puts the mode back before it returns
fn _edit(prompt: str) str:
    b = ""
    pos = 0
    at = len(_HIST.get().lines)        # at == len(lines): the line being typed
    draft = ""                         # what was typed before Up was pressed
    done = 0                           # 1 a line, 2 the end of input, 3 Ctrl-C
    _draw(prompt, b, pos)
    while done == 0:
        c = _key()
        to = at                        # a history move: the entry to show
        if c == -1:
            done = 2
        elif c == 13 or c == 10:
            done = 1
        elif c == 3:
            done = 3
        elif c == 4:                   # Ctrl-D: the end of input, or delete
            if len(b) == 0:
                done = 2
            elif pos < len(b):
                b = b[..pos] + b[_next(b, pos)..]
        elif c == 1:
            pos = 0
        elif c == 5:
            pos = len(b)
        elif c == 2:
            pos = _prev(b, pos)
        elif c == 6:
            pos = _next(b, pos)
        elif c == 11:
            b = b[..pos]
        elif c == 21:
            b = b[pos..]
            pos = 0
        elif c == 23:                  # Ctrl-W: the word before the cursor
            i = pos
            while i > 0 and b.byte(i - 1) == 32:
                i -= 1
            while i > 0 and b.byte(i - 1) != 32:
                i -= 1
            b = b[..i] + b[pos..]
            pos = i
        elif c == 12:
            _ewrite("\x1b[H\x1b[2J")
        elif c == 16:
            to = at - 1
        elif c == 14:
            to = at + 1
        elif c == 127 or c == 8:
```
