```tern
            if pos > 0:
                p = _prev(b, pos)
                b = b[..p] + b[pos..]
                pos = p
        elif c == 9:
            b = b[..pos] + "    " + b[pos..]
            pos += 4
        elif c == 27:                  # ESC [ A, ESC [ 3 ~, ESC O H ...
            a = _key()
            k = -1
            if a == 0x5b or a == 0x4f:
                k = _key()
            if k >= 0x30 and k <= 0x39:
                d = _key()
                while d >= 0x30 and d <= 0x39:
                    d = _key()
                if d == 0x3b:          # ESC [ 1 ; 5 C
                    d = _key()
                    d = _key()
                if d == 0x7e and k == 0x33 and pos < len(b):
                    b = b[..pos] + b[_next(b, pos)..]
                if d == 0x7e and (k == 0x31 or k == 0x37):
                    pos = 0
                if d == 0x7e and (k == 0x34 or k == 0x38):
                    pos = len(b)
                if d == 0x43:
                    pos = _next(b, pos)
                if d == 0x44:
                    pos = _prev(b, pos)
            elif k == 0x41:
                to = at - 1
            elif k == 0x42:
                to = at + 1
            elif k == 0x43:
                pos = _next(b, pos)
            elif k == 0x44:
                pos = _prev(b, pos)
            elif k == 0x48:
                pos = 0
            elif k == 0x46:
                pos = len(b)
        elif c >= 32:
            b = b[..pos] + chr(c) + b[pos..]
            pos += 1
        if to != at:
            lines = _HIST.get().lines
            if to >= 0 and to <= len(lines):
                if at == len(lines):
                    draft = b
                b = draft if to == len(lines) else lines[to]
                pos = len(b)
                at = to
        if done == 0:
            _draw(prompt, b, pos)
    _draw(prompt, b, len(b))
    _mode(0)
    if done == 3:
        _ewrite("^C\r\n")
        return "\x03"
    _ewrite("\r\n")
    if done == 2:
        return ""
    if len(b) > 0:
        _HIST.update(fn(h) _remember(&h, b))
    return b + "\n"
```

## library/std/testing.tn

```tern
# testing: checks for `tern test` (see docs/cli.md, "Testing").
#
#   import testing
#   fn test_add():
#       testing.eq_int(add(2, 2), 4)
#
# Each check that fails prints `FAIL: <what> <details>` and ends the test (exit
# status 1); `tern test` reports it with the test's output. A runtime error fails a test too.
#
#   testing.eq_int(got: int, want: int)         testing.eq_str(got: str, want: str)
#   testing.eq_float(got: float, want: float)   testing.eq_bool(got: bool, want: bool)
#   testing.near(got: float, want: float, tolerance: float)
#   testing.eq_ints(got: [int], want: [int])    testing.eq_strs(got: [str], want: [str])
#   testing.is_true(cond: bool, what: str)      testing.is_false(cond: bool, what: str)
#   testing.includes(s: str, sub: str)
#   testing.fail(msg: str)                      (always fails)
import os

fn fail(msg: str):
    print("FAIL: " + msg)
    os.exit(1)

fn eq_int(got: int, want: int):
    if got != want:
        fail(f"eq_int: got {got}, want {want}")

fn eq_str(got: str, want: str):
    if got != want:
        fail(f"eq_str: got {json_quote(got)}, want {json_quote(want)}")

fn eq_float(got: float, want: float):
    if got != want:
        fail(f"eq_float: got {got}, want {want}")

fn near(got: float, want: float, tolerance: float):
    if abs(got - want) > tolerance:
        fail(f"near: got {got}, want {want} (within {tolerance})")

fn eq_bool(got: bool, want: bool):
    if got != want:
        fail(f"eq_bool: got {got}, want {want}")

fn eq_ints(got: [int], want: [int]):
    if len(got) != len(want):
        fail(f"eq_ints: got {len(got)} values, want {len(want)}")
    for i, g in got:
        if g != want[i]:
            fail(f"eq_ints: [{i}] is {g}, want {want[i]}")

fn eq_strs(got: [str], want: [str]):
    if len(got) != len(want):
        fail(f"eq_strs: got {len(got)} values, want {len(want)}")
    for i, g in got:
        if g != want[i]:
            fail(f"eq_strs: [{i}] is {json_quote(g)}, want {json_quote(want[i])}")

fn is_true(cond: bool, what: str):
    if not cond:
        fail(f"is_true: {what}")

fn is_false(cond: bool, what: str):
    if cond:
        fail(f"is_false: {what}")

fn includes(s: str, sub: str):
    if not s.contains(sub):
        fail(f"includes: {json_quote(s)} doesn't contain {json_quote(sub)}")
```

## library/std/time.tn

```tern
# time: clocks, sleeping, formatting and parsing, calendar fields, durations.
# A time is a float: seconds since 1970-01-01 00:00 UTC (the Unix epoch), like time.now().
#
#   time.now() float                  wall clock        time.now_ms() int
#   time.mono_ns() int  time.mono_ms() int     a monotonic clock for measuring intervals
#                                     (never jumps when the wall clock is set)
#   time.sleep(ms)                    (in a task, only the task waits)
#
#   time.rfc3339(t) str               "2026-09-28T06:45:12Z" ("...12.345Z" when t has milliseconds)
#   time.rfc3339_local(t) str         "2026-09-28T08:45:12+02:00" (the system's time zone)
#   time.parse_rfc3339(s) float       accepts Z or +hh:mm offsets and any fraction of a second
#   time.format(t, layout) str        strftime layouts in UTC: "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", plus %L
#   time.format_local(t, layout) str  (milliseconds) and %f (microseconds)
#   time.parse(s, layout) float       strptime layouts, read as UTC   time.parse_local(s, layout) float
#   time.error() str                  why the last parse failed ("" after a success; a failed
#                                     parse returns 0.0)
#
#   time.utc(t) Date   time.local(t) Date    calendar fields (see struct Date)
#   time.date(year, month, day, hour, minute, second) float     a UTC time from fields
#                                     (months and days out of range carry over, like timegm)
#   time.offset(t) int                the local zone's offset from UTC at t, in seconds
#
#   time.duration(seconds float) str  "1h2m3.5s", "250ms", "12us" (Go's style)
#   time.parse_duration(s) float      "1h30m", "2.5s", "300ms", "-1m", "7d", "2w" -> seconds
#
#   start = time.mono_ns()
#   work()
#   print("took", time.duration(float(time.mono_ns() - start) / 1e9))
#   d = time.utc(time.parse_rfc3339("2026-02-28T23:30:00-05:00"))    # d.day == 1, d.month == 3
#
# Layouts (format and parse): %Y year, %m month, %d day (%e space-padded), %H hour (%k
# space-padded), %I %l 12-hour, %p AM/PM, %M minute, %S second, %L milliseconds, %f
# microseconds, %y two-digit year, %C century, %j day of the year, %a %A weekday, %b %h %B
# month, %z offset (+0000), %Z zone name, %s seconds since 1970, %u %w weekday number, %U %W
# %V week number, %G %g ISO year, %F %T %D %R %r %c %x %X %+ the usual combinations, %n %t
# %% (E and O modifiers are ignored). Names are English (the C locale).
# Parsing reads the same directives, and the whole input must match the whole layout;
# numbers may have spaces before them; %z (+hhmm, +hh:mm or Z), %Z (UTC, GMT) and %s set
# the time; weekday names and %j are read but don't. Missing fields are 1900-01-01 00:00:00.

import binary
import math

struct Date:
    year: int
    month: int                  # 1..12
    day: int                    # 1..31
    hour: int
    minute: int
    second: int
    nano: int                   # nanoseconds within the second
    weekday: int                # 0 = Sunday .. 6 = Saturday
    yday: int                   # 1..366
    offset: int                 # seconds east of UTC (0 for utc())

const _DAYS = ["Sunday", "Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday"]
const _POW10 = [1.0, 10.0, 100.0, 1000.0, 10000.0, 100000.0, 1000000.0, 10000000.0, 100000000.0, 1000000000.0, 10000000000.0, 100000000000.0, 1000000000000.0, 10000000000000.0, 100000000000000.0, 1000000000000000.0]
const _MONTHS = ["January", "February", "March", "April", "May", "June", "July", "August", "September", "October", "November", "December"]

fn utc(t: float) Date:
    sn = _split(t)
    return _civil(sn.0, sn.1)

fn local(t: float) Date:
    return _fields(t, true)

# the local zone's offset from UTC at t, in seconds
fn offset(t: float) int:
    return _fields(t, true).offset

# A UTC time from fields; months and days out of range carry over, like timegm
fn date(year: int, month: int, day: int, hour: int, minute: int, second: int) float:
    return _utc_from(year, month, day, hour, minute, float(second))

# with Result: t = time.try_parse_rfc3339(s)?   (Err: "time: not an RFC 3339 time: ...")
fn try_parse_rfc3339(s: str) Result[float, str]:
    t = parse_rfc3339(s)
    if error() != "":
        return Err("time: " + error())
    return Ok(t)

fn try_parse(s: str, layout: str) Result[float, str]:
    t = parse(s, layout)
    if error() != "":
        return Err("time: " + error())
    return Ok(t)

fn try_parse_duration(s: str) Result[float, str]:
    d = parse_duration(s)
    if error() != "":
        return Err("time: " + error())
    return Ok(d)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- calendar arithmetic

# t as whole seconds (rounded toward -infinity) and nanoseconds (rounded to nearest)
fn _split(t: float) (int, int):
    f = math.floor(t)
    s = int(f)
    ns = int((t - f) * 1e9 + 0.5)
    if ns >= 1000000000:
        s += 1
        ns -= 1000000000
    return (s, ns)

fn _leap(y: int) bool:
    return (y % 4 == 0 and y % 100 != 0) or y % 400 == 0

# the UTC fields of s seconds since 1970
fn _civil(s: int, ns: int) Date:
    days = s / 86400
    sod = s % 86400
    if sod < 0:
        sod += 86400
        days -= 1
    # C. Neri and L. Schneider, "Euclidean affine functions and their application to calendar
    # algorithms" (2022): three divisions. The day number is shifted by 730000000 eras of 400
    # years so that everything is positive for any day a 64-bit time can name.
    n = days + 106650810719468                      # 719468 + 146097 * 730000000
    n1 = 4 * n + 3
    c = n1 / 146097
    n2 = (n1 % 146097) | 3                          # 4 * (day in the century) + 3
    p2 = 2939745 * n2
    ny = (p2 & 4294967295) / 11758980               # day of the year from March 1 (2939745 * 4)
    n3 = 2141 * ny + 197913
    m = n3 >> 16
    d = (n3 & 65535) / 2141 + 1
    y = 100 * c + (p2 >> 32) - 292000000000         # 400 * 730000000
    yday = 0
    if ny >= 306:                                   # January, February: next year's
        y += 1
        m -= 12
        yday = ny - 305
    else:
        yday = ny + 60 + (1 if _leap(y) else 0)
    wday = (days % 7 + 11) % 7
    return Date(y, m, d, sod / 3600, sod / 60 % 60, sod % 60, ns, wday, yday, 0)

fn _days_from_civil(y0: int, m: int, d: int) int:
    y = y0 - (1 if m <= 2 else 0)
    era = (y if y >= 0 else y - 399) / 400
    yoe = y - era * 400
    doy = (153 * (m + (-3 if m > 2 else 9)) + 2) / 5 + d - 1
    doe = yoe * 365 + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100 + doy
    return era * 146097 + doe - 719468

fn _utc_from(y: int, mo: int, d: int, h: int, mi: int, s: float) float:
    m0 = mo - 1
    yy = y + (m0 / 12 if m0 >= 0 else -((11 - m0) / 12))
    m0 = ((m0 % 12) + 12) % 12
    return float(_days_from_civil(yy, m0 + 1, 1) + d - 1) * 86400.0 + float(h * 3600 + mi * 60) + s

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- formatting

fn format(t: float, layout: str) str:
    sn = _split(t)
    return _format(_civil(sn.0, sn.1), sn.0, t, false, layout)

fn format_local(t: float, layout: str) str:
    return _format(_fields(t, true), _split(t).0, t, true, layout)

fn rfc3339(t: float) str:
    return _rfc(t, false)

fn rfc3339_local(t: float) str:
    return _rfc(t, true)

fn _rfc(t: float, local: bool) str:
    sn = _split(t)
    d = _fields(t, true) if local else _civil(sn.0, sn.1)
    y = d.year
    msv = d.nano / 1000000
    if y >= 0 and y <= 9999 and d.offset == 0:      # (one string, written once)
        o = ""
        o.reserve(32)
        if msv == 0:
            o += chr(48 + y / 1000) + chr(48 + y / 100 % 10) + chr(48 + y / 10 % 10) + chr(48 + y % 10) + "-" + chr(48 + d.month / 10) + chr(48 + d.month % 10) + "-" + chr(48 + d.day / 10) + chr(48 + d.day % 10) + "T" + chr(48 + d.hour / 10) + chr(48 + d.hour % 10) + ":" + chr(48 + d.minute / 10) + chr(48 + d.minute % 10) + ":" + chr(48 + d.second / 10) + chr(48 + d.second % 10) + "Z"
            return o
        o += chr(48 + y / 1000) + chr(48 + y / 100 % 10) + chr(48 + y / 10 % 10) + chr(48 + y % 10) + "-" + chr(48 + d.month / 10) + chr(48 + d.month % 10) + "-" + chr(48 + d.day / 10) + chr(48 + d.day % 10) + "T" + chr(48 + d.hour / 10) + chr(48 + d.hour % 10) + ":" + chr(48 + d.minute / 10) + chr(48 + d.minute % 10) + ":" + chr(48 + d.second / 10) + chr(48 + d.second % 10) + "." + chr(48 + msv / 100) + chr(48 + msv / 10 % 10) + chr(48 + msv % 10) + "Z"
        return o
    o = ""
    o.reserve(32)
    _num(&o, y, 4, "0")
    o += "-" + chr(48 + d.month / 10) + chr(48 + d.month % 10) + "-" + chr(48 + d.day / 10) + chr(48 + d.day % 10)
    o += "T" + chr(48 + d.hour / 10) + chr(48 + d.hour % 10) + ":" + chr(48 + d.minute / 10) + chr(48 + d.minute % 10)
    o += ":" + chr(48 + d.second / 10) + chr(48 + d.second % 10)
    if msv != 0:
        o += "." + chr(48 + msv / 100) + chr(48 + msv / 10 % 10) + chr(48 + msv % 10)
    if d.offset == 0:
        o += "Z"
    else:
        a = abs(d.offset)
        o += ("-" if d.offset < 0 else "+") + chr(48 + a / 36000) + chr(48 + a / 3600 % 10) + ":" + chr(48 + a % 3600 / 600) + chr(48 + a % 3600 / 60 % 10)
    return o

# v in at least width digits, padded with pad (the sign counts toward the width, like printf)
fn _num(o: mut str, v: int, width: int, pad: str):
    if v >= 0 and v < 100 and width == 2:
        if v < 10:
            o += pad + chr(48 + v)
        else:
            o += chr(48 + v / 10) + chr(48 + v % 10)
        return
    t = str(v if v >= 0 else -v)
    w = width
    if v < 0:
        o += "-"
        w -= 1
    if len(t) < w:
        o += pad * (w - len(t))
    o += t

# ISO 8601 week-based year and week number
fn _iso_week(d: Date) (int, int):
    yd = d.yday - 1
    wd = (d.weekday + 6) % 7                        # 0 Monday
    w = (yd - wd + 10) / 7
    y = d.year
    if w < 1:
        y -= 1
        w = (yd + (366 if _leap(y) else 365) - wd + 10) / 7
    elif w == 53:
        if yd - wd + 3 >= (366 if _leap(y) else 365):      # this week's Thursday is in next year
            w = 1
            y += 1
    return (y, w)

# "+0200"
fn _zone_num(off: int) str:
    a = abs(off)
    return ("-" if off < 0 else "+") + chr(48 + a / 36000) + chr(48 + a / 3600 % 10) + chr(48 + a % 3600 / 600) + chr(48 + a % 3600 / 60 % 10)

# v in at least width digits, padded with pad (the sign counts toward the width, like printf)
fn _numstr(v: int, width: int, pad: str) str:
    o = ""
    _num(&o, v, width, pad)
    return o

# (every append in the loop is of pieces, so it runs as a string builder)
fn _format(d: Date, epoch: int, t: float, local: bool, lay: str) str:
    o = ""
    o.reserve(len(lay) * 3 + 16)
    i = 0
    n = len(lay)
    while i < n:
        c = lay.byte(i)
        if c != 37:
            j = i + 1
            while j < n and lay.byte(j) != 37:
                j += 1
            if j == i + 1:
                o += chr(c)
            else:
                o += lay[i..j]
            i = j
            continue
        i += 1
        if i >= n:
            o += "%"
            break
        c = lay.byte(i)
        i += 1
        if c == 69 or c == 79:                      # E, O (the C locale: the same as without)
            if i < n:
                c = lay.byte(i)
                i += 1
        match c:
            89:                                     # Y
                y = d.year
                if y >= 1000 and y < 10000:
                    o += chr(48 + y / 1000) + chr(48 + y / 100 % 10) + chr(48 + y / 10 % 10) + chr(48 + y % 10)
                else:
                    x = _numstr(y, 4, "0")
                    o += x
            109:                                    # m
                o += chr(48 + d.month / 10) + chr(48 + d.month % 10)
            100:                                    # d
                o += chr(48 + d.day / 10) + chr(48 + d.day % 10)
            72:                                     # H
                o += chr(48 + d.hour / 10) + chr(48 + d.hour % 10)
            77:                                     # M
                o += chr(48 + d.minute / 10) + chr(48 + d.minute % 10)
            83:                                     # S
                o += chr(48 + d.second / 10) + chr(48 + d.second % 10)
            76:                                     # L
                v = d.nano / 1000000
                o += chr(48 + v / 100) + chr(48 + v / 10 % 10) + chr(48 + v % 10)
            102:                                    # f
                v = d.nano / 1000
                o += chr(48 + v / 100000) + chr(48 + v / 10000 % 10) + chr(48 + v / 1000 % 10) + chr(48 + v / 100 % 10) + chr(48 + v / 10 % 10) + chr(48 + v % 10)
            70:                                     # F
                y = d.year
                if y >= 1000 and y < 10000:
                    o += chr(48 + y / 1000) + chr(48 + y / 100 % 10) + chr(48 + y / 10 % 10) + chr(48 + y % 10)
                else:
                    x = _numstr(y, 4, "0")
                    o += x
                o += "-" + chr(48 + d.month / 10) + chr(48 + d.month % 10) + "-" + chr(48 + d.day / 10) + chr(48 + d.day % 10)
            84 | 88:                                # T X
                o += chr(48 + d.hour / 10) + chr(48 + d.hour % 10) + ":" + chr(48 + d.minute / 10) + chr(48 + d.minute % 10) + ":" + chr(48 + d.second / 10) + chr(48 + d.second % 10)
            101 | 107:                              # e k
                v = d.day if c == 101 else d.hour
                if v < 10:
                    o += " " + chr(48 + v)
                else:
                    o += chr(48 + v / 10) + chr(48 + v % 10)
            73 | 108:                               # I l
                h = d.hour % 12
                v = 12 if h == 0 else h
                if v >= 10:
                    o += "1" + chr(48 + v % 10)
                elif c == 73:
                    o += "0" + chr(48 + v)
                else:
                    o += " " + chr(48 + v)
            106:                                    # j
                o += chr(48 + d.yday / 100) + chr(48 + d.yday / 10 % 10) + chr(48 + d.yday % 10)
            121:                                    # y
                v = abs(d.year % 100)
                o += chr(48 + v / 10) + chr(48 + v % 10)
            67:                                     # C
                if d.year < 0 and d.year > -100:
                    o += "-0"
                else:
                    x = _numstr(d.year / 100, 2, "0")
                    o += x
            97:                                     # a
                o += _DAYS[d.weekday][..3]
            65:                                     # A
                x = _DAYS[d.weekday]
                o += x
            98 | 104:                               # b h
                o += _MONTHS[d.month - 1][..3]
            66:                                     # B
                x = _MONTHS[d.month - 1]
                o += x
            112:                                    # p
                if d.hour < 12:
                    o += "AM"
                else:
                    o += "PM"
            117:                                    # u
                o += chr(48 + (7 if d.weekday == 0 else d.weekday))
            119:                                    # w
                o += chr(48 + d.weekday)
            85:                                     # U
                v = (d.yday - 1 + 7 - d.weekday) / 7
                o += chr(48 + v / 10) + chr(48 + v % 10)
            87:                                     # W
                v = (d.yday - 1 + 7 - (d.weekday + 6) % 7) / 7
                o += chr(48 + v / 10) + chr(48 + v % 10)
            86 | 71 | 103:                          # V G g
                yw = _iso_week(d)
                if c == 86:
                    o += chr(48 + yw.1 / 10) + chr(48 + yw.1 % 10)
                elif c == 71:
                    x = _numstr(yw.0, 4, "0")
                    o += x
                else:
                    v = abs(yw.0 % 100)
                    o += chr(48 + v / 10) + chr(48 + v % 10)
            115:                                    # s
                x = str(epoch)
                o += x
            122:                                    # z
                x = _zone_num(d.offset)
                o += x
            90:                                     # Z
                if local:
                    x = _zone(t)
                    o += x
                else:
                    o += "UTC"
            110:                                    # n
                o += "\n"
            116:                                    # t
                o += "\t"
            37:
                o += "%"
            82:                                     # R
                x = _format(d, epoch, t, local, "%H:%M")
                o += x
            114:                                    # r
                x = _format(d, epoch, t, local, "%I:%M:%S %p")
                o += x
            68 | 120:                               # D x
                x = _format(d, epoch, t, local, "%m/%d/%y")
                o += x
            99:                                     # c
                x = _format(d, epoch, t, local, "%a %b %e %H:%M:%S %Y")
                o += x
            43:                                     # +
                x = _format(d, epoch, t, local, "%a %b %e %H:%M:%S %Z %Y")
                o += x
            _:
                o += chr(c)
    return o

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- durations

# the float's bits
fn _bits(x: float) int:
    b = "\x00" * 8
    binary.set_f64le(&b, 0, x)
    return binary.u64le(b, 0)

# printf's %.<d>f for 0 <= x < 2^53 / 10^d, d <= 4: the exact binary value, rounded half to even
fn _fixed(x: float, d: int) str:
    pow = 1
    for k in 0..d:
        pow *= 10
    bits = _bits(x)
    e = (bits >> 52) & 2047
    m = bits & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFF
    if e == 0:
        e = 1
    else:
        m = m | (1 << 52)
    sh = 1075 - e                                   # x = m / 2^sh
    v = 0                                           # x * 10^d, truncated
    up = false
    if sh <= 0:
        v = (m << (-sh)) * pow
    else:
        sticky = false
        if sh > 60:
            cut = sh - 60
            if cut >= 63:
                sticky = m != 0
                m = 0
            else:
                sticky = m & ((1 << cut) - 1) != 0
                m = m >> cut
            sh = 60
        mask = (1 << sh) - 1
        v = m >> sh
        r = m & mask
        for k in 0..d:
            r *= 10
            v = v * 10 + (r >> sh)
            r = r & mask
        half = 1 << (sh - 1)
        up = r > half or (r == half and (sticky or v % 2 == 1))
    if up:
        v += 1
    ip = str(v / pow)
    if d == 0:
        return ip
    f = str(v % pow)
    return ip + "." + "0" * (d - len(f)) + f

# without trailing zeros after the point (and the point if nothing is left after it)
fn _trim0(s: str) str:
    if not s.contains("."):
        return s
    e = len(s)
    while e > 0 and s.byte(e - 1) == 48:
        e -= 1
    if e > 0 and s.byte(e - 1) == 46:
        e -= 1
    return s[..e]

# printf's %.4g for 1 <= x < 1000
fn _g4(x: float) str:
    d = 3 if x < 10.0 else 2 if x < 100.0 else 1
    s = _fixed(x, d)
    if len(s) - d - 1 > 4 - d:                      # rounded up to the next power of ten
        s = _fixed(x, max(d - 1, 0))
    return _trim0(s)

# "1h2m3.5s", "250ms", "12us", "0s" (Go's style)
fn duration(secs: float) str:
    o = ""
    x = secs
    if x < 0.0:
        o += "-"
        x = -x
    if x == 0.0:
        return o + "0s"
    if x < 1e-6:
        return o + _fixed(x * 1e9, 0) + "ns"
    if x < 1e-3:
        return o + _g4(x * 1e6) + "us"
    if x < 1.0:
        return o + _g4(x * 1e3) + "ms"
    whole = int(x)
    h = whole / 3600
    m = whole % 3600 / 60
    s = x - float(h * 3600 + m * 60)
    if h != 0:
        o += str(h) + "h"
    if h != 0 or m != 0:
        o += str(m) + "m"
    return o + _trim0(_fixed(s, 3)) + "s"

# (the longest number at s[a..b], which holds only digits and dots)
fn _strtod(s: str, a: int, b: int) float:
    e = a
    while e < b and s.byte(e) >= 48 and s.byte(e) <= 57:
        e += 1
    if e < b and s.byte(e) == 46:
        f = e + 1
        while f < b and s.byte(f) >= 48 and s.byte(f) <= 57:
            f += 1
        if f > e + 1 or e > a:
            e = f
    if e == a:
        return 0.0
    # digits and at most 15 of them: m / 10^k is exact in both parts, so the one division
    # rounds correctly (strtod's answer); otherwise strtod itself
    m = 0
    k = -1
    nd = 0
    for i in a..e:
        c = s.byte(i)
        if c == 46:
            k = 0
        else:
            m = m * 10 + c - 48
            nd += 1
            if k >= 0:
                k += 1
    if nd > 15:
        return s[a..e].to_float(0.0)
    if k <= 0:
        return float(m)
    return float(m) / _POW10[k]

fn _digit_or_dot(c: int) bool:
    return (c >= 48 and c <= 57) or c == 46

# "1h30m", "2.5s", "300ms", "-1m", "7d", "2w" -> seconds; 0.0 and time.error() set if s isn't one
fn parse_duration(s: str) float:
    n = len(s)
    p = 0
    sign = 1.0
    if p < n and (s.byte(p) == 45 or s.byte(p) == 43):
        sign = -1.0 if s.byte(p) == 45 else 1.0
        p += 1
    if p == n:
        return _bad_duration(s)
    if n - p == 1 and s.byte(p) == 48:
        _set_error("")
        return 0.0
    total = 0.0
    while p < n:
        num = p
        while p < n and _digit_or_dot(s.byte(p)):
            p += 1
        if p == num:
            return _bad_duration(s)
        v = _strtod(s, num, p)
        u = p
        while p < n and not _digit_or_dot(s.byte(p)):
            p += 1
        k = p - u
        if k == 0:
            return _bad_duration(s)
        c = s.byte(u)
        if k == 1 and c == 119:                     # w
            total += v * 604800.0
        elif k == 1 and c == 100:                   # d
            total += v * 86400.0
        elif k == 1 and c == 104:                   # h
            total += v * 3600.0
        elif k == 1 and c == 109:                   # m
            total += v * 60.0
        elif k == 1 and c == 115:                   # s
            total += v
        elif k == 2 and s.byte(u + 1) == 115 and c == 109:      # ms (divide for the small
            total += v / 1e3                                    # units: 45us is exactly 45/1e6)
        elif (k == 2 and s.byte(u + 1) == 115 and c == 117) or (k == 3 and s[u..p] == "\xc2\xb5s"):
            total += v / 1e6
        elif k == 2 and s.byte(u + 1) == 115 and c == 110:      # ns
            total += v / 1e9
        else:
            return _bad_duration(s)
    _set_error("")
    return sign * total

fn _bad_duration(s: str) float:
    _set_error("not a duration: \"" + _clip(s, 40) + "\" (write e.g. \"1h30m\", \"7d\", \"2.5s\", \"300ms\")")
    return 0.0

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- parsing

# s's first n bytes, up to a NUL (as the error messages quote their input)
fn _clip(s: str, n: int) str:
    z = s.find("\x00")
    e = z if z >= 0 and z < n else min(len(s), n)
    return s[..e]

# n digits at p, or -1
fn _digits(s: str, p: int, n: int) int:
    if p + n > len(s):
        return -1
    v = 0
    for k in 0..n:
        c = s.byte(p + k)
        if c < 48 or c > 57:
            return -1
        v = v * 10 + c - 48
    return v

# RFC 3339 / ISO 8601: "2026-09-28T06:45:12Z", "...12.345+02:00", "2026-09-28 06:45:12Z";
# 0.0 and time.error() set if s isn't one
fn parse_rfc3339(s: str) float:
    y = _digits(s, 0, 4)
    if y < 0 or len(s) < 19 or s.byte(4) != 45:
        return _bad_rfc(s)
    mo = _digits(s, 5, 2)
    if mo < 0 or s.byte(7) != 45:
        return _bad_rfc(s)
    d = _digits(s, 8, 2)
    t = s.byte(10)
    if d < 0 or (t != 84 and t != 116 and t != 32):
        return _bad_rfc(s)
    h = _digits(s, 11, 2)
    if h < 0 or s.byte(13) != 58:
        return _bad_rfc(s)
    mi = _digits(s, 14, 2)
    if mi < 0 or s.byte(16) != 58:
        return _bad_rfc(s)
    sec = _digits(s, 17, 2)
    if sec < 0 or mo < 1 or mo > 12 or d < 1 or d > 31 or h > 23 or mi > 59 or sec > 60:
        return _bad_rfc(s)
    p = 19
    n = len(s)
    frac = 0.0
    scale = 0.1
    if p < n and (s.byte(p) == 46 or s.byte(p) == 44):
        p += 1
        if p >= n or s.byte(p) < 48 or s.byte(p) > 57:
            return _bad(0.0, "not an RFC 3339 time: bad fraction")
        while p < n and s.byte(p) >= 48 and s.byte(p) <= 57:
            frac += float(s.byte(p) - 48) * scale
            scale /= 10.0
            p += 1
    off = 0
    if p < n and (s.byte(p) == 90 or s.byte(p) == 122):
        p += 1
    elif p < n and (s.byte(p) == 43 or s.byte(p) == 45):
        sign = -1 if s.byte(p) == 45 else 1
        p += 1
        oh = _digits(s, p, 2)
        om = _digits(s, p + 3, 2) if p + 2 < n and s.byte(p + 2) == 58 else -1
        if oh < 0 or om < 0:
            return _bad(0.0, "not an RFC 3339 time: bad offset")
        off = sign * (oh * 3600 + om * 60)
        p += 5
    else:
        return _bad(0.0, "not an RFC 3339 time: no time zone (Z or +hh:mm)")
    if p != n:
        return _bad(0.0, "not an RFC 3339 time: extra text")
    _set_error("")
    return _utc_from(y, mo, d, h, mi, float(sec) + frac) - float(off)

fn _bad_rfc(s: str) float:
    return _bad(0.0, "not an RFC 3339 time: " + _clip(s, 60))

fn _bad(v: float, why: str) float:
    _set_error(why)
    return v

# strptime-style parsing (the C locale)
struct _P:
    s: str
    p: int
    year: int
    month: int
    day: int
    hour: int
    minute: int
    second: int
    frac: float
    pm: int                     # -1 none, 0 AM, 1 PM
    h12: bool
    off: int                    # %z, in seconds east of UTC
    has_off: bool
    epoch: int                  # %s
    has_epoch: bool

fn _space(c: int) bool:
    return c == 32 or (c >= 9 and c <= 13)

# up to max digits (at least one, after any white space); -1 if none
fn _pnum(st: mut _P, max: int) int:
    while st.p < len(st.s) and _space(st.s.byte(st.p)):
        st.p += 1
    v = 0
    k = 0
    while k < max and st.p < len(st.s) and st.s.byte(st.p) >= 48 and st.s.byte(st.p) <= 57:
        v = v * 10 + st.s.byte(st.p) - 48
        st.p += 1
        k += 1
    return v if k > 0 else -1

# a name from names (in full or its first 3 letters, ASCII case ignored): its index or -1
fn _pname(st: mut _P, names: [str]) int:
    for i, nm in names:
        for l in [len(nm), 3]:
            if st.p + l <= len(st.s) and st.s[st.p..st.p + l].lower() == nm[..l].lower():
                st.p += l
                return i
    return -1

fn _pfield(st: mut _P, c: int) bool:
    if c == 89:                                     # Y
        v = _pnum(&st, 4)
        if v < 0:
            return false
        st.year = v
    elif c == 109:                                  # m
        v = _pnum(&st, 2)
        if v < 1 or v > 12:
            return false
        st.month = v
    elif c == 100 or c == 101:                      # d e
        v = _pnum(&st, 2)
        if v < 1 or v > 31:
            return false
        st.day = v
    elif c == 72 or c == 107:                       # H k
        v = _pnum(&st, 2)
        if v < 0 or v > 23:
            return false
        st.hour = v
        st.h12 = false
    elif c == 73 or c == 108:                       # I l
        v = _pnum(&st, 2)
        if v < 1 or v > 12:
            return false
        st.hour = v
        st.h12 = true
    elif c == 77:                                   # M
        v = _pnum(&st, 2)
        if v < 0 or v > 59:
            return false
        st.minute = v
    elif c == 83:                                   # S
        v = _pnum(&st, 2)
        if v < 0 or v > 61:
            return false
        st.second = v
    elif c == 76 or c == 102:                       # L f: a fraction of a second
        at = st.p
        v = _pnum(&st, 3 if c == 76 else 9)
        if v < 0:
            return false
        st.frac = float(v) / math.pow(10.0, float(st.p - at))
    elif c == 121:                                  # y
        v = _pnum(&st, 2)
        if v < 0:
            return false
        st.year = v + (2000 if v < 69 else 1900)
    elif c == 67:                                   # C
        v = _pnum(&st, 2)
        if v < 0:
            return false
        st.year = v * 100 + st.year % 100
    elif c == 98 or c == 66 or c == 104:            # b B h
        v = _pname(&st, _MONTHS)
        if v < 0:
            return false
        st.month = v + 1
    elif c == 97 or c == 65:                        # a A
        if _pname(&st, _DAYS) < 0:
            return false
    elif c == 112:                                  # p
        if st.p + 2 > len(st.s):
            return false
        ap = st.s[st.p..st.p + 2].lower()
        if ap == "am":
            st.pm = 0
        elif ap == "pm":
            st.pm = 1
        else:
            return false
        st.p += 2
    elif c == 106:                                  # j (read, not applied)
        v = _pnum(&st, 3)
        if v < 1 or v > 366:
            return false
    elif c == 117 or c == 119:                      # u w (read, not applied)
        v = _pnum(&st, 1)
        if v < 0 or v > 7:
            return false
    elif c == 115:                                  # s
        neg = st.p < len(st.s) and st.s.byte(st.p) == 45
        if neg:
            st.p += 1
        v = _pnum(&st, 18)
        if v < 0:
            return false
        st.epoch = -v if neg else v
        st.has_epoch = true
    elif c == 122:                                  # z: Z, +hh, +hhmm, +hh:mm
        if st.p < len(st.s) and (st.s.byte(st.p) == 90 or st.s.byte(st.p) == 122):
            st.p += 1
            st.has_off = true
            st.off = 0
            return true
        if st.p >= len(st.s) or (st.s.byte(st.p) != 43 and st.s.byte(st.p) != 45):
            return false
        sign = -1 if st.s.byte(st.p) == 45 else 1
        st.p += 1
        h = _digits(st.s, st.p, 2)
        if h < 0:
            return false
        st.p += 2
        m = 0
        if st.p < len(st.s) and st.s.byte(st.p) == 58:
            st.p += 1
            m = _digits(st.s, st.p, 2)
            if m < 0:
                return false
            st.p += 2
        elif _digits(st.s, st.p, 2) >= 0:
            m = _digits(st.s, st.p, 2)
            st.p += 2
        if h > 23 or m > 59:
            return false
        st.off = sign * (h * 3600 + m * 60)
        st.has_off = true
    elif c == 90:                                   # Z: UTC or GMT
        if st.p + 3 <= len(st.s) and (st.s[st.p..st.p + 3] == "UTC" or st.s[st.p..st.p + 3] == "GMT"):
            st.p += 3
            st.off = 0
            st.has_off = true
        else:
            return false
    elif c == 110 or c == 116:                      # n t: any white space
        while st.p < len(st.s) and _space(st.s.byte(st.p)):
            st.p += 1
    elif c == 37:
        if st.p >= len(st.s) or st.s.byte(st.p) != 37:
            return false
        st.p += 1
    elif c == 68 or c == 120:                       # D x
        return _players(&st, "%m/%d/%y")
    elif c == 84 or c == 88:                        # T X
        return _players(&st, "%H:%M:%S")
    elif c == 82:                                   # R
        return _players(&st, "%H:%M")
    elif c == 114:                                  # r
        return _players(&st, "%I:%M:%S %p")
    elif c == 70:                                   # F
        return _players(&st, "%Y-%m-%d")
    elif c == 99:                                   # c
        return _players(&st, "%a %b %e %H:%M:%S %Y")
    else:
        return false
    return true

fn _players(st: mut _P, lay: str) bool:
    i = 0
    n = len(lay)
    while i < n:
        c = lay.byte(i)
        if c == 37 and i + 1 < n:
            d = lay.byte(i + 1)
            i += 2
            if (d == 69 or d == 79) and i < n:
                d = lay.byte(i)
                i += 1
            if not _pfield(&st, d):
                return false
        elif _space(c):
            while st.p < len(st.s) and _space(st.s.byte(st.p)):
                st.p += 1
            i += 1
        else:
            if st.p >= len(st.s) or st.s.byte(st.p) != c:
                return false
            st.p += 1
            i += 1
    return true

fn parse(s: str, layout: str) float:
    return _parse(s, layout, false)

fn parse_local(s: str, layout: str) float:
    return _parse(s, layout, true)

fn _parse(s: str, lay: str, local: bool) float:
    st = _P(s, 0, 1900, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0.0, -1, false, 0, false, 0, false)
    if not _players(&st, lay) or st.p != len(s):
        return _bad(0.0, "\"" + _clip(s, 60) + "\" doesn't match the layout \"" + _clip(lay, 60) + "\"")
    _set_error("")
    if st.has_epoch:
        return float(st.epoch) + st.frac
    h = st.hour
    if st.pm >= 0 and st.h12:
        h = h % 12 + (12 if st.pm == 1 else 0)
    elif st.pm == 1 and h < 12:
        h += 12
    if st.has_off:
        return _utc_from(st.year, st.month, st.day, h, st.minute, float(st.second) + st.frac) - float(st.off)
    if local:
        return _mktime(st.year, st.month, st.day, h, st.minute, st.second) + st.frac
    return _utc_from(st.year, st.month, st.day, h, st.minute, float(st.second) + st.frac)
```

## library/std/tls.tn

```tern
# tls: encrypted connections (TLS 1.2 / 1.3, aws-lc linked statically into programs that
# import tls, built once per target by tern; nothing is linked otherwise; TERN_TLS=system
# uses the system's OpenSSL). Importing tls also turns on https:// in
# http.get / http.fetch and HTTPS serving (http.listen_tls, roost.serve_tls).
#
#   import net
#   import tls
#   c = tls.connect("example.com", 443)       # verifies the certificate and the host name
#   if not c.ok():
#       print(tls.error())                    # e.g. "tls handshake: certificate verify failed: ..."
#   c.write("GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: example.com\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n")
#   print(c.read_line())                      # every net function works on a TLS connection
#
# The result is an ordinary net.Conn: c.read / read_line / read_exact / write / close all
# encrypt and decrypt. Reads and handshakes wait like any socket wait (only the task).
#
#   tls.connect(host str, port int) net.Conn          check c.ok(); tls.error() says why not
#   tls.connect_insecure(host str, port int) net.Conn  no certificate check (tests, self-signed)
#   tls.upgrade(c net.Conn, host str) bool              start TLS on a connected socket (STARTTLS,
#                                                       PostgreSQL's SSLRequest); false: see error()
#   tls.server(cert str, key str) Server                a certificate chain and key (PEM files);
#                                                       a runtime error if they can't be loaded
#   tls.accept(c net.Conn, s Server) bool               the server side of the handshake
#   tls.version(c net.Conn) str                         "TLSv1.3" ("" for a plain connection)
#   tls.trust(ca_file str) bool                         also trust the CAs in this PEM file, for
#                                                       every verified connection (a private CA)
#   tls.error() str                                     why the last connect / upgrade / accept failed
#
# ALPN (which protocol the connection speaks, agreed in the handshake: "h2" for HTTP/2 and gRPC,
# "http/1.1"):
#   tls.set_alpn(s Server, protocols [str])             the protocols s speaks, preferred first; a
#                                                       client offering only others fails the
#                                                       handshake; one offering none gets none
#   tls.connect_alpn(host str, port int, protocols [str]) net.Conn   connect (verified), offering these
#   tls.alpn(c net.Conn) str                            the protocol agreed ("" if none, or plain)
#
# Certificates are checked against $SSL_CERT_FILE / $SSL_CERT_DIR if set, else the system's
# CA bundle (/etc/ssl/cert.pem on macOS; /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt and the like on
# Linux). Not available on wasm.

import net

struct Server:
    ctx: int

fn upgrade(c: net.Conn, host: str) bool:
    return _client(c.fd, host, true, 30000)

fn _connect(host: str, port: int, verify: bool) net.Conn:
    c = net.connect(host, port)
    if c.ok() and not _client(c.fd, host, verify, 30000):
        c.close()
        return net.Conn(-1)
    return c

fn connect(host: str, port: int) net.Conn:
    return _connect(host, port, true)

fn connect_insecure(host: str, port: int) net.Conn:
    return _connect(host, port, false)

fn server(cert: str, key: str) Server:
    return Server(_server_ctx(cert, key))

fn accept(c: net.Conn, s: Server) bool:
    return _accept(c.fd, s.ctx, 10000)

fn version(c: net.Conn) str:
    return _version(c.fd)

# ALPN's wire form: each name after its length (names of 1 to 255 bytes; others are skipped)
fn _alpn_list(protocols: [str]) str:
    out = ""
    for p in protocols:
        if len(p) > 0 and len(p) < 256:
            out += chr(len(p)) + p
    return out

fn set_alpn(s: Server, protocols: [str]):
    _alpn_server(s.ctx, _alpn_list(protocols))

fn connect_alpn(host: str, port: int, protocols: [str]) net.Conn:
    c = net.connect(host, port)
    if c.ok() and not _client_alpn(c.fd, host, true, 30000, _alpn_list(protocols)):
        c.close()
        return net.Conn(-1)
    return c

fn alpn(c: net.Conn) str:
    return _alpn(c.fd)

fn error() str:
    return net.error()

# with Result: c = tls.dial("example.com", 443)?
#   (Err: "tls: handshake: certificate verify failed: hostname mismatch")
fn dial(host: str, port: int) Result[net.Conn, str]:
    c = connect(host, port)
    if not c.ok():
        why = error()
        if why.starts_with("tls "):
            why = why[4..]
        return Err("tls: " + why)
    return Ok(c)
```

## library/std/toml/emit.tn

```tern
# toml: the parsed tree as JSON text. tagged writes scalars as toml-test wants them
# ({"type": "integer", "value": "1"}).

import simd

const _HEX = "0123456789abcdef"

fn _json_of(c: Doc, tagged: bool) str:
    out = ""
    out.reserve(len(c.text) + len(c.text) / 4 + 64)
    _emit(c, 0, &out, tagged)
    return out

# s[a..a+n] as a JSON string
fn _jstr(out: mut str, s: str, a: int, n: int):
    out += "\""
    _jbody(&out, s, a, n)
    out += "\""

# s[a..a+n] escaped for a JSON string (without its quotes)
fn _jbody(out: mut str, s: str, a: int, n: int):
    e = a + n
    q = simd.splat(34)
    bs = simd.splat(92)
    sp = simd.splat(32)
    p = a
    ls = len(s)
    while true:
        r = p
        while r < e:              # (16 at a time while s has 16 more bytes, even past e)
            if r + 16 <= ls:
                v = simd.load(s, r)
                k = simd.first_lane(simd.lt(v, sp) | simd.eq(v, q) | simd.eq(v, bs))
                r += k
                if k < 16:
                    break
            else:
                ch = s.byte(r)
                if ch < 32 or ch == 34 or ch == 92:
                    break
                r += 1
        if r > e:
            r = e
        out += s[p..r]
        if r >= e:
            break
        ch = s.byte(r)
        if ch == 34:
            out += "\\\""
        elif ch == 92:
            out += "\\\\"
        elif ch == 10:
            out += "\\n"
        elif ch == 9:
            out += "\\t"
        elif ch == 13:
            out += "\\r"
        elif ch == 8:
            out += "\\b"
        elif ch == 12:
            out += "\\f"
        else:
            out += "\\u00"
            out += _HEX[ch >> 4]
            out += _HEX[ch & 15]
        p = r + 1

# a float's text without "_" and a leading "+"
fn _float_text(out: mut str, s: str, a: int, n: int):
    p = a
    e = a + n
    if s.byte(p) == 43:
        p += 1
    u = s.find_from("_", p)
    while u >= 0 and u < e:
        out += s[p..u]
        p = u + 1
        u = s.find_from("_", p)
    out += s[p..e]

# a date-time as RFC 3339: "T" between the date and the time, "Z" in upper case
fn _date_text(out: mut str, s: str, a: int, n: int, kind: int):
    if kind == T_ODT or kind == T_LDT:
        out += s[a..a + 10]
        out += "T"
        if s.byte(a + n - 1) == 122:
            out += s[a + 11..a + n - 1]
            out += "Z"
        else:
            out += s[a + 11..a + n]
    else:
        out += s[a..a + n]

const _TYPES = ["", "string", "integer", "float", "bool", "datetime", "datetime-local", "date-local", "time-local"]

# Output is a few appends per member: the punctuation around a key or a string value is one
# literal (`,"` before a key, `":"` after one when a string follows, `","` between strings)
fn _emit(c: Doc, v: int, out: mut str, tagged: bool):
    m = c.nd[v].meta
    kind = m & 255
    if kind == T_TAB or kind == T_ARR:
        tab = kind == T_TAB
        if c.nd[v].val == 0:
            out += "{}" if tab else "[]"
            return
        x = c.nd[v].val & LO
        first = true
        q = false                 # the last value was a string: its closing quote is to come
        while x != 0:
            sv = not tagged and c.nd[x].meta & 255 == T_STR
            if tab:
                out += "{\"" if first else "\",\"" if q else ",\""
                k = c.nd[x].key
                _jbody(&out, c.buf, k & LO, k >>> 32)
                out += "\":\"" if sv else "\":"
            elif sv:
                out += "[\"" if first else "\",\"" if q else ",\""
            else:
                out += "[" if first else "\"," if q else ","
            if sv:
                val = c.nd[x].val
                _jbody(&out, c.buf, val & LO, val >>> 32)
            else:
                _emit(c, x, &out, tagged)
            q = sv
            first = false
            x = c.nd[x].meta >>> 32
        if tab:
            out += "\"}" if q else "}"
        else:
            out += "\"]" if q else "]"
        return
    val = c.nd[v].val
    if tagged:
        out += "{\"type\":\""
        out += _TYPES[kind]
        out += "\",\"value\":"
        if kind == T_STR:
            _scalar(c, &out, kind, val, true)
        else:
            out += "\""
            _scalar(c, &out, kind, val, true)
            out += "\""
        out += "}"
        return
    _scalar(c, &out, kind, val, false)

fn _scalar(c: Doc, out: mut str, kind: int, val: int, tagged: bool):
    a = val & LO
    n = val >>> 32
    if kind == T_STR:
        _jstr(&out, c.buf, a, n)
    elif kind == T_INT:
        out += str(val)
    elif kind == T_BOOL:
        out += "true" if val == 1 else "false"
    elif kind == T_FLOAT:
        last = c.buf.byte(a + n - 1)
        if last == 110:                     # nan
            out += "nan" if tagged else "null"
        elif last == 102:                   # inf: JSON has none, so a number too big for a double
            neg = c.buf.byte(a) == 45
            if tagged:
                out += "-inf" if neg else "inf"
            else:
                out += "-1e999" if neg else "1e999"
        else:
            _float_text(&out, c.buf, a, n)
    elif tagged:
        _date_text(&out, c.buf, a, n, kind)
    else:
        out += "\""
        _date_text(&out, c.buf, a, n, kind)
        out += "\""
```

## library/std/toml/parse.tn

```tern
# toml: the parser. TOML 1.0 (https://toml.io/en/v1.0.0) in one pass into a tree of nodes
# held in one [Node] (a node is an index: no allocation per value), then written out as JSON
# (emit.tn) for the json module's decoders and Value. A table's members are a list in the
# order written; a table with more than SMALL of them is also in a hash index shared by the
# whole document.
#
# Text is never copied: values and keys are offsets into buf, which is the text itself until a
# string with escapes has to be decoded somewhere (it is appended to buf, past the text).

import binary
import simd

const T_STR = 1
const T_INT = 2
const T_FLOAT = 3
const T_BOOL = 4
const T_ODT = 5               # an offset date-time, a local one, a local date, a local time
const T_LDT = 6
const T_LD = 7
const T_LT = 8
const T_ARR = 9
const T_TAB = 10

const F_EXPLICIT = 1 << 8     # a [table] header made it (or it is the root)
const F_DOTTED = 2 << 8       # made by a dotted key
const F_INLINE = 4 << 8       # an inline table (or inside one): closed
const F_AOT = 8 << 8          # an array of tables
const F_INDEXED = 16 << 8     # a table whose members are in the hash index

const LO = 0xffffffff
const MAX_KEYS = 128
const SMALL = 8               # tables up to this many members aren't indexed

struct Node:
    meta: int                 # kind | flags | next << 32: the next member of its table or
                              # array (0: none. The root, node 0, is no one's member)
    val: int                  # string, float, date: offset | length << 32 in buf; int: its
                              # value; bool: 0 or 1; table, array: first | last << 32 member
                              # (0: none)
    key: int                  # a table member's key: offset | length << 32 in buf

struct Doc:
    text: str
    buf: str                  # text, then decoded strings
    p: int
    e: int
    err: str
    errat: int                # where err is (-1: no error)
    depth: int
    nd: [Node]                # node 0 is the root table
    ht: [int]                 # (table, key) -> node + 1, open addressing, made when a table
                              # first needs it; hp: the slot's table
    hp: [int]
    hn: int
    ks: [int]                 # the key just read, a part at a time
    nks: int
    ksat: int
    cur: int                  # the table key = value lines go into

fn _doc(text: str) Doc:
    return Doc(text, text, 0, len(text), "", -1, 0, [], [], [], 0, [0] * 8, 0, 0, 0)

# the first error is kept; every function returns as soon as err is set
fn _fail(c: mut Doc, at: int, msg: str):
    if c.errat < 0:
        c.err = msg
        c.errat = at

fn _fail_here(c: mut Doc, msg: str):
    at = c.p
    _fail(&c, at, msg)

fn _fail_key(c: mut Doc, msg: str):
    at = c.ksat
    _fail(&c, at, msg)

fn _new(c: mut Doc, kind: int, key: int) int:
    n = len(c.nd)
    c.nd.push(Node(kind, 0, key))
    return n

fn _new_val(c: mut Doc, kind: int, key: int, val: int) int:
    n = len(c.nd)
    c.nd.push(Node(kind, val, key))
    return n

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- tables

fn _hash(c: Doc, t: int, k: int) int:
    a = k & LO
    n = k >>> 32
    h = (0xcbf2_9ce4_8422_2325 ^ n) + t * 0x9e37_79b9_7f4a_7c15
    for i in a..a + n:
        h = (h ^ c.buf.byte(i)) * 0x100_0000_01b3
    return h ^ (h >>> 29)

fn _same(c: Doc, k1: int, k2: int) bool:
    n = k1 >>> 32
    if n != k2 >>> 32:
        return false
    a = k1 & LO
    b = k2 & LO
    t = c.buf
    if n >= 8:                    # 8 bytes at a time, the last 8 overlapping
        i = 0
        while i + 8 < n:
            if binary.u64le(t, a + i) != binary.u64le(t, b + i):
                return false
            i += 8
        return binary.u64le(t, a + n - 8) == binary.u64le(t, b + n - 8)
    if n >= 4:
        return binary.u32le(t, a) == binary.u32le(t, b) and binary.u32le(t, a + n - 4) == binary.u32le(t, b + n - 4)
    for i in 0..n:
        if t.byte(a + i) != t.byte(b + i):
            return false
    return true

# table t's member named k, or (none) -1 - the number of members it has if it isn't indexed:
# _put's miss. A small table is a scan of its members; one past SMALL members is also in the
# hash index (F_INDEXED)
fn _get(c: Doc, t: int, k: int) int:
    if c.nd[t].meta & F_INDEXED == 0:
        x = c.nd[t].val & LO
        if x == 0:
            return -1
        n = 1
        while true:
            kx = c.nd[x].key
            if kx == k or _same(c, kx, k):
                return x
            x = c.nd[x].meta >>> 32
            if x == 0:
                return -1 - n
            n += 1
    hm = len(c.ht) - 1
    s = _hash(c, t, k) & hm
    while c.ht[s] != 0:
        v = c.ht[s] - 1
        if c.hp[s] == t and _same(c, c.nd[v].key, k):
            return v
        s = (s + 1) & hm
    return -1

fn _slot(c: mut Doc, t: int, v: int):
    m = len(c.ht) - 1
    s = _hash(c, t, c.nd[v].key) & m
    while c.ht[s] != 0:
        s = (s + 1) & m
    c.ht[s] = v + 1
    c.hp[s] = t

fn _grow(c: mut Doc):
    old = c.ht
    oldp = c.hp
    n = max(64, len(old) * 2)
    c.ht = [0] * n
    c.hp = [0] * n
    for i in 0..len(old):
        if old[i] != 0:
            _slot(&c, oldp[i], old[i] - 1)

# a member at the end of table or array a
fn _link(c: mut Doc, a: int, v: int):
    x = c.nd[a].val
    if x == 0:
        c.nd[a].val = v | (v << 32)
    else:
        l = x >>> 32
        c.nd[l].meta = c.nd[l].meta | (v << 32)
        c.nd[a].val = (x & LO) | (v << 32)

fn _index(c: mut Doc, t: int, v: int):
    c.hn += 1
    if c.hn * 2 > len(c.ht):
        _grow(&c)
    _slot(&c, t, v)

# node v (made with its key) into table t, where _get(t, its key) gave miss
fn _put(c: mut Doc, t: int, v: int, miss: int):
    _link(&c, t, v)
    m = c.nd[t].meta
    if m & F_INDEXED != 0:
        _index(&c, t, v)
    elif -miss > SMALL:
        c.nd[t].meta = m | F_INDEXED
        x = c.nd[t].val & LO
        while x != 0:
            _index(&c, t, x)
            x = c.nd[x].meta >>> 32

fn _last(c: Doc, a: int) int:
    return c.nd[a].val >>> 32

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- text

# TOML text must be UTF-8 (no overlong forms, surrogates or code points past U+10FFFF);
# the offset of the first bad byte, or -1
fn _bad_utf8(s: str) int:
    hi = simd.splat(128)
    e = len(s)
    p = 0
    while p < e:
        if p + 64 <= e and not simd.any((simd.load(s, p) | simd.load(s, p + 16) | simd.load(s, p + 32) | simd.load(s, p + 48)) & hi):
            p += 64
            continue
        if p + 16 <= e and not simd.any(simd.load(s, p) & hi):
            p += 16
            continue
        b = s.byte(p)
        if b < 128:
            p += 1
            continue
        n = 3 if b >= 0xf0 else 2 if b >= 0xe0 else 1 if b >= 0xc2 else -1
        if n < 0 or b > 0xf4 or e - p <= n:
            return p
        cp = b & (0x3f >> n)
        for i in 1..n + 1:
            x = s.byte(p + i)
            if x & 0xc0 != 0x80:
                return p
            cp = (cp << 6) | (x & 0x3f)
        if (n == 2 and cp < 0x800) or (n == 3 and (cp < 0x10000 or cp > 0x10ffff)) or (cp >= 0xd800 and cp <= 0xdfff):
            return p
        p += n + 1
    return -1

fn _ws(c: mut Doc):
    p = c.p
    while p < c.e:
        ch = c.text.byte(p)
        if ch != 32 and ch != 9:
            break
        p += 1
    c.p = p

# a comment: "#" to the end of the line, with no control characters but tab
fn _comment(c: mut Doc):
    if c.p >= c.e or c.text.byte(c.p) != 35:
        return
    p = c.p + 1
    e = c.e
    while p < e:
        ch = c.text.byte(p)
        if ch == 10:
            break
        if (ch < 32 and ch != 9 and not (ch == 13 and p + 1 < e and c.text.byte(p + 1) == 10)) or ch == 127:
            _fail(&c, p, "control character in a comment")
            return
        p += 1
    c.p = p

# the end of a line (or of the text); false if something else is there
fn _eol(c: mut Doc) bool:
    if c.p >= c.e:
        return true
    ch = c.text.byte(c.p)
    if ch == 10:
        c.p += 1
        return true
    if ch == 13 and c.p + 1 < c.e and c.text.byte(c.p + 1) == 10:
        c.p += 2
        return true
    return false

# blank lines and comments inside an array
fn _ws_nl(c: mut Doc):
    while true:
        _ws(&c)
        _comment(&c)
        if c.errat >= 0:
            return
        if c.p < c.e and (c.text.byte(c.p) == 10 or c.text.byte(c.p) == 13):
            if not _eol(&c):
                _fail_here(&c, "a carriage return must be followed by a newline")
                return
            continue
        return

fn _utf8(c: mut Doc, cp: int):
    if cp < 0x80:
        c.buf += chr(cp)
    elif cp < 0x800:
        c.buf += chr(0xc0 | (cp >> 6))
        c.buf += chr(0x80 | (cp & 0x3f))
    elif cp < 0x10000:
        c.buf += chr(0xe0 | (cp >> 12))
        c.buf += chr(0x80 | ((cp >> 6) & 0x3f))
        c.buf += chr(0x80 | (cp & 0x3f))
    else:
        c.buf += chr(0xf0 | (cp >> 18))
        c.buf += chr(0x80 | ((cp >> 12) & 0x3f))
        c.buf += chr(0x80 | ((cp >> 6) & 0x3f))
        c.buf += chr(0x80 | (cp & 0x3f))

fn _hexval(ch: int) int:
    if ch >= 48 and ch <= 57:
        return ch - 48
    l = ch | 32
    if l >= 97 and l <= 102:
        return l - 87
    return -1

# where the run of plain bytes from p ends: the first control byte, DEL, backslash or quote q
fn _plain_end(s: str, p0: int, e: int, q: int) int:
    p = p0
    sp = simd.splat(32)
    qq = simd.splat(q)
    bs = simd.splat(92)
    del = simd.splat(127)
    while p + 16 <= e:
        v = simd.load(s, p)
        k = simd.first_lane(simd.lt(v, sp) | simd.eq(v, qq) | simd.eq(v, bs) | simd.eq(v, del))
        if k < 16:
            return p + k
        p += 16
    while p < e:
        ch = s.byte(p)
        if ch < 32 or ch == q or ch == 92 or ch == 127:
            return p
        p += 1
    return e

# The string at c.p (its opening quote), decoded: offset | length << 32 in buf. Basic strings
# ("...", """...""") take escapes; literal ones ('...', '''...''') don't. Multi-line ones
# can't be keys. Decoding (into buf) starts only once an escape needs it.
fn _string(c: mut Doc, key: bool) int:
    p = c.p
    e = c.e
    q = c.text.byte(p)
    multi = e - p >= 3 and c.text.byte(p + 1) == q and c.text.byte(p + 2) == q
    if multi and key:
        _fail(&c, p, "a multi-line string can't be a key")
        return 0
    p += 3 if multi else 1
    if multi:                     # a newline right after the quotes isn't part of it
        if p < e and c.text.byte(p) == 10:
            p += 1
        elif e - p >= 2 and c.text.byte(p) == 13 and c.text.byte(p + 1) == 10:
            p += 2
    start = p
    w = -1                        # where the decoded copy starts in buf (-1: none yet)
    run = p                       # (decoding: the plain bytes from run are still to be copied)
    while true:
        p = _plain_end(c.text, p, e, q)
        if p >= e:
            _fail_here(&c, "unterminated multi-line string" if multi else "unterminated string")
            return 0
        ch = c.text.byte(p)
        if ch == q:
            if not multi:
                break
            if e - p >= 3 and c.text.byte(p + 1) == q and c.text.byte(p + 2) == q:
                extra = 0             # up to two more quotes belong to the string
                while extra < 3 and p + 3 + extra < e and c.text.byte(p + 3 + extra) == q:
                    extra += 1
                if extra > 2:
                    _fail(&c, p, "too many quotes at the end of a multi-line string")
                    return 0
                p += extra
                break
            p += 1
            continue
        if ch == 92 and q == 34:
            if w < 0:
                w = len(c.buf)
            c.buf += c.text[run..p]
            p += 1
            if p >= e:
                _fail(&c, p, "unterminated string")
                return 0
            x = c.text.byte(p)
            p += 1
            if x == 98:
                c.buf += "\x08"
            elif x == 116:
                c.buf += "\t"
            elif x == 110:
                c.buf += "\n"
            elif x == 102:
                c.buf += "\x0c"
            elif x == 114:
                c.buf += "\r"
            elif x == 34:
                c.buf += "\""
            elif x == 92:
                c.buf += "\\"
            elif x == 117 or x == 85:
                nd = 4 if x == 117 else 8
                if e - p < nd:
                    _fail(&c, p - 2, "bad \\u escape")
                    return 0
                cp = 0
                for i in 0..nd:
                    h = _hexval(c.text.byte(p + i))
                    if h < 0:
                        _fail(&c, p - 2, "bad \\u escape")
                        return 0
                    cp = (cp << 4) | h
                if cp > 0x10ffff or (cp >= 0xd800 and cp <= 0xdfff):
                    _fail(&c, p - 2, "\\u escape isn't a Unicode scalar value")
                    return 0
                p += nd
                _utf8(&c, cp)
            elif multi and (x == 32 or x == 9 or x == 10 or x == 13):
                # a line ending backslash: the newline and the whitespace after it go
                b = p - 1
                while b < e and (c.text.byte(b) == 32 or c.text.byte(b) == 9):
                    b += 1
                if b + 1 < e and c.text.byte(b) == 13 and c.text.byte(b + 1) == 10:
                    b += 1
                if b >= e or c.text.byte(b) != 10:
                    _fail(&c, p - 2, "a \\ before spaces must end the line")
                    return 0
                while b < e:
                    y = c.text.byte(b)
                    if y == 32 or y == 9 or y == 10 or (y == 13 and b + 1 < e and c.text.byte(b + 1) == 10):
                        b += 1
                    else:
                        break
                p = b
            else:
                _fail(&c, p - 2, "unknown escape")
                return 0
            run = p
            continue
        if ch == 10 or ch == 13:
            if not multi:
                _fail(&c, p, "newline in a single-line string")
                return 0
            if ch == 13 and not (p + 1 < e and c.text.byte(p + 1) == 10):
                _fail(&c, p, "a carriage return must be followed by a newline")
                return 0
        elif (ch < 32 and ch != 9) or ch == 127:
            _fail(&c, p, "control character in a string")
            return 0
        p += 1
    c.p = p + (3 if multi else 1)
    if w < 0:
        return start | ((p - start) << 32)
    c.buf += c.text[run..p]
    return w | ((len(c.buf) - w) << 32)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- keys

fn _bare(ch: int) bool:
    l = ch | 32
    return (l >= 97 and l <= 122) or (ch >= 48 and ch <= 57) or ch == 95 or ch == 45

# where the run of bare key bytes (A-Za-z0-9_-) from p ends
fn _bare_end(t: str, p0: int, e: int) int:
    p = p0
    a = simd.splat(97)
    z = simd.splat(25)
    zero = simd.splat(48)
    nine = simd.splat(9)
    us = simd.splat(95)
    dash = simd.splat(45)
    sp = simd.splat(32)
    while p + 16 <= e:
        v = simd.load(t, p)
        bare = simd.le((v | sp) - a, z) | simd.le(v - zero, nine) | simd.eq(v, us) | simd.eq(v, dash)
        k = simd.first_lane(~bare)
        if k < 16:
            return p + k
        p += 16
    while p < e and _bare(t.byte(p)):
        p += 1
    return p

# a key (dotted: several parts) into c.ks
fn _key(c: mut Doc):
    c.nks = 0
    c.ksat = c.p
    while true:
        if c.nks == len(c.ks):
            if c.nks == MAX_KEYS:
                _fail_here(&c, "key has too many parts")
                return
            c.ks.extend([0] * c.nks)
        ch = c.text.byte(c.p) if c.p < c.e else 0
        if ch == 34 or ch == 39:
            k = _string(&c, true)
            if c.errat >= 0:
                return
            c.ks[c.nks] = k
        else:
            s = c.p
            p = _bare_end(c.text, s, c.e)
            if p == s:
                _fail(&c, s, "expected a key")
                return
            c.p = p
            c.ks[c.nks] = s | ((p - s) << 32)
        c.nks += 1
        _ws(&c)
        if c.p < c.e and c.text.byte(c.p) == 46:
            c.p += 1
            _ws(&c)
            continue
        return

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- values

fn _digit(ch: int) bool:
    return ch >= 48 and ch <= 57

fn _num2(c: mut Doc, p: int) int:
    a = c.text.byte(p)
    b = c.text.byte(p + 1)
    if not _digit(a) or not _digit(b):
        _fail(&c, p, "bad date or time")
        return 0
    return (a - 48) * 10 + b - 48

# HH:MM:SS(.frac)? at p; returns its end
fn _time(c: mut Doc, p0: int) int:
    p = p0
    if c.e - p < 8 or c.text.byte(p + 2) != 58 or c.text.byte(p + 5) != 58:
        _fail(&c, p, "bad time (HH:MM:SS)")
        return c.e
    h = _num2(&c, p)
    m = _num2(&c, p + 3)
    s = _num2(&c, p + 6)
    if c.errat >= 0:
        return c.e
    if h > 23 or m > 59 or s > 60:
        _fail(&c, p, "time out of range")
        return c.e
    p += 8
    if p < c.e and c.text.byte(p) == 46:
        p += 1
        if p >= c.e or not _digit(c.text.byte(p)):
            _fail(&c, p, "bad fraction of a second")
            return c.e
        while p < c.e and _digit(c.text.byte(p)):
            p += 1
    return p

fn _leap(y: int) bool:
    return (y % 4 == 0 and y % 100 != 0) or y % 400 == 0

fn _mdays(m: int, y: int) int:
    if m == 2:
        return 29 if _leap(y) else 28
    if m == 4 or m == 6 or m == 9 or m == 11:
        return 30
    return 31

# a date, a time, or a date and time (with an offset or without) at c.p, into node v (new:
# its meta is only its kind)
fn _datetime(c: mut Doc, v: int):
    p = c.p
    s = p
    t = c.text
    if c.e - p >= 3 and t.byte(p + 2) == 58:
        p = _time(&c, p)
        if c.errat >= 0:
            return
        c.nd[v].meta = T_LT
        c.nd[v].val = s | ((p - s) << 32)
        c.p = p
        return
    if c.e - p < 10 or t.byte(p + 4) != 45 or t.byte(p + 7) != 45:
        _fail(&c, p, "bad date (YYYY-MM-DD)")
        return
    for i in 0..4:
        if not _digit(t.byte(p + i)):
            _fail(&c, p, "bad date (YYYY-MM-DD)")
            return
    y = (t.byte(p) - 48) * 1000 + (t.byte(p + 1) - 48) * 100 + (t.byte(p + 2) - 48) * 10 + t.byte(p + 3) - 48
    mo = _num2(&c, p + 5)
    d = _num2(&c, p + 8)
    if c.errat >= 0:
        return
    if mo < 1 or mo > 12 or d < 1 or d > _mdays(mo, y):
        _fail(&c, p, "date out of range")
        return
    p += 10
    sep = false
    if p < c.e:
        ch = t.byte(p)
        sep = ch == 84 or ch == 116 or (ch == 32 and p + 1 < c.e and _digit(t.byte(p + 1)))
    if not sep:
        c.nd[v].meta = T_LD
        c.nd[v].val = s | (10 << 32)
        c.p = p
        return
    p = _time(&c, p + 1)
    if c.errat >= 0:
        return
    kind = T_LDT
    if p < c.e and (t.byte(p) == 90 or t.byte(p) == 122):
        p += 1
        kind = T_ODT
    elif p < c.e and (t.byte(p) == 43 or t.byte(p) == 45):
        if c.e - p < 6 or t.byte(p + 3) != 58:
            _fail(&c, p, "bad offset (+HH:MM)")
            return
        oh = _num2(&c, p + 1)
        om = _num2(&c, p + 4)
        if c.errat >= 0:
            return
        if oh > 23 or om > 59:
            _fail(&c, p, "offset out of range")
            return
        p += 6
        kind = T_ODT
    c.nd[v].meta = kind              # (emit writes it as RFC 3339: "T" and "Z" in upper case)
    c.nd[v].val = s | ((p - s) << 32)
    c.p = p

fn _is_digit_of(ch: int, base: int) bool:
    if base == 16:
        return _hexval(ch) >= 0
    return ch >= 48 and ch < 48 + base

# digits of a base with "_" only between digits; returns the end (any: whether there was one)
fn _digits(c: mut Doc, p0: int, base: int, any: mut bool) int:
    p = p0
    s = p
    any = false
    while p < c.e:
        ch = c.text.byte(p)
        if _is_digit_of(ch, base):
            any = true
            p += 1
            continue
        if ch == 95:
            if p == s or c.text.byte(p - 1) == 95 or p + 1 >= c.e or not _is_digit_of(c.text.byte(p + 1), base):
                _fail(&c, p, "\"_\" must be between digits")
                return c.e
            p += 1
            continue
        break
    return p

fn _number(c: mut Doc, v: int):
    p = c.p
    s = p
    e = c.e
    t = c.text
    neg = false
    sign = false
    any = false
    ch = t.byte(p)
    if ch == 43 or ch == 45:
        neg = ch == 45
        sign = true
        p += 1
    if e - p >= 3 and (t.byte(p) == 105 or t.byte(p) == 110) and (t[p..p + 3] == "inf" or t[p..p + 3] == "nan"):
        c.nd[v].meta = T_FLOAT       # (the text: emit knows inf and nan by their last byte)
        c.nd[v].val = s | ((p + 3 - s) << 32)
        c.p = p + 3
        return
    if not sign and e - p >= 2 and t.byte(p) == 48 and (t.byte(p + 1) == 120 or t.byte(p + 1) == 111 or t.byte(p + 1) == 98):
        b1 = t.byte(p + 1)
        base = 16 if b1 == 120 else 8 if b1 == 111 else 2
        d0 = p + 2
        d1 = _digits(&c, d0, base, &any)
        if c.errat >= 0:
            return
        if not any or t.byte(d0) == 95:
            _fail(&c, s, "expected digits after 0x, 0o or 0b")
            return
        x = 0
        for q in d0..d1:
            dc = t.byte(q)
            if dc == 95:
                continue
            dv = _hexval(dc)
            if x > (0x7fff_ffff_ffff_ffff - dv) / base:
                _fail(&c, s, "integer too big for 64 bits")
                return
            x = x * base + dv
        c.nd[v].meta = T_INT
        c.nd[v].val = x
        c.p = d1
        return
    if p >= e or not _digit(t.byte(p)):
        _fail(&c, s, "expected a value")
        return
    i0 = p
    i1 = _digits(&c, p, 10, &any)
    if c.errat >= 0:
        return
    if t.byte(i0) == 48 and i1 - i0 > 1:
        _fail(&c, s, "leading zeros aren't allowed")
        return
    p = i1
    flt = false
    if p < e and t.byte(p) == 46:
        flt = true
        if p + 1 >= e or not _digit(t.byte(p + 1)):
            _fail(&c, p, "expected digits after \".\"")
            return
        p = _digits(&c, p + 1, 10, &any)
        if c.errat >= 0:
            return
    if p < e and (t.byte(p) == 101 or t.byte(p) == 69):
        flt = true
        p += 1
        if p < e and (t.byte(p) == 43 or t.byte(p) == 45):
            p += 1
        if p >= e or not _digit(t.byte(p)):
            _fail(&c, p, "expected digits in the exponent")
            return
        p = _digits(&c, p, 10, &any)
        if c.errat >= 0:
            return
    if flt:
        c.nd[v].meta = T_FLOAT       # (emit drops "_" and a leading "+")
        c.nd[v].val = s | ((p - s) << 32)
        c.p = p
        return
    # an integer must fit in 64 bits: built negative, where there is room for the smallest
    x = 0
    for q in i0..i1:
        dc = t.byte(q)
        if dc == 95:
            continue
        d = dc - 48
        if x < -922_3372_0368_5477_580 or (x == -922_3372_0368_5477_580 and d > 8):
            _fail(&c, s, "integer too big for 64 bits")
            return
        x = x * 10 - d
    if not neg:
        if x == -0x7fff_ffff_ffff_ffff - 1:
            _fail(&c, s, "integer too big for 64 bits")
            return
        x = -x
    c.nd[v].meta = T_INT
    c.nd[v].val = x
    c.p = p

fn _freeze(c: mut Doc, t: int):
    c.nd[t].meta = c.nd[t].meta | F_INLINE
    if c.nd[t].val == 0:
        return
    m = c.nd[t].val & LO
    while m != 0:
        if c.nd[m].meta & 255 == T_TAB:
            _freeze(&c, m)
        m = c.nd[m].meta >>> 32

# a value, as a node with key k (0: an array's element)
fn _value(c: mut Doc, k: int) int:
    p = c.p
    e = c.e
    if p >= e:
        _fail(&c, p, "expected a value")
        return 0
    c.depth += 1
    if c.depth > 1000:
        _fail(&c, p, "nested too deeply")
        return 0
    v = 0
    ch = c.text.byte(p)
    if ch == 34 or ch == 39:
        sv = _string(&c, false)
        if c.errat >= 0:
            return 0
        v = _new_val(&c, T_STR, k, sv)
    elif ch == 116 and e - p >= 4 and binary.u32le(c.text, p) == 0x6575_7274:          # true
        v = _new_val(&c, T_BOOL, k, 1)
        c.p += 4
    elif ch == 102 and e - p >= 5 and binary.u32le(c.text, p + 1) == 0x6573_6c61:      # (f)alse
        v = _new(&c, T_BOOL, k)
        c.p += 5
    elif ch == 91:
        v = _new(&c, T_ARR, k)
        c.p += 1
        while true:
            _ws_nl(&c)
            if c.errat >= 0:
                return 0
            if c.p < e and c.text.byte(c.p) == 93:
                c.p += 1
                break
            x = _value(&c, 0)
            if c.errat >= 0:
                return 0
            _link(&c, v, x)
            _ws_nl(&c)
            if c.errat >= 0:
                return 0
            if c.p < e and c.text.byte(c.p) == 44:
                c.p += 1
                continue
            if c.p < e and c.text.byte(c.p) == 93:
                c.p += 1
                break
            _fail_here(&c, "expected \",\" or \"]\" in an array")
            return 0
    elif ch == 123:
        v = _new(&c, T_TAB, k)
        c.p += 1
        _ws(&c)
        if c.p < e and c.text.byte(c.p) == 125:
            c.p += 1
        else:
            while true:
                if c.p < e and (c.text.byte(c.p) == 10 or c.text.byte(c.p) == 13):
                    _fail_here(&c, "an inline table must be on one line")
                    return 0
                _keyval(&c, v)
                if c.errat >= 0:
                    return 0
                _ws(&c)
                if c.p < e and c.text.byte(c.p) == 44:
                    c.p += 1
                    _ws(&c)
                    if c.p < e and c.text.byte(c.p) == 125:
                        _fail_here(&c, "no \",\" after an inline table's last pair")
                        return 0
                    continue
                if c.p < e and c.text.byte(c.p) == 125:
                    c.p += 1
                    break
                _fail_here(&c, "expected \",\" or \"}\" in an inline table (all on one line)")
                return 0
        _freeze(&c, v)
    elif _digit(ch) or ch == 43 or ch == 45 or ch == 105 or ch == 110:
        v = _new(&c, T_INT, k)
        # a date (YYYY-) or a time (HH:)
        if e - p >= 5 and _digit(ch) and _digit(c.text.byte(p + 1)) and ((_digit(c.text.byte(p + 2)) and _digit(c.text.byte(p + 3)) and c.text.byte(p + 4) == 45) or c.text.byte(p + 2) == 58):
            _datetime(&c, v)
        else:
            _number(&c, v)
        if c.errat >= 0:
            return 0
    else:
        _fail(&c, p, "expected a value")
        return 0
    c.depth -= 1
    return v

fn _is_table(c: Doc, x: int) bool:
    return c.nd[x].meta & 255 == T_TAB

# key = value into table t (dotted keys make tables on the way)
fn _keyval(c: mut Doc, t0: int):
    t = t0
    _key(&c)
    if c.errat >= 0:
        return
    if c.p >= c.e or c.text.byte(c.p) != 61:
        _fail_here(&c, "expected \"=\" after a key")
        return
    c.p += 1
    _ws(&c)
    for i in 0..c.nks - 1:
        ki = c.ks[i]
        x = _get(c, t, ki)
        if x < 0:
            miss = x
            x = _new(&c, T_TAB | F_DOTTED, ki)
            _put(&c, t, x, miss)
        elif not _is_table(c, x):
            _fail_key(&c, "key already has a value that isn't a table")
            return
        elif c.nd[x].meta & F_INLINE != 0:
            _fail_key(&c, "an inline table can't be added to")
            return
        elif c.nd[x].meta & F_EXPLICIT != 0:
            _fail_key(&c, "a [table] can't be added to with dotted keys")
            return
        t = x
    k = c.ks[c.nks - 1]
    miss = _get(c, t, k)
    if miss >= 0:
        _fail_key(&c, "key defined twice")
        return
    v = _value(&c, k)
    if c.errat >= 0:
        return
    _put(&c, t, v, miss)

# [a.b.c] and [[a.b.c]]
fn _header(c: mut Doc):
    aot = c.e - c.p >= 2 and c.text.byte(c.p + 1) == 91
    c.p += 2 if aot else 1
    _ws(&c)
    _key(&c)
    if c.errat >= 0:
        return
    if aot:
        if c.e - c.p < 2 or c.text.byte(c.p) != 93 or c.text.byte(c.p + 1) != 93:
            _fail_here(&c, "expected \"]]\"")
            return
        c.p += 2
    else:
        if c.p >= c.e or c.text.byte(c.p) != 93:
            _fail_here(&c, "expected \"]\"")
            return
        c.p += 1
    t = 0
    for i in 0..c.nks - 1:
        ki = c.ks[i]
        x = _get(c, t, ki)
        if x < 0:
            miss = x
            x = _new(&c, T_TAB, ki)
            _put(&c, t, x, miss)
        elif c.nd[x].meta & 255 == T_ARR and c.nd[x].meta & F_AOT != 0:
            x = _last(c, x)
        elif not _is_table(c, x) or c.nd[x].meta & F_INLINE != 0:
            _fail_key(&c, "key already has a value that isn't a table")
            return
        t = x
    k = c.ks[c.nks - 1]
    x = _get(c, t, k)
    if aot:
        if x < 0:
            miss = x
            x = _new(&c, T_ARR | F_AOT, k)
            _put(&c, t, x, miss)
        elif c.nd[x].meta & 255 != T_ARR or c.nd[x].meta & F_AOT == 0:
            _fail_key(&c, "key already has a value that isn't an array of tables")
            return
        n = _new(&c, T_TAB | F_EXPLICIT, 0)
        _link(&c, x, n)
        c.cur = n
        return
    if x < 0:
        miss = x
        x = _new(&c, T_TAB, k)
        _put(&c, t, x, miss)
    else:
        m = c.nd[x].meta
        if m & 255 != T_TAB:
            _fail_key(&c, "key already has a value that isn't a table")
            return
        if m & F_DOTTED != 0:
            _fail_key(&c, "table already made by dotted keys")
            return
        if m & F_INLINE != 0:
            _fail_key(&c, "an inline table can't be added to")
            return
        if m & F_EXPLICIT != 0:
            _fail_key(&c, "table defined twice")
            return
    c.nd[x].meta = c.nd[x].meta | F_EXPLICIT
    c.cur = x

fn _document(c: mut Doc):
    while c.p < c.e:
        _ws(&c)
        if c.p >= c.e:
            break
        ch = c.text.byte(c.p)
        if ch == 91:
            _header(&c)
        elif ch != 35 and ch != 10 and ch != 13:
            cur = c.cur
            _keyval(&c, cur)
        if c.errat >= 0:
            return
        _ws(&c)
        _comment(&c)
        if c.errat >= 0:
            return
        if not _eol(&c):
            _fail_here(&c, "expected the end of the line")
            return

# "line N: msg" for an error at offset at
fn _error(text: str, at: int, msg: str) str:
    line = 1
    i = text.find_from("\n", 0)
    while i >= 0 and i < at:
        line += 1
        i = text.find_from("\n", i + 1)
    return f"line {line}: {msg}"

# the text parsed; the root is node 0
fn _parse(text: str) Result[Doc, str]:
    bad = _bad_utf8(text)
    if bad >= 0:
        return Err(_error(text, bad, "not valid UTF-8"))
    c = _doc(text)
    if len(text) >= 3 and text[..3] == "\xef\xbb\xbf":     # a byte order mark
        c.p = 3
    _new(&c, T_TAB | F_EXPLICIT, 0)
    _document(&c)
    if c.errat >= 0:
        return Err(_error(text, c.errat, c.err))
    return Ok(c)
```

## library/std/toml/toml.tn

```tern
# toml: TOML 1.0 (config files) into a struct or a json.Value, and structs back to TOML.
#
#   import toml
#   struct Server:
#       host: str
#       port: int
#   struct Config:
#       name: str
#       server: Server
#       tags: [str]
#   cfg = Config("app", Server("localhost", 8080), [])    # defaults: keys the file leaves out keep them
#   toml.decode(fs.read("app.toml"), &cfg)?               # Err("toml: line 3: key defined twice")
#   v = toml.parse(text)?                                 # a json.Value: v.field("server").field("port").int_or(80)
```
