```tern
# the length of one whole RESP reply at s[p..] (0: not all here yet, -1: not RESP)
fn _resp_len(s: str, p: int, depth: int) int:
    n = len(s) - p
    if n < 3:
        return 0
    if depth > 32:
        return -1
    e = p
    while e < len(s) and s.byte(e) != 10:
        e += 1
    if e == len(s):
        return 0
    line = e + 1 - p
    k = s.byte(p)
    if k == 43 or k == 45 or k == 58 or k == 95 or k == 44 or k == 35 or k == 40:     # + - : _ , # (
        return line
    v = _num(s, p + 1, e)
    if k == 36 or k == 33 or k == 61:           # $ ! =: a length, then that many bytes
        if v < 0:
            return line
        return 0 if n < line + v + 2 else line + v + 2
    if k == 42 or k == 126 or k == 62 or k == 37:   # * ~ > %: that many replies (% pairs)
        if v < 0:
            return line
        if k == 37:
            v *= 2
        off = line
        for i in 0..v:
            r = _resp_len(s, p + off, depth + 1)
            if r <= 0:
                return r
            off += r
        return off
    return -1

fn _crlf(s: str, i: int) int:                   # where "\r\n" is, from i on (-1: nowhere)
    k = i
    while k + 1 < len(s):
        if s.byte(k) == 13 and s.byte(k + 1) == 10:
            return k
        k += 1
    return -1

fn _num(s: str, i: int, e: int) int:            # the integer in s[i..e] ("\r" ends it)
    neg = i < e and s.byte(i) == 45
    k = i + 1 if neg else i
    v = 0
    while k < e and s.byte(k) >= 48 and s.byte(k) <= 57:
        v = v * 10 + s.byte(k) - 48
        k += 1
    return -v if neg else v

# why the last call failed: the calling task's own (task.local_set)
fn _set_error(msg: str):
    if msg != "" or task.local_get("redis.error") != "":
        task.local_set("redis.error", msg)

fn error() str:
    return task.local_get("redis.error")

fn _lost(n: int, why: str) [Reply]:
    out: [Reply] = []
    for i in 0..n:
        out.push(Reply("error", why, 0, []))
    return out

# a reply out of raw RESP bytes, from pos on (pos moves past it)
fn _parse(s: str, pos: mut int) Reply:
    e = _crlf(s, pos)
    if e < 0:
        return Reply("error", "redis: protocol error", 0, [])
    kind = s[pos]
    body = s[pos + 1..e]
    pos = e + 2
    if kind == "+":
        return Reply("str", body, 0, [])
    if kind == "-":
        return Reply("error", body, 0, [])
    if kind == ":":
        return Reply("int", "", body.to_int(0), [])
    if kind == "$":
        n = body.to_int(-1)
        if n < 0:
            return Reply("nil", "", 0, [])
        data = s[pos..pos + n]
        pos += n + 2
        return Reply("str", data, 0, [])
    if kind == "*":
        n = body.to_int(-1)
        if n < 0:
            return Reply("nil", "", 0, [])
        items: [Reply] = []
        for i in 0..n:
            items.push(_parse(s, &pos))
        return Reply("array", "", 0, items)
    return Reply("error", "redis: protocol error", 0, [])

# A task uses the pool's connection for the thread it runs on, so a connection's callers and
# its two tasks tend to share one thread, and tasks woken by one batch of replies send their
# next commands together, in one write. (Connections beyond the number of threads stay idle;
# with more threads than connections, some threads share one.)
fn _mux_for(c: Client) _Mux:
    return c.muxes[task.thread_slot() % len(c.muxes)]

fn _blocking(args: [str]) bool:
    b = args[0].byte(0) if len(args[0]) > 0 else 0
    if not (b == 66 or b == 98 or b == 87 or b == 119 or b == 88 or b == 120):      # (B, W or X)
        return false
    name = args[0].upper()
    if name == "BLPOP" or name == "BRPOP" or name == "BLMOVE" or name == "BRPOPLPUSH" or name == "BLMPOP":
        return true
    if name == "BZPOPMIN" or name == "BZPOPMAX" or name == "BZMPOP" or name == "WAIT" or name == "WAITAOF":
        return true
    if name == "XREAD" or name == "XREADGROUP":
        for a in args:
            if a.upper() == "BLOCK":
                return true
    return false

# a blocking command on a connection of its own (it would hold up a shared one)
fn _alone(c: Client, cmds: [[str]]) [Reply]:
    fd = 0
    match _dial(c):
        Ok(f):
            fd = f
        Err(e):
            return _lost(len(cmds), e)
    conn = net.Conn(fd)
    out = ""
    for args in cmds:
        out += _encode(args)
    conn.write(out)
    replies: [Reply] = []
    for i in 0..len(cmds):
        replies.push(_read_reply(conn))
    conn.close()
    return replies

# run commands in one round trip: every reply, in order (the commands go out together, so a
# MULTI ... EXEC pipeline is a transaction)
fn pipeline(c: Client, cmds: [[str]]) [Reply]:
    replies: [Reply] = []
    if len(cmds) == 0:
        return replies
    if len(c.muxes) == 0:
        replies = _lost(len(cmds), "redis: not connected (check c.ok())")
    elif len(cmds) == 1 and _blocking(cmds[0]):
        replies = _alone(c, cmds)
    else:
        out = ""
        for args in cmds:
            out += f"*{len(args)}\r\n"
            _encode_into(&out, args)
        res = _call(c, _mux_for(c), out, len(cmds))
        if res.err != "":
            replies = _lost(len(cmds), res.err)
        else:
            pos = 0
            for i in 0..len(cmds):
                replies.push(_parse(res.raw, &pos))
    msg = ""
    for r in replies:
        if r.kind == "error":
            msg = r.text
    _set_error(msg)                                     # (last, after every wait: see redis.error)
    return replies

fn cmd(c: Client, args: [str]) Reply:
    return pipeline(c, [args])[0]

fn get_str(c: Client, key: str) str:
    return cmd(c, ["GET", key]).text

fn set_str(c: Client, key: str, value: str) bool:
    return cmd(c, ["SET", key, value]).kind == "str"

fn set_ex(c: Client, key: str, value: str, seconds: int) bool:
    return cmd(c, ["SET", key, value, "EX", str(seconds)]).kind == "str"

fn set_nx(c: Client, key: str, value: str) bool:
    return cmd(c, ["SET", key, value, "NX"]).kind == "str"

fn del(c: Client, key: str) int:
    return cmd(c, ["DEL", key]).num

fn exists(c: Client, key: str) bool:
    return cmd(c, ["EXISTS", key]).num > 0

fn incr(c: Client, key: str) int:
    return cmd(c, ["INCR", key]).num

fn incr_by(c: Client, key: str, n: int) int:
    return cmd(c, ["INCRBY", key, str(n)]).num

fn expire(c: Client, key: str, seconds: int) bool:
    return cmd(c, ["EXPIRE", key, str(seconds)]).num == 1

fn ttl(c: Client, key: str) int:
    return cmd(c, ["TTL", key]).num

fn mget(c: Client, keys: [str]) [str]:
    args = ["MGET"]
    for k in keys:
        args.push(k)
    out: [str] = []
    for it in cmd(c, args).items:
        out.push(it.text)
    return out

fn publish(c: Client, channel: str, message: str) int:
    return cmd(c, ["PUBLISH", channel, message]).num

fn _pump(conn: net.Conn, ch: chan[Message]):
    while true:
        r = _read_reply(conn)
        if r.kind != "array":
            break
        if len(r.items) == 3 and r.items[0].text == "message":
            ch.send(Message(r.items[1].text, r.items[2].text))
        elif len(r.items) == 4 and r.items[0].text == "pmessage":
            ch.send(Message(r.items[2].text, r.items[3].text))
    ch.close()

# messages published to these channels (a pattern like "news.*" too), on a connection of
# its own; sub.messages closes if that connection drops or after sub.close()
fn subscribe(c: Client, channels: [str]) Subscription:
    ch: chan[Message] = task.channel(1024)
    fd = -1
    match _dial(c):
        Ok(f):
            fd = f
        Err(e):
            _set_error(e)
    conn = net.Conn(fd)
    if fd < 0:
        ch.close()
        return Subscription(conn, ch)
    args = ["SUBSCRIBE"]
    pargs = ["PSUBSCRIBE"]
    for name in channels:
        if name.contains("*") or name.contains("?"):
            pargs.push(name)
        else:
            args.push(name)
    out = ""
    n = 0
    if len(args) > 1:
        out += _encode(args)
        n += len(args) - 1
    if len(pargs) > 1:
        out += _encode(pargs)
        n += len(pargs) - 1
    conn.write(out)
    for i in 0..n:
        _read_reply(conn)                              # the subscribe confirmations
    task.spawn(fn() _pump(conn, ch))
    return Subscription(conn, ch)

fn next(s: Subscription, m: mut Message) bool:
    return s.messages.next(&m)

fn unsubscribe(s: Subscription):
    s.conn.close()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- with Result
#   v = c.try_get(key)?          Option[str]: None when the key doesn't exist
#   r = c.try_cmd(["HGET", "user:7", "name"])?
# (Err: "redis: command failed: WRONGTYPE ...", or "redis: connection lost")
fn try_cmd(c: Client, args: [str]) Result[Reply, str]:
    r = cmd(c, args)
    if r.kind == "error":
        if r.text.starts_with("redis: "):
            return Err(r.text)
        return Err("redis: command failed: " + r.text)
    return Ok(r)

fn try_get(c: Client, key: str) Result[Option[str], str]:
    r = try_cmd(c, ["GET", key])?
    none: Option[str] = None
    if r.kind == "nil":
        return Ok(none)
    return Ok(Some(r.text))
```

## library/sqlite/sqlite.tn

```tern
# sqlite: SQLite databases, through the system's SQLite library (libsqlite3).
#
#   import sqlite
#
#   d = sqlite.open("app.db")
#   d.exec("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS todos (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT)", [])
#   id = d.exec("INSERT INTO todos (title) VALUES (?)", [title])     # returns the new row id
#   rows = d.query("SELECT id, title FROM todos WHERE id = ?", [str(id)])   # [{str: str}]
#
# Parameters are passed as strings and bound safely (no SQL injection); SQLite converts
# them by column type. A Db can be used by every task and thread at once: each takes a
# connection of its own from the database's pool for the length of a statement (or of a
# transaction it opened), with its own prepared statements, so queries run in parallel. A
# single INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE from a task shares its commit with the other tasks' writes
# at that moment (it returns once committed; a write per web request stays fast). SQL errors
# are runtime errors (inside a web request they become a 500).
#   sqlite.open(path str) Db                 opens (creating) the database file
#   d.exec(sql str, params [str]) int        runs one statement; the new row id for an INSERT
#   d.exec_count(sql, params) int            runs one statement; the rows it changed
#   d.query(sql str, params [str]) [{str: str}]   one map per row, column name -> text
#   d.query_into(sql, params, &out) int      rows read into a struct or [struct] (below)
#   d.run_script(sql) Result[int, str]   every statement in sql, errors returned (migrations)
#   d.exec_later(sql, params)            queue a write and return at once: a background task commits
#                                        the queue in order every 50 ms, and at exit. For writes a
#                                        crash may lose (clicks, view counts); errors go to stderr.
#                                        The fastest way to write on a hot path.
#   d.flush()                            commit what exec_later queued, now (before a read that must
#                                        see it)
#   d.describe(sql) Result[Statement, str]   its parameters and columns, without running it
#   sqlite.NULL                              a parameter that is NULL (["x", sqlite.NULL])

from sql import decode_rows, decode_error, rows, rows_from, row_id, row_field, set_int, set_float, set_text, set_null
import task
import os
import time

extern "sqlite3.h" link "sqlite3":
    fn _tern_panic(line: int, msg: str) = "tern_panic"
    fn _sq_open(path: str, db: mut ptr, flags: int, vfs: ptr) int = "sqlite3_open_v2"
    fn _sq_close(db: ptr) int = "sqlite3_close_v2"
    fn _sq_errmsg(db: ptr) str = "sqlite3_errmsg"
    fn _sq_extended_errcode(db: ptr) int = "sqlite3_extended_errcode"
    fn _sq_prepare(db: ptr, sql: [byte], n: int, flags: int, st: mut ptr, tail: ptr) int = "sqlite3_prepare_v3"
    fn _sq_sql(st: ptr) str = "sqlite3_sql"
    fn _sq_finalize(st: ptr) int = "sqlite3_finalize"
    fn _sq_reset(st: ptr) int = "sqlite3_reset"
    fn _sq_clear_bindings(st: ptr) int = "sqlite3_clear_bindings"
    fn _sq_step(st: ptr) int = "sqlite3_step"
    fn _sq_readonly(st: ptr) bool = "sqlite3_stmt_readonly"
    fn _sq_bind_int64(st: ptr, i: int, v: int) int = "sqlite3_bind_int64"
    fn _sq_bind_text(st: ptr, i: int, v: [byte], n: int, keep: ptr) int = "sqlite3_bind_text"
    fn _sq_bind_null(st: ptr, i: int) int = "sqlite3_bind_null"
    fn _sq_param_count(st: ptr) int = "sqlite3_bind_parameter_count"
    fn _sq_param_name(st: ptr, i: int) str = "sqlite3_bind_parameter_name"
    fn _sq_column_count(st: ptr) int = "sqlite3_column_count"
    fn _sq_column_name(st: ptr, i: int) str = "sqlite3_column_name"
    fn _sq_column_type(st: ptr, i: int) int = "sqlite3_column_type"
    fn _sq_column_int64(st: ptr, i: int) int = "sqlite3_column_int64"
    fn _sq_column_double(st: ptr, i: int) float = "sqlite3_column_double"
    fn _sq_column_text(st: ptr, i: int) ptr = "sqlite3_column_text"
    fn _sq_column_bytes(st: ptr, i: int) int = "sqlite3_column_bytes"
    fn _sq_column_decltype(st: ptr, i: int) str = "sqlite3_column_decltype"
    fn _sq_column_table(st: ptr, i: int) str = "sqlite3_column_table_name"
    fn _sq_column_origin(st: ptr, i: int) str = "sqlite3_column_origin_name"
    fn _sq_changes(db: ptr) int = "sqlite3_changes64"
    fn _sq_total_changes(db: ptr) int = "sqlite3_total_changes64"
    fn _sq_rowid(db: ptr) int = "sqlite3_last_insert_rowid"
    fn _sq_autocommit(db: ptr) bool = "sqlite3_get_autocommit"
    fn _req_active() bool = "tern_req_active"
    fn _req_snap_add(db: ptr) bool = "tern_req_snap_add"
    fn _req_snap_del(db: ptr) = "tern_req_snap_del"
    fn _req_snap_pop() ptr = "tern_req_snap_pop"
    fn _req_snaps() int = "tern_req_snaps"
    fn _req_tid() int = "tern_req_tid"

const _ROW = 100
const _DONE = 101
const _BUSY = 5
const _OPEN_FLAGS = 0x8046                 # READWRITE | CREATE | NOMUTEX | URI

# A parameter that is SQL NULL: pass sqlite.NULL in params (["x", sqlite.NULL]). It is the one-byte
# string "\x00" (so that exact string can't be passed as text).
const NULL = "\x00"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- connections

# A prepared statement and what follows its first statement in the SQL ("": nothing)
struct _Stmt:
    st: ptr
    rest: str
    ncols: int                  # its result columns
    head: str                   # the header of its rows in std sql's format ("" until query_into wants it)
    map: [int]                  # for each result column, the field of the struct query_into last filled
    mapid: int                  # ... and which struct that was (sql.row_id)

const _NO_STMT = _Stmt(null, "", 0, "", [], 0)

# A connection and its prepared statements (by their SQL; all are finalized past 64).
struct _Conn:
    db: ptr
    stmts: {str: _Stmt}
    snap: int                   # the thread whose request's read snapshot it holds (see _snapshot); 0: none

# Connection settings run with exec ("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON"): every connection opened
# afterwards runs them too.
struct _Settings:
    pragmas: [str]

struct _Later:
    items: [_Item]              # writes that didn't commit (put back ahead of what's in d._lq)
    c: _Conn                    # the connection they commit on (opened by the first commit)
    failing: bool               # the last commit failed (reported once, until one works)

struct _Item:
    sql: str
    params: [str]

struct _Write:                  # a single write, for the writer (group commit)
    sql: str
    params: [str]
    done: chan[_Wrote]

struct _Wrote:
    rowid: int
    changes: int
    err: str

struct Db:
    path: str
    _solo: bool                 # in memory: each connection is its own database (no sharing)
    _free: [chan[_Conn]]        # the connections not in use, by thread (_req_tid): a channel is a spin lock and no more
    _snaps: [chan[_Conn]]       # the connections parked inside a request's snapshot, by thread
    _owned: shared[{int: _Conn}]      # connections with a transaction open, by owner
    _nowned: task.Atomic
    _settings: shared[_Settings]
    _writes: chan[_Write]
    _writer: task.Atomic        # 1 once the writer task runs
    _later: shared[_Later]
    _run: task.Atomic           # 1 while a commit of exec_later's writes runs (one at a time: they stay in order)
    _bg: shared[[task[int]]]    # the background tasks (the writer, the exec_later loop), joined at exit
    _stop: task.Atomic          # 1 once the program is ending: the background tasks stop
    _hook: task.Atomic          # 1 once os.at_exit has been given _shutdown
    _lq: chan[_Item]            # exec_later's queue (a channel, not a shared value: the threads
                                #   that call exec_later never wait for a task that holds a lock)
    _lrun: task.Atomic          # 1 once the exec_later task runs
    _lnext: task.Atomic         # when (ms) a caller of exec_later commits next, if the task hasn't
    _lowner: task.Atomic        # the thread (_req_tid) that commits for exec_later's callers
    _lfail: task.Atomic         # 1 while the last commit failed (callers leave the retrying to the task)

fn open(path: str) Db:
    solo = path == "" or path == ":memory:" or path.contains("mode=memory")
    free: [chan[_Conn]] = []
    snaps: [chan[_Conn]] = []
    for i in 0..task.workers() + 2:
        free.push(task.channel(0))
        snaps.push(task.channel(0))
    owned: {int: _Conn} = {}
    bg: [task[int]] = []
    d = Db(path, solo, free, snaps, task.shared(owned), task.atomic(0), task.shared(_Settings([])), task.channel(0), task.atomic(0), task.shared(_Later([], _Conn(null, {}, 0), false)), task.atomic(0), task.shared(bg), task.atomic(0), task.atomic(0), task.channel(0), task.atomic(0), task.atomic(0), task.atomic(0), task.atomic(0))
    probe: ptr = null                       # fail early if it can't be opened
    if _sq_open(path, &probe, 6, null) != 0:
        _sq_close(probe)
        _raise("sqlite.open: can't open database " + path)
    _script(probe, "PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;")
    _sq_close(probe)
    return d

# who owns an open transaction: the task, or outside tasks the thread
fn _me() int:
    id = task.id()
    return id if id != 0 else -1 - _req_tid()

# A runtime error that names SQLite's message, not this file: "runtime error: sqlite: ..."
# (the message is the user's, whichever of the package's functions found it).
fn _raise(msg: str):
    _tern_panic(0, msg)

# A new connection, or why not: _Conn.db is null and err says why.
struct _Opened:
    c: _Conn
    err: str

fn _connect(d: Db) _Conn:
    o = _try_connect(d)
    if o.err != "":
        _raise("sqlite: " + o.err)
    return o.c

fn _try_connect(d: Db) _Opened:
    db: ptr = null
    if _sq_open(d.path, &db, _OPEN_FLAGS, null) != 0:
        why = _sq_errmsg(db)
        _sq_close(db)
        return _Opened(_Conn(null, {}, 0), "can't open database " + d.path + ": " + why)
    # memory-mapped reads skip the page cache and pread(): much faster lookups
    _script(db, "PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL; PRAGMA mmap_size=1073741824;")
    for p in d._settings.get().pragmas:
        _script(db, p)
    return _Opened(_Conn(db, {}, 0), "")

# the connection a statement runs on: the caller's own (its transaction is open, or the
# snapshot of its request), else a free one from this thread's list, else a new one
fn _take(d: Db) _Conn:
    if d._nowned.load() > 0:
        me = _me()
        fn mine(m: mut {int: _Conn}) _Conn:
            if me in m:
                c = m[me]
                m.remove(me)
                return c
            return _Conn(null, {}, 0)
        c = d._owned.update(mine)
        if not c.db.is_null():
            d._nowned.add(-1)
            return c
    tid = _req_tid()
    slot = tid % len(d._free)
    c = _Conn(null, {}, 0)
    if _req_active() and d._snaps[slot].try_recv(&c):
        if _sq_autocommit(c.db):             # (its request ended: a plain connection again)
            c.snap = 0
            return c
        if c.snap == tid:
            return c
        d._snaps[slot].send(c)               # (another thread's)
    if d._free[slot].try_recv(&c):
        return c
    return _connect(d)

# after a statement: back to this thread's free list, or kept for the caller if it left a
# transaction open
fn _give(d: Db, c: _Conn):
    if not _sq_autocommit(c.db):
        if c.snap != 0:                      # a request's snapshot stays with its thread
            d._snaps[c.snap % len(d._free)].send(c)
            return
        me = _me()
        fn keep(m: mut {int: _Conn}) int:
            m[me] = c
            return 0
        d._owned.update(keep)
        d._nowned.add(1)
        return
    d._free[_req_tid() % len(d._free)].send(c)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- request snapshots
# Inside a web request (http.serve's handler), the reads of a thread share one read transaction
# per database, committed when the response is ready (_request_end, called by the generated
# glue): one lock round-trip per request instead of one per query, and every read in the
# request sees the same data. A write, a script, flush or a transaction of the caller's own
# ends the snapshot first, so they behave as without it.

# before a read: begins the request's snapshot on this connection if it has none
fn _snapshot(c: mut _Conn, st: ptr):
    if c.snap != 0 or not _req_active() or not _sq_readonly(st) or not _sq_autocommit(c.db):
        return
    if _script(c.db, "BEGIN") != "":
        return
    if _req_snap_add(c.db):
        c.snap = _req_tid()
    else:
        _script(c.db, "COMMIT")

fn _end_snap(c: mut _Conn):
    if c.snap != 0:
        c.snap = 0
        _req_snap_del(c.db)
        _script(c.db, "COMMIT")

# ends this thread's snapshot of d, if it has one (before anything that must see or order
# with writes)
fn _drop_snap(d: Db):
    if not _req_active() or _req_snaps() == 0:
        return
    tid = _req_tid()
    c = _Conn(null, {}, 0)
    if d._snaps[tid % len(d._free)].try_recv(&c):
        if c.snap == tid:
            _end_snap(&c)
        _give(d, c)

# at the end of a request: commits every snapshot it began
fn _request_end():
    p = _req_snap_pop()
    while not p.is_null():
        _script(p, "COMMIT")
        p = _req_snap_pop()

# the prepared statement for q on c, from its cache (st is null if it can't be prepared: rest says why). rest: the
# statements after the first ("" if none)
fn _prepare(c: mut _Conn, q: str) _Stmt:
    x = c.stmts.get(q, _NO_STMT)
    if not x.st.is_null():
        return x
    st: ptr = null
    b = q.to_bytes()
    if _sq_prepare(c.db, b, len(b), 1, &st, null) != 0:      # 1: SQLITE_PREPARE_PERSISTENT
        return _Stmt(null, _sq_errmsg(c.db), 0, "", [], 0)
    if st.is_null():
        return _Stmt(null, "no SQL statement", 0, "", [], 0)
    if len(c.stmts) >= 64:                   # (a full cache starts over)
        for q0, x in c.stmts:
            _sq_finalize(x.st)
        c.stmts = {}
    rest = _rest_of(q, _sq_sql(st))
    ncols = _sq_column_count(st)
    x = _Stmt(st, rest, ncols, "", [], 0)
    c.stmts[q] = x
    return x

# the names of a statement's result columns
fn _names(st: ptr) [str]:
    names: [str] = []
    for i in 0.._sq_column_count(st):
        names.push(_sq_column_name(st, i))
    return names

# what follows the first statement (first: its text as SQLite kept it): "" if only blanks and ;
fn _rest_of(q: str, first: str) str:
    i = len(first)
    while i < len(q):
        b = q.byte(i)
        if not (b == 59 or b == 32 or b == 10 or b == 9 or b == 13):
            return q[i..]
        i += 1
    return ""

# Binds params ("\x00" is NULL; a canonical integer, "42" not "007", an integer so key lookups
# stay fast; the rest is text, bound as the string's own bytes: params outlives the statement's
# use, and so do they).
fn _bind(st: ptr, params: [str]):
    for i, v in params:
        if v == NULL:
            _sq_bind_null(st, i + 1)
        else:
            n = _canonical(v)
            if n != _NOT_INT:
                _sq_bind_int64(st, i + 1, n)
            else:
                b = v.to_bytes()
                _sq_bind_text(st, i + 1, b, len(b), null)       # (null: SQLITE_STATIC)

const _NOT_INT = -9223372036854775807 - 1

# the value of v if it is a canonical integer ("42", "-7"; not "007", "-0", "+1", or 19 digits), else _NOT_INT
fn _canonical(v: str) int:
    n = len(v)
    if n == 0 or n > 18:
        return _NOT_INT
    i = 1 if v.byte(0) == 45 else 0
    if i == n or (v.byte(i) == 48 and n > i + 1) or (i == 1 and v.byte(1) == 48):
        return _NOT_INT
    x = 0
    while i < n:
        b = v.byte(i)
        if b < 48 or b > 57:
            return _NOT_INT
        x = x * 10 + b - 48
        i += 1
    return -x if v.byte(0) == 45 else x

# A step, waiting out another connection's lock: in a task only the task waits. Up to 5 s.
fn _step(db: ptr, st: ptr) int:
    return _step_for(db, st, 5000)

fn _step_for(db: ptr, st: ptr, limit: int) int:
    waited = 0
    while true:
        rc = _sq_step(st)
        if rc != _BUSY or waited >= limit or _sq_extended_errcode(db) != _BUSY:
            return rc
        ms = 1 if waited < 10 else 5
        task.sleep(ms)
        waited += ms
    return 0

fn _in_transaction(d: Db) bool:             # does the caller have one open?
    return d._nowned.load() > 0 and _me() in d._owned.get()

# Every statement in q, in order, each waiting out locks like _step: "" or SQLite's error.
# (sqlite3_exec would fail at once on a lock, or block the whole thread with a timeout.)
fn _script(db: ptr, q: str) str:
    return _script_for(db, q, 5000)

fn _script_for(db: ptr, q: str, limit: int) str:
    b = q.to_bytes()
    at = 0
    while at < len(b):
        st: ptr = null
        rest = b[at..]
        if _sq_prepare(db, rest, len(rest), 0, &st, null) != 0:
            return _sq_errmsg(db)
        if st.is_null():
            return ""                           # (only blanks and comments were left)
        used = len(_sq_sql(st))
        rc = _step_for(db, st, limit)
        while rc == _ROW:
            rc = _step_for(db, st, limit)
        why = _sq_errmsg(db) if rc != _DONE else ""
        _sq_finalize(st)
        if why != "":
            return why
        if used <= 0:
            return ""
        at += used
    return ""

fn _done(st: ptr):
    _sq_reset(st)
    _sq_clear_bindings(st)

# the statement failed: the connection goes back, then a runtime error with SQLite's message
fn _fail(d: Db, c: _Conn, st: ptr, why: str):
    if not st.is_null():
        _done(st)
    _give(d, c)
    _raise("sqlite: " + why)

fn _first_word(q: str) str:
    i = 0
    while i < len(q) and (q.byte(i) == 32 or q.byte(i) == 10 or q.byte(i) == 9 or q.byte(i) == 13):
        i += 1
    j = i
    while j < len(q) and j < i + 8 and ((q.byte(j) >= 65 and q.byte(j) <= 90) or (q.byte(j) >= 97 and q.byte(j) <= 122)):
        j += 1
    return q[i..j].upper()

fn _row_write(q: str) bool:
    w = _first_word(q)
    return w == "INSERT" or w == "UPDATE" or w == "DELETE" or w == "REPLACE" or w == "WITH"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- statements

fn exec(d: Db, sql: str, params: [str]) int:
    return _exec(d, sql, params).rowid

# The rows it changed (an UPDATE's or DELETE's matches; an INSERT's 1), instead of the row id.
fn exec_count(d: Db, sql: str, params: [str]) int:
    return _exec(d, sql, params).changes

fn _exec(d: Db, q: str, params: [str]) _Wrote:
    _drop_snap(d)
    if task.id() != 0 and not d._solo and _row_write(q) and not _in_transaction(d):
        w = _group(d, q, params)                 # (a single write: committed with others)
        if w.err == "":
            return w
        if w.err != "-":
            _raise("sqlite: " + w.err)
    return _exec_here(d, q, params)

# (apart from _exec so that a task waiting for its group commit keeps a small frame)
fn _exec_here(d: Db, q: str, params: [str]) _Wrote:
    c = _take(d)
    p = _prepare(&c, q)
    if p.st.is_null():
        _fail(d, c, null, p.rest)
    if p.rest != "" and len(params) > 0:
        _fail(d, c, p.st, "exec: with ? parameters, run one SQL statement per call")
    _bind(p.st, params)
    rc = _step(c.db, p.st)
    while rc == _ROW:
        rc = _step(c.db, p.st)
    if rc != _DONE:
        _fail(d, c, p.st, _sq_errmsg(c.db))
    _done(p.st)
    out = _Wrote(_sq_rowid(c.db), _sq_changes(c.db), "")
    if p.rest != "":
        why = _script(c.db, p.rest)
        if why != "":
            _fail(d, c, null, why)
        out = _Wrote(_sq_rowid(c.db), _sq_changes(c.db), "")
    if len(params) == 0:
        _remember(d, q)
    _give(d, c)
    return out

# "PRAGMA name = value" (not journal_mode, which is the database's): for new connections too
fn _remember(d: Db, q: str):
    if _first_word(q) != "PRAGMA" or not q.contains("=") or q.lower().contains("journal_mode"):
        return
    fn add(s: mut _Settings) int:
        s.pragmas.push(q)
        return 0
    d._settings.update(add)

fn query(d: Db, sql: str, params: [str]) [{str: str}]:
    c = _take(d)
    p = _prepare(&c, sql)
    if p.st.is_null():
        _fail(d, c, null, p.rest)
    if p.rest != "":
        _fail(d, c, p.st, "sqlite.query runs one SQL statement; run the others with sqlite.exec")
    _snapshot(&c, p.st)
    _bind(p.st, params)
    n = _sq_column_count(p.st)
    names = _names(p.st)
    out: [{str: str}] = []
    rc = _step(c.db, p.st)
    while rc == _ROW:
        row: {str: str} = {}
        for i in 0..n:
            row[names[i]] = string_at(_sq_column_text(p.st, i), _sq_column_bytes(p.st, i))
        out.push(row)
        rc = _step(c.db, p.st)
    if rc != _DONE:
        _fail(d, c, p.st, _sq_errmsg(c.db))
    _done(p.st)
    _give(d, c)
    return out

# Typed queries read rows straight into your structs (columns matched to fields by name;
# fields may be int, float, bool, str, a payload-free enum read from its label, an array or
# any type json.decode reads from JSON text, or an Option of one). Returns the number of rows.
#   worlds: [World] = []
#   n = d.query_into("SELECT id, randomNumber FROM world", [], &worlds)
#   w = World(0, 0)
#   found = d.query_into("SELECT id, randomNumber FROM world WHERE id = ?", [str(id)], &w) > 0
fn query_into[T](d: Db, sql: str, params: [str], out: mut T) int:
    tid = row_id(&out)
    if tid != 0:                             # (into one struct: straight from the statement)
        return _fill(d, sql, params, &out, tid)
    n = decode_rows(_rows(d, sql, params), &out)
    if n < 0:
        why = decode_error()
        _raise("sqlite: " + (why if why != "" else "the rows don't fit"))
    return n

# query_into a struct: the first row's columns go into its fields as they are read (std sql's
# set_int ...), no rows string in between; the other rows are counted
fn _fill[T](d: Db, q: str, params: [str], out: mut T, tid: int) int:
    c = _take(d)
    p = _prepare(&c, q)
    if p.st.is_null():
        _fail(d, c, null, p.rest)
    if p.rest != "":
        _fail(d, c, p.st, "sqlite.query runs one SQL statement; run the others with sqlite.exec")
    st = p.st
    _snapshot(&c, st)
    _bind(st, params)
    n = p.ncols
    map = p.map
    if p.mapid != tid:                       # (the same statement into another struct: map again)
        map = []
        for name in _names(st):
            map.push(row_field(&out, name))
        c.stmts[q] = _Stmt(st, p.rest, p.ncols, p.head, map, tid)
    row = out
    seen = 0
    ok = true
    rc = _step(c.db, st)
    while rc == _ROW:
        if seen == 0:
            for i in 0..n:
                f = map[i]
                if f < 0:
                    continue
                t = _sq_column_type(st, i)
                if t == 1:
                    ok = set_int(&row, f, _sq_column_int64(st, i))
                elif t == 2:
                    ok = set_float(&row, f, _sq_column_double(st, i))
                elif t == 5:
                    ok = set_null(&row, f)
                else:
                    ok = set_text(&row, f, string_at(_sq_column_text(st, i), _sq_column_bytes(st, i)))
                if not ok:
                    break
        seen += 1
        if not ok:
            break
        rc = _step(c.db, st)
    if ok and rc != _DONE:
        _fail(d, c, st, _sq_errmsg(c.db))
    _done(st)
    _give(d, c)
    if not ok:
        why = decode_error()
        _raise("sqlite: " + (why if why != "" else "the rows don't fit"))
    out = row
    return seen

# the rows of q, in std sql's format (each value as SQLite has it: integer, float, text, NULL)
fn _rows(d: Db, q: str, params: [str]) str:
    c = _take(d)
    p = _prepare(&c, q)
    if p.st.is_null():
        _fail(d, c, null, p.rest)
    if p.rest != "":
        _fail(d, c, p.st, "sqlite.query runs one SQL statement; run the others with sqlite.exec")
    _snapshot(&c, p.st)
    _bind(p.st, params)
    n = p.ncols
    head = p.head
    if head == "":                           # (the header is the same every time: kept with the statement)
        hb = rows(_names(p.st))
        head = hb.head()
        c.stmts[q] = _Stmt(p.st, p.rest, p.ncols, head, p.map, p.mapid)
    b = rows_from(head)
    rc = _step(c.db, p.st)
    while rc == _ROW:
        b.row(n)
        for i in 0..n:
            t = _sq_column_type(p.st, i)
            if t == 1:
                b.put_int(_sq_column_int64(p.st, i))
            elif t == 2:
                b.put_float(_sq_column_double(p.st, i))
            elif t == 5:
                b.put_null()
            else:
                b.put_text(string_at(_sq_column_text(p.st, i), _sq_column_bytes(p.st, i)))
        rc = _step(c.db, p.st)
    if rc != _DONE:
        _fail(d, c, p.st, _sq_errmsg(c.db))
    _done(p.st)
    _give(d, c)
    return b.bytes()

# Every statement in sql, in order, with the error returned instead of being a runtime error
# (a migration, a schema file). The rows inserted, updated or deleted. No ? parameters.
#   d.run_script("CREATE TABLE a (x INT); CREATE INDEX a_x ON a (x);")?
fn run_script(d: Db, sql: str) Result[int, str]:
    _drop_snap(d)
    c = _take(d)
    before = _sq_total_changes(c.db)
    why = _script(c.db, sql)
    changed = _sq_total_changes(c.db) - before
    _give(d, c)
    if why != "":
        return Err("sqlite: script failed: " + why)
    return Ok(changed)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- group commit
# A single INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE from a task, outside a transaction, goes to the database's
# writer task, which runs every write waiting at that moment in one transaction and commits
# once for all of them; each caller then gets its own row id and count (or its own error: a
# failing statement fails alone, and if the commit fails, all of them do). SQLite writes one
# transaction at a time anyway; this way they don't queue at its file lock.

fn _group(d: Db, q: str, params: [str]) _Wrote:
    if d._stop.load() != 0:
        return _Wrote(0, 0, "-")                 # (the program is ending: the caller runs it)
    done: chan[_Wrote] = task.channel(1)
    d._writes.send(_Write(q, params, done))
    # (started after the write is queued: a writer that dies empties the queue, and the next
    # write finds none running and starts another, so no write is left waiting for nobody)
    if d._writer.load() == 0 and d._writer.cas(0, 1):
        _start(d)
        _spawn(d, fn() _writer(d))
    return done.recv()

fn _spawn(d: Db, f: fn() int):
    h = task.spawn(f)
    fn add(l: mut [task[int]]) int:
        live: [task[int]] = []
        for x in l:
            if not x.done():                 # (writers that died are dropped)
                live.push(x)
        live.push(h)
        l = live
        return 0
    d._bg.update(add)

# The writer can't open its connection: every write waiting gets the reason (it is raised in
# its caller, as for any failing write), and the next write starts a new writer, which tries
# again.
fn _writer_failed(d: Db, why: str):
    d._writer.store(0)
    w = _Write("", [], task.channel(1))
    while d._writes.try_recv(&w):
        w.done.send(_Wrote(0, 0, why))

fn _writer(d: Db) int:
    o = _try_connect(d)
    if o.err != "":
        _writer_failed(d, o.err)
        return 0
    c = o.c
    w = _Write("", [], task.channel(1))
    while d._writes.next(&w):
        batch = [w]
        task.yield_now()                     # (the other ready tasks add theirs)
        while d._writes.try_recv(&w):
            batch.push(w)
        why = _script(c.db, "BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
        if why != "":
            for x in batch:
                x.done.send(_Wrote(0, 0, why))
            continue
        results: [_Wrote] = []
        dead = ""
        for x in batch:
            if dead != "":
                results.push(_Wrote(0, 0, dead))
                continue
            p = _prepare(&c, x.sql)
            if p.st.is_null():
                results.push(_Wrote(0, 0, p.rest))
                continue
            if p.rest != "":
                results.push(_Wrote(0, 0, "-"))     # (several statements: the caller runs them)
                continue
            _bind(p.st, x.params)
            rc = _sq_step(p.st)
            while rc == _ROW:
                rc = _sq_step(p.st)
            if rc != _DONE:
                results.push(_Wrote(0, 0, _sq_errmsg(c.db)))
                _done(p.st)
                if _sq_autocommit(c.db):             # the error undid the whole transaction
                    dead = _sq_errmsg(c.db)
                    for k in 0..len(results):
                        if results[k].err == "":
                            results[k] = _Wrote(0, 0, dead)
                continue
            _done(p.st)
            results.push(_Wrote(_sq_rowid(c.db), _sq_changes(c.db), ""))
        if dead == "":
            dead = _script(c.db, "COMMIT")
        if dead != "":
            _script(c.db, "ROLLBACK")
            for k in 0..len(results):
                if results[k].err == "":
                    results[k] = _Wrote(0, 0, dead)
        for k, x in batch:
            x.done.send(results[k])
    _close(c)
    return 0

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- exec_later

fn exec_later(d: Db, sql: str, params: [str]):
    d._lq.send(_Item(sql, params))
    if d._lrun.load() == 0 and d._lrun.cas(0, 1):
        _start(d)
        _spawn(d, fn() _later_loop(d))
    # (The task below commits every 50 ms, but a server busy with requests may not give it a
    # turn for as long as it stays busy: then the callers do it, one of them each 50 ms.)
    now = time.mono_ns() / 1000000
    due = d._lnext.load()
    full = len(d._lq) >= _LATER_MAX
    if (now >= due or full) and d._lfail.load() == 0:
        # one thread does it while it keeps calling (a heap keeps what it frees: every thread
        # that committed would hold on to a batch of other threads' blocks); any, when it doesn't.
        # A full queue is committed at once by that thread: what waits is memory.
        me = _req_tid()
        if full and me == d._lowner.load():
            d._lnext.store(now + _LATER_EVERY)
            _commit_later(d, false)
        elif (me == d._lowner.load() or now >= due + 2 * _LATER_EVERY) and d._lnext.cas(due, now + _LATER_EVERY):
            d._lowner.store(me)
            _commit_later(d, false)

fn _later_loop(d: Db) int:
    while d._stop.load() == 0:
        for i in 0..10:                      # (let a batch gather; look up often to stop soon)
            if d._stop.load() == 0:
                task.sleep(5)
        _commit_later(d, true)
    return 0

# The first background task of a Db asks os.at_exit for _shutdown. Tern's leak accounting (and
# a clean exit) want no task left running, holding the Db.
fn _start(d: Db):
    if d._hook.cas(0, 1):
        os.at_exit(fn() _shutdown(d))

# At the end of the program: stop the writer and the exec_later task, wait for them (they
# finish what they were doing), then commit what is still queued.
fn _shutdown(d: Db):
    d._stop.store(1)
    d._writes.close()
    fn grab(l: mut [task[int]]) [task[int]]:
        hs = l
        l = []
        return hs
    for h in d._bg.update(grab):
        waited = 0
        # (outside a task, when the program ends on a runtime error or os.exit, the scheduler
        # may be gone: don't wait)
        while task.id() != 0 and not h.done() and waited < 2000:
            task.sleep(1)
            waited += 1
    left = 1
    for i in 0..5:                           # (the last chance for what's still queued)
        left = _commit_later(d, true)
        if left == 0:
            break
    if left > 0:
        os.eprint(f"sqlite: {left} writes from exec_later couldn't be committed before the program ended (writes lost)")
    c = d._later.get().c
    _close(c)
    fn forget(l: mut _Later) int:
        l.c = _Conn(null, {}, 0)         # (a later flush opens a new one)
        return 0
    d._later.update(forget)

# Finalizes a connection's statements and closes it.
fn _close(c: _Conn):
    if c.db.is_null():
        return
    for q, x in c.stmts:
        _sq_finalize(x.st)
    _sq_close(c.db)

# Commits what's queued; if the database stays locked it keeps trying (for up to a minute),
# and what still can't be written stays queued for the background task.
fn flush(d: Db):
    _drop_snap(d)
    for i in 0..30:
        if _commit_later(d, true) == 0:
            return

const _LATER_WAIT = 2000        # ms a try at the write lock waits
const _LATER_EVERY = 50        # ms between commits
const _LATER_MAX = 1024         # writes waiting that make a commit now

# Puts a batch back at the front of the queue, ahead of what was queued meanwhile. why: what
# went wrong with the database ("": nothing, a statement of the batch failed alone).
fn _requeue(d: Db, items: [_Item], why: str):
    if len(items) == 0:
        return
    fn put(l: mut _Later) int:
        all = items
        for x in l.items:
            all.push(x)
        l.items = all
        if why != "" and not l.failing:
            l.failing = true
            os.eprint(f"sqlite: writes from exec_later wait: {why} ({len(items)} queued; trying again)")
        return 0
    d._later.update(put)
    if why != "":
        d._lfail.store(1)

fn _ok_again(l: mut _Later) int:
    l.failing = false
    return 0

# Commits what's queued, in order, in one transaction (one commit at a time: d._run), and
# returns how many writes are still queued. A write that fails (bad SQL, a constraint) is
# reported on stderr and the others still commit, as in the C code before. A batch that
# can't start or commit (the database is locked, say) is rolled back and stays queued, in
# order and ahead of newer writes, for the next try; the background task tries every 50 ms.
fn _commit_later(d: Db, wait: bool) int:
    if not d._run.cas(0, 1):
        if not wait:
            return -1                            # (another is committing: that one takes what's queued)
        while not d._run.cas(0, 1):
            task.sleep(1)
    _commit_batch(d)
    d._run.store(0)
    return len(d._later.get().items) + len(d._lq)

# the items but the ones at the (ascending) indexes in failed
fn _without(items: [_Item], failed: [int]) [_Item]:
    out: [_Item] = []
    f = 0
    for k, it in items:
        if f < len(failed) and failed[f] == k:
            f += 1
        else:
            out.push(it)
    return out

fn _commit_batch(d: Db):
    fn drain(l: mut _Later) [_Item]:      # the writes put back, then what was queued since
        all = l.items
        l.items = []
        x = _Item("", [])
        while d._lq.try_recv(&x):
            all.push(x)
        return all
    items = d._later.update(drain)
    if len(items) == 0:
        return
    c = d._later.get().c
    if c.db.is_null():
        o = _try_connect(d)
        if o.err != "":
            _requeue(d, items, o.err)
            task.sleep(_LATER_WAIT)
            return
        c = o.c
    fn keep_conn(l: mut _Later) int:
        l.c = c
        return 0
    why = _script_for(c.db, "BEGIN IMMEDIATE", _LATER_WAIT)
    if why != "":
        d._later.update(keep_conn)
        _requeue(d, items, why)
        return
    failed: [int] = []                     # the writes that failed alone (not queued again)
    for k, it in items:
        p = _prepare(&c, it.sql)
        if p.st.is_null():
            os.eprint(f"sqlite: a write from exec_later failed: {p.rest} ({it.sql})")
            failed.push(k)
            continue
        _bind(p.st, it.params)
        rc = _sq_step(p.st)
        while rc == _ROW:
            rc = _sq_step(p.st)
        if rc != _DONE:
            os.eprint(f"sqlite: a write from exec_later failed: {_sq_errmsg(c.db)} ({it.sql})")
            failed.push(k)
            if _sq_autocommit(c.db):             # (the error undid the transaction: the
                _done(p.st)                      # rest, and what was done, go round again)
                d._later.update(keep_conn)
                _requeue(d, _without(items, failed), "")
                return
        _done(p.st)
    why = _script_for(c.db, "COMMIT", _LATER_WAIT)
    d._later.update(keep_conn)
    if why != "":
        _script(c.db, "ROLLBACK")
        _requeue(d, _without(items, failed), why)
        return
    d._later.update(_ok_again)
    d._lfail.store(0)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- describe

# A statement's parameters and result columns, without running it (what sqlgen reads).
#   s = d.describe("SELECT id, email FROM users WHERE id = @id")?
#   s.params        ["@id"]
#   s.columns[1]    Column{name: "email", decl_type: "TEXT", table: "users", column: "email", not_null: false}
struct Column:
    name: str
    decl_type: str              # the declared type ("INTEGER", "TEXT", ...); "" for an expression
    table: str                  # the table the value comes from ("" for an expression)
    column: str                 # ... and its column there
    not_null: bool              # a table column declared NOT NULL (an outer join can still make it null)

struct Statement:
    params: [str]               # "@id", ":name", "$x", "?1"; "" for a plain ?
    columns: [Column]

struct _Info:
    name: str
    notnull: int
    pk: int
    type: str

fn describe(d: Db, sql: str) Result[Statement, str]:
    c = _take(d)
    st: ptr = null
    b = sql.to_bytes()
    if _sq_prepare(c.db, b, len(b), 0, &st, null) != 0 or st.is_null():
        why = _sq_errmsg(c.db) if not st.is_null() or _sq_extended_errcode(c.db) != 0 else "no SQL statement"
        _give(d, c)
        return Err("sqlite: describe failed: " + why)
    out = Statement([], [])
    for i in 1.._sq_param_count(st) + 1:
        out.params.push(_sq_param_name(st, i))
    for i in 0.._sq_column_count(st):
        out.columns.push(Column(_sq_column_name(st, i), _sq_column_decltype(st, i), _sq_column_table(st, i), _sq_column_origin(st, i), false))
    _sq_finalize(st)
    _give(d, c)
    tables: {str: [_Info]} = {}
    for k in 0..len(out.columns):
        col = out.columns[k]
        if col.table == "" or col.column == "":
            continue
        if not (col.table in tables):
            infos: [_Info] = []
            decode_rows(_rows(d, "SELECT name, \"notnull\", pk, type FROM pragma_table_info(?)", [col.table]), &infos)
            tables[col.table] = infos
        for info in tables[col.table]:
            if info.name.lower() == col.column.lower():
                # the rowid (an INTEGER PRIMARY KEY) is never NULL
                out.columns[k].not_null = info.notnull != 0 or (info.pk != 0 and info.type.upper() == "INTEGER")
    return Ok(out)
```

# Packages (`tern add NAME`)

Imported by name once added (`import roost`).

## deps/auth/auth.tn

```tern
# auth: JSON Web Tokens (HS256) and signed-cookie sessions for web apps. A package of its
# own, so plain web programs don't carry crypto. Password hashing is crypto.hash_password.
#
#   import auth
#   import roost
#
#   token = auth.jwt_for("user-7", secret, 3600)          # {"sub":"user-7","iat":...,"exp":...}
#   t = auth.jwt_verify(token, secret)                    # t.ok, t.subject, t.payload, t.error
#
#   r.layer(auth.require_jwt(secret))                     # 401 unless "Authorization: Bearer <jwt>";
#                                                         #   (a JSON body: {"error":"unauthorized: why"})
#   ... req.ctx_value("jwt.sub")                          # handlers then find the subject here
#
#   s = auth.session(req, secret)                         # {str: str}; {} if none / tampered / expired
#   res = roost.text("hi")
#   auth.set_session(&res, secret, {"user": "7"})         # Set-Cookie: session=...; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax
#   auth.clear_session(&res)
#
# JWTs:
#   auth.jwt_encode(payload_json str, secret str) str     sign any JSON object
#   auth.jwt_for(subject str, secret str, ttl_seconds int) str
#   auth.jwt_verify(token str, secret str) Token          checks the signature (constant time),
#       that alg is HS256, and exp / nbf when present. Token fields: ok, payload (the JSON; decode
#       it into your struct with json.decode), subject ("sub"), error ("" when ok)
#   auth.require_jwt(secret str) middleware               sets ctx "jwt.sub" and "jwt" (the payload)
# Sessions: the data is in the cookie itself (JSON, base64url, HMAC-SHA256 signed; readable by
# the user but not changeable), so keep it small (cookies hold ~4 KB) and never put secrets in it.
#   auth.session(req http.Request, secret str) {str: str}
#   auth.set_session(res mut http.Response, secret str, data {str: str})      30 days
#   auth.set_session_for(res mut http.Response, secret str, data {str: str}, max_age_seconds int, attrs str)
#       attrs: extra cookie attributes, e.g. "Secure" behind HTTPS
#   auth.clear_session(res mut http.Response)
# (http.Request and http.Response are roost.Request and roost.Response: the same types.)
# Use a long random secret (crypto.base64url(crypto.random_bytes(32))), kept out of the code.

import crypto
import http
import json
import time

struct Token:
    ok: bool
    payload: str
    subject: str
    error: str

struct _Claims:
    sub: str
    exp: int
    nbf: int

struct _Header:
    alg: str
    typ: str

fn _sign(data: str, secret: str) str:
    return crypto.base64url(crypto.hmac_sha256(secret, data))

fn jwt_encode(payload_json: str, secret: str) str:
    head = crypto.base64url("{\"alg\":\"HS256\",\"typ\":\"JWT\"}") + "." + crypto.base64url(payload_json)
    return head + "." + _sign(head, secret)

fn jwt_for(subject: str, secret: str, ttl_seconds: int) str:
    now = int(time.now())
    return jwt_encode("{\"sub\":" + subject.json_quote() + ",\"iat\":" + str(now) + ",\"exp\":" + str(now + ttl_seconds) + "}", secret)

fn jwt_verify(token: str, secret: str) Token:
    parts = token.split(".")
    if len(parts) != 3:
        return Token(false, "", "", "malformed token")
    head = parts[0] + "." + parts[1]
    if not crypto.equal(_sign(head, secret), parts[2]):
        return Token(false, "", "", "bad signature")
    h = _Header("", "")
    if not json.decode(crypto.base64url_decode(parts[0]), &h) or h.alg != "HS256":
        return Token(false, "", "", "unsupported algorithm (only HS256)")
    payload = crypto.base64url_decode(parts[1])
    c = _Claims("", 0, 0)
    if not json.decode(payload, &c):
        return Token(false, "", "", "malformed payload")
    now = int(time.now())
    if c.exp != 0 and now >= c.exp:
        return Token(false, payload, c.sub, "expired")
    if c.nbf != 0 and now < c.nbf:
        return Token(false, payload, c.sub, "not valid yet")
    return Token(true, payload, c.sub, "")

fn _require(req: http.Request, inner: fn(http.Request) http.Response, secret: str) http.Response:
    h = req.header("authorization")
    if not h.starts_with("Bearer "):
        return _unauthorized("missing bearer token")
    t = jwt_verify(h[7..].trim(), secret)
    if not t.ok:
        return _unauthorized(t.error)
    r2 = req
    r2.set_ctx("jwt.sub", t.subject)
    r2.set_ctx("jwt", t.payload)
    return inner(r2)

fn _unauthorized(why: str) http.Response:              # JSON, like the rest of an API
    res = http.with_status(http.json("{\"error\":" + ("unauthorized: " + why).json_quote() + "}"), 401)
    res.set_header("WWW-Authenticate", "Bearer")
    return res

fn require_jwt(secret: str) fn(http.Request, fn(http.Request) http.Response) http.Response:
    return fn(req: http.Request, inner: fn(http.Request) http.Response) _require(req, inner, secret)

fn session(req: http.Request, secret: str) {str: str}:
    out: {str: str} = {}
    raw = req.cookie("session")
    dot = raw.find(".")
    if dot <= 0:
        return out
    body = raw[..dot]
    if not crypto.equal(_sign("session." + body, secret), raw[dot + 1..]):
        return out
    data: {str: str} = {}
    if not json.decode(crypto.base64url_decode(body), &data):
        return out
    if "_exp" in data:
        if int(time.now()) >= data["_exp"].to_int(0):
            return out
        data.remove("_exp")
    return data

fn set_session_for(res: mut http.Response, secret: str, data: {str: str}, max_age_seconds: int, attrs: str):
    d = data
    d["_exp"] = str(int(time.now()) + max_age_seconds)
    body = crypto.base64url(json.encode(d))
    extra = "Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Max-Age=" + str(max_age_seconds)
    if attrs != "":
        extra += "; " + attrs
    res.set_cookie_with("session", body + "." + _sign("session." + body, secret), extra)

fn set_session(res: mut http.Response, secret: str, data: {str: str}):
    set_session_for(&res, secret, data, 30 * 86400, "")

fn clear_session(res: mut http.Response):
    res.set_cookie_with("session", "", "Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Max-Age=0")

# with Result: user = auth.verify(token, secret)?   the subject ("sub");
#   Err: "auth: invalid token: expired"
fn verify(token: str, secret: str) Result[str, str]:
    t = jwt_verify(token, secret)
    if not t.ok:
        return Err("auth: invalid token: " + t.error)
    return Ok(t.subject)
```

## deps/grpc/client.tn

```tern
# Part of the grpc package (see grpc.tn): a small unary client, one connection per call
# (tests, tools, health checks; not a pooled, multiplexing client).

fn _read_frame(c: net.Conn, buf: mut str, at: mut int, typ: mut int, flags: mut int, sid: mut int, payload: mut str) bool:
    while len(buf) - at < 9:
        if c.refill(&buf, at, 65536) <= 0:
            return false
        at = 0
    n = (buf.byte(at) << 16) | (buf.byte(at + 1) << 8) | buf.byte(at + 2)
    while len(buf) - at < 9 + n:
        if c.refill(&buf, at, 65536 + n) <= 0:
            return false
        at = 0
    typ = buf.byte(at + 3)
    flags = buf.byte(at + 4)
    sid = _be32(buf, at + 5) & 0x7fffffff
    payload = buf[at + 9..at + 9 + n]
    at += 9 + n
    return true

# Calls method ("/pkg.Service/Method") on host:port (h2c) with one request message; the reply's
# status is UNAVAILABLE when the server can't be reached or the connection breaks.
fn call(host: str, port: int, method: str, metadata: {str: str}, message: str) Reply:
    c = net.connect(host, port)
    if not c.ok():
        return fail(UNAVAILABLE, net.error())
    r = _call(c, host, port, method, metadata, message, "\x86")
    c.close()
    return r

# The same over TLS (ALPN "h2"), checking the server's certificate against host.
fn call_tls(host: str, port: int, method: str, metadata: {str: str}, message: str) Reply:
    c = tls.connect_alpn(host, port, ["h2"])
    if not c.ok():
        return fail(UNAVAILABLE, tls.error())
    if tls.alpn(c) != "h2":
        c.close()
        return fail(UNAVAILABLE, "the server didn't agree to HTTP/2 (ALPN h2)")
    r = _call(c, host, port, method, metadata, message, "\x87")
    c.close()
    return r

fn _call(c: net.Conn, host: str, port: int, method: str, metadata: {str: str}, message: str, scheme: str) Reply:
    big = 1 << 30
    hello = PREFACE + frame(F_SETTINGS, 0, 0, _setting(2, 0) + _setting(4, big)) + _window(0, big)
    head = "\x83" + scheme + hpack_literal_idx(4, method) + hpack_literal_idx(1, host + ":" + str(port))
    head += hpack_literal_idx(31, "application/grpc") + hpack_literal("te", "trailers")
    for k, v in metadata:
        head += hpack_literal(k, v)
    if not c.write(hello + frame(F_HEADERS, END_HEADERS, 1, head)):
        return fail(UNAVAILABLE, net.error())
    body = "\x00" + _u32(len(message)) + message
    sent = 0
    conn_win = 65535
    win = 65535
    max_frame = 16384
    hp = hpack_decoder(hpack_tables(), 4096)
    buf = ""
    at = 0
    typ = 0
    flags = 0
    sid = 0
    p = ""
    data = ""
    status = -1
    msg = ""
    http = ""
    while true:
        # send what the windows allow
        out = ""
        while sent < len(body):
            n = min(min(len(body) - sent, max_frame), min(conn_win, win))
            if n <= 0:
                break
            out += frame(F_DATA, END_STREAM if sent + n == len(body) else 0, 1, body[sent..sent + n])
            sent += n
            conn_win -= n
            win -= n
        if out != "" and not c.write(out):
            return fail(UNAVAILABLE, net.error())
        if not _read_frame(c, &buf, &at, &typ, &flags, &sid, &p):
            return fail(UNAVAILABLE, "the connection closed before the answer")
        match typ:
            4:
                if flags & ACK == 0:
                    for k in 0..len(p) / 6:
                        id = (p.byte(k * 6) << 8) | p.byte(k * 6 + 1)
                        v = _be32(p, k * 6 + 2)
                        if id == 4:
                            win += v - 65535
                        elif id == 5:
                            max_frame = v
                    c.write(frame(F_SETTINGS, ACK, 0, ""))
            8:
                inc = _be32(p, 0) & 0x7fffffff
                if sid == 0:
                    conn_win += inc
                elif sid == 1:
                    win += inc
            6:
                if flags & ACK == 0:
                    c.write(frame(F_PING, ACK, 0, p))
            7:
                if len(p) >= 8 and _be32(p, 4) != 0:
                    return fail(UNAVAILABLE, "GOAWAY: " + p[8..])
            3:
                if sid == 1:
                    return fail(UNAVAILABLE, "stream reset: code " + str(_be32(p, 0)))
            0:
                if sid == 1:
                    a = 0
                    b = len(p)
                    if flags & PADDED != 0:
                        a = 1
                        b -= p.byte(0)
                    data += p[a..b]
                    if len(p) > 0:
                        c.write(_window(0, len(p)) + _window(1, len(p)))
            1 | 9:
                blk = p
                if typ == 1 and flags & PADDED != 0:
                    blk = p[1..len(p) - p.byte(0)]
                if typ == 1 and flags & PRIORITY_FLAG != 0:
                    blk = blk[5..]
                hdrs: [str] = []
                size = 0
                if not hpack_decode(&hp, blk, &hdrs, &size):
                    return fail(INTERNAL, "hpack: " + hp.err)
                i = 0
                while i < len(hdrs):
                    if hdrs[i] == "grpc-status":
                        status = hdrs[i + 1].to_int(UNKNOWN)
                    elif hdrs[i] == "grpc-message":
                        msg = _unpct(hdrs[i + 1])
                    elif hdrs[i] == ":status":
                        http = hdrs[i + 1]
                    i += 2
            _:
                pass
        if (typ == 0 or typ == 1) and sid == 1 and flags & END_STREAM != 0:
            break
    if status < 0:
        return fail(UNKNOWN if http == "200" else INTERNAL, "no grpc-status (HTTP " + http + ")")
    if status != OK:
        return fail(status, msg)
    if len(data) < 5 or _be32(data, 1) != len(data) - 5:
        return fail(INTERNAL, "bad response framing")
    return ok(data[5..])

fn _unhex(b: int) int:
    if b >= 48 and b <= 57:
        return b - 48
    if b >= 65 and b <= 70:
        return b - 55
    if b >= 97 and b <= 102:
        return b - 87
    return -1

fn _unpct(s: str) str:
    out = ""
    i = 0
    while i < len(s):
        if s[i] == "%" and i + 2 < len(s) and _unhex(s.byte(i + 1)) >= 0 and _unhex(s.byte(i + 2)) >= 0:
            out += chr(_unhex(s.byte(i + 1)) * 16 + _unhex(s.byte(i + 2)))
            i += 3
        else:
            out += s[i]
            i += 1
    return out
```

## deps/grpc/grpc.tn

```tern
# grpc: a gRPC server (unary calls) over HTTP/2, in Tern: what OTLP/gRPC exporters and most
# unary clients need. HTTP/2 over TLS (ALPN "h2", as gRPC clients do for https:// endpoints)
# or over cleartext with prior knowledge (h2c: the client starts with the HTTP/2 preface, as
# gRPC clients do for http:// endpoints), HPACK with Huffman, many concurrent streams per
# connection, flow control with generous windows, and gRPC's framing.
#
#   import grpc
#   fn handle(call: grpc.Call) grpc.Reply:
#       if call.method != "/helloworld.Greeter/SayHello":
#           return grpc.fail(grpc.UNIMPLEMENTED, "unknown method " + call.method)
#       if call.metadata.get("authorization", "") != "Bearer secret":
#           return grpc.fail(grpc.UNAUTHENTICATED, "bad key")
#       return grpc.ok(reply_bytes(call.message))       # call.message: the request (protobuf bytes)
#   fn main():
#       s = grpc.start("", 50051, handle, grpc.options())   # serves in tasks; returns at once
#       grpc.wait(s)                                     # until grpc.stop(s, ms) elsewhere
#
# grpc.start(host str, port int, h fn(Call) Reply, o Options) Server   ("" host: every address;
#     port 0: any free port, see grpc.port). A runtime error if the port can't be bound.
# grpc.start_tls(host str, port int, h fn(Call) Reply, o Options, cert str, key str) Server
#     the same over TLS: cert is the certificate chain, key its private key (PEM files; a runtime
#     error if they can't be loaded). The handshake must agree on "h2" by ALPN, as every gRPC
#     client offers; a client that doesn't offer it is refused. Clients check the certificate
#     against the name they dialed (a self-signed one: give the client it as its CA).
# grpc.port(s Server) int          grpc.wait(s Server)       grpc.serve(port, h): start + wait
# grpc.stop(s Server, drain_ms int)  stops accepting, sends GOAWAY to every connection, waits up
#     to drain_ms for the calls running to answer, then closes the connections.
# grpc.ok(body str) Reply          grpc.fail(status int, message str) Reply
# grpc.options() Options           the defaults below; change fields before start
#
# Call:     method ("/package.Service/Method"), metadata ({str: str}: the request's headers,
#           lowercase names, without the ":" pseudo-headers; repeated ones joined with ", "),
#           message (the request message's bytes), encoding ("" unless the message came
#           compressed: then its grpc-encoding, e.g. "gzip", one of Options.encodings, for the
#           handler to decompress), conn (the net.Conn it came on: conn.peer()).
# Reply:    status (grpc.OK ... grpc.UNAUTHENTICATED), message (grpc-message, for errors), body
#           (the response message's bytes, for OK).
# Options:  max_message (4 MiB: a bigger request gets RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED), max_frame (1 MiB,
#           the largest frame a client may send), max_header_list (64 KiB of headers per call),
#           max_streams (256 calls at once per connection; more are refused, and clients retry),
#           stream_window (4 MiB) and conn_window (64 MiB): flow-control windows, credited back
#           as data arrives, so a big export never waits on them; header_table (4096, HPACK's),
#           encodings ([]: compressions the handler decompresses; a compressed message in
#           another gets UNIMPLEMENTED with grpc-accept-encoding, as gRPC says).
#
# Status codes: OK 0, CANCELLED 1, UNKNOWN 2, INVALID_ARGUMENT 3, DEADLINE_EXCEEDED 4,
# NOT_FOUND 5, ALREADY_EXISTS 6, PERMISSION_DENIED 7, RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED 8,
# FAILED_PRECONDITION 9, ABORTED 10, OUT_OF_RANGE 11, UNIMPLEMENTED 12, INTERNAL 13,
# UNAVAILABLE 14, DATA_LOSS 15, UNAUTHENTICATED 16.
#
# Each call's handler runs in its own task (calls on one connection run at once); a
# connection's frames are read by one task and written by another, which batches what is
# ready into one write. Malformed input ends the stream (RST_STREAM) or the connection
# (GOAWAY) with the error code RFC 9113 gives; it never ends the program.
# Not supported: streaming RPCs (a call is one request message, one response), server push,
# HTTP/1 upgrade to h2c, client certificates (mTLS), and response compression (responses go
# uncompressed, which every client accepts).
# Client (tests, tools; one connection per call): grpc.call(host, port, method, metadata, message)
# Reply over h2c, grpc.call_tls(...) the same over TLS (verified; tls.trust(ca) for a private CA).
# Parts: hpack.tn (header compression), wire.tn (frames, the connection's reader and writer),
# client.tn. The package imports tls, so programs using it link aws-lc (see the tls module).
# Not available on wasm.

import net
import task
import time
import tls

const OK = 0
const CANCELLED = 1
const UNKNOWN = 2
const INVALID_ARGUMENT = 3
const DEADLINE_EXCEEDED = 4
const NOT_FOUND = 5
const ALREADY_EXISTS = 6
const PERMISSION_DENIED = 7
const RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED = 8
const FAILED_PRECONDITION = 9
const ABORTED = 10
const OUT_OF_RANGE = 11
const UNIMPLEMENTED = 12
const INTERNAL = 13
const UNAVAILABLE = 14
const DATA_LOSS = 15
const UNAUTHENTICATED = 16

struct Call:
    method: str
    metadata: {str: str}
    message: str
    encoding: str
    conn: net.Conn

struct Reply:
    status: int
    message: str
    body: str

struct Options:
    max_message: int
    max_frame: int
    max_header_list: int
    max_streams: int
    stream_window: int
    conn_window: int
    header_table: int
    encodings: [str]

# a live connection, for stop: its socket and its writer's queue
struct _Live:
    sock: net.Conn
    out: chan[Out]

struct Server:
    listener: net.Listener
    host: str
    port: int
    stopping: shared[bool]
    inflight: shared[int]               # calls whose handler hasn't answered yet
    conns: shared[{int: _Live}]         # by socket
    done: chan[int]                     # closed by stop (wait returns)
    tls: tls.Server                     # (ctx 0: cleartext, h2c)

fn options() Options:
    return Options(4 << 20, 1 << 20, 65536, 256, 4 << 20, 64 << 20, 4096, [])

fn ok(body: str) Reply:
    return Reply(OK, "", body)

fn fail(status: int, message: str) Reply:
    return Reply(status, message, "")

fn _clamp(v: int, lo: int, hi: int) int:
    return max(lo, min(v, hi))

fn start(host: str, port: int, handler: fn(Call) Reply, opts: Options) Server:
    return _start(host, port, handler, opts, tls.Server(0))

fn start_tls(host: str, port: int, handler: fn(Call) Reply, opts: Options, cert: str, key: str) Server:
    t = tls.server(cert, key)
    tls.set_alpn(t, ["h2"])
    return _start(host, port, handler, opts, t)

fn _start(host: str, port: int, handler: fn(Call) Reply, opts: Options, sec: tls.Server) Server:
    o = opts
    o.max_frame = _clamp(o.max_frame, 16384, 16777215)
    o.stream_window = _clamp(o.stream_window, 65535, 2147483647)
    o.conn_window = _clamp(o.conn_window, 65535, 2147483647)
    o.max_streams = max(o.max_streams, 1)
    o.header_table = _clamp(o.header_table, 0, 1 << 20)
    l = net.listen_on(host, port) if host != "" else net.listen(port)
    done: chan[int] = task.channel(1)
    s = Server(l, host, net.port(l), task.shared(false), task.shared(0), task.shared({0: _Live(net.Conn(-1), task.channel(1))}), done, sec)
    fn clear(m: mut {int: _Live}) int:
        m = {}
        return 0
    s.conns.update(clear)
    t = hpack_tables()
    task.spawn(fn() _accept_loop(s, handler, o, t))
    return s

fn port(s: Server) int:
    return s.port

fn wait(s: Server):
    x = 0
    while s.done.next(&x):
        pass

fn serve(port: int, handler: fn(Call) Reply):
    wait(start("", port, handler, options()))

fn _accept_loop(s: Server, handler: fn(Call) Reply, o: Options, t: Tables):
    while true:
        c = net.accept(s.listener)
        if s.stopping.get():
            c.close()
            break
        task.spawn(fn() _serve_conn(s, c, handler, o, t))

fn stop(s: Server, drain_ms: int):
    fn flag(b: mut bool) bool:
        was = b
        b = true
        return was
    if s.stopping.update(flag):
        return
    # wake the accept loop (it sees stopping and ends), then close the listener
    wake = net.connect("127.0.0.1" if s.host == "" or s.host == "0.0.0.0" else s.host, s.port)
    wake.close()
    task.sleep(10)
    net.stop(s.listener)
    live = s.conns.get()
    for fd, lv in live:
        lv.out.send(Out.Raw(_goaway(2147483647, NO_ERROR, "server stopping")))
    deadline = time.mono_ms() + drain_ms
    while s.inflight.get() > 0 and time.mono_ms() < deadline:
        task.sleep(5)
    task.sleep(20)                        # (the writers send the last answers)
    live = s.conns.get()
    for fd, lv in live:
        lv.sock.close()
    s.done.close()
```

## deps/grpc/hpack.tn

```tern
# Part of the grpc package (see grpc.tn): HPACK (RFC 7541), the header compression of HTTP/2.
# The decoder has the static table, a dynamic table (a ring of entries, evicted oldest first as
# the table's size says), integers and string literals, and Huffman-coded strings (a 4-bit
# state machine built at start from the code table below, like nghttp2's). The encoder writes
# literals without indexing and without Huffman: responses are small, and it keeps no state.

# the Huffman code (RFC 7541 appendix B): "code.bits" for bytes 0..255, then EOS
const HUFFMAN = "1ff8.13 7fffd8.23 fffffe2.28 fffffe3.28 fffffe4.28 fffffe5.28 fffffe6.28 fffffe7.28 fffffe8.28 ffffea.24 3ffffffc.30 fffffe9.28 fffffea.28 3ffffffd.30 fffffeb.28 fffffec.28 fffffed.28 fffffee.28 fffffef.28 ffffff0.28 ffffff1.28 ffffff2.28 3ffffffe.30 ffffff3.28 ffffff4.28 ffffff5.28 ffffff6.28 ffffff7.28 ffffff8.28 ffffff9.28 ffffffa.28 ffffffb.28 14.6 3f8.10 3f9.10 ffa.12 1ff9.13 15.6 f8.8 7fa.11 3fa.10 3fb.10 f9.8 7fb.11 fa.8 16.6 17.6 18.6 0.5 1.5 2.5 19.6 1a.6 1b.6 1c.6 1d.6 1e.6 1f.6 5c.7 fb.8 7ffc.15 20.6 ffb.12 3fc.10 1ffa.13 21.6 5d.7 5e.7 5f.7 60.7 61.7 62.7 63.7 64.7 65.7 66.7 67.7 68.7 69.7 6a.7 6b.7 6c.7 6d.7 6e.7 6f.7 70.7 71.7 72.7 fc.8 73.7 fd.8 1ffb.13 7fff0.19 1ffc.13 3ffc.14 22.6 7ffd.15 3.5 23.6 4.5 24.6 5.5 25.6 26.6 27.6 6.5 74.7 75.7 28.6 29.6 2a.6 7.5 2b.6 76.7 2c.6 8.5 9.5 2d.6 77.7 78.7 79.7 7a.7 7b.7 7ffe.15 7fc.11 3ffd.14 1ffd.13 ffffffc.28 fffe6.20 3fffd2.22 fffe7.20 fffe8.20 3fffd3.22 3fffd4.22 3fffd5.22 7fffd9.23 3fffd6.22 7fffda.23 7fffdb.23 7fffdc.23 7fffdd.23 7fffde.23 ffffeb.24 7fffdf.23 ffffec.24 ffffed.24 3fffd7.22 7fffe0.23 ffffee.24 7fffe1.23 7fffe2.23 7fffe3.23 7fffe4.23 1fffdc.21 3fffd8.22 7fffe5.23 3fffd9.22 7fffe6.23 7fffe7.23 ffffef.24 3fffda.22 1fffdd.21 fffe9.20 3fffdb.22 3fffdc.22 7fffe8.23 7fffe9.23 1fffde.21 7fffea.23 3fffdd.22 3fffde.22 fffff0.24 1fffdf.21 3fffdf.22 7fffeb.23 7fffec.23 1fffe0.21 1fffe1.21 3fffe0.22 1fffe2.21 7fffed.23 3fffe1.22 7fffee.23 7fffef.23 fffea.20 3fffe2.22 3fffe3.22 3fffe4.22 7ffff0.23 3fffe5.22 3fffe6.22 7ffff1.23 3ffffe0.26 3ffffe1.26 fffeb.20 7fff1.19 3fffe7.22 7ffff2.23 3fffe8.22 1ffffec.25 3ffffe2.26 3ffffe3.26 3ffffe4.26 7ffffde.27 7ffffdf.27 3ffffe5.26 fffff1.24 1ffffed.25 7fff2.19 1fffe3.21 3ffffe6.26 7ffffe0.27 7ffffe1.27 3ffffe7.26 7ffffe2.27 fffff2.24 1fffe4.21 1fffe5.21 3ffffe8.26 3ffffe9.26 ffffffd.28 7ffffe3.27 7ffffe4.27 7ffffe5.27 fffec.20 fffff3.24 fffed.20 1fffe6.21 3fffe9.22 1fffe7.21 1fffe8.21 7ffff3.23 3fffea.22 3fffeb.22 1ffffee.25 1ffffef.25 fffff4.24 fffff5.24 3ffffea.26 7ffff4.23 3ffffeb.26 7ffffe6.27 3ffffec.26 3ffffed.26 7ffffe7.27 7ffffe8.27 7ffffe9.27 7ffffea.27 7ffffeb.27 ffffffe.28 7ffffec.27 7ffffed.27 7ffffee.27 7ffffef.27 7fffff0.27 3ffffee.26 3fffffff.30"

# the static table (RFC 7541 appendix A): "name=value|..." for indexes 1..61
const STATIC = ":authority=|:method=GET|:method=POST|:path=/|:path=/index.html|:scheme=http|:scheme=https|:status=200|:status=204|:status=206|:status=304|:status=400|:status=404|:status=500|accept-charset=|accept-encoding=gzip, deflate|accept-language=|accept-ranges=|accept=|access-control-allow-origin=|age=|allow=|authorization=|cache-control=|content-disposition=|content-encoding=|content-language=|content-length=|content-location=|content-range=|content-type=|cookie=|date=|etag=|expect=|expires=|from=|host=|if-match=|if-modified-since=|if-none-match=|if-range=|if-unmodified-since=|last-modified=|link=|location=|max-forwards=|proxy-authenticate=|proxy-authorization=|range=|referer=|refresh=|retry-after=|server=|set-cookie=|strict-transport-security=|transfer-encoding=|user-agent=|vary=|via=|www-authenticate="

# The tables every decoder shares (built once by hpack_tables; copies are O(1)).
struct Tables:
    names: [str]                # the static table, index 1.. at [i - 1]
    values: [str]
    fsm: [int]                  # Huffman: state * 16 + nibble -> next | sym + 1 << 8 | flags
    accept: [bool]              # a state where the string may end (only EOS-prefix padding)

# An HPACK decoder: one per connection, fed every header block in order.
struct Hpack:
    t: Tables
    ring_names: [str]           # the dynamic table: a ring, newest at head
    ring_values: [str]
    head: int                   # where the next entry goes
    count: int                  # entries in the table
    size: int                   # their size (RFC 7541 4.1: name + value + 32 each)
    max_size: int               # the table's current limit (size updates)
    limit: int                  # the most a size update may ask for (SETTINGS_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE)
    err: str                    # why the last decode failed

const H_EMIT = 256              # (fsm entry flags)
const H_FAIL = 1 << 17

fn _hex(s: str) int:
    n = 0
    for c in s:
        b = c.byte(0)
        n = n * 16 + (b - 48 if b <= 57 else b - 87)
    return n

# Builds the static table and the Huffman state machine.
fn hpack_tables() Tables:
    names: [str] = []
    values: [str] = []
    for e in STATIC.split("|"):
        i = e.find("=")
        names.push(e[..i])
        values.push(e[i + 1..])
    # the code tree: internal nodes 0.. (0 the root); a child >= 0 is a node, < 0 a symbol (-sym - 1)
    left = [0]
    right = [0]
    left[0] = 1 << 40
    right[0] = 1 << 40
    unset = 1 << 40
    for sym, e in HUFFMAN.split(" "):
        dot = e.find(".")
        code = _hex(e[..dot])
        bits = e[dot + 1..].to_int(0)
        node = 0
        for k in 0..bits:
            bit = (code >> (bits - 1 - k)) & 1
            last = k == bits - 1
            nxt = left[node] if bit == 0 else right[node]
            if last:
                if bit == 0:
                    left[node] = -sym - 1
                else:
                    right[node] = -sym - 1
            else:
                if nxt == unset:
                    nxt = len(left)
                    left.push(unset)
                    right.push(unset)
                    if bit == 0:
                        left[node] = nxt
                    else:
                        right[node] = nxt
                node = nxt
    n = len(left)
    # the states that may end a string: the root, and up to 7 one-bits from it
    accept: [bool] = []
    for i in 0..n:
        accept.push(false)
    accept[0] = true
    node = 0
    for k in 0..7:
        node = right[node]
        if node < 0:
            break
        accept[node] = true
    fsm: [int] = []
    for s in 0..n:
        for v in 0..16:
            cur = s
            emit = -1
            fail = false
            for k in 0..4:
                bit = (v >> (3 - k)) & 1
                nxt = left[cur] if bit == 0 else right[cur]
                if nxt < 0:
                    sym = -nxt - 1
                    if sym == 256 or emit >= 0:
                        fail = true              # EOS in a string (or can't happen: two in 4 bits)
                        break
                    emit = sym
                    cur = 0
                elif nxt == unset:
                    fail = true
                    break
                else:
                    cur = nxt
            fsm.push(H_FAIL if fail else cur | ((emit + 1) << 8))
    return Tables(names, values, fsm, accept)

fn hpack_decoder(t: Tables, limit: int) Hpack:
    cap = limit / 32 + 1
    rn: [str] = []
    rv: [str] = []
    for i in 0..cap:
        rn.push("")
        rv.push("")
    return Hpack(t, rn, rv, 0, 0, 0, limit, limit, "")

# Decodes a Huffman-coded string; false when it's malformed.
fn huffman_decode(t: Tables, s: str, a: int, b: int, out: mut str) bool:
    st = 0
    for i in a..b:
        x = s.byte(i)
        e = t.fsm[st * 16 + (x >> 4)]
        if e == H_FAIL:
            return false
        if e >= H_EMIT:
            out += chr((e >> 8) - 1)
        st = e & 255
        e = t.fsm[st * 16 + (x & 15)]
        if e == H_FAIL:
            return false
        if e >= H_EMIT:
            out += chr((e >> 8) - 1)
        st = e & 255
    return t.accept[st]

# (the tree has 256 internal nodes, so a state fits the low 8 bits)

# An HPACK integer with an n-bit prefix at s[pos]; -1 when it's truncated or too big.
fn _int(s: str, pos: mut int, n: int) int:
    if pos >= len(s):
        return -1
    mask = (1 << n) - 1
    v = s.byte(pos) & mask
    pos += 1
    if v < mask:
        return v
    m = 0
    while true:
        if pos >= len(s) or m > 28:
            return -1
        b = s.byte(pos)
        pos += 1
        v += (b & 127) << m
        m += 7
        if b < 128:
            break
    return v if v < (1 << 32) else -1

fn _string(h: Hpack, s: str, pos: mut int, out: mut str) bool:
    if pos >= len(s):
        return false
    huff = s.byte(pos) >= 128
    n = _int(s, &pos, 7)
    if n < 0 or pos + n > len(s):
        return false
    if huff:
        out = ""
        ok = huffman_decode(h.t, s, pos, pos + n, &out)
        pos += n
        return ok
    out = s[pos..pos + n]
    pos += n
    return true

# entry i (1-based, 1..61 static, 62.. dynamic, newest first)
fn _entry(h: Hpack, i: int, name: mut str, value: mut str) bool:
    if i >= 1 and i <= 61:
        name = h.t.names[i - 1]
        value = h.t.values[i - 1]
        return true
    d = i - 62
    if i < 1 or d >= h.count:
        return false
    cap = len(h.ring_names)
    at = (h.head - 1 - d + cap * 2) % cap
    name = h.ring_names[at]
    value = h.ring_values[at]
    return true

fn _evict(h: mut Hpack, room: int):
    cap = len(h.ring_names)
    while h.count > 0 and h.size + room > h.max_size:
        at = (h.head - h.count + cap) % cap
        h.size -= len(h.ring_names[at]) + len(h.ring_values[at]) + 32
        h.ring_names[at] = ""
        h.ring_values[at] = ""
        h.count -= 1

fn _add(h: mut Hpack, name: str, value: str):
    sz = len(name) + len(value) + 32
    _evict(&h, sz)
    if sz > h.max_size:
        return                          # bigger than the table: it just empties it (4.4)
    cap = len(h.ring_names)
    h.ring_names[h.head] = name
    h.ring_values[h.head] = value
    h.head = (h.head + 1) % cap
    h.count += 1
    h.size += sz

fn _fail(h: mut Hpack, why: str) bool:
    h.err = why
    return false
```
