```tern
# Decodes one header block onto out (name, value, name, value, ...). False: a compression error
# (h.err says what); the connection can't go on then, since the table is out of step.
# `size` gets the header list's size (RFC 7540 6.5.2: name + value + 32 each).
fn hpack_decode(h: mut Hpack, block: str, out: mut [str], size: mut int) bool:
    pos = 0
    n = len(block)
    first = true
    while pos < n:
        b = block.byte(pos)
        name = ""
        value = ""
        if b >= 128:                                    # indexed
            i = _int(block, &pos, 7)
            if i <= 0 or not _entry(h, i, &name, &value):
                return _fail(&h, "bad index")
        elif b >= 64 or b < 32:                         # a literal: with indexing (01), without (0000) or never (0001)
            idx = b >= 64
            i = _int(block, &pos, 6 if idx else 4)
            if i < 0:
                return _fail(&h, "bad literal")
            if i == 0:
                if not _string(h, block, &pos, &name):
                    return _fail(&h, "bad name")
            elif not _entry(h, i, &name, &value):
                return _fail(&h, "bad name index")
            if not _string(h, block, &pos, &value):
                return _fail(&h, "bad value")
            if idx:
                _add(&h, name, value)
        else:                                           # 001: dynamic table size update
            if not first:
                return _fail(&h, "size update after a header")
            m = _int(block, &pos, 5)
            if m < 0 or m > h.limit:
                return _fail(&h, "size update too big")
            h.max_size = m
            _evict(&h, 0)
            continue
        first = false
        size += len(name) + len(value) + 32
        out.push(name)
        out.push(value)
    return true

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- encoding

fn hpack_int(prefix: int, n: int, value: int) str:
    v = value
    mask = (1 << n) - 1
    if v < mask:
        return chr(prefix | v)
    out = chr(prefix | mask)
    v -= mask
    while v >= 128:
        out += chr((v & 127) | 128)
        v >>= 7
    return out + chr(v)

# a header as a literal without indexing, new name (no Huffman)
fn hpack_literal(name: str, value: str) str:
    return "\x00" + hpack_int(0, 7, len(name)) + name + hpack_int(0, 7, len(value)) + value

# a header as a literal without indexing, its name from the static table
fn hpack_literal_idx(index: int, value: str) str:
    return hpack_int(0, 4, index) + hpack_int(0, 7, len(value)) + value
```

## deps/grpc/wire.tn

```tern
# Part of the grpc package (see grpc.tn): HTTP/2 frames (RFC 9113), a connection's reader (a
# Session: frames in, calls out) and its writer (the only task that writes to the socket).

const PREFACE = "PRI * HTTP/2.0\r\n\r\nSM\r\n\r\n"

# frame types
const F_DATA = 0
const F_HEADERS = 1
const F_PRIORITY = 2
const F_RST = 3
const F_SETTINGS = 4
const F_PUSH = 5
const F_PING = 6
const F_GOAWAY = 7
const F_WINDOW = 8
const F_CONTINUATION = 9

# flags
const END_STREAM = 1
const ACK = 1
const END_HEADERS = 4
const PADDED = 8
const PRIORITY_FLAG = 32

# error codes
const NO_ERROR = 0
const PROTOCOL_ERROR = 1
const INTERNAL_ERROR = 2
const FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR = 3
const STREAM_CLOSED = 5
const FRAME_SIZE_ERROR = 6
const REFUSED_STREAM = 7
const CANCEL = 8
const COMPRESSION_ERROR = 9
const ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM = 11

# what the writer is asked to do
enum Out:
    Raw(bytes: str)                             # frames, ready to send
    Answer(sid: int, head: str, body: str, trailers: str)   # a call's answer ("" head: trailers only)
    Window(sid: int, inc: int)                  # the client's WINDOW_UPDATE
    Settings(window: int, frame: int)           # the client's SETTINGS (-1: not given); ack them
    Reset(sid: int)                             # the client reset the stream: drop its answer
    Close(answers: int)                         # the reader is done: close after this many answers

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- frames

fn _u32(n: int) str:
    return chr((n >> 24) & 255) + chr((n >> 16) & 255) + chr((n >> 8) & 255) + chr(n & 255)

fn _be32(s: str, i: int) int:
    return (s.byte(i) << 24) | (s.byte(i + 1) << 16) | (s.byte(i + 2) << 8) | s.byte(i + 3)

fn frame(typ: int, flags: int, sid: int, payload: str) str:
    n = len(payload)
    return chr((n >> 16) & 255) + chr((n >> 8) & 255) + chr(n & 255) + chr(typ) + chr(flags) + _u32(sid) + payload

fn _goaway(last: int, code: int, debug: str) str:
    return frame(F_GOAWAY, 0, 0, _u32(last) + _u32(code) + debug)

fn _rst(sid: int, code: int) str:
    return frame(F_RST, 0, sid, _u32(code))

fn _window(sid: int, inc: int) str:
    return frame(F_WINDOW, 0, sid, _u32(inc))

fn _setting(id: int, v: int) str:
    return chr(0) + chr(id) + _u32(v)

# grpc-message: percent-encoded (gRPC's HTTP/2 mapping)
fn _pct(s: str) str:
    out = ""
    hex = "0123456789ABCDEF"
    for c in s:
        b = c.byte(0)
        if b < 32 or b > 126 or b == 37:
            out += "%" + hex[b >> 4] + hex[b & 15]
        else:
            out += c
    return out

fn _grpc_head() str:
    return "\x88" + hpack_literal_idx(31, "application/grpc")     # :status 200, content-type

# the frames a call's answer turns into: head, body, trailers (encoded header blocks)
fn _answer(sid: int, r: Reply, encodings: str) Out:
    if r.status == OK:
        head = _grpc_head()
        if encodings != "":
            head += hpack_literal("grpc-accept-encoding", encodings)
        body = "\x00" + _u32(len(r.body)) + r.body
        return Out.Answer(sid, head, body, hpack_literal("grpc-status", "0"))
    t = _grpc_head() + hpack_literal("grpc-status", str(r.status))
    if r.message != "":
        t += hpack_literal("grpc-message", _pct(r.message))
    if encodings != "" and r.status == UNIMPLEMENTED:
        t += hpack_literal("grpc-accept-encoding", encodings)
    return Out.Answer(sid, "", "", t)

# a plain HTTP answer (not a gRPC request: wrong method or content type)
fn _http_answer(sid: int, status: int) Out:
    return Out.Answer(sid, "", "", hpack_literal_idx(8, str(status)) + hpack_literal("grpc-status", str(UNKNOWN if status != 415 else INTERNAL)))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the reader

struct Stream:
    method: str
    meta: {str: str}
    data: str                   # the DATA received (gRPC-framed messages)
    window: int                 # what the client may still send on it
    unacked: int                # received, not yet credited back
    dead: bool                  # answered early (too big): what else arrives is dropped
    encoding: str

struct Session:
    sock: net.Conn
    out: chan[Out]
    o: Options
    accept_enc: str             # Options.encodings, joined (grpc-accept-encoding)
    hp: Hpack
    streams: {int: Stream}
    last: int                   # the highest stream id the client opened
    cont: int                   # a header block in progress (CONTINUATION expected on it), else 0
    block: str
    block_end: bool             # ... and whether its HEADERS had END_STREAM
    window: int                 # what the client may still send on the connection
    unacked: int
    ctl: str                    # control frames to send when the reader next waits
    started: int                # calls handed to handlers
    live: shared[int]           # this connection's calls running
    inflight: shared[int]       # the server's
    h: fn(Call) Reply
    buf: str
    at: int
    err: int                    # a connection error (GOAWAY sent): -1 while fine
    seen_settings: bool

fn _dec(n: mut int) int:
    n -= 1
    return n

fn _inc(n: mut int) int:
    n += 1
    return n

fn new_session(sock: net.Conn, out: chan[Out], o: Options, t: Tables, h: fn(Call) Reply, inflight: shared[int]) Session:
    return Session(sock, out, o, ", ".join(o.encodings), hpack_decoder(t, o.header_table), {}, 0, 0, "", false, o.conn_window, 0, "", 0, task.shared(0), inflight, h, "", 0, -1, false)

fn _conn_error(s: mut Session, code: int, why: str):
    if s.err < 0:
        s.err = code
        s.ctl += _goaway(s.last, code, why)

fn _stream_error(s: mut Session, sid: int, code: int):
    s.ctl += _rst(sid, code)
    s.streams.remove(sid)

# our first frames: SETTINGS, and the connection window
fn _hello(s: mut Session):
    p = _setting(3, s.o.max_streams) + _setting(4, s.o.stream_window) + _setting(5, s.o.max_frame) + _setting(6, s.o.max_header_list)
    s.ctl += frame(F_SETTINGS, 0, 0, p)
    if s.o.conn_window > 65535:
        s.ctl += _window(0, s.o.conn_window - 65535)

fn _run_call(h: fn(Call) Reply, c: Call, data: str, sid: int, out: chan[Out], enc: str, live: shared[int], inflight: shared[int]):
    r = h(Call(c.method, c.metadata, data[5..], c.encoding, c.conn))   # (the copy: in the call's task)
    out.send(_answer(sid, r, enc))
    live.update(_dec)
    inflight.update(_dec)

# the whole request is in: answer it (a handler, in a task) or refuse it
fn _finish(s: mut Session, sid: int):
    st = s.streams[sid]
    s.streams.remove(sid)
    if st.dead:
        return
    # every call gets exactly one answer (s.started counts them for the writer)
    s.started += 1
    d = st.data
    if len(d) < 5:
        s.out.send(_answer(sid, fail(INTERNAL, "no request message"), s.accept_enc))
        return
    n = _be32(d, 1)
    if n != len(d) - 5:
        why = "more than one request message (streaming calls aren't supported)" if n < len(d) - 5 else "the request message is cut short"
        s.out.send(_answer(sid, fail(INTERNAL if n > len(d) - 5 else UNIMPLEMENTED, why), s.accept_enc))
        return
    flag = d.byte(0)
    enc = ""
    if flag == 1:
        enc = st.encoding
        if enc == "" or enc == "identity" or not (enc in s.o.encodings):
            s.out.send(_answer(sid, fail(UNIMPLEMENTED, "grpc-encoding " + (enc if enc != "" else "(none)") + " isn't supported"), s.accept_enc))
            return
    elif flag != 0:
        s.out.send(_answer(sid, fail(INTERNAL, "bad message flag"), s.accept_enc))
        return
    c = Call(st.method, st.meta, "", enc, s.sock)
    s.live.update(_inc)
    s.inflight.update(_inc)
    handler = s.h
    out = s.out
    ae = s.accept_enc
    live = s.live
    inflight = s.inflight
    task.spawn(fn() _run_call(handler, c, d, sid, out, ae, live, inflight))  # (a captured `h` breaks the C: tern bug)

fn _bad_name(n: str) bool:
    for c in n:
        b = c.byte(0)
        if (b >= 65 and b <= 90) or b <= 32 or b >= 127 or b == 58:
            return true
    return false

fn _bad_value(v: str) bool:
    return v.contains("\r") or v.contains("\n") or v.contains("\0")

# a complete header block for stream sid
fn _headers(s: mut Session, sid: int, block: str, end: bool):
    hdrs: [str] = []
    size = 0
    if not hpack_decode(&s.hp, block, &hdrs, &size):
        why = s.hp.err
        _conn_error(&s, COMPRESSION_ERROR, why)
        return
    if sid in s.streams:                        # trailers (a client sends none for unary calls)
        if not end:
            _stream_error(&s, sid, PROTOCOL_ERROR)
        else:
            _finish(&s, sid)
        return
    if sid <= s.last or sid % 2 == 0:
        _conn_error(&s, PROTOCOL_ERROR, "stream id went back")
        return
    s.last = sid
    if s.err >= 0:
        return
    if size > s.o.max_header_list:
        s.ctl += _rst(sid, REFUSED_STREAM)      # (a stream error: the table is in step)
        s.started += 1
        s.out.send(_answer(sid, fail(RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, "headers too large"), s.accept_enc))
        return
    if len(s.streams) + s.live.get() >= s.o.max_streams:
        s.ctl += _rst(sid, REFUSED_STREAM)
        return
    st = Stream("", {}, "", s.o.stream_window, 0, false, "")
    method = ""
    ctype = ""
    regular = false
    malformed = false
    i = 0
    while i < len(hdrs):
        n = hdrs[i]
        v = hdrs[i + 1]
        i += 2
        if _bad_value(v):
            malformed = true
        if n.starts_with(":"):
            if regular:
                malformed = true
            match n:
                ":method":
                    method = v
                ":path":
                    st.method = v
                ":scheme" | ":authority":
                    pass
                _:
                    malformed = true
            continue
        regular = true
        if _bad_name(n) or n == "connection" or n == "keep-alive" or n == "transfer-encoding" or n == "upgrade" or n == "proxy-connection":
            malformed = true
            continue
        if n == "content-type":
            ctype = v
        elif n == "grpc-encoding":
            st.encoding = v
        if n in st.meta:
            st.meta[n] = st.meta[n] + ", " + v
        else:
            st.meta[n] = v
    if malformed or st.method == "":
        _stream_error(&s, sid, PROTOCOL_ERROR)
        return
    if method != "POST" or not ctype.starts_with("application/grpc"):
        s.started += 1
        s.out.send(_http_answer(sid, 405 if method != "POST" else 415))
        if not end:
            st.dead = true
            s.streams[sid] = st
        return
    s.streams[sid] = st
    if end:
        _finish(&s, sid)

fn _data(s: mut Session, sid: int, flags: int, p: int, n: int):
    # p: the payload's start in s.buf, n: its length (the whole frame counts for flow control)
    s.window -= n
    s.unacked += n
    if s.window < 0:
        _conn_error(&s, FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR, "sent past the connection window")
        return
    if s.unacked >= s.o.conn_window / 2:
        s.ctl += _window(0, s.unacked)
        s.window += s.unacked
        s.unacked = 0
    a = p
    b = p + n
    if flags & PADDED != 0:
        if n < 1:
            _conn_error(&s, PROTOCOL_ERROR, "padding")
            return
        pad = s.buf.byte(p)
        a += 1
        if pad > b - a:
            _conn_error(&s, PROTOCOL_ERROR, "padding longer than the frame")
            return
        b -= pad
    if not (sid in s.streams):
        if sid > s.last or sid == 0:
            _conn_error(&s, PROTOCOL_ERROR, "DATA on a stream that isn't open")
        return                                  # (a stream we answered or reset: dropped)
    s.streams[sid].window -= n
    if s.streams[sid].window < 0:
        _stream_error(&s, sid, FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR)
        return
    if not s.streams[sid].dead:
        if len(s.streams[sid].data) + (b - a) > s.o.max_message + 5:
            s.streams[sid].dead = true
            s.streams[sid].data = ""
            s.started += 1
            s.out.send(_answer(sid, fail(RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, f"the request is larger than {s.o.max_message} bytes"), s.accept_enc))
            if flags & END_STREAM == 0:
                s.ctl += _rst(sid, NO_ERROR)      # (after the answer: the writer sends ctl first, see _flush)
        else:
            s.streams[sid].data += s.buf[a..b]
    if flags & END_STREAM != 0:
        _finish(&s, sid)
        return
    s.streams[sid].unacked += n
    if s.streams[sid].unacked >= s.o.stream_window / 2 and not s.streams[sid].dead:
        u = s.streams[sid].unacked
        s.ctl += _window(sid, u)
        s.streams[sid].window += u
        s.streams[sid].unacked = 0

fn _settings(s: mut Session, flags: int, p: int, n: int):
    if flags & ACK != 0:
        if n != 0:
            _conn_error(&s, FRAME_SIZE_ERROR, "SETTINGS ack with a payload")
        return
    if n % 6 != 0:
        _conn_error(&s, FRAME_SIZE_ERROR, "SETTINGS length")
        return
    win = -1
    fr = -1
    for k in 0..n / 6:
        id = (s.buf.byte(p + k * 6) << 8) | s.buf.byte(p + k * 6 + 1)
        v = _be32(s.buf, p + k * 6 + 2)
        match id:
            2:
                if v > 1:
                    _conn_error(&s, PROTOCOL_ERROR, "ENABLE_PUSH")
                    return
            4:
                if v > 2147483647:
                    _conn_error(&s, FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR, "INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE")
                    return
                win = v
            5:
                if v < 16384 or v > 16777215:
                    _conn_error(&s, PROTOCOL_ERROR, "MAX_FRAME_SIZE")
                    return
                fr = v
            _:
                pass                            # table size (our encoder has no table), limits
    s.out.send(Out.Settings(win, fr))           # the writer applies them, then acks

# Handles the complete frames in s.buf from s.at on. False once the connection is done.
fn process(s: mut Session) bool:
    while s.err < 0:
        have = len(s.buf) - s.at
        if have < 9:
            return true
        at = s.at
        n = (s.buf.byte(at) << 16) | (s.buf.byte(at + 1) << 8) | s.buf.byte(at + 2)
        typ = s.buf.byte(at + 3)
        flags = s.buf.byte(at + 4)
        sid = _be32(s.buf, at + 5) & 0x7fffffff
        if n > s.o.max_frame:
            _conn_error(&s, FRAME_SIZE_ERROR, "frame larger than MAX_FRAME_SIZE")
            return false
        if have < 9 + n:
            return true
        p = at + 9
        s.at = at + 9 + n
        if not s.seen_settings:
            if typ != F_SETTINGS or flags & ACK != 0:
                _conn_error(&s, PROTOCOL_ERROR, "expected SETTINGS first")
                return false
            s.seen_settings = true
        if s.cont != 0 and (typ != F_CONTINUATION or sid != s.cont):
            _conn_error(&s, PROTOCOL_ERROR, "expected CONTINUATION")
            return false
        match typ:
            0:
                if sid == 0:
                    _conn_error(&s, PROTOCOL_ERROR, "DATA on stream 0")
                else:
                    _data(&s, sid, flags, p, n)
            1:
                if sid == 0:
                    _conn_error(&s, PROTOCOL_ERROR, "HEADERS on stream 0")
                    return false
                a = p
                b = p + n
                if flags & PADDED != 0:
                    if n < 1:
                        _conn_error(&s, FRAME_SIZE_ERROR, "padding")
                        return false
                    pad = s.buf.byte(p)
                    a += 1
                    b -= pad
                if flags & PRIORITY_FLAG != 0:
                    a += 5
                if b < a:
                    _conn_error(&s, PROTOCOL_ERROR, "padding longer than the frame")
                    return false
                if b - a > s.o.max_header_list * 2 + 1024:
                    _conn_error(&s, ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM, "header block too large")
                    return false
                if flags & END_HEADERS != 0:
                    _headers(&s, sid, s.buf[a..b], flags & END_STREAM != 0)
                else:
                    s.cont = sid
                    s.block = s.buf[a..b]
                    s.block_end = flags & END_STREAM != 0
            9:
                if s.cont == 0:
                    _conn_error(&s, PROTOCOL_ERROR, "CONTINUATION without HEADERS")
                    return false
                s.block += s.buf[p..p + n]
                if len(s.block) > s.o.max_header_list * 2 + 1024:
                    _conn_error(&s, ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM, "header block too large")
                    return false
                if flags & END_HEADERS != 0:
                    blk = s.block
                    s.block = ""
                    s.cont = 0
                    end = s.block_end
                    _headers(&s, sid, blk, end)
            2:
                if n != 5:
                    _conn_error(&s, FRAME_SIZE_ERROR, "PRIORITY length")
            3:
                if n != 4 or sid == 0:
                    _conn_error(&s, PROTOCOL_ERROR if sid == 0 else FRAME_SIZE_ERROR, "RST_STREAM")
                elif sid > s.last:
                    _conn_error(&s, PROTOCOL_ERROR, "RST_STREAM on an idle stream")
                else:
                    if sid in s.streams:
                        if s.streams[sid].dead:
                            s.streams.remove(sid)
                        else:
                            s.streams.remove(sid)
                    s.out.send(Out.Reset(sid))
            4:
                if sid != 0:
                    _conn_error(&s, PROTOCOL_ERROR, "SETTINGS on a stream")
                else:
                    _settings(&s, flags, p, n)
            5:
                _conn_error(&s, PROTOCOL_ERROR, "a client can't push")
            6:
                if n != 8 or sid != 0:
                    _conn_error(&s, FRAME_SIZE_ERROR if n != 8 else PROTOCOL_ERROR, "PING")
                elif flags & ACK == 0:
                    s.ctl += frame(F_PING, ACK, 0, s.buf[p..p + 8])
            7:
                if sid != 0:
                    _conn_error(&s, PROTOCOL_ERROR, "GOAWAY on a stream")
                # the client is leaving: answer what's open, then it closes
            8:
                if n != 4:
                    _conn_error(&s, FRAME_SIZE_ERROR, "WINDOW_UPDATE length")
                else:
                    inc = _be32(s.buf, p) & 0x7fffffff
                    if inc == 0:
                        if sid == 0:
                            _conn_error(&s, PROTOCOL_ERROR, "zero WINDOW_UPDATE")
                        elif sid in s.streams:
                            _stream_error(&s, sid, PROTOCOL_ERROR)
                    elif sid > s.last and sid != 0:
                        _conn_error(&s, PROTOCOL_ERROR, "WINDOW_UPDATE on an idle stream")
                    else:
                        s.out.send(Out.Window(sid, inc))
            _:
                pass                            # unknown types are ignored
    return false

# sends the control frames gathered so far (before the reader waits)
fn _flush(s: mut Session):
    if s.ctl != "":
        s.out.send(Out.Raw(s.ctl))
        s.ctl = ""

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the writer

struct Pending:
    sid: int
    body: str
    at: int                     # sent so far
    window: int
    trailers: str

fn _headers_frames(sid: int, block: str, end: bool, max_frame: int) str:
    fl = END_STREAM if end else 0
    if len(block) <= max_frame:
        return frame(F_HEADERS, fl | END_HEADERS, sid, block)
    out = frame(F_HEADERS, fl, sid, block[..max_frame])
    i = max_frame
    while i < len(block):
        j = min(i + max_frame, len(block))
        out += frame(F_CONTINUATION, END_HEADERS if j == len(block) else 0, sid, block[i..j])
        i = j
    return out

struct Writer:
    sock: net.Conn
    window: int                 # what we may still send on the connection
    initial: int                # the client's INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE
    max_frame: int
    deltas: {int: int}          # WINDOW_UPDATEs for streams not answered yet
    pending: [Pending]          # answers waiting on flow control
    out: str
    answers: int
    close_after: int            # -1 until the reader is done
    dead: bool

# as much of p as the windows allow; true when it's all out
fn _push(w: mut Writer, p: mut Pending) bool:
    while p.at < len(p.body):
        n = min(min(len(p.body) - p.at, w.max_frame), min(w.window, p.window))
        if n <= 0:
            return false
        w.out += frame(F_DATA, 0, p.sid, p.body[p.at..p.at + n])
        p.at += n
        w.window -= n
        p.window -= n
    w.out += _headers_frames(p.sid, p.trailers, true, w.max_frame)
    return true

fn _retry(w: mut Writer):
    if len(w.pending) == 0:
        return
    keep: [Pending] = []
    for i in 0..len(w.pending):
        p = w.pending[i]
        if not _push(&w, &p):
            keep.push(p)
    w.pending = keep

fn _write_item(w: mut Writer, it: Out):
    match it:
        Raw(b):
            w.out += b
        Answer(sid, head, body, trailers):
            w.answers += 1
            if head == "":
                w.out += _headers_frames(sid, trailers, true, w.max_frame)
                w.deltas.remove(sid)
                return
            w.out += _headers_frames(sid, head, false, w.max_frame)
            p = Pending(sid, body, 0, w.initial + w.deltas.get(sid, 0), trailers)
            w.deltas.remove(sid)
            if not _push(&w, &p):
                w.pending.push(p)
        Window(sid, inc):
            if sid == 0:
                w.window += inc
                if w.window > 2147483647:
                    w.out += _goaway(0, FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR, "window overflow")
                    w.dead = true
                    return
            else:
                found = false
                for i in 0..len(w.pending):
                    if w.pending[i].sid == sid:
                        w.pending[i].window += inc
                        found = true
                if not found:
                    if len(w.deltas) > 4096:
                        w.deltas = {}
                    w.deltas[sid] = w.deltas.get(sid, 0) + inc
            _retry(&w)
        Settings(win, fr):
            if win >= 0:
                for i in 0..len(w.pending):
                    w.pending[i].window += win - w.initial
                w.initial = win
            if fr >= 0:
                w.max_frame = fr
            w.out += frame(F_SETTINGS, ACK, 0, "")
            _retry(&w)
        Reset(sid):
            w.deltas.remove(sid)
            w.pending = w.pending.filter(fn(p) p.sid != sid)
        Close(n):
            w.close_after = n

fn _writer(sock: net.Conn, ch: chan[Out]):
    w = Writer(sock, 65535, 65535, 16384, {}, [], "", 0, -1, false)
    it = Out.Raw("")
    while true:
        if w.close_after >= 0 and (w.dead or (w.answers >= w.close_after and len(w.pending) == 0)):
            break
        got = false
        if w.close_after >= 0:
            got = ch.recv_timeout(&it, 30000)       # (a call that never answers: don't wait forever)
            if not got:
                break
        else:
            got = ch.next(&it)
            if not got:
                break
        _write_item(&w, it)
        while len(w.out) < 1 << 20 and ch.try_recv(&it):
            _write_item(&w, it)
        if w.out != "" and not w.dead:
            if not sock.write(w.out):
                w.dead = true
                w.pending = []
            w.out = ""
    sock.close()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- a connection

fn _serve_conn(srv: Server, c: net.Conn, handler: fn(Call) Reply, o: Options, t: Tables):
    out: chan[Out] = task.channel(0)
    fn add(m: mut {int: _Live}) int:
        m[c.fd] = _Live(c, out)
        return 0
    fn drop(m: mut {int: _Live}) int:
        m.remove(c.fd)
        return 0
    if srv.tls.ctx != 0 and not (tls.accept(c, srv.tls) and tls.alpn(c) == "h2"):
        c.close()                               # (not TLS, or no "h2": not a gRPC client)
        return
    s = new_session(c, out, o, t, handler, srv.inflight)
    # the preface
    while len(s.buf) < len(PREFACE):
        if c.refill(&s.buf, 0, 65536) <= 0:
            c.close()
            return
        if not PREFACE.starts_with(s.buf[..min(len(s.buf), len(PREFACE))]):
            if s.buf.starts_with("POST ") or s.buf.starts_with("GET ") or s.buf.starts_with("PUT "):
                msg = "this port speaks gRPC (HTTP/2); send OTLP/HTTP to the HTTP port\n"
                c.write(f"HTTP/1.1 505 HTTP Version Not Supported\r\ncontent-type: text/plain\r\ncontent-length: {len(msg)}\r\nconnection: close\r\n\r\n{msg}")
            c.close()
            return
    srv.conns.update(add)
    task.spawn(fn() _writer(c, out))
    s.at = len(PREFACE)
    _hello(&s)
    while process(&s):
        _flush(&s)
        while len(out) > 1024:                  # the client isn't reading (a PING flood?): wait
            task.sleep(2)
        if c.refill(&s.buf, s.at, 262144) <= 0:
            break
        s.at = 0
    _flush(&s)
    s.streams = {}
    out.send(Out.Close(s.started))
    srv.conns.update(drop)
```

## deps/migrate/files.tn

```tern
# migrate: reading migration files (see migrate.tn)

struct Migration:
    version: int
    name: str
    up: str
    down: str                   # "" if the migration can't be rolled back
    transaction: bool           # false: `-- migrate:no-transaction`
    checksum: str               # sha256 of up, hex: an applied migration must not change

# One migration from its text. The text is the up SQL, optionally split by marker lines:
#   -- migrate:up                   (optional) the SQL that applies it
#   -- migrate:down                 the SQL that undoes it
#   -- migrate:no-transaction       run it outside a transaction (CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY)
fn parse(version: int, name: str, text: str) Result[Migration, str]:
    up = ""
    down = ""
    in_down = false
    seen_up = false
    tx = true
    lines = text.replace("\r\n", "\n").split("\n")
    for line in lines:
        t = line.trim()
        if t.starts_with("-- migrate:"):
            what = t[11..].trim()
            if what == "up":
                if seen_up or in_down:
                    return Err(f"migrate: {_label(version, name)}: `-- migrate:up` must come once, before `-- migrate:down`")
                seen_up = true
            elif what == "down":
                if in_down:
                    return Err(f"migrate: {_label(version, name)}: `-- migrate:down` appears twice")
                in_down = true
            elif what == "no-transaction":
                tx = false
            else:
                return Err(f"migrate: {_label(version, name)}: unknown marker `{t}` (use -- migrate:up, -- migrate:down, or -- migrate:no-transaction)")
            continue
        if in_down:
            down += line + "\n"
        else:
            up += line + "\n"
    if not _has_sql(up):
        return Err(f"migrate: {_label(version, name)}: no SQL to apply (the up part is empty or only comments)")
    if not _has_sql(down):
        down = ""
    return Ok(Migration(version, name, up, down, tx, crypto.hex(crypto.sha256(up))))

# The migrations in a directory, oldest first. Files are named VERSION_NAME.sql
# (0001_create_users.sql, 20260928120000_add_email.sql), or VERSION_NAME.up.sql with an
# optional VERSION_NAME.down.sql beside it. Other files are ignored.
fn load(dir: str) Result[[Migration], str]:
    ups: {int: str} = {}
    downs: {int: str} = {}
    files = _files(dir)?
    for v in files.keys():
        for f in files[v]:
            text = fs.try_read(dir + "/" + f).context("migrate")?
            if f.ends_with(".down.sql"):
                downs[v] = text
            else:
                ups[v] = text
    out: [Migration] = []
    versions = files.keys().sort_by(fn(k) k)
    for v in versions:
        first = files[v][0]
        if not (v in ups):
            return Err(f"migrate: {first} has no {first[..len(first) - 9]}.up.sql")
        text = ups[v]
        if v in downs:
            if text.contains("-- migrate:down"):
                return Err(f"migrate: version {v} has a `-- migrate:down` section and a .down.sql file; keep one")
            text += "\n-- migrate:down\n" + downs[v]
        out.push(parse(v, _title(first), text)?)
    return Ok(out)

# the migration files in dir by version: [the .sql file] or [.down.sql, .up.sql]
fn _files(dir: str) Result[{int: [str]}, str]:
    names = fs.try_list(dir).context("migrate")?
    out: {int: [str]} = {}
    sorted = names.sort_by(fn(n) n)
    for f in sorted:
        if not f.ends_with(".sql"):
            continue
        base = f[..len(f) - 4]
        v = _version_of(base)
        if v < 0:
            return Err(f"migrate: {f}: name migration files VERSION_NAME.sql, like 0001_create_users.sql")
        if v in out:
            prev = out[v][0]
            # (sorted, so a .down.sql comes before its .up.sql)
            pair = len(out[v]) == 1 and prev.ends_with(".down.sql") and f.ends_with(".up.sql") and _title(prev) == _title(f)
            if not pair:
                return Err(f"migrate: {prev} and {f} have the same version, {v}; renumber one of them")
            out[v].push(f)
        else:
            out[v] = [f]
    return Ok(out)

# "0002_add_email.up.sql" -> "add_email"
fn _title(file: str) str:
    base = file[..len(file) - 4]
    if base.ends_with(".down"):
        base = base[..len(base) - 5]
    elif base.ends_with(".up"):
        base = base[..len(base) - 3]
    return base[_digits(base) + 1..]

# the next file name for `migrate new`: one more than the newest version, as wide as the
# existing names (0001_...), or a UTC timestamp if the versions are timestamps
fn next_file(versions: [int], name: str) str:
    last = 0
    for v in versions:
        last = max(last, v)
    if last >= 10000000000000:
        d = time.utc(time.now())
        return f"{d.year}{fmt.zero_pad(d.month, 2)}{fmt.zero_pad(d.day, 2)}{fmt.zero_pad(d.hour, 2)}{fmt.zero_pad(d.minute, 2)}{fmt.zero_pad(d.second, 2)}_{name}.sql"
    return f"{fmt.zero_pad(last + 1, 4)}_{name}.sql"

fn _digits(s: str) int:
    i = 0
    while i < len(s) and s.byte(i) >= 48 and s.byte(i) <= 57:
        i += 1
    return i

# "0001_create_users" -> 1; -1 if it doesn't start with digits, a _ or -, and a name
fn _version_of(base: str) int:
    n = _digits(base)
    if n == 0 or n > 18 or n + 1 >= len(base) or not (base[n] == "_" or base[n] == "-"):
        return -1
    return base[..n].to_int(-1)

# anything but whitespace and -- comments
fn _has_sql(s: str) bool:
    lines = s.split("\n")
    for line in lines:
        t = line.trim()
        if t != "" and not t.starts_with("--"):
            return true
    return false

# The statements in a script, split at the semicolons that end them (not ones in quotes,
# $$ bodies, or comments): PostgreSQL runs a multi-statement string in one transaction, so a
# no-transaction migration sends its statements one at a time.
fn split_statements(sql: str) [str]:
    out: [str] = []
    start = 0
    i = 0
    n = len(sql)
    while i < n:
        c = sql.byte(i)
        if c == 39 or c == 34:                              # '...' or "..." ('' and "" double up)
            i += 1
            while i < n and sql.byte(i) != c:
                i += 1
            i += 1
        elif c == 45 and i + 1 < n and sql.byte(i + 1) == 45:      # -- to the end of the line
            while i < n and sql.byte(i) != 10:
                i += 1
        elif c == 47 and i + 1 < n and sql.byte(i + 1) == 42:      # /* ... */, nested
            depth = 1
            i += 2
            while i < n and depth > 0:
                if sql.byte(i) == 47 and i + 1 < n and sql.byte(i + 1) == 42:
                    depth += 1
                    i += 1
                elif sql.byte(i) == 42 and i + 1 < n and sql.byte(i + 1) == 47:
                    depth -= 1
                    i += 1
                i += 1
        elif c == 36 and (i == 0 or not _ident_byte(sql.byte(i - 1))):     # $tag$ ... $tag$
            j = i + 1
            while j < n and _ident_byte(sql.byte(j)) and sql.byte(j) != 36:
                j += 1
            if j < n and sql.byte(j) == 36 and (j == i + 1 or not _is_digit(sql.byte(i + 1))):
                tag = sql[i..j + 1]
                end = sql[j + 1..].find(tag)
                i = n if end < 0 else j + 1 + end + len(tag)
            else:
                i += 1
        elif c == 59:                                       # ;
            _push_statement(&out, sql[start..i])
            i += 1
            start = i
        else:
            i += 1
    _push_statement(&out, sql[start..])
    return out

fn _push_statement(out: mut [str], s: str):
    if _has_sql(s):
        out.push(s.trim())

fn _is_digit(c: int) bool:
    return c >= 48 and c <= 57

fn _ident_byte(c: int) bool:
    return _is_digit(c) or (c >= 65 and c <= 90) or (c >= 97 and c <= 122) or c == 95 or c == 36 or c >= 128
```

## deps/migrate/migrate.tn

```tern
# migrate: database migrations for PostgreSQL and SQLite, from a directory of .sql files.
#
#   migrations/0001_create_users.sql:
#       -- migrate:up
#       CREATE TABLE users (id bigserial PRIMARY KEY, name text NOT NULL);
#       -- migrate:down
#       DROP TABLE users;
#
#   import migrate
#   import pg
#
#   fn main() Result[int, str]:
#       p = pg.pool(os.env("DATABASE_URL", ""), 8)
#       done = migrate.postgres(p).up("migrations")?        # or migrate.sqlite(sqlite.open("app.db"))
#       print(f"applied {len(done)} migrations")
#       ...
#
# Or a migration command of its own (`tern run migrate.tn -- up | down [N] | status | new NAME`):
#
#   fn main() Result[int, str]:
#       return migrate.cli("migrations", os.env("DATABASE_URL", "sqlite:app.db"))
#
# Databases:
#   migrate.postgres(p pg.Pool) Target     migrate.sqlite(d sqlite.Db) Target
#   migrate.open(url str) Result[Target, str]      postgres://... or sqlite:PATH
# Running (dir: the migrations directory; each returns the migrations it ran, in order):
#   t.up(dir) Result[[Migration], str]              every pending migration, oldest first
#   t.down(dir, n int) Result[[Migration], str]     undo the newest n applied migrations
#   t.status(dir) Result[[Status], str]             Status fields: version, name, state
#                                                   ("applied" "pending" "changed" "missing"), applied_at
#   t.apply(ms [Migration])  t.rollback(ms, n)  t.report(ms)     the same, for migrations you
#                                                   built in code (migrate.parse) instead of files
# Files:
#   migrate.load(dir) Result[[Migration], str]      Migration fields: version, name, up, down,
#                                                   transaction, checksum
#   migrate.parse(version int, name str, text str) Result[Migration, str]
#   migrate.create(dir, name) Result[str, str]      a new, empty migration file; its path
#   migrate.label(m) str                            "0001_create_users"
#   migrate.label_of(s Status) str                  the same, for a Status
#   migrate.cli(dir, url) Result[int, str]          up, down [N], status, new NAME (os.args())
#   migrate.command(dir, url, args) Result[int, str]    ... with the arguments given
#   migrate.split_statements(sql) [str]             a script's statements (quotes, $$ bodies and
#                                                   comments understood)
#
# Files are named VERSION_NAME.sql: 0001_create_users.sql, or a timestamp,
# 20260928120000_add_email.sql. The version is the number; they run in version order. A file
# holds the up SQL, and optionally `-- migrate:down` followed by the SQL that undoes it (or
# put that in VERSION_NAME.down.sql next to VERSION_NAME.up.sql). `-- migrate:no-transaction`
# runs it outside a transaction, for statements that refuse one (CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY,
# ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE on old servers, VACUUM); keep those to one statement per file.
#
# How it runs:
# - Each migration runs in a transaction together with its row in the tern_migrations table,
#   so it is applied completely or not at all. (PostgreSQL rolls back DDL too; SQLite does,
#   except that some PRAGMAs do nothing inside a transaction.)
# - Only one run at a time: on PostgreSQL a run holds an advisory lock on a connection of its
#   own (so several instances of an app can all call up() as they start: one applies, the
#   others wait and then find nothing to do); on SQLite each migration takes the write lock.
# - An applied migration must not change: up() refuses to run if a file's up SQL differs
#   from what was applied (state "changed"). Put the change in a new migration.
# - A migration in the database but not in the directory ("missing": the code was rolled
#   back to an older version) is allowed, and reported by status.
# - A pending migration older than the newest applied one (merged from another branch) is
#   applied like any other.
# - Not available on wasm.

import crypto
import sqlite
import fmt
import fs
import os
import pg
import task
import time

struct Status:
    version: int
    name: str
    state: str                  # "applied", "pending", "changed", or "missing"
    applied_at: str             # "2026-09-28T12:00:00Z" ("" if pending)

fn up(t: Target, dir: str) Result[[Migration], str]:
    ms = load(dir)?
    return apply(t, ms)

fn down(t: Target, dir: str, n: int) Result[[Migration], str]:
    ms = load(dir)?
    return rollback(t, ms, n)

fn status(t: Target, dir: str) Result[[Status], str]:
    ms = load(dir)?
    return report(t, ms)

fn apply(t: Target, ms: [Migration]) Result[[Migration], str]:
    s = _begin(t)?
    r = _apply_all(s, ms)
    _end(s)
    return r

fn rollback(t: Target, ms: [Migration], n: int) Result[[Migration], str]:
    s = _begin(t)?
    r = _rollback_newest(s, ms, n)
    _end(s)
    return r

fn report(t: Target, ms: [Migration]) Result[[Status], str]:
    s = _begin(t)?
    r = _applied(s)
    _end(s)
    return Ok(_states(ms, r?))

fn label(m: Migration) str:
    return _label(m.version, m.name)

fn label_of(s: Status) str:
    return _label(s.version, s.name)

fn _label(version: int, name: str) str:
    return f"{fmt.zero_pad(version, 4)}_{name}"

# a new migration file in dir (created if needed), numbered after the newest one
fn create(dir: str, name: str) Result[str, str]:
    for ch in name:
        if not (_ident_byte(ch.byte(0)) and ch != "$"):
            return Err(f"migrate: name a migration with letters, digits and _ (like add_email), not `{name}`")
    if not fs.exists(dir) and not fs.mkdir(dir):
        return Err("migrate: " + fs.error())
    files = _files(dir)?
    path = dir + "/" + next_file(files.keys(), name)
    fs.try_write(path, "-- migrate:up\n\n\n-- migrate:down\n\n").context("migrate")?
    return Ok(path)

fn _apply_all(s: Target, ms: [Migration]) Result[[Migration], str]:
    done: {int: str} = {}
    applied = _applied(s)?
    for a in applied:
        done[a.version] = a.checksum
    todo: [Migration] = []
    sorted = ms.sort_by(fn(m) m.version)
    for m in sorted:
        if not (m.version in done):
            todo.push(m)
        elif done[m.version] != m.checksum:
            return Err(f"migrate: {label(m)} was changed after it was applied; undo the edit and put the change in a new migration")
    ran: [Migration] = []
    for m in todo:
        if _apply(s, m)?:
            ran.push(m)
    return Ok(ran)

fn _rollback_newest(s: Target, ms: [Migration], n: int) Result[[Migration], str]:
    by_version: {int: Migration} = {}
    for m in ms:
        by_version[m.version] = m
    applied = _applied(s)?
    undo: [Migration] = []
    i = len(applied) - 1
    while i >= 0 and len(undo) < n:
        a = applied[i]
        if not (a.version in by_version):
            return Err(f"migrate: can't roll back {_label(a.version, a.name)}: its file is gone")
        m = by_version[a.version]
        if m.down == "":
            return Err(f"migrate: can't roll back {label(m)}: it has no `-- migrate:down` section")
        undo.push(m)
        i -= 1
    for m in undo:
        _revert(s, m)?
    return Ok(undo)

fn _states(ms: [Migration], applied: [Applied]) [Status]:
    got: {int: Applied} = {}
    for a in applied:
        got[a.version] = a
    known: {int: bool} = {}
    out: [Status] = []
    for m in ms:
        known[m.version] = true
        if m.version in got:
            a = got[m.version]
            out.push(Status(m.version, m.name, "applied" if a.checksum == m.checksum else "changed", a.applied_at))
        else:
            out.push(Status(m.version, m.name, "pending", ""))
    for a in applied:
        if not (a.version in known):
            out.push(Status(a.version, a.name, "missing", a.applied_at))
    return out.sort_by(fn(s) s.version)

# A migration command: up, down [N], status, new NAME (from os.args()). url: see open().
fn cli(dir: str, url: str) Result[int, str]:
    return command(dir, url, os.args()[1..])

# the same, with the arguments given
fn command(dir: str, url: str, args: [str]) Result[int, str]:
    cmd = args[0] if len(args) > 0 else ""
    if cmd == "new":
        if len(args) != 2:
            return Err("usage: new NAME (like: new add_email)")
        print("created", create(dir, args[1])?)
        return Ok(0)
    if not (cmd in ["up", "down", "status"]) or len(args) > 2 or (len(args) == 2 and cmd != "down"):
        return Err("usage: up | down [N] | status | new NAME")
    t = open(url)?
    if cmd == "up":
        ran = up(t, dir)?
        for m in ran:
            print("applied", label(m))
        if len(ran) == 0:
            print("nothing to apply")
    elif cmd == "down":
        n = args[1].to_int(0) if len(args) == 2 else 1
        if n < 1:
            return Err(f"down: N is how many migrations to undo, not `{args[1]}`")
        for m in down(t, dir, n)?:
            print("rolled back", label(m))
    else:
        for st in status(t, dir)?:
            print(f"{fmt.pad_right(st.state, 8, " ")} {label_of(st)}  {st.applied_at}".trim())
    return Ok(0)
```

## deps/migrate/store.tn

```tern
# migrate: the migrations table, locking, and running migrations, for PostgreSQL and SQLite

enum Target:
    Postgres(p: pg.Pool)
    Sqlite(d: sqlite.Db)

struct Applied:
    version: int
    name: str
    checksum: str
    applied_at: str

const TABLE = "tern_migrations"
const LOCK_KEY = 7271047361946082313            # pg advisory lock: one migration run at a time

fn postgres(p: pg.Pool) Target:
    return Target.Postgres(p)

fn sqlite(d: sqlite.Db) Target:
    return Target.Sqlite(d)

# postgres://... or postgresql://... (PostgreSQL), sqlite:PATH or a file path (SQLite)
fn open(url: str) Result[Target, str]:
    if url.starts_with("postgres://") or url.starts_with("postgresql://"):
        p = pg.connect(url)
        if not p.ok():
            return Err("migrate: can't connect: " + pg.error())
        return Ok(Target.Postgres(p))
    path = url
    if url.starts_with("sqlite://"):
        path = url[9..]
    elif url.starts_with("sqlite:"):
        path = url[7..]
    if path == "":
        return Err("migrate: no database given (postgres://user:pass@host/db, or sqlite:app.db)")
    return Ok(Target.Sqlite(sqlite.open(path)))

# A run starts here. PostgreSQL: a connection of its own that holds the advisory lock until
# _end (other runs wait for it); SQLite: each migration takes the write lock instead.
fn _begin(t: Target) Result[Target, str]:
    match t:
        Postgres(p):
            own = pg.connect(p.url)
            if not own.ok():
                return Err("migrate: can't connect: " + pg.error())
            r = _pg_setup(own)
            if r is Err(e):
                own.close()
                return Err(e)
            return Ok(Target.Postgres(own))
        Sqlite(d):
            d.run_script(f"CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS {TABLE} (version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, checksum TEXT NOT NULL, applied_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', 'now')))").context("migrate")?
            return Ok(t)

fn _pg_setup(p: pg.Pool) Result[int, str]:
    # Waiting runs poll instead of blocking in pg_advisory_lock(): a session blocked there is
    # in the middle of a statement, holding a snapshot, and CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY in the
    # running migration waits for every snapshot: a deadlock that PostgreSQL breaks by
    # failing the index build.
    wait = 5
    while true:
        rows = p.query("SELECT pg_try_advisory_lock($1)::int AS ok", [str(LOCK_KEY)])
        if len(rows) == 0:
            return Err("migrate: taking the lock: " + pg.error())
        if rows[0]["ok"] == "1":
            break
        task.sleep(wait)
        wait = min(wait * 2, 250)
    p.run_script(f"CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS {TABLE} (version bigint PRIMARY KEY, name text NOT NULL, checksum text NOT NULL, applied_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now())").context("migrate")?
    return Ok(0)

fn _end(s: Target):
    if s is Postgres(p):
        p.close()                       # ending the session releases the lock

fn _applied(s: Target) Result[[Applied], str]:
    match s:
        Postgres(p):
            rows = p.fetch[Applied](f"SELECT version, name, checksum, to_char(applied_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD\"T\"HH24:MI:SS\"Z\"') AS applied_at FROM {TABLE} ORDER BY version", []).context("migrate")?
            return Ok(rows)
        Sqlite(d):
            rows: [Applied] = []
            d.query_into(f"SELECT version, name, checksum, applied_at FROM {TABLE} ORDER BY version", [], &rows)
            return Ok(rows)

# Applies m and records it, together. Ok(false): another process applied it first (SQLite).
fn _apply(s: Target, m: Migration) Result[bool, str]:
    record = f"INSERT INTO {TABLE} (version, name, checksum) VALUES ({m.version}, {_quote(m.name)}, {_quote(m.checksum)})"
    match s:
        Postgres(p):
            _pg_still_locked(p)?
            if m.transaction:
                _pg_tx(p, m, m.up, record)?
            else:
                statements = split_statements(m.up)
                for st in statements:
                    p.run_script(st).map_err(fn(e) _failed(m, e))?
                p.run_script(record).context("migrate")?
            return Ok(true)
        Sqlite(d):
            if not m.transaction:
                d.run_script(m.up).map_err(fn(e) _failed(m, e))?
                d.run_script(record).context("migrate")?
                return Ok(true)
            d.run_script("BEGIN IMMEDIATE").context("migrate")?
            if len(d.query(f"SELECT 1 AS x FROM {TABLE} WHERE version = ?", [str(m.version)])) > 0:
                d.run_script("COMMIT").context("migrate")?
                return Ok(false)
            _sqlite_tx(d, m, m.up, record)?
            return Ok(true)

# Undoes m (its down SQL) and forgets it, together.
fn _revert(s: Target, m: Migration) Result[bool, str]:
    forget = f"DELETE FROM {TABLE} WHERE version = {m.version}"
    match s:
        Postgres(p):
            _pg_still_locked(p)?
            if m.transaction:
                _pg_tx(p, m, m.down, forget)?
            else:
                statements = split_statements(m.down)
                for st in statements:
                    p.run_script(st).map_err(fn(e) _failed(m, e))?
                p.run_script(forget).context("migrate")?
            return Ok(true)
        Sqlite(d):
            if not m.transaction:
                d.run_script(m.down).map_err(fn(e) _failed(m, e))?
                d.run_script(forget).context("migrate")?
                return Ok(true)
            d.run_script("BEGIN IMMEDIATE").context("migrate")?
            _sqlite_tx(d, m, m.down, forget)?
            return Ok(true)

# one round trip: the migration's SQL and the bookkeeping commit or roll back together
fn _pg_tx(p: pg.Pool, m: Migration, sql: str, then: str) Result[int, str]:
    r = p.run_script("BEGIN;\n" + sql + "\n;\n" + then + ";\nCOMMIT;")
    if r is Err(e):
        p.run_script("ROLLBACK")                # the script stopped inside its transaction
        return Err(_failed(m, e))
    return Ok(0)

fn _sqlite_tx(d: sqlite.Db, m: Migration, sql: str, then: str) Result[int, str]:
    r = d.run_script(sql + "\n;\n" + then + ";\nCOMMIT;")
    if r is Err(e):
        d.run_script("ROLLBACK")
        return Err(_failed(m, e))
    return Ok(0)

# The run's connection holds the lock; if it was lost and replaced, a new one must get it
# back before anything else happens (pg_try_advisory_lock is re-entrant for its holder).
fn _pg_still_locked(p: pg.Pool) Result[int, str]:
    rows = p.query("SELECT pg_try_advisory_lock($1)::int AS ok", [str(LOCK_KEY)])
    if len(rows) == 0 or rows[0]["ok"] != "1":
        return Err("migrate: lost the migration lock (the connection dropped and another run holds it now); run again")
    return Ok(0)

fn _failed(m: Migration, e: str) str:
    why = e
    for prefix in ["pg: script failed: ", "sqlite: script failed: "]:
        if why.starts_with(prefix):
            why = why[len(prefix)..]
    return f"migrate: {label(m)} failed: {why}"

fn _quote(s: str) str:
    return "'" + s.replace("'", "''") + "'"
```

## deps/openapi/openapi.tn

```tern
# openapi: describe a web API with Tern types; get an OpenAPI 3.1 document, Swagger UI, and a
# typed TypeScript client, all from the same routes you register.
#
#   import openapi
#   import roost
#
#   struct User:
#       id: int
#       name: str
#
#   fn main():
#       api = openapi.new("users", "1.0.0", "A small user service")
#       r = roost.router()
#       o = openapi.op("GET", "/users/{id}", "Get a user").returns[User]()
#       openapi.add(&api, &r, o, fn(req) roost.json(...))
#       openapi.serve(api, &r)                 # GET /openapi.json, GET /docs (Swagger UI)
#       roost.serve(r, 8080)
#
# Describing an operation (each returns the changed Op, so calls chain):
#   openapi.op(method, path, summary) Op     path params come from the path ("/users/{id}")
#   o.returns[T]()   o.accepts[T]()          the JSON response / request body is T
#   o.returns_text()                         a text/plain response
#   o.status(code)   o.describe(text)   o.tag(name)   o.id(operation_id)
#   o.query(name, type, description)         type: "string", "integer", "number", "boolean"
#   o.fails(code, description)               a documented error response (a 401 is added for
#                                            secured operations unless you give your own)
#   o.public()                               no key needed (default: the spec's security applies)
# Building and serving:
#   openapi.new(title, version, description) Spec
#   openapi.bearer(&spec, description)       every operation (but public ones) needs a bearer token
#   openapi.server(&spec, url)
#   openapi.add(&spec, &r, o, handler)       registers the route on r and records the operation
#   openapi.record(&spec, o)                 records an operation routed some other way (nested routers)
#   openapi.document(spec) str               the OpenAPI 3.1 JSON
#   openapi.typescript(spec) str             TypeScript types for every schema, and a fetch client
#   openapi.serve(spec, &r)                  GET /openapi.json and GET /docs (Swagger UI from
#                                            jsDelivr); call it after the last add
#
# Schemas come from json.schema[T](), so they always match what json.encode writes: every
# struct field is required, maps are objects with additionalProperties, int is int64.

import json
import roost

struct Param:
    name: str
    loc: str            # "path" or "query"
    ty: str             # JSON Schema type: string, integer, number, boolean
    required: bool
    description: str

struct Op:
    method: str
    path: str
    summary: str
    description: str
    tags: [str]
    op_id: str
    params: [Param]
    request: str        # JSON Schema text ("" for no body)
    response: str       # JSON Schema text ("" for no JSON body)
    text: bool          # the response is text/plain
    code: int
    open: bool          # no security requirement
    errors: [(int, str)]    # documented error responses: (status, description)

struct Spec:
    title: str
    version: str
    description: str
    servers: [str]
    bearer: str         # "" = no security scheme; else its description
    ops: [Op]

fn new(title: str, version: str, description: str) Spec:
    return Spec(title, version, description, [], "", [])

fn bearer(s: mut Spec, description: str):
    s.bearer = description

fn server(s: mut Spec, url: str):
    s.servers.push(copy(url))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- operations
fn _path_params(path: str) [Param]:
    out: [Param] = []
    rest = path
    i = rest.find("{")
    while i >= 0:
        j = rest.find("}")
        if j < i:
            break
        n = rest[i + 1..j]
        if n.starts_with("*"):
            n = n[1..]
        out.push(Param(n, "path", "string", true, ""))
        rest = rest[j + 1..]
        i = rest.find("{")
    return out

fn _op_id(method: str, path: str) str:
    out = method.lower()
    up = true
    for i in 0..len(path):
        ch = path[i]
        if ch == "/" or ch == "{" or ch == "}" or ch == "*" or ch == "-" or ch == "_" or ch == ".":
            up = true
        elif up:
            out += ch.upper()
            up = false
        else:
            out += ch
    return out

fn op(method: str, path: str, summary: str) Op:
    m = method.upper()
    return Op(m, path, summary, "", [], _op_id(m, path), _path_params(path), "", "", false, 200, false, [])

fn returns[T](o: Op) Op:
    out = o
    out.response = json.schema[T]()
    return out

fn accepts[T](o: Op) Op:
    out = o
    out.request = json.schema[T]()
    return out

fn returns_text(o: Op) Op:
    out = o
    out.text = true
    return out

fn status(o: Op, code: int) Op:
    out = o
    out.code = code
    return out

fn describe(o: Op, text: str) Op:
    out = o
    out.description = text
    return out

fn tag(o: Op, name: str) Op:
    out = o
    out.tags.push(copy(name))
    return out

fn id(o: Op, operation_id: str) Op:
    out = o
    out.op_id = operation_id
    return out

fn query(o: Op, name: str, ty: str, description: str) Op:
    out = o
    out.params.push(Param(name, "query", ty, false, description))
    return out

fn fails(o: Op, code: int, description: str) Op:
    out = o
    out.errors.push((code, copy(description)))
    return out

fn public(o: Op) Op:
    out = o
    out.open = true
    return out

fn add(s: mut Spec, r: mut roost.Router, o: Op, h: fn(roost.Request) roost.Response):
    r.route(o.method, o.path, h)
    s.ops.push(o)

# document an operation whose route is registered some other way (a nested router, a
# streaming handler, middleware in front of it)
fn record(s: mut Spec, o: Op):
    s.ops.push(o)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the document
# json.schema's output keeps its structs under a trailing "$defs"; the document moves them
# to components/schemas, shared by every operation
fn _split(schema: str, defs: mut {str: str}) str:
    k = schema.find(",\"$defs\":{")
    if k < 0:
        return schema
    root = schema[..k] + "}"
    body = schema[k + 10..len(schema) - 2]
    i = 0
    while i < len(body):
        e = body.find("\":")
        if body[i] != "\"" or e < 0:
            break
        rel = body[i..]
        q = rel.find("\":")
        name = rel[1..q]
        start = i + q + 2
        depth = 0
        j = start
        while j < len(body):
            ch = body.byte(j)
            if ch == 123:
                depth += 1
            elif ch == 125:
                depth -= 1
                if depth == 0:
                    break
            j += 1
        defs[name] = _refs(body[start..j + 1])
        i = j + 2
    return _refs(root)

fn _refs(s: str) str:
    return s.replace("#/$defs/", "#/components/schemas/")

fn _short_names(defs: {str: str}) {str: str}:
    counts: {str: int} = {}
    for k in defs.keys():
        short = _ts_name(k, {})
        counts[short] = counts.get(short, 0) + 1
    names: {str: str} = {}
    for k in defs.keys():
        names[copy(k)] = _ts_name(k, counts)
    return names

fn _rename(s: str, names: {str: str}) str:
    out = s
    for k, v in names:
        if k != v:
            out = out.replace("#/components/schemas/" + k + "\"", "#/components/schemas/" + v + "\"")
    return out

fn _openapi_path(p: str) str:
    return p.replace("{*", "{")

fn _op_json(s: Spec, o: Op, defs: mut {str: str}) str:
    parts: [str] = ["\"operationId\":" + json_quote(o.op_id), "\"summary\":" + json_quote(o.summary)]
    if o.description != "":
        parts.push("\"description\":" + json_quote(o.description))
    if len(o.tags) > 0:
        parts.push("\"tags\":" + json.encode(o.tags))
    if len(o.params) > 0:
        ps: [str] = []
        for p in o.params:
            ps.push("{\"name\":" + json_quote(p.name) + ",\"in\":" + json_quote(p.loc) + ",\"required\":" + ("true" if p.required else "false") + ",\"schema\":{\"type\":" + json_quote(p.ty) + "}" + (",\"description\":" + json_quote(p.description) if p.description != "" else "") + "}")
        parts.push("\"parameters\":[" + ",".join(ps) + "]")
    if o.request != "":
        parts.push("\"requestBody\":{\"required\":true,\"content\":{\"application/json\":{\"schema\":" + _split(o.request, &defs) + "}}}")
    ok = "{\"description\":\"OK\"}"
    if o.response != "":
        ok = "{\"description\":\"OK\",\"content\":{\"application/json\":{\"schema\":" + _split(o.response, &defs) + "}}}"
    elif o.text:
        ok = "{\"description\":\"OK\",\"content\":{\"text/plain\":{\"schema\":{\"type\":\"string\"}}}}"
    resp = "\"" + str(o.code) + "\":" + ok
    has401 = false
    for e in o.errors:
        resp += ",\"" + str(e.0) + "\":{\"description\":" + json_quote(e.1) + "}"
        has401 = has401 or e.0 == 401
    if s.bearer != "" and not o.open and not has401:
        resp += ",\"401\":{\"description\":\"Missing or unknown credentials\"}"
    parts.push("\"responses\":{" + resp + "}")
    if o.open and s.bearer != "":
        parts.push("\"security\":[]")
    return "{" + ",".join(parts) + "}"

fn document(s: Spec) str:
    defs: {str: str} = {}
    paths: [str] = []
    by_path: {str: [str]} = {}
    for o in s.ops:
        p = _openapi_path(o.path)
        if not (p in by_path):
            by_path[copy(p)] = []
            paths.push(copy(p))
        by_path[p].push(json_quote(o.method.lower()) + ":" + _op_json(s, o, &defs))
    ps: [str] = []
    for p in paths:
        ps.push(json_quote(p) + ":{" + ",".join(by_path[p]) + "}")
    info = "{\"title\":" + json_quote(s.title) + ",\"version\":" + json_quote(s.version)
    if s.description != "":
        info += ",\"description\":" + json_quote(s.description)
    info += "}"
    out = "{\"openapi\":\"3.1.0\",\"info\":" + info
    sv: [str] = []
    for u in s.servers:
        sv.push("{\"url\":" + json_quote(u) + "}")
    if len(sv) == 0:
        sv.push("{\"url\":\"/\"}")                  # wherever the document is served from
    out += ",\"servers\":[" + ",".join(sv) + "]"
    out += ",\"paths\":{" + _rename(",".join(ps), _short_names(defs)) + "}"
    # short component names (User, not models.User) unless two would collide
    names = _short_names(defs)
    comps: [str] = []
    if len(defs) > 0:
        ds: [str] = []
        for k, v in defs:
            ds.push(json_quote(names[k]) + ":" + _rename(v, names))
        comps.push("\"schemas\":{" + ",".join(ds) + "}")
    if s.bearer != "":
        comps.push("\"securitySchemes\":{\"bearer\":{\"type\":\"http\",\"scheme\":\"bearer\",\"description\":" + json_quote(s.bearer) + "}}")
    if len(comps) > 0:
        out += ",\"components\":{" + ",".join(comps) + "}"
    if s.bearer != "":
        out += ",\"security\":[{\"bearer\":[]}]"
    return out + "}"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- serving
const SWAGGER = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/swagger-ui-dist@5"

fn serve(s: Spec, r: mut roost.Router):
    doc = document(s)
    page = "<!doctype html><html><head><meta charset=utf-8><meta name=viewport content='width=device-width,initial-scale=1'><title>" + html_text(s.title) + " API</title><link rel=stylesheet href='" + SWAGGER + "/swagger-ui.css'></head><body><div id=swagger-ui></div><script src='" + SWAGGER + "/swagger-ui-bundle.js'></script><script src='/docs/init.js'></script></body></html>"
    init = "window.ui = SwaggerUIBundle({ url: '/openapi.json', dom_id: '#swagger-ui', deepLinking: true, persistAuthorization: true });"
    r.get("/openapi.json", fn(req) roost.json(doc))
    r.get("/docs", fn(req) roost.html(page))
    fn js(req: roost.Request) roost.Response:
        res = roost.text(init)
        res.content_type = "text/javascript; charset=utf-8"
        return res
    r.get("/docs/init.js", js)

fn html_text(s: str) str:
    return s.replace("&", "&amp;").replace("<", "&lt;").replace(">", "&gt;").replace("'", "&#39;")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- TypeScript
# typescript(spec): a type for every schema, and createClient() with one typed method per
# operation (named by its operationId): path parameters, then the body, then the query.
# int64 becomes number: exact up to 2^53.

fn _ts_name(def: str, taken: {str: int}) str:
    short = def
    d = def.find(".")
    while d >= 0:
        short = short[d + 1..]
        d = short.find(".")
    if taken.get(short, 0) > 1:                 # store.Stats and forward.Stats: StoreStats, ForwardStats
        out = ""
        for part in def.split("."):
            if len(part) > 0:
                out += part[0].upper() + part[1..]
        return out
    return short

fn _ts_type(v: json.Value, names: {str: str}) str:
    ref = v.field("$ref").str_or("")
    if ref != "":
        n = ref[ref.find("/schemas/") + 9..]
        if ref.starts_with("#/$defs/"):
            n = ref[8..]
        return names.get(n, "unknown")
    alts = v.field("anyOf").elems()                 # Option[T]: T or null
    if len(alts) == 0:
        alts = v.field("oneOf").elems()             # an enum with payloads
    if len(alts) > 0:
        return " | ".join(alts.map(fn(a) _ts_type(a, names)))
    if v.field("const") is Str(c):                  # one variant's name
        return json_quote(c)
    labels = v.field("enum").elems()                # a string enum: "Active" | "Banned"
    if len(labels) > 0:
        return " | ".join(labels.map(fn(l) json_quote(l.str_or(""))))
    t = v.field("type").str_or("")
    if t == "null":
        return "null"
    if t == "integer" or t == "number":
        return "number"
    if t == "string":
        return "string"
    if t == "boolean":
        return "boolean"
    if t == "array":
        it = _ts_type(v.field("items"), names)
        if it.contains(" ") or it.contains("<"):
            return "Array<" + it + ">"
        return it + "[]"
    if t == "object":
        ap = v.field("additionalProperties")
        if ap is Obj(_, _):                           # (false: a closed object, not a map)
            return "Record<string, " + _ts_type(ap, names) + ">"
        props = v.field("properties")
        parts: [str] = []
        for k in props.fields():
            parts.push(_ts_key(k) + ": " + _ts_type(props.field(k), names))
        return "{ " + "; ".join(parts) + " }"
    return "unknown"

fn _ts_key(k: str) str:
    for i in 0..len(k):
        c = k.byte(i)
        if not ((c >= 97 and c <= 122) or (c >= 65 and c <= 90) or (c >= 48 and c <= 57 and i > 0) or c == 95 or c == 36):
            return json_quote(k)
    return k

fn _ts_schema(schema: str, names: {str: str}) str:
    match json.parse(schema):
        Ok(v):
            return _ts_type(v, names)
        Err(_):
            return "unknown"

fn _ts_param_type(ty: str) str:
    if ty == "integer" or ty == "number":
        return "number"
    if ty == "boolean":
        return "boolean"
    return "string"

fn typescript(s: Spec) str:
    defs: {str: str} = {}
    for o in s.ops:
        _split(o.request, &defs)
        _split(o.response, &defs)
    names = _short_names(defs)
    out = "// Generated from the " + s.title + " API (" + s.version + ") by Tern's openapi.typescript: don't edit.\n\n"
    for k, v in defs:
        out += "export type " + names[k] + " = " + _ts_schema(v, names) + ";\n"
    out += "\nexport class ApiError extends Error {\n  constructor(public status: number, public body: string) {\n    super(`${status}: ${body}`);\n  }\n}\n\n"
    out += "export type ClientOptions = { baseUrl?: string; token?: string; fetch?: typeof fetch; init?: RequestInit };\n\n"
    out += "export function createClient(opts: ClientOptions = {}) {\n"
    out += "  const base = opts.baseUrl ?? \"\";\n"
    out += "  async function call<T>(method: string, path: string, query: object | undefined, body: unknown, kind: \"json\" | \"text\" | \"none\"): Promise<T> {\n"
    out += "    let url = base + path;\n"
    out += "    if (query) {\n      const u = new URLSearchParams();\n      for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(query)) if (v !== undefined && v !== null && v !== \"\") u.set(k, String(v));\n      const q = u.toString();\n      if (q) url += \"?\" + q;\n    }\n"
    out += "    const headers: Record<string, string> = { ...(opts.init?.headers as Record<string, string> | undefined) };\n"
    out += "    if (opts.token) headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${opts.token}`;\n"
    out += "    if (body !== undefined) headers[\"Content-Type\"] = \"application/json\";\n"
    out += "    const res = await (opts.fetch ?? fetch)(url, { credentials: \"same-origin\", ...opts.init, method, headers, body: body === undefined ? undefined : JSON.stringify(body) });\n"
    out += "    if (!res.ok) throw new ApiError(res.status, await res.text());\n"
    out += "    if (kind === \"none\") return undefined as T;\n"
    out += "    return (kind === \"text\" ? await res.text() : await res.json()) as T;\n  }\n"
    out += "  return {\n"
    for o in s.ops:
        args: [str] = []
        pp: [str] = []
        qp: [str] = []
        for p in o.params:
            if p.loc == "path":
                pp.push(_ts_key(p.name) + ": string")
            else:
                qp.push(_ts_key(p.name) + "?: " + _ts_param_type(p.ty))
        if len(pp) > 0:
            args.push("p: { " + "; ".join(pp) + " }")
        body = "undefined"
        if o.request != "":
            args.push("body: " + _ts_schema(_split(o.request, &defs), names))
            body = "body"
        query = "undefined"
        if len(qp) > 0:
            args.push("q: { " + "; ".join(qp) + " } = {}")
            query = "q"
        ret = "void"
        kind = "none"
        if o.response != "":
            ret = _ts_schema(_split(o.response, &defs), names)
            kind = "json"
        elif o.text:
            ret = "string"
            kind = "text"
        path = _openapi_path(o.path)
        for p in o.params:
            if p.loc == "path":
                path = path.replace("{" + p.name + "}", "${encodeURIComponent(p." + p.name + ")}")
        out += "    /** " + o.summary.replace("*/", "* /") + " */\n"
        out += "    " + o.op_id + ": (" + ", ".join(args) + ") => call<" + ret + ">(" + json_quote(o.method) + ", `" + path + "`, " + query + ", " + body + ", " + json_quote(kind) + "),\n"
    out += "  };\n}\n"
    return out
```

## deps/pg/pg.tn

```tern
# pg: a PostgreSQL client for tasks: a connection pool, parameters bound safely, rows read
# into your structs, and transactions that belong to the task that started them.
#
#   import pg
#   import json
#
#   struct World:
#       id: int
#       randomNumber: int
#
#   db = pg.pool("postgres://user:password@localhost:5432/app", 16)   # 16 connections, shared by every task
#   if not db.ok():
#       print(pg.error())                          # why the first connection failed
#   n = db.exec("UPDATE world SET randomNumber = $1 WHERE id = $2", ["42", "7"])    # rows changed (-1: error)
#   rows = db.query("SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id = $1", ["7"])            # [{str: str}]
#   worlds: [World] = []
#   json.decode(db.query_json("SELECT id, randomNumber FROM world LIMIT 5", []), &worlds)
#   w = World(0, 0)
#   json.decode(db.query_row_json("SELECT * FROM world WHERE id = $1", ["7"]), &w)
#
#   db.begin()                                     # from here until commit/rollback, this task's
#   db.exec("INSERT INTO log (msg) VALUES ($1)", ["hi"])    # statements run on one connection,
#   db.commit()                                    # which no other task can use meanwhile
#
# Functions (a Pool is shared by copying it, like a channel):
#   pg.pool(url str, size int) Pool     at most size connections, opened as needed (the first
#                                       one right away, so p.ok() can report a bad url or password)
#   pg.connect(url str) Pool            pg.pool(url, 1)
#   p.ok() bool                         pg.error() str: why the last call failed ("" after a success)
#   p.exec(sql str, params [str]) int   rows affected, or -1 (pg.error() has the server's message,
#                                       e.g. "ERROR 23505: duplicate key value violates unique constraint ...")
#   p.query(sql str, params [str]) [{str: str}]     every value as text; NULL is ""
#   p.query_json(sql str, params [str]) str         the rows as a JSON array: numbers, booleans and
#                                                   null stay typed, so json.decode fills structs
#   p.query_row_json(sql str, params [str]) str     the first row as a JSON object ("null" if none)
#   p.begin() bool  p.commit() bool  p.rollback() bool
#   p.run_script(sql str) Result[int, str]   several statements (a schema, a migration): the
#                                       simple query protocol, no parameters
#   p.describe(sql str) Result[Statement, str]    the types of its parameters and columns,
#                                       without running it (see "describing a statement" below)
#   pg.array_int(xs) str  array_float  array_bool  array_str     a list as one parameter:
#                                       `WHERE id = ANY($1)` with [pg.array_int(ids)]
#   pg.NULL                             a parameter that is NULL
#   p.stats() PoolStats                 size open idle in_use waiting waits wait_ms timeouts opened closed
#   p.prune()                           closes the connections idle longer than max_idle (the
#                                       pool also does this by itself now and then)
#   p.close()                           closes the idle connections
#
# Parameters are $1, $2, ... and are sent separately from the SQL (no injection), as text;
# PostgreSQL converts them to the column types; pg.NULL is NULL. Statements are prepared on
# each connection the first time and reused after that.
#
# Transactions are bound to the task: any statement that leaves its connection inside a
# transaction (begin(), or exec("BEGIN")) keeps that connection for the task until the
# transaction ends, so other tasks never see or join it. A task that waits (a channel, a
# socket, a sleep) in the middle of a transaction keeps holding its connection.
#
# URL: postgres://user:password@host:port/dbname?sslmode=require (sslmode=require or
# verify-full need `import tls`; the default is no TLS); &application_name=app names the
# connections in pg_stat_activity (default: tern). Login: SCRAM-SHA-256 (PostgreSQL's
# default) or password. Not available on wasm.
# The pool: &pool_timeout=30s (how long a statement waits for a free connection, then fails),
# &max_lifetime=1h (a connection is replaced after this long), &max_idle=30m (an idle one is
# closed), &statement_cache=off (no prepared statements kept: PgBouncer); 0 turns a limit off.
# A connection the server closed is noticed and replaced before it is used.
#
# The protocol is Tern too: wire.tn.

import crypto
import json
import net
import sql
import task
import time

struct Pool:
    url: str
    size: int
    free: chan[Conn]            # idle connections; one not live is a slot not connected yet
    state: shared[_State]
    shards: [shared[_Shard]]    # transactions' connections and the waiting counts, by task (see _Shard)
    key: str                    # the task-local that marks a task holding one of its connections
    first_ok: bool
    timeout_ms: int             # ?pool_timeout: how long a task waits for a free connection (0: forever)
    lifetime_ms: int            # ?max_lifetime: a connection is replaced after this long (0: never)
    idle_ms: int                # ?max_idle: an idle connection is closed after this long (0: never)

# what p.stats() reports
struct PoolStats:
    size: int                   # the most connections it opens
    open: int                   # connections open now
    idle: int                   # ... of them not in use
    in_use: int                 # ... running a statement, or held by a task's transaction
    waiting: int                # tasks waiting for a connection now
    waits: int                  # times a task had to wait (every connection was in use)
    wait_ms: int                # ... and the milliseconds it waited, added up
    timeouts: int               # waits that gave up after pool_timeout
    opened: int                 # connections opened, ever
    closed: int                 # ... and closed (broken, too old, idle too long, p.close())

# What the tasks using a pool share, behind a lock. A statement that finds a free connection
# doesn't take it: only opening and closing connections do.
struct _State:
    stats: PoolStats            # (idle and in_use are worked out by stats(); the waiting counts
                                # are the shards')
    pruned: int                 # when idle connections were last closed (time.mono_ms)

# What transactions and waits touch, split by task.id() over _SHARDS locks. Each statement in
# a transaction takes its task's connection out and puts it back; with one lock for the pool,
# tasks queued on it, and a lock handed to a task that has to be woken first is held all the
# while it waits to run (a convoy: every statement of every transaction waited in it).
struct _Shard:
    bound: {int: Conn}          # connections held by a task's open transaction, by task.id()
    waiting: int                # (PoolStats' fields of the same names, for these tasks)
    waits: int
    wait_ms: int
    timeouts: int

const _SHARDS = 32

fn _shard(p: Pool, tid: int) shared[_Shard]:
    return p.shards[tid % len(p.shards)]

fn pool(url: str, size: int) Pool:
    n = max(size, 1)
    free: chan[Conn] = task.channel(0)
    first = _open(url)
    st = _State(PoolStats(n, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0), time.mono_ms())
    if first.live:
        st.stats.open = 1
        st.stats.opened = 1
    ok = first.live
    free.send(first)
    for i in 1..n:
        free.send(_no_conn())
    key = "pg.tx." + crypto.hex(crypto.random_bytes(8))
    shards: [shared[_Shard]] = []
    for i in 0.._SHARDS:
        shards.push(task.shared(_Shard({}, 0, 0, 0, 0)))
    return Pool(url, n, free, task.shared(st), shards, key, ok, _ms(_param(url, "pool_timeout"), 30000),
                _ms(_param(url, "max_lifetime"), 3600000), _ms(_param(url, "max_idle"), 1800000))

fn connect(url: str) Pool:
    return pool(url, 1)

fn ok(p: Pool) bool:
    return p.first_ok

# the counters, and how many connections are idle and in use right now
fn stats(p: Pool) PoolStats:
    idle = 0
    for i in 0..len(p.free):
        c = _no_conn()
        if not p.free.try_recv(&c):
            break
        if c.live:
            idle += 1
        p.free.send(c)
    s = p.state.get().stats
    for sh in p.shards:
        w = sh.get()
        s.waiting += w.waiting
        s.waits += w.waits
        s.wait_ms += w.wait_ms
        s.timeouts += w.timeouts
    s.idle = idle
    s.in_use = max(s.open - idle, 0)
    return s

# why the last call on this task failed ("" after a success)
fn error() str:
    return task.local_get("pg.error")

fn _set_err(msg: str):
    if msg != "" or task.local_get("pg.error") != "":
        task.local_set("pg.error", msg)

# The connection for a statement: the task's own (in a transaction), or one from the pool
# that is still good (not broken, too old, idle too long, or closed by the server). Not
# live: none (pg.error() says why).
fn _take(p: Pool) Conn:
    if task.local_get(p.key) != "":             # this task holds one, in a transaction
        tid = task.id()
        mine = _shard(p, tid).update(fn(s) _held(&s, tid))
        if mine is Some(held):
            return held
    c = _no_conn()
    if not p.free.try_recv(&c):
        got = _wait(p)
        if got is Some(w):
            c = w
        else:
            return _no_conn()
    closed = 0
    if c.live and (c.broken or _stale(p, c)):
```
