```tern
        _close_conn(c)
        closed = 1
        idled = p.idle_ms > 0 and time.mono_ms() - c.used_ms > p.idle_ms
        c = _no_conn()
        if idled:
            prune(p)                                 # (the others have likely idled too)
    if c.live:
        return c
    c = _open(p.url)
    opened = 1 if c.live else 0
    p.state.update(fn(s) _count(&s, opened - closed, opened, closed))
    if not c.live:
        p.free.send(_no_conn())
    return c

fn _held(s: mut _Shard, tid: int) Option[Conn]:
    if not (tid in s.bound):
        return None
    c = s.bound[tid]
    s.bound.remove(tid)
    return Some(c)

fn _count(s: mut _State, open: int, opened: int, closed: int) int:
    s.stats.open += open
    s.stats.opened += opened
    s.stats.closed += closed
    return 0

# every connection is in use: wait for one, up to pool_timeout
fn _wait(p: Pool) Option[Conn]:
    sh = _shard(p, task.id())
    sh.update(fn(s) _waiting(&s, 1, 0, false))
    t0 = time.mono_ms()
    c = _no_conn()
    got = true
    if p.timeout_ms > 0:
        got = p.free.recv_timeout(&c, p.timeout_ms)
    else:
        c = p.free.recv()
    waited = time.mono_ms() - t0
    sh.update(fn(s) _waiting(&s, -1, waited, not got))
    if not got:
        busy = "the pool's one connection is" if p.size == 1 else f"all {p.size} connections are"
        _set_err(f"pg: no connection free after {p.timeout_ms} ms: {busy} in use (a bigger pool, shorter transactions, or a longer ?pool_timeout=)")
        return None
    return Some(c)

fn _waiting(s: mut _Shard, now: int, waited: int, gave_up: bool) int:
    s.waiting += now
    if now < 0:
        s.waits += 1
        s.wait_ms += waited
    if gave_up:
        s.timeouts += 1
    return 0

fn _stale(p: Pool, c: Conn) bool:
    now = time.mono_ms()
    jitter = c.born_ms % 10 * (p.lifetime_ms / 100)     # (up to 9% early: not all at once)
    if p.lifetime_ms > 0 and now - c.born_ms > p.lifetime_ms - jitter:
        return true
    idle = now - c.used_ms
    if p.idle_ms > 0 and idle > p.idle_ms:
        return true
    return idle >= 100 and c.sock.pending()          # the server closed it (a restart, a kill)

# after a statement: keep the connection for the task while a transaction is open
fn _give_back(p: Pool, c: Conn):
    if not c.live:
        return
    if c.broken:
        _close_conn(c)
        p.state.update(fn(s) _count(&s, -1, 0, 1))
        p.free.send(_no_conn())
        _unmark(p)
        return
    if c.txs != 73:                                  # in a transaction ('T', or 'E': failed)
        tid = task.id()
        _shard(p, tid).update(fn(s) _hold(&s, tid, c))
        task.local_set(p.key, "1")
        return
    _unmark(p)
    back = c
    back.used_ms = time.mono_ms()
    back.uses += 1
    p.free.send(back)
    if p.idle_ms > 0 and back.uses % 256 == 0:       # now and then: close idle connections
        every = min(p.idle_ms / 2, 60000)
        now = back.used_ms
        if p.state.update(fn(s) _due(&s, now, every)):
            prune(p)

fn _unmark(p: Pool):
    if task.local_get(p.key) != "":
        task.local_set(p.key, "")

fn _hold(s: mut _Shard, tid: int, c: Conn) int:
    s.bound[tid] = c
    return 0

fn _due(s: mut _State, now: int, every: int) bool:
    if now - s.pruned < every:
        return false
    s.pruned = now
    return true

# Closes the connections idle longer than max_idle, so a pool shrinks after a busy spell.
# The pool does this by itself now and then, as connections come back.
fn prune(p: Pool):
    if p.idle_ms <= 0:
        return
    now = time.mono_ms()
    closed = 0
    for i in 0..len(p.free):
        c = _no_conn()
        if not p.free.try_recv(&c):
            break
        if c.live and now - c.used_ms > p.idle_ms:
            _close_conn(c)
            closed += 1
            c = _no_conn()
        p.free.send(c)
    if closed > 0:
        p.state.update(fn(s) _count(&s, -closed, 0, closed))

# closes the idle connections (the pool opens new ones when it needs them again)
fn close(p: Pool):
    closed = 0
    for i in 0..len(p.free):
        c = _no_conn()
        if not p.free.try_recv(&c):
            break
        if c.live:
            _close_conn(c)
            closed += 1
        p.free.send(_no_conn())
    if closed > 0:
        p.state.update(fn(s) _count(&s, -closed, 0, closed))

# a URL's ?name=value ("" if it has none)
fn _param(url: str, name: str) str:
    q = url.find("?")
    if q < 0:
        return ""
    for kv in url[q + 1..].split("&"):
        if kv.starts_with(name + "="):
            return kv[len(name) + 1..]
    return ""

# "5s", "500ms", "30m", "1h", "90" (seconds), "0" (off) -> milliseconds; dflt if empty or not one
fn _ms(text: str, dflt: int) int:
    units = [("ms", 1), ("s", 1000), ("m", 60000), ("h", 3600000)]
    for u in units:
        if text.ends_with(u.0) and len(text) > len(u.0):
            n = text[..len(text) - len(u.0)].to_float(-1.0)
            if n >= 0.0:
                return int(n * float(u.1))
    n = text.to_float(-1.0)
    if n >= 0.0 and text != "":
        return int(n * 1000.0)
    return dflt

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- statements

fn exec(p: Pool, sql: str, params: [str]) int:
    c = _take(p)
    if not c.live:
        return -1
    r = _run(&c, sql, params, 0)
    _give_back(p, c)
    return r.affected if r.ok else -1

fn _rows(p: Pool, sql: str, params: [str], mode: int) str:
    c = _take(p)
    if not c.live:
        return "null" if mode == 3 else ("" if mode == 4 else "[]")
    r = _run(&c, sql, params, mode)
    _give_back(p, c)
    if not r.ok:
        return "null" if mode == 3 else ("" if mode == 4 else "[]")
    return r.out

fn query_json(p: Pool, sql: str, params: [str]) str:
    return _rows(p, sql, params, 1)

fn query_row_json(p: Pool, sql: str, params: [str]) str:
    return _rows(p, sql, params, 3)

fn query(p: Pool, sql: str, params: [str]) [{str: str}]:
    rows: [{str: str}] = []
    json.decode(_rows(p, sql, params, 2), &rows)
    return rows

fn begin(p: Pool) bool:
    return exec(p, "BEGIN", []) >= 0

fn commit(p: Pool) bool:
    return exec(p, "COMMIT", []) >= 0

fn rollback(p: Pool) bool:
    return exec(p, "ROLLBACK", []) >= 0

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- with Result
# The same queries, returning Result: rows decoded straight into your struct type, and the
# server's message as the error ("pg: query failed: ERROR 42P01: relation \"x\" does not exist").
#   users: [User] = db.fetch("SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE team = $1", [team])?
#   u = db.fetch_one[User]("SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id = $1", [id])?     # Option[User]
#   n = db.run("DELETE FROM sessions WHERE expires < now()", [])?                 # rows affected

fn _fail(what: str) str:
    return "pg: " + what + ": " + error()

fn fetch[T](p: Pool, sql: str, params: [str]) Result[[T], str]:
    raw = _rows(p, sql, params, 4)               # the rows as the server sent them
    if error() != "":
        return Err(_fail("query failed"))
    rows: [T] = []
    if sql.decode_rows(raw, &rows) < 0:          # decoded by code made for T
        why = sql.decode_error()                 # (which value didn't fit which field)
        if why != "":
            return Err("pg: query failed: " + why)
        return Err("pg: query failed: the rows don't fit the type (check the column names and types)")
    return Ok(rows)

fn fetch_one[T](p: Pool, sql: str, params: [str]) Result[Option[T], str]:
    rows: [T] = fetch(p, sql, params)?
    none: Option[T] = None
    if len(rows) == 0:
        return Ok(none)
    return Ok(Some(rows[0]))

fn run(p: Pool, sql: str, params: [str]) Result[int, str]:
    n = exec(p, sql, params)
    if n < 0:
        return Err(_fail("statement failed"))
    return Ok(n)

# several statements in one string (a schema file, a migration), run with the simple query
# protocol: in one implicit transaction unless the script has its own BEGIN / COMMIT, and
# with no $1 parameters. The rows affected, added up; the first error stops the script.
fn run_script(p: Pool, sql: str) Result[int, str]:
    c = _take(p)
    if not c.live:
        return Err(_fail("script failed"))
    r = _script(&c, sql)
    _give_back(p, c)
    if not r.ok:
        return Err(_fail("script failed"))
    return Ok(r.affected)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- describing a statement
# What the server knows about a statement, without running it: the types of its $1, $2, ...
# parameters and of the columns it returns (the base for generating typed query code).
#   s = db.describe("SELECT id, email FROM users WHERE id = $1")?
#   s.params                    ["int8"]
#   s.columns[1]                Column{name: "email", type_name: "text", table: "users", not_null: false, ...}

struct Column:
    name: str
    type_name: str              # pg_type.typname: "int8", "text", "timestamptz", "_int4" (int4[]), ...
    type_oid: int
    kind: str                   # pg_type.typtype: "b" base, "e" enum, "d" domain, "c" composite, ...
    base_type: str              # a domain's underlying type ("" otherwise)
    table: str                  # the table (or view) the column comes from; "" for an expression
    not_null: bool              # a table column declared NOT NULL (an outer join can still make it null)

struct Statement:
    params: [str]               # the type names of $1, $2, ...
    param_oids: [int]
    param_kinds: [str]          # ... and their pg_type.typtype ("e": an enum)
    columns: [Column]           # [] for a statement that returns no rows

struct _Type:
    oid: int
    name: str
    kind: str
    base: str

struct _Attr:
    rel: int
    num: int
    notnull: bool
    relname: str

fn describe(p: Pool, sql: str) Result[Statement, str]:
    c = _take(p)
    if not c.live:
        return Err(_fail("describe failed"))
    got = _describe_raw(&c, sql)
    _give_back(p, c)
    raw = got.map_err(fn(e) "pg: describe failed: " + e.replace("pg: ", ""))?
    oids: [int] = []
    rels: [int] = []
    for o in raw.params:
        oids.push(o)
    for c in raw.columns:
        oids.push(c.oid)
        if c.table != 0:
            rels.push(c.table)
    types: {int: _Type} = {}
    ts = fetch[_Type](p, "SELECT t.oid::int8 AS oid, t.typname::text AS name, t.typtype::text AS kind, coalesce(b.typname::text, '') AS base FROM pg_type t LEFT JOIN pg_type b ON b.oid = t.typbasetype AND t.typtype = 'd' WHERE t.oid = ANY($1::oid[])", [_oid_array(oids)])?
    for t in ts:
        types[t.oid] = t
    attrs: {str: _Attr} = {}
    if len(rels) > 0:
        as_ = fetch[_Attr](p, "SELECT a.attrelid::int8 AS rel, a.attnum::int8 AS num, a.attnotnull AS notnull, c.relname::text AS relname FROM pg_attribute a JOIN pg_class c ON c.oid = a.attrelid WHERE a.attrelid = ANY($1::oid[]) AND a.attnum > 0", [_oid_array(rels)])?
        for a in as_:
            attrs[f"{a.rel}.{a.num}"] = a
    out = Statement([], [], [], [])
    for o in raw.params:
        out.params.push(_type_of(types, o).name)
        out.param_kinds.push(_type_of(types, o).kind)
        out.param_oids.push(o)
    for c in raw.columns:
        t = _type_of(types, c.oid)
        col = Column(c.name, t.name, c.oid, t.kind, t.base, "", false)
        key = f"{c.table}.{c.column}"
        if c.table != 0 and key in attrs:
            col.table = attrs[key].relname
            col.not_null = attrs[key].notnull
        out.columns.push(col)
    return Ok(out)

fn _type_of(types: {int: _Type}, oid: int) _Type:
    if oid in types:
        return types[oid]
    return _Type(oid, "unknown", "", "")

fn _oid_array(xs: [int]) str:
    return "{" + ",".join(xs.map(fn(x) str(x))) + "}"

# A parameter that is SQL NULL: pass pg.NULL in params (["x", pg.NULL]). It is the one-byte
# string "\x00", which PostgreSQL text can never contain.
const NULL = "\x00"

# Arrays as parameters, in PostgreSQL's text form: `WHERE id = ANY($1)` with [pg.array_int(ids)].
# (Rows read arrays back into [int], [float], [bool] and [str] fields by themselves.)
fn array_int(xs: [int]) str:
    return "{" + ",".join(xs.map(fn(x) str(x))) + "}"

fn array_float(xs: [float]) str:
    return "{" + ",".join(xs.map(fn(x) str(x))) + "}"

fn array_bool(xs: [bool]) str:
    return "{" + ",".join(xs.map(fn(x) "t" if x else "f")) + "}"

fn array_str(xs: [str]) str:
    return "{" + ",".join(xs.map(fn(x) "\"" + x.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("\"", "\\\"") + "\"")) + "}"
```

## deps/pg/wire.tn

```tern
# pg: the PostgreSQL wire protocol (version 3), in Tern (pg.tn builds the API on it):
# connecting (TLS through SSLRequest; SCRAM-SHA-256 or password logins), statements through
# the extended protocol with each connection's prepared statements kept by their SQL, scripts
# through the simple protocol, and replies read into what the API returns.

# a statement prepared on a connection
struct Stmt:
    name: str                   # "t3" ("": unnamed, prepared again each time)
    cols: [str]                 # the columns it returns
    keys: [str]                 # ... as JSON keys: "\"id\":"
    types: [int]                # ... and their type OIDs
    head: str                   # Bind's constant start: portal, name, parameter formats ("": not prepared)
    fmts: str                   # ... and its result formats for pg.fetch (numbers in binary; "": all text)

struct Conn:
    sock: net.Conn
    live: bool                  # false: no connection (an empty slot in a pool)
    buf: str                    # bytes read and not used yet, from `at` on
    at: int
    ms: int                     # the message just read: where its body starts in buf,
    ml: int                     # ... its length,
    mt: int                     # ... and its type ('D', 'Z', ...)
    stmts: {str: Stmt}          # the statements prepared here, by their SQL
    txs: int                    # from ReadyForQuery: 'I' idle, 'T' in a transaction, 'E' a failed one
    broken: bool
    no_cache: bool              # ?statement_cache=off: unnamed statements only (PgBouncer)
    born_ms: int                # opened, and last used (time.mono_ms): for the pool
    used_ms: int
    uses: int                   # statements run (the pool looks at idle connections every so often)

# what a statement's reply comes to
struct Reply:
    ok: bool
    affected: int               # rows changed (or returned)
    out: str                    # the rows: JSON (modes 1-3) or raw (mode 4)

struct Url:
    user: str
    password: str
    host: str
    port: int
    db: str
    ssl: str
    app: str
    cache: str

fn _no_conn() Conn:
    return Conn(net.Conn(-1), false, "", 0, 0, 0, 0, {}, 73, true, false, 0, 0, 0)

fn _fail_reply(msg: str) Reply:
    _set_err(msg)
    return Reply(false, -1, "")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- bytes

fn _u32(n: int) str:
    return chr((n >> 24) & 255) + chr((n >> 16) & 255) + chr((n >> 8) & 255) + chr(n & 255)

fn _u16(n: int) str:
    return chr((n >> 8) & 255) + chr(n & 255)

fn _le32(n: int) str:                   # (the raw rows' header is read with memcpy: native order)
    return chr(n & 255) + chr((n >> 8) & 255) + chr((n >> 16) & 255) + chr((n >> 24) & 255)

fn _msg(t: str, body: str) str:
    return t + _u32(len(body) + 4) + body

fn _be32(s: str, i: int) int:
    return (s.byte(i) << 24) | (s.byte(i + 1) << 16) | (s.byte(i + 2) << 8) | s.byte(i + 3)

fn _be16(s: str, i: int) int:
    return (s.byte(i) << 8) | s.byte(i + 1)

fn _i32(s: str, i: int) int:
    v = _be32(s, i)
    return v - 4294967296 if v >= 2147483648 else v

# the NUL-terminated string at s[i..] (before e)
fn _cstr(s: str, i: int, e: int) str:
    j = i
    while j < e and s.byte(j) != 0:
        j += 1
    return s[i..j]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- reading and writing

# at least n bytes from c.at in c.buf
fn _read(c: mut Conn, n: int) bool:
    while len(c.buf) - c.at < n:
        got = c.sock.refill(&c.buf, c.at, 65536)       # (what was at c.at is now at 0)
        c.ms -= c.at
        c.at = 0
        if got == 0:
            c.broken = true
            why = net.error()
            _set_err("pg: connection lost" + (" (" + why + ")" if why != "" else ""))
            return false
    return true

# the next message (notices, parameter changes and notifications skipped): c.mt, c.ms, c.ml
fn _next(c: mut Conn) bool:
    while true:
        c.at = c.ms + c.ml
        if len(c.buf) - c.at < 5 and not _read(&c, 5):
            return false
        n = _be32(c.buf, c.at + 1)
        if n < 4 or n > 1073741824:
            c.broken = true
            _set_err("pg: protocol error (bad message length)")
            return false
        c.ms = c.at + 5
        c.ml = 0
        if len(c.buf) - c.at < n + 1 and not _read(&c, n + 1):
            return false
        c.mt = c.buf.byte(c.at)
        c.ms = c.at + 5
        c.ml = n - 4
        if not (c.mt == 78 or c.mt == 83 or c.mt == 65):
            return true
    return false

fn _send(c: mut Conn, out: str) bool:
    if c.sock.write(out):
        return true
    c.broken = true
    why = net.error()
    _set_err("pg: connection lost" + (" (" + why + ")" if why != "" else ""))
    return false

# an ErrorResponse: "ERROR 42P01: relation \"x\" does not exist (DETAIL) hint: HINT"
fn _server_error(c: Conn) str:
    sev = "ERROR"
    code = ""
    msg = ""
    detail = ""
    hint = ""
    i = c.ms
    e = c.ms + c.ml
    while i < e and c.buf.byte(i) != 0:
        f = c.buf.byte(i)
        v = _cstr(c.buf, i + 1, e)
        i += len(v) + 2
        if f == 83:
            sev = v
        elif f == 67:
            code = v
        elif f == 77:
            msg = v
        elif f == 68:
            detail = v
        elif f == 72:
            hint = v
    out = f"{sev} {code}: {msg}"
    if detail != "":
        out += f" ({detail})"
    if hint != "":
        out += " hint: " + hint
    return out

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- connecting

# postgres://user:password@host:port/dbname?sslmode=require&application_name=x&statement_cache=off
fn _parse_url(url: str) Result[Url, str]:
    rest = ""
    if url.starts_with("postgresql://"):
        rest = url[13..]
    elif url.starts_with("postgres://"):
        rest = url[11..]
    else:
        return Err("pg: not a postgres:// url")
    u = Url("postgres", "", "localhost", 5432, "", "prefer", "tern", "")
    query = ""
    q = rest.find("?")
    if q >= 0:
        query = rest[q + 1..]
        rest = rest[..q]
    hostpart = rest
    slash = rest.find("/")
    if slash >= 0:
        u.db = _unescape(rest[slash + 1..])
        hostpart = rest[..slash]
    at = _last(hostpart, "@")
    if at >= 0:
        cred = hostpart[..at]
        hostpart = hostpart[at + 1..]
        colon = cred.find(":")
        if colon >= 0:
            u.user = _unescape(cred[..colon])
            u.password = _unescape(cred[colon + 1..])
        else:
            u.user = _unescape(cred)
    if hostpart.starts_with("["):
        rb = hostpart.find("]")
        if rb < 0:
            return Err("pg: not a postgres:// url")
        u.host = hostpart[1..rb]
        if hostpart[rb + 1..].starts_with(":"):
            u.port = hostpart[rb + 2..].to_int(5432)
    else:
        colon = _last(hostpart, ":")
        if colon >= 0:
            u.port = hostpart[colon + 1..].to_int(5432)
            hostpart = hostpart[..colon]
        if hostpart != "":
            u.host = _unescape(hostpart)
    if u.db == "":
        u.db = u.user
    for kv in query.split("&"):
        eq = kv.find("=")
        if eq < 0:
            continue
        v = _unescape(kv[eq + 1..])
        k = kv[..eq]
        if k == "sslmode":
            u.ssl = v
        elif k == "application_name":
            u.app = v
        elif k == "statement_cache":
            u.cache = v
    return Ok(u)

fn _last(s: str, sub: str) int:        # (sub: one byte)
    b = sub.byte(0)
    i = len(s) - 1
    while i >= 0 and s.byte(i) != b:
        i -= 1
    return i

fn _unescape(s: str) str:             # %40 -> @
    if not s.contains("%"):
        return s
    out = ""
    i = 0
    while i < len(s):
        if s[i] == "%" and i + 2 < len(s) + 0 and _hex(s.byte(i + 1)) >= 0 and _hex(s.byte(i + 2)) >= 0:
            out += chr(_hex(s.byte(i + 1)) * 16 + _hex(s.byte(i + 2)))
            i += 3
        else:
            out += s[i]
            i += 1
    return out

fn _hex(c: int) int:
    if c >= 48 and c <= 57:
        return c - 48
    if c >= 97 and c <= 102:
        return c - 87
    if c >= 65 and c <= 70:
        return c - 55
    return -1

# a new connection, logged in and ready; or not live, and pg.error() says why
fn _open(url: str) Conn:
    r = _open_r(url)
    if r is Err(e):
        _set_err(e)
        return _no_conn()
    _set_err("")
    return r.unwrap()

fn _open_r(url: str) Result[Conn, str]:
    u = _parse_url(url)?
    sock = net.connect(u.host, u.port)
    if not sock.ok():
        return Err("pg: " + net.error())
    now = time.mono_ms()
    c = Conn(sock, true, "", 0, 0, 0, 0, {}, 73, false, u.cache == "off", now, now, 0)
    r = _login(&c, u)
    if r is Err(e):
        sock.close()
        return Err(e)
    return Ok(c)

fn _login(c: mut Conn, u: Url) Result[int, str]:
    if not (u.ssl in ["disable", "prefer", "allow"]):
        if not _send(&c, _u32(8) + _u32(80877103)):           # SSLRequest
            return Err(error())
        answer = c.sock.read_exact(1)
        if answer != "S":
            return Err("pg: the server doesn't accept TLS connections")
        if not c.sock.starttls(u.host, u.ssl == "verify-full"):
            return Err("pg: " + net.error())
    body = _u32(196608) + "user\x00" + u.user + "\x00database\x00" + u.db + "\x00application_name\x00" + u.app + "\x00client_encoding\x00UTF8\x00\x00"
    if not _send(&c, _u32(len(body) + 4) + body):
        return Err(error())
    while true:
        if not _next(&c):
            return Err(error())
        if c.mt == 69:
            return Err(_server_error(c))
        if c.mt == 90:
            c.txs = c.buf.byte(c.ms)
            return Ok(0)
        if c.mt != 82 or c.ml < 4:
            continue                                          # BackendKeyData, ...
        kind = _be32(c.buf, c.ms)
        if kind == 0:
            continue                                          # AuthenticationOk
        if kind == 3:                                         # a password in clear (over TLS, one hopes)
            if not _send(&c, _msg("p", u.password + "\x00")):
                return Err(error())
        elif kind == 10:
            mechs = c.buf[c.ms + 4..c.ms + c.ml]
            if not mechs.contains("SCRAM-SHA-256\x00"):
                return Err("pg: the server wants a SASL mechanism other than SCRAM-SHA-256")
            _scram(&c, u.password)?
        else:
            return Err(f"pg: unsupported authentication method {kind} (use scram-sha-256 or password)")
    return Err("pg: login failed")

# SCRAM-SHA-256 (RFC 5802 / 7677), what PostgreSQL uses by default
fn _scram(c: mut Conn, password: str) Result[int, str]:
    nonce = crypto.base64(crypto.random_bytes(18))
    first_bare = "n=,r=" + nonce
    first = "n,," + first_bare
    if not _send(&c, _msg("p", "SCRAM-SHA-256\x00" + _u32(len(first)) + first)):
        return Err(error())
    server_first = _sasl_reply(&c, 11)?
    rnonce = ""
    salt64 = ""
    iters = 0
    for part in server_first.split(","):
        if part.starts_with("r="):
            rnonce = part[2..]
        elif part.starts_with("s="):
            salt64 = part[2..]
        elif part.starts_with("i="):
            iters = part[2..].to_int(0)
    if not rnonce.starts_with(nonce):
        return Err("pg: SCRAM: bad server message")
    salt = crypto.base64_decode(salt64)
    if salt == "" or iters < 1:
        return Err("pg: SCRAM: bad salt")
    salted = crypto.pbkdf2_sha256(password, salt, iters, 32)
    client_key = crypto.hmac_sha256(salted, "Client Key")
    final_bare = "c=biws,r=" + rnonce
    auth = first_bare + "," + server_first + "," + final_bare
    sig = crypto.hmac_sha256(crypto.sha256(client_key), auth)
    proof = ""
    for i in 0..32:
        proof += chr(client_key.byte(i) ^ sig.byte(i))
    if not _send(&c, _msg("p", final_bare + ",p=" + crypto.base64(proof))):
        return Err(error())
    server_final = _sasl_reply(&c, 12)?
    want = "v=" + crypto.base64(crypto.hmac_sha256(crypto.hmac_sha256(salted, "Server Key"), auth))
    if not server_final.starts_with(want):
        return Err("pg: SCRAM: the server's signature is wrong (not the real server?)")
    return Ok(0)

fn _sasl_reply(c: mut Conn, want: int) Result[str, str]:
    if not _next(&c):
        return Err(error())
    if c.mt == 69:
        return Err(_server_error(c))
    if c.mt != 82 or c.ml < 4 or _be32(c.buf, c.ms) != want:
        return Err("pg: SCRAM: unexpected reply")
    return Ok(c.buf[c.ms + 4..c.ms + c.ml])

fn _close_conn(c: Conn):
    if c.live and not c.broken:
        c.sock.write("X\x00\x00\x00\x04")                    # Terminate
    if c.live:
        c.sock.close()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- statements

# Types a prepared statement's rows bring back in binary, for pg.fetch (mode 4): numbers
# and booleans, which the server then needn't format nor the decoder parse.
fn _binary(oid: int) bool:
    return oid == 16 or oid == 20 or oid == 21 or oid == 23 or oid == 26 or oid == 700 or oid == 701

# Runs sql with params. mode 0: the rows affected; 1: the rows as JSON (typed); 2: as JSON,
# every value a string (NULL: ""); 3: like 1, only the first row, an object ("null": none);
# 4: raw, for the decoders the compiler writes (sql.decode_rows).
fn _run(c: mut Conn, sql: str, params: [str], mode: int) Reply:
    if c.broken:
        return _fail_reply("pg: the connection is broken")
    st = c.stmts.get(sql, Stmt("", [], [], [], "", ""))
    cached = st.head != ""
    pre = ""
    if not cached:
        name = "t" + str(len(c.stmts)) if not c.no_cache and len(c.stmts) < 256 else ""
        st = Stmt(name, [], [], [], "\x00" + name + "\x00\x00\x00", "")
        pre = _msg("P", name + "\x00" + sql + "\x00\x00\x00") + _msg("D", "S" + name + "\x00")
    binary = mode == 4 and cached and st.fmts != ""
    fm = st.fmts if binary else "\x00\x00"
    vals: [str] = []                                          # the parameters, as Bind has them
    size = 0
    for v in params:
        if v == "\x00":
            vals.push("\xff\xff\xff\xff")                     # pg.NULL
            size += 4
        else:
            vals.push(_u32(len(v)))
            vals.push(v)
            size += 4 + len(v)
    out = pre + "B" + _u32(6 + len(st.head) + size + len(fm)) + st.head + _u16(len(params)) + "".join(vals) + fm + "E\x00\x00\x00\x09\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00S\x00\x00\x00\x04"
    if not _send(&c, out):
        return Reply(false, -1, "")
    res = "[" if mode == 1 or mode == 2 else ""
    rows = 0
    affected = 0
    err = ""
    parsed = cached
    described = cached
    while _next(&c):
        t = c.mt
        if t == 90:                                           # ReadyForQuery
            c.txs = c.buf.byte(c.ms)
            if not cached and parsed and st.name != "" and described:
                c.stmts[sql] = st                             # kept, even if running it failed
            if err != "":
                return _fail_reply(err)
            if mode == 1 or mode == 2:
                res += "]"
            elif mode == 3 and rows == 0:
                res = "null"
            elif mode == 4 and rows == 0:
                res = _raw_header(st, binary)
            _set_err("")
            return Reply(true, affected, res)
        if t == 69:
            if err == "":
                err = _server_error(c)
        elif err != "":
            pass
        elif t == 49:                                         # ParseComplete
            parsed = true
        elif t == 84 and not cached:                          # RowDescription
            st = _row_description(c, st.name, st.head)
            described = true
        elif t == 110 and not cached:                         # NoData
            described = true
        elif t == 68:                                         # DataRow
            if mode == 4:
                if rows == 0:
                    res = _raw_header(st, binary)
                # this row and the ones right after it in the buffer, copied as one block
                # (whole messages: the decoder steps over each one's type and length)
                end = c.ms + c.ml
                k = 1
                while end + 5 <= len(c.buf) and c.buf.byte(end) == 68:
                    m = _be32(c.buf, end + 1)
                    if end + 1 + m > len(c.buf):
                        break
                    end += 1 + m
                    k += 1
                res += c.buf[c.ms - 5..end]
                rows += k
                c.ml = end - c.ms                                 # (the next message is after the block)
                continue
            rows += 1
            if mode != 0 and not (mode == 3 and rows > 1):
                if rows > 1:
                    res += ","
                res += _json_row(c, st, mode)
        elif t == 67:                                         # CommandComplete: "UPDATE 2"
            affected = _tag_count(_cstr(c.buf, c.ms, c.ms + c.ml), rows)
    return Reply(false, -1, "")

fn _row_description(c: Conn, name: str, head: str) Stmt:
    st = Stmt(name, [], [], [], head, "")
    n = _be16(c.buf, c.ms)
    i = c.ms + 2
    e = c.ms + c.ml
    for k in 0..n:
        col = _cstr(c.buf, i, e)
        i += len(col) + 1
        st.cols.push(copy(col))
        st.keys.push(json_quote(col) + ":")
        st.types.push(_be32(c.buf, i + 6))
        i += 18
    fm = _u16(n)
    any = false
    for t in st.types:
        fm += "\x00\x01" if _binary(t) else "\x00\x00"
        any = any or _binary(t)
    if any:
        st.fmts = fm
    return st

fn _tag_count(tag: str, rows: int) int:
    sp = _last(tag, " ")
    return rows if sp < 0 else tag[sp + 1..].to_int(rows)

# a DataRow as a JSON object
fn _json_row(c: Conn, st: Stmt, mode: int) str:
    out = "{"
    n = min(_be16(c.buf, c.ms), len(st.keys))
    i = c.ms + 2
    for k in 0..n:
        vlen = _i32(c.buf, i)
        i += 4
        if k > 0:
            out += ","
        out += st.keys[k]
        if vlen < 0:
            out += "\"\"" if mode == 2 else "null"
            continue
        v = c.buf[i..i + vlen]
        i += vlen
        out += _json_value(v, st.types[k], mode)
    return out + "}"

fn _json_value(v: str, oid: int, mode: int) str:
    if mode != 2:
        if oid == 16:
            return "true" if v == "t" else "false"
        if oid == 20 or oid == 21 or oid == 23 or oid == 26:
            return v
        if (oid == 700 or oid == 701 or oid == 1700) and len(v) > 0 and not v.ends_with("y") and (v[0] == "-" or (v.byte(0) >= 48 and v.byte(0) <= 57)):
            return v
    return json_quote(v)

# the raw rows' header (library/std/sql.tn): the columns and how their values are written;
# after it come the DataRow messages, whole (they're the rows sql.decode_rows reads)
fn _raw_header(st: Stmt, binary: bool) str:
    out = _le32(len(st.cols))
    for k, col in st.cols:
        out += _le32(_format(st.types[k]) if binary else sql.TEXT) + _le32(len(col)) + col
    return out

# how a binary field of PostgreSQL type oid is written, as std sql names it
fn _format(oid: int) int:
    if oid == 16:
        return sql.BOOL
    if oid == 20 or oid == 21 or oid == 23:
        return sql.INT
    if oid == 26:
        return sql.UINT
    if oid == 700 or oid == 701:
        return sql.FLOAT
    return sql.TEXT

# Several statements in one string, through the simple protocol: in one implicit transaction
# unless the script has its own BEGIN / COMMIT; the first error stops the rest. The rows
# affected, added up.
fn _script(c: mut Conn, sql: str) Reply:
    if c.broken:
        return _fail_reply("pg: the connection is broken")
    if not _send(&c, _msg("Q", sql + "\x00")):
        return Reply(false, -1, "")
    total = 0
    err = ""
    while _next(&c):
        t = c.mt
        if t == 90:
            c.txs = c.buf.byte(c.ms)
            if err != "":
                return _fail_reply(err)
            _set_err("")
            return Reply(true, total, "")
        if t == 69 and err == "":
            err = _server_error(c)
        elif t == 67:
            tag = _cstr(c.buf, c.ms, c.ms + c.ml)
            sp = _last(tag, " ")
            if sp >= 0:
                total += tag[sp + 1..].to_int(0)
        elif t == 71:                                         # CopyInResponse: a script can't send data
            if not _send(&c, _msg("f", "COPY FROM STDIN is not supported in a script\x00")):
                return Reply(false, -1, "")
    return Reply(false, -1, "")

struct _RawCol:
    name: str
    oid: int
    table: int
    column: int

struct _Raw:
    params: [int]
    columns: [_RawCol]

# what the server knows about a statement, without running it (Parse and Describe, unnamed)
fn _describe_raw(c: mut Conn, sql: str) Result[_Raw, str]:
    if c.broken:
        return Err("pg: the connection is broken")
    out = _msg("P", "\x00" + sql + "\x00\x00\x00") + _msg("D", "S\x00") + "S\x00\x00\x00\x04"
    if not _send(&c, out):
        return Err(error())
    raw = _Raw([], [])
    err = ""
    while _next(&c):
        t = c.mt
        if t == 90:
            c.txs = c.buf.byte(c.ms)
            if err != "":
                return Err(err)
            return Ok(raw)
        if t == 69 and err == "":
            err = _server_error(c)
        elif t == 116 and err == "":                          # ParameterDescription
            for k in 0.._be16(c.buf, c.ms):
                raw.params.push(_be32(c.buf, c.ms + 2 + 4 * k))
        elif t == 84 and err == "":
            i = c.ms + 2
            e = c.ms + c.ml
            for k in 0.._be16(c.buf, c.ms):
                col = _cstr(c.buf, i, e)
                i += len(col) + 1
                raw.columns.push(_RawCol(copy(col), _be32(c.buf, i + 6), _be32(c.buf, i), _be16(c.buf, i + 4)))
                i += 18
    return Err(error())
```

## deps/queue/queue.tn

```tern
# queue: a client for ternq, the message queue broker (examples/queue/).
#
#   import queue
#   c = queue.connect("127.0.0.1", 7070)          # check c.ok
#   c.publish("jobs", "hello")                     # true once the broker has it on disk
#   s = c.subscribe("jobs", "workers", 64)         # group "workers", up to 64 unacked at once
#   m = queue.empty_msg()
#   while s.next(&m):
#       print(m.body)
#       c.ack(m)                                   # or c.nack(m) to have it redelivered
#
# queue.connect(host: str, port: int) Client       one connection, shared by any number of tasks
# queue.connect_many(addrs: [str]) Client          several brokers ("host:port"); each queue lives
#                                                  on one, chosen by a hash of its name (sharding).
#                                                  An entry can list a primary and its followers,
#                                                  "h1:7070,h2:7070": the client moves to whichever
#                                                  of them is the primary (failover)
# queue.connect_auth(addrs: [str], token: str) Client   the same, for brokers started with --token
# c.shard_of(q: str) int                           which of them holds q
# queue.empty_msg() Msg                            a Msg to receive into
# c.ok bool                                        the first connect worked (it reconnects by itself later)
# c.publish(q: str, body: str) bool                waits for the broker's ack (false: client closed)
# c.publish_delayed(q: str, body: str, delay_ms: int) bool   deliver no sooner than delay_ms from now
# c.publish_batch(q: str, bodies: [str]) bool      one frame, one ack for all of them
# c.publish_async(q: str, body: str) chan[bool]    don't wait: recv() the result later (pipelining)
# c.subscribe(q: str, group: str, prefetch: int) Sub   each group gets every message; the
#                                                  consumers in a group share them. prefetch 0: pull only
# s.next(m: mut Msg) bool                          waits for the next message (false: client closed)
# s.next_timeout(m: mut Msg, ms: int) bool         false if none came within ms
# s.msgs chan[Msg]                                 the subscription's messages, as a channel
# c.fetch(s: Sub, max: int) [Msg]                  pull up to max messages now (any subscription)
# c.fetch_wait(s: Sub, max: int, ms: int) [Msg]    the same, but with none there, wait up to ms for some
# c.ack(m: Msg)   c.nack(m: Msg)                   acks are batched into one frame per burst
# c.unsubscribe(s: Sub)                            its unacked messages go back to the group
# c.stats(q: str) str                              JSON: depth, in-flight, rates, per group
# c.queues() str                                   JSON array of queue names
# c.shutdown_broker()                             ask the broker to stop gracefully (admin)
# c.close()
#
# Delivery is at least once: a message is redelivered if it isn't acked within the
# broker's visibility timeout, if it's nacked, or if its consumer disconnects. After a
# lost connection the client reconnects (with backoff), resends every publish that
# wasn't acked yet, and subscribes again, so a publish may arrive twice. With a failover
# list it tries the next address after a lost connection, and it tells every broker the
# highest epoch it has seen, so a replaced primary that is still running stops rather
# than taking writes (see examples/queue/README.md).
#
# Inside: one task owns the connection. Callers send it requests on a channel; it
# writes whatever has piled up with one write, and a reader task parses what the
# broker sends back (messages go straight to their subscription's channel).

import net
import task
import time

struct Msg:
    sid: int
    seq: int
    attempt: int
    body: str
    shard: int                                     # which broker (connect_many)

struct Client:
    ok: bool
    shards: [chan[Req]]                            # one connection task per broker

struct Sub:
    sid: int
    shard: int
    msgs: chan[Msg]

enum Req:
    Publish(queue: str, body: str, delay: int, reply: chan[bool])
    PublishBatch(queue: str, bodies: [str], reply: chan[bool])
    Subscribe(queue: str, group: str, prefetch: int, msgs: chan[Msg], reply: chan[int])
    Unsubscribe(sid: int)
    Ack(sid: int, seq: int, ok: bool)
    Fetch(sid: int, max: int, wait: int, reply: chan[int])
    Query(line: str, reply: chan[str])
    Raw(line: str)
    Close
    Reply(gen: int, id: int, ok: bool)            # from the reader
    Json(gen: int, id: int, text: str)
    Fetched(gen: int, sid: int, n: int)
    Lost(gen: int)
    Deliver(gen: int, m: Msg)
    Epoch(gen: int, epoch: int)

struct Pending:                                    # a request waiting for its reply
    frame: str
    ok: chan[bool]
    txt: chan[str]
    kind: int                                      # 0 publish, 1 query

struct SubInfo:
    queue: str
    group: str
    prefetch: int
    msgs: chan[Msg]

struct Addr:
    host: str
    port: int

struct State:
    addrs: [Addr]                                  # a primary and its followers
    cur: int                                       # the one we're connected to
    token: str
    epoch: int                                     # the highest the brokers told us
    shard: int
    conn: net.Conn
    gen: int
    next_id: int
    pend: {int: Pending}
    subs: {int: SubInfo}
    fetches: {int: [chan[int]]}
    out: str
    acks: {int: str}
    closed: bool
    up: bool

fn empty_msg() Msg:
    return Msg(0, 0, 0, "", 0)

fn connect(host: str, port: int) Client:
    return connect_many([f"{host}:{port}"])

fn connect_many(addrs: [str]) Client:
    return connect_auth(addrs, "")

# several brokers: each queue lives on one of them, picked by hashing its name
# (every client given the same list agrees on where each queue is)
fn connect_auth(addrs: [str], token: str) Client:
    shards: [chan[Req]] = []
    ok = len(addrs) > 0
    for i, entry in addrs:
        list = entry.split(",").map(fn(a) _addr(a.trim()))
        reqs: chan[Req] = task.channel(0)
        st = State(list, 0, token, 0, i, net.Conn(-1), 1, 1, {}, {}, {}, "", {}, false, true)
        if _dial(&st):
            task.spawn(fn() run(st, reqs))
        else:
            ok = false
        shards.push(reqs)
    return Client(ok, shards)

fn _addr(a: str) Addr:
    k = a.find(":")
    j = k
    while j >= 0:                                  # the last ":" ("[::1]:7070" works too)
        k = j
        rest = a[k + 1..]
        j = rest.find(":")
        if j >= 0:
            j += k + 1
    return Addr(a[..k].replace("[", "").replace("]", ""), a[k + 1..].to_int(7070))

# connect to the current address, or the next ones in turn: false if none answered
fn _dial(s: mut State) bool:
    for i in 0..len(s.addrs):
        a = s.addrs[s.cur]
        c = net.connect(a.host, a.port)
        if c.ok():
            s.conn = c
            if s.token != "" or len(s.addrs) > 1:
                c.write(f"I {s.epoch} {s.token}\n")
            return true
        s.cur = (s.cur + 1) % len(s.addrs)
    return false

# which broker holds queue q: the one scoring highest for it (rendezvous hashing, so
# adding a broker to the list moves only the queues that now score highest on it)
fn shard_of(c: Client, q: str) int:
    best = 0
    top = -1
    for i in 0..len(c.shards):
        h = i + 1
        for k in 0..len(q):
            h = (h * 31 + q.byte(k)) % 1000000007
        h = (h * 2654435761 + i * 40503) % 1000000007
        if h > top:
            top = h
            best = i
    return best

fn _to(c: Client, q: str) chan[Req]:
    return c.shards[shard_of(c, q)]

fn publish(c: Client, q: str, body: str) bool:
    return publish_async(c, q, body).recv()

fn publish_delayed(c: Client, q: str, body: str, delay_ms: int) bool:
    r: chan[bool] = task.channel(1)
    _to(c, q).send(Req.Publish(q, body, delay_ms, r))
    return r.recv()

fn publish_async(c: Client, q: str, body: str) chan[bool]:
    r: chan[bool] = task.channel(1)
    _to(c, q).send(Req.Publish(q, body, 0, r))
    return r

fn publish_batch(c: Client, q: str, bodies: [str]) bool:
    r: chan[bool] = task.channel(1)
    _to(c, q).send(Req.PublishBatch(q, bodies, r))
    return r.recv()

fn subscribe(c: Client, q: str, group: str, prefetch: int) Sub:
    msgs: chan[Msg] = task.channel(0)
    r: chan[int] = task.channel(1)
    _to(c, q).send(Req.Subscribe(q, group, prefetch, msgs, r))
    return Sub(r.recv(), shard_of(c, q), msgs)

fn next(s: Sub, m: mut Msg) bool:
    return task.next(s.msgs, &m)

fn next_timeout(s: Sub, m: mut Msg, ms: int) bool:
    return s.msgs.recv_timeout(&m, ms)

fn fetch(c: Client, s: Sub, max: int) [Msg]:
    return fetch_wait(c, s, max, 0)

fn fetch_wait(c: Client, s: Sub, max: int, ms: int) [Msg]:
    r: chan[int] = task.channel(1)
    c.shards[s.shard].send(Req.Fetch(s.sid, max, ms, r))
    n = r.recv()
    out: [Msg] = []
    m = empty_msg()
    for i in 0..n:
        if not task.next(s.msgs, &m):
            break
        out.push(copy(m))
    return out

fn ack(c: Client, m: Msg):
    c.shards[m.shard].send(Req.Ack(m.sid, m.seq, true))

fn nack(c: Client, m: Msg):
    c.shards[m.shard].send(Req.Ack(m.sid, m.seq, false))

fn unsubscribe(c: Client, s: Sub):
    c.shards[s.shard].send(Req.Unsubscribe(s.sid))

fn stats(c: Client, q: str) str:
    r: chan[str] = task.channel(1)
    _to(c, q).send(Req.Query("T {id} " + q, r))
    return r.recv()

fn queues(c: Client) str:
    out = ""
    for sh in c.shards:
        r: chan[str] = task.channel(1)
        sh.send(Req.Query("L {id}", r))
        txt = r.recv()
        if len(txt) > 2:
            if out != "":
                out += ","
            out += txt[1..len(txt) - 1]
    return "[" + out + "]"

fn shutdown_broker(c: Client):
    for sh in c.shards:
        sh.send(Req.Raw("X\n"))

fn close(c: Client):
    for sh in c.shards:
        sh.send(Req.Close)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the connection's task
fn run(st: State, reqs: chan[Req]):
    s = st
    g = s.gen
    cn = s.conn
    task.spawn(fn() reader(cn, g, reqs))
    r = Req.Close
    while not s.closed and task.next(reqs, &r):
        handle(&s, r, reqs)
        n = 0
        while n < 1024 and reqs.try_recv(&r):
            handle(&s, r, reqs)
            n += 1
        if not s.up and not s.closed:
            reconnect(&s, reqs)
        if s.closed:
            if s.up:
                s.conn.write(s.out + "Q\n")      # the broker closes the connection; the reader ends
            break
        send_out(&s)
    for id, p in s.pend:
        if p.kind == 0:
            p.ok.send(false)
        else:
            p.txt.send("")
    for sid, si in s.subs:
        task.close(si.msgs)
    for sid, fs in s.fetches:
        for f in fs:
            f.send(0)

fn send_out(s: mut State):
    out = s.out
    for sid, seqs in s.acks:
        out += seqs + "\n"
    s.acks = {}
    s.out = ""
    if out != "":
        s.conn.write(out)          # if this fails, the reader sees the end and we reconnect

fn handle(s: mut State, r: Req, reqs: chan[Req]):
    match r:
        Publish(q, body, delay, reply):
            id = s.next_id
            s.next_id += 1
            f = f"P {id} {q} {delay} {len(body)}\n" + body
            _cat(&s.out, f)
            s.pend[id] = Pending(f, reply, dummy_txt(), 0)
        PublishBatch(q, bodies, reply):
            id = s.next_id
            s.next_id += 1
            head = f"B {id} {q} 0 {len(bodies)}"
            for b in bodies:
                head += f" {len(b)}"
            f = head + "\n" + "".join(bodies)
            _cat(&s.out, f)
            s.pend[id] = Pending(f, reply, dummy_txt(), 0)
        Subscribe(q, group, prefetch, msgs, reply):
            sid = s.next_id
            s.next_id += 1
            s.subs[sid] = SubInfo(q, group, prefetch, msgs)
            _cat(&s.out, f"S {sid} {q} {group} {prefetch}\n")
            reply.send(sid)
        Unsubscribe(sid):
            if sid in s.subs:
                task.close(s.subs[sid].msgs)
                s.subs.remove(sid)
                _cat(&s.out, f"U {sid}\n")
        Ack(sid, seq, ok):
            key = sid * 2
            tag = "A"
            if not ok:
                key += 1
                tag = "N"
            if key in s.acks:
                _cat(&s.acks[key], f" {seq}")
            else:
                s.acks[key] = f"{tag} {sid} {seq}"
        Fetch(sid, max, wait, reply):
            if not (sid in s.subs):
                reply.send(0)
            else:
                if not (sid in s.fetches):
                    s.fetches[sid] = []
                s.fetches[sid].push(reply)
                if wait > 0:
                    _cat(&s.out, f"F {sid} {max} {wait}\n")
                else:
                    _cat(&s.out, f"F {sid} {max}\n")
        Query(line, reply):
            id = s.next_id
            s.next_id += 1
            f = line.replace("{id}", str(id)) + "\n"
            _cat(&s.out, f)
            s.pend[id] = Pending(f, dummy_ok(), reply, 1)
        Raw(line):
            _cat(&s.out, line)
        Close:
            s.closed = true
        Reply(gen, id, ok):
            if gen == s.gen and id in s.pend:
                p = s.pend[id]
                s.pend.remove(id)
                if p.kind == 0:
                    p.ok.send(ok)
                else:
                    p.txt.send("")
        Json(gen, id, text):
            if gen == s.gen and id in s.pend:
                p = s.pend[id]
                s.pend.remove(id)
                p.txt.send(text)
        Fetched(gen, sid, n):
            if gen == s.gen and sid in s.fetches and len(s.fetches[sid]) > 0:
                s.fetches[sid][0].send(n)
                s.fetches[sid] = s.fetches[sid][1..]
        Lost(gen):
            if gen == s.gen:
                s.up = false
        Epoch(gen, epoch):
            if epoch > s.epoch:
                s.epoch = epoch
        Deliver(gen, m):
            if gen == s.gen and m.sid in s.subs:
                mm = m
                mm.shard = s.shard
                s.subs[m.sid].msgs.send(mm)

fn dummy_ok() chan[bool]:
    c: chan[bool] = task.channel(1)
    return c

fn dummy_txt() chan[str]:
    c: chan[str] = task.channel(1)
    return c

# connect again (the next address of a failover list first, then backing off up to
# 2s), then resend what's pending and resubscribe. Requests keep being taken meanwhile
# (a publish waits in s.pend; a Close gives up).
fn reconnect(s: mut State, reqs: chan[Req]):
    wait = 50
    r = Req.Close
    s.cur = (s.cur + 1) % len(s.addrs)
    while true:
        if _dial(&s):
            break
        until = time.now_ms() + wait
        while not s.closed:
            left = until - time.now_ms()
            if left <= 0 or not reqs.recv_timeout(&r, left):
                break
            handle(&s, r, reqs)
        if s.closed:
            return
        wait = min(wait * 2, 2000)
    s.up = true
    s.gen += 1
    g = s.gen
    cn = s.conn
    task.spawn(fn() reader(cn, g, reqs))
    out = ""
    for sid, si in s.subs:
        out += f"S {sid} {si.queue} {si.group} {si.prefetch}\n"
    for id, p in s.pend:
        out += p.frame
    for sid, fs in s.fetches:
        for f in fs:
            f.send(0)
    s.fetches = {}
    s.acks = {}
    s.out = ""
    s.conn.write(out)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- reading the broker's frames
fn reader(c: net.Conn, gen: int, reqs: chan[Req]):
    while true:
        line = c.read_line()
        if len(line) < 2 or not line.ends_with("\n"):
            break
        op = line.byte(0)
        pos = 1
        if op == 77:                                   # M sid seq attempt len
            sid = _int(line, &pos)
            seq = _int(line, &pos)
            att = _int(line, &pos)
            n = _int(line, &pos)
            body = _body(c, n)
            if len(body) < n:
                break
            reqs.send(Req.Deliver(gen, Msg(sid, seq, att, body, 0)))
        elif op == 75 or op == 69:                     # K id / E id msg
            id = _int(line, &pos)
            if id == 0 and op == 69:                   # this broker won't talk to us (unauthorized,
                break                                  # or replaced by a newer primary)
            reqs.send(Req.Reply(gen, id, op == 75))
        elif op == 86:                                 # V epoch
            reqs.send(Req.Epoch(gen, _int(line, &pos)))
        elif op == 74:                                 # J id len
            id = _int(line, &pos)
            n = _int(line, &pos)
            body = _body(c, n)
            if len(body) < n:
                break
            reqs.send(Req.Json(gen, id, body))
        elif op == 70:                                 # F sid n
            sid = _int(line, &pos)
            reqs.send(Req.Fetched(gen, sid, _int(line, &pos)))
    net.close(c)
    reqs.send(Req.Lost(gen))

fn _body(c: net.Conn, n: int) str:
    b = c.read(n)
    while len(b) < n:
        more = c.read(n - len(b))
        if more == "":
            return b
        b += more
    return b

fn _int(s: str, pos: mut int) int:
    n = len(s)
    while pos < n and s.byte(pos) == 32:
        pos += 1
    v = 0
    while pos < n:
        b = s.byte(pos)
        if b < 48 or b > 57:
            break
        v = v * 10 + (b - 48)
        pos += 1
    return v

# b += x in place (`s.field += x` would copy the whole string each time)
fn _cat(b: mut str, x: str):
    b += x
```

## deps/roost/check.tn

```tern
# Part of the roost package (see roost.tn for the overview): input validation.

# Validating input: collect every problem, then answer 422 with all of them at once.
#   v = roost.check()
#   v.required("name", u.name)
#   v.max_len("name", u.name, 100)
#   v.email("email", u.email)
#   v.between("age", u.age, 0, 150)
#   if not v.valid():
#       return v.problems()        # 422 {"errors": {"name": "is required", ...}}
# Each field keeps its first problem.
struct Check:
    errors: {str: str}

fn check() Check:
    return Check({})

fn valid(v: Check) bool:
    return len(v.errors) == 0

fn fail(v: mut Check, field: str, message: str):
    if not (field in v.errors):
        v.errors[field] = message

fn required(v: mut Check, field: str, value: str):
    if value.trim() == "":
        fail(&v, field, "is required")

fn min_len(v: mut Check, field: str, value: str, n: int):
    if len(value) < n:
        fail(&v, field, f"must be at least {n} characters")

fn max_len(v: mut Check, field: str, value: str, n: int):
    if len(value) > n:
        fail(&v, field, f"must be at most {n} characters")

fn between(v: mut Check, field: str, value: int, lo: int, hi: int):
    if value < lo or value > hi:
        fail(&v, field, f"must be between {lo} and {hi}")

fn one_of(v: mut Check, field: str, value: str, options: [str]):
    if not (value in options):
        fail(&v, field, "must be one of " + ", ".join(options))

# a plausible address: one @, something before it, a dot in the domain, no spaces
fn email(v: mut Check, field: str, value: str):
    at = value.find("@")
    domain = ""
    if at > 0:
        domain = value[at + 1..]
    if at <= 0 or domain.find("@") >= 0 or domain.find(".") <= 0 or domain.ends_with(".") or value.contains(" "):
        fail(&v, field, "must be an email address")

# 422 Unprocessable Content with {"errors": {field: message, ...}}
fn problems(v: Check) Response:
    body = "{\"errors\":{"
    first = true
    for k, m in v.errors:
        if not first:
            body += ","
        first = false
        body += k.json_quote() + ":" + m.json_quote()
    return Response(422, "application/json", body + "}}", "", 0)
```

## deps/roost/middleware.tn

```tern
# Part of the roost package (see roost.tn for the overview): middleware.

fn _fmt_us(us: int) str:
    if us < 1000:
        return str(us) + "us"
    if us < 1_000_000:
        return str(us / 1000) + "." + str(us / 100 % 10) + "ms"
    return str(us / 1_000_000) + "." + str(us / 100_000 % 10) + "s"

fn _log_mw(req: Request, inner: fn(Request) Response) Response:
    t0 = http.now_us()
    res = inner(req)
    http.log(req.method + " " + req.path + " " + str(res.status) + " " + _fmt_us(http.now_us() - t0))
    return res

fn logger() fn(Request, fn(Request) Response) Response:
    return _log_mw

# Rate limiting: a token bucket per client IP (client_ip), refilled at per_second tokens a
# second up to burst. A request that finds its bucket empty gets 429 Too Many Requests with
# Retry-After. Buckets are shared by every thread; idle ones are forgotten.
fn rate_limit(per_second: float, burst: int) fn(Request, fn(Request) Response) Response:
    lim = http.limiter(per_second, burst)
    return fn(req: Request, inner: fn(Request) Response) _limited(req, inner, lim, req.client_ip())

# the same, with your own key (an API key, a user id from the session, ...)
fn rate_limit_by(per_second: float, burst: int, key: fn(Request) str) fn(Request, fn(Request) Response) Response:
    lim = http.limiter(per_second, burst)
    return fn(req: Request, inner: fn(Request) Response) _limited(req, inner, lim, key(req))

fn _limited(req: Request, inner: fn(Request) Response, lim: http.Limiter, key: str) Response:
    wait = lim.consume(key)
    if wait <= 0.0:
        return inner(req)
    secs = int(wait) + 1
    return Response(429, "text/plain; charset=utf-8", "too many requests", "Retry-After: " + str(secs) + "\r\n", 0)

fn _list_has(list: str, item: str) bool:
    for x in list.split(","):
        if x.trim() == item:
            return true
    return false

fn _cors(req: Request, inner: fn(Request) Response, origins: str) Response:
    origin = req.header("origin")
    allow = ""
    if origins == "*":
        allow = "*"
    elif origin != "" and _list_has(origins, origin):
        allow = origin
    if req.method == "OPTIONS" and req.header("access-control-request-method") != "":
        pre = Response(204, "", "", "", 0)
        if allow != "":
            asked = req.header("access-control-request-headers")
            pre.headers = "Access-Control-Allow-Origin: " + allow + "\r\nAccess-Control-Allow-Methods: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS\r\nAccess-Control-Max-Age: 86400\r\n"
            if asked != "":
                pre.headers += "Access-Control-Allow-Headers: " + asked + "\r\n"
            if allow != "*":
                pre.headers += "Vary: Origin\r\n"
        return pre
    res = inner(req)
    if allow == "*":
        res.headers += "Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *\r\n"
    elif allow != "":
        res.headers += "Access-Control-Allow-Origin: " + allow + "\r\nVary: Origin\r\n"
    return res

fn cors(origins: str) fn(Request, fn(Request) Response) Response:
    return fn(req: Request, inner: fn(Request) Response) _cors(req, inner, origins)

fn _request_id_mw(req: Request, inner: fn(Request) Response) Response:
    id = req.header("x-request-id")
    if id == "":
        id = http.request_id()
        r2 = req
        r2.head += "x-request-id: " + id + "\r\n"
        res = inner(r2)
        res.headers += "x-request-id: " + id + "\r\n"
        return res
    res = inner(req)
    res.headers += "x-request-id: " + id + "\r\n"
    return res

fn request_id() fn(Request, fn(Request) Response) Response:
    return _request_id_mw

fn _deliver(ch: chan[Response], inner: fn(Request) Response, req: Request):
    task.send(ch, inner(req))

fn _timeout(req: Request, inner: fn(Request) Response, ms: int) Response:
    ch: chan[Response] = task.channel(1)
    h = task.spawn(fn() _deliver(ch, inner, req))
    res = Response(503, "text/plain; charset=utf-8", "request timed out", "", 0)
    left = ms
    while left > 0:
        step = min(left, 25)                 # (looks in on the task, so a failure answers early)
        if task.recv_timeout(ch, &res, step):
            return res
        left -= step
        if task.done(h):
            if task.try_recv(ch, &res):
                return res
            # the handler failed (its error is reported when the task is dropped)
            return Response(500, "text/plain; charset=utf-8", "internal server error", "", 0)
    task.cancel(h)
    return res

fn timeout(ms: int) fn(Request, fn(Request) Response) Response:
    return fn(req: Request, inner: fn(Request) Response) _timeout(req, inner, ms)

fn _unauthorized() Response:
    return Response(401, "text/plain; charset=utf-8", "unauthorized", "WWW-Authenticate: Bearer\r\n", 0)

fn _bearer(req: Request, inner: fn(Request) Response, want: str) Response:
    if http.secure_equal(req.header("authorization"), want):
        return inner(req)
    return _unauthorized()

fn bearer_auth(token: str) fn(Request, fn(Request) Response) Response:
    want = "Bearer " + token
    return fn(req: Request, inner: fn(Request) Response) _bearer(req, inner, want)

fn _check(req: Request, inner: fn(Request) Response, ok: fn(Request) bool) Response:
    if ok(req):
        return inner(req)
    return _unauthorized()

fn auth(check: fn(Request) bool) fn(Request, fn(Request) Response) Response:
    return fn(req: Request, inner: fn(Request) Response) _check(req, inner, check)

fn _compressible(ct: str) bool:
    return ct.starts_with("text/") or ct.contains("json") or ct.contains("javascript") or ct.contains("xml") or ct.contains("svg")

fn _gzip_mw(req: Request, inner: fn(Request) Response) Response:
    res = inner(req)
    if res.upgrade != 0 or len(res.body) < 860 or not _compressible(res.content_type):
        return res
    if not req.header("accept-encoding").contains("gzip") or res.get_header("content-encoding") != "":
        return res
    z = http.gzip(res.body)
    if len(z) == 0 or len(z) >= len(res.body):
        return res
    res.body = z
    res.headers += "Content-Encoding: gzip\r\nVary: Accept-Encoding\r\n"
    return res

fn gzip() fn(Request, fn(Request) Response) Response:
    return _gzip_mw
```

## deps/roost/response.tn

```tern
# Part of the roost package (see roost.tn for the overview): responses, and the other http
# functions a roost program calls by name (roost.text(...), roost.metric_add(...)); the
# functions on requests and responses (req.param(...), res.set_header(...)) are http's.

fn text(body: str) Response:
    return http.text(body)

fn html(body: str) Response:
    return http.html(body)

fn json(body: str) Response:
    return http.json(body)

fn status(code: int, body: str) Response:
    return http.status(code, body)

fn not_found() Response:
    return http.not_found()

fn no_content() Response:
    return http.no_content()

fn redirect(to: str) Response:
    return http.redirect(to)

fn redirect_permanent(to: str) Response:
    return http.redirect_permanent(to)

fn with_status(res: Response, code: int) Response:
    return http.with_status(res, code)

fn file_response(path: str, req: Request) Response:
    return http.file_response(path, req)

fn metric_add(name: str, labels: str, v: float):
    http.metric_add(name, labels, v)

fn metric_set(name: str, labels: str, v: float):
    http.metric_set(name, labels, v)

fn trust_proxies(n: int):
    http.trust_proxies(n)

fn track_routes():
    http.track_routes()
```

## deps/roost/roost.tn

```tern
# roost: an axum-style web framework on the standard library's http engine: routing with path
# parameters, extractors, middleware, WebSockets, server-sent events and static files.
# roost.Request, Response, Socket, Stream, Part and Server are http's types
# (aliases), so their functions (req.param, res.set_header, ws.send, ...) are http's.
#
#   import roost
#   import json
#   import task
#
#   struct User:
#       id: int
#       name: str
#
#   fn show_user(req: roost.Request) roost.Response:
#       id = req.param_int("id", -1)
#       if id < 0:
#           return roost.status(400, "bad id")
#       return roost.json(json.encode(User(id, "ada")))
#
#   fn bump(n: mut int) int:
#       n += 1
#       return n
#
#   fn main():
#       hits = task.shared(0)                      # app state: captured by the handlers
#       r = roost.router()
#       r.get("/", fn(req) roost.text("hello"))
#       r.get("/users/{id}", show_user)
#       r.post("/hits", fn(req) roost.text(str(hits.update(bump))))
#       r.layer(roost.logger())                      # middleware for the routes above
#       roost.serve(r, 8080)                         # a task per connection, every core
#
# Handlers are closures `fn(roost.Request) roost.Response`; state they need is captured (a
# `shared[T]` for state that changes). A runtime error in a handler answers 500 and the
# server keeps running. Each connection runs as a task, so handlers may wait (sleep,
# channels, http.get) without holding up other requests.
#
# Router (r.get(...) changes r in place):
#   roost.router() Router
#   r.get(path, h)  r.post(path, h)  r.put(path, h)  r.delete(path, h)  r.patch(path, h)
#   r.route(method, path, h)        any method name; "*" matches every method
#   r.any(path, h)                  every method
#   r.ws(path, fn(req: roost.Request, ws: roost.Socket))      a WebSocket endpoint
#   r.sse(path, fn(req: roost.Request, out: roost.Stream))    a server-sent events endpoint
#   r.nest(prefix, sub)             sub's routes under prefix ("/api" + "/users")
#   r.fallback(h)                   answers requests no route matches (default: 404)
#   r.post_stream(path, h)  r.put_stream(path, h)   the handler runs when the headers arrive and
#                                   reads the body itself (big uploads in constant memory):
#     req.read_body(max) str        the next piece ("" at the end)   req.save_body(path) int
#     req.next_part(&p) bool        multipart: the next part's name / filename / content_type
#     req.read_part(max) str        that part's bytes, a piece at a time   req.save_part(path) int
#   r.max_connections(n)            at most n connections at once (then accepting waits)
#   r.metrics(path)                 GET path: Prometheus metrics (requests, latency by route, ...)
#   roost.metric_add(name, labels, v)  roost.metric_set(name, labels, v)   your own counters / gauges
#                                   (labels: "" or `kind="x",zone="eu"`)
# Validation: roost.check() Check; v.required / min_len / max_len / between / one_of / email /
#   fail(field, message); v.valid() bool; v.problems() Response (422 with every problem)
#   r.files(prefix, dir)            static files: GET prefix/a/b.css serves dir/a/b.css (ETag, 304,
#                                   ranges, content types; ".." and dot files are refused)
#   roost.file_response(path, req) Response    one file as a response (with the same headers; the
#                                   path is relative to the working directory, and ".." is refused)
#   r.layer(mw)                     wraps the routes added so far (and the fallback)
#   r.wrap(mw)                      wraps everything, including 404s and 405s
#   Paths: "/users/{id}" (one segment), "/files/{*rest}" (the rest of the path).
#   Static segments win over {params}, which win over {*wildcards}. A path that matches
#   with the wrong method gets 405 with an Allow header; GET routes also answer HEAD.
#
# Serving:
#   roost.serve(r, port)              serve forever (prints the address to stderr)
#   roost.start(r, port) Server       serve in the background; port 0 picks a free port
#   roost.start_on(r, host, port) Server
#   srv.port (a field, int)         srv.stop()   (closes connections, waits for their handlers)
#   roost.serve_tls(r, port, cert, key)          HTTPS: cert and key are PEM files (the cert file
#   roost.start_tls(r, host, port, cert, key) Server    may hold the chain); needs `import tls`
#
# Request fields: method, path, raw_query, head (header lines), body, params, ctx
#   req.param(name) str             a path parameter ("" if absent); req.param_int(name, default) int
#   req.query(name) str             from the query string, decoded; req.queries() {str: str}
#   req.header(name) str            case-insensitive; req.headers() {str: str} (lowercase names)
#   req.cookie(name) str            req.form(name) str (an x-www-form-urlencoded body); req.forms() {str: str}
#   req.parts() [roost.Part]          a multipart/form-data body (file uploads): name, filename,
#   req.part(name) roost.Part         content_type, data of each part
#   req.json(&value) bool           decode the JSON body into value (false: left unchanged)
#   req.params() {str: str}         every path parameter
#   req.add_header(name, value)     (middleware) add a request header for inner handlers
#   req.set_ctx(key, value)  req.ctx_value(key) str    values middleware passes inward
#   req.peer() str                  "1.2.3.4:5678", the connection's address
#   req.client_ip() str             the client's IP (see roost.trust_proxies(n) behind a proxy)
#   req.matched_route() str         the matched route's pattern ("/users/{id}"), once
#                                   roost.track_routes() was called ("" before, or if none matched)
#
# Responses (fields: status, content_type, body, headers, upgrade):
#   roost.text(s)  roost.html(s)  roost.json(s)  roost.status(code, body)  roost.not_found()
#   roost.redirect(url) (302)  roost.redirect_permanent(url) (308)  roost.no_content()
#   res.set_header(name, value)     res.set_cookie(name, value)   res.set_cookie_with(name, value, attrs)
#   res.get_header(name) str        roost.with_status(res, code) Response
#
# Middleware is a closure fn(req: roost.Request, next: fn(roost.Request) roost.Response) roost.Response:
#   roost.logger()                    "GET /path 200 1.2ms" per request, to stderr (buffered)
#   roost.rate_limit(per_second, burst)   429 + Retry-After past a token bucket per client IP
#   roost.rate_limit_by(per_second, burst, key)   ... per key(req) (fn(roost.Request) str)
#   roost.cors(origins)               "*" or "https://a.com, https://b.com"; answers preflights
#   roost.request_id()                x-request-id on the request (if missing) and the response
#   roost.timeout(ms)                 runs the handler in a task; 503 when it takes too long
#   roost.bearer_auth(token)          401 unless "Authorization: Bearer <token>"
#   roost.auth(check)                 401 unless check(req) (check: fn(roost.Request) bool)
#   roost.gzip()                      compresses text/JSON bodies for clients that accept gzip
#
# WebSockets (roost.Socket):
#   ws.next(&msg) bool              the next text or binary message; false once closed
#   ws.recv() str                   the next message ("" once closed)
#   ws.is_binary() bool             whether the last message received was binary
#   ws.send(text) bool  ws.send_binary(data) bool  ws.ping(data) bool   (false: gone)
#   ws.close()                      ws.is_open() bool
#   (a WebSocket client is http.ws_connect(url))
#   Pings are answered automatically; fragmented messages are put together.
#
# Server-sent events (roost.Stream):
#   out.send(data) bool             one event (multi-line data is fine); false: client gone
#   out.event(name, data) bool      a named event        out.comment(text) bool  (keep-alive)
#   out.forward(ch) bool            every message from a chan[str] as an event, until ch closes
#                                   (false: client gone, noticed within 1s); waiting messages share a write
#
# HTTP client: http.get, http.post, http.fetch(http.request(method, url)) (see `tern guide http`);
# roost has none of its own, as axum leaves the client to reqwest.
#
# Environment: TERN_ASYNC_THREADS (worker threads), TERN_WEB_IDLE_SEC (60),
# TERN_WEB_HEADER_SEC (10), TERN_WEB_MAX_BODY_MB (16), TERN_WEB_WS_MAX_MB (16).
# Not available on wasm (no sockets or threads there).

import http
import task

type Request = http.Request
type Response = http.Response
type Socket = http.Socket
type Stream = http.Stream
type Part = http.Part
type Server = http.Server

struct Route:
    method: str
    pattern: str
    handler: fn(Request) Response
    ws: fn(Request, Socket)
    sse: fn(Request, Stream)
    layers: int                 # how many of the router's layers existed when it was added
    stream: bool                # the handler reads the body itself (post_stream / put_stream)

struct Router:
    routes: [Route]
    layers: [fn(Request, fn(Request) Response) Response]
    wraps: [fn(Request, fn(Request) Response) Response]
    fallback_handler: fn(Request) Response
    fallback_layers: int
    has_fallback: bool
    max_conns: int              # 0: no limit (see max_connections)
```

## deps/roost/router.tn

```tern
# Part of the roost package (see roost.tn for the overview): the router.

fn _not_found_handler(req: Request) Response:
    return not_found()

fn router() Router:
    return Router([], [], [], _not_found_handler, 0, false, 0)

# GET path answers with Prometheus metrics (text format 0.0.4): tern_http_requests_total and
# tern_http_request_duration_seconds by route, method and status (counted from now on, for
# every server in the program), tern_http_connections, process CPU / memory / uptime, and the
# program's own roost.metric_add / roost.metric_set values.
fn metrics(r: mut Router, path: str):
    http.enable_metrics()
    route(&r, "GET", path, _metrics_page)

fn _metrics_page(req: Request) Response:
    return Response(200, "text/plain; version=0.0.4; charset=utf-8", http.metrics_text(), "", 0)

# At most n connections at once (0: no limit, the default; TERN_WEB_MAX_CONNS sets it too).
# Past the limit the server stops accepting until a connection closes; new clients wait in
# the kernel's queue rather than being refused.
fn max_connections(r: mut Router, n: int):
    r.max_conns = n

fn route(r: mut Router, method: str, path: str, h: fn(Request) Response):
    r.routes.push(Route(method.upper(), path, h, http.no_ws, http.no_sse, len(r.layers), false))

# r.get(path, h), r.post, r.put, r.delete, r.patch
fn get(r: mut Router, path: str, h: fn(Request) Response):
    route(&r, "GET", path, h)

fn post(r: mut Router, path: str, h: fn(Request) Response):
    route(&r, "POST", path, h)

fn put(r: mut Router, path: str, h: fn(Request) Response):
    route(&r, "PUT", path, h)

fn delete(r: mut Router, path: str, h: fn(Request) Response):
    route(&r, "DELETE", path, h)

fn patch(r: mut Router, path: str, h: fn(Request) Response):
    route(&r, "PATCH", path, h)

fn any(r: mut Router, path: str, h: fn(Request) Response):
    route(&r, "*", path, h)

# Streaming uploads: the handler runs as soon as the headers arrive, and reads the body
# itself, a piece at a time (no size limit, constant memory). req.body is "".
fn post_stream(r: mut Router, path: str, h: fn(Request) Response):
    r.routes.push(Route("POST", path, h, http.no_ws, http.no_sse, len(r.layers), true))

fn put_stream(r: mut Router, path: str, h: fn(Request) Response):
    r.routes.push(Route("PUT", path, h, http.no_ws, http.no_sse, len(r.layers), true))

# r.files("/assets", "./public"): GET /assets/app.js serves ./public/app.js (a directory
# serves its index.html). Content types from the file extension, ETag / Last-Modified with
# 304 answers, single byte ranges (206), and big files streamed from disk. Paths with ".."
# or dot files (other than .well-known) are 404.
fn files(r: mut Router, prefix: str, dir: str):
    p = prefix
    while p.ends_with("/"):
        p = p[..len(p) - 1]
    h = fn(req: Request) http.static_file(dir, req.param("path"), req)
    route(&r, "GET", p + "/{*path}", h)
    if p != "":
        route(&r, "GET", p, h)
    else:
        route(&r, "GET", "/", h)

fn ws(r: mut Router, path: str, h: fn(Request, Socket)):
    r.routes.push(Route("GET", path, http.ws_upgrade, h, http.no_sse, len(r.layers), false))

fn sse(r: mut Router, path: str, h: fn(Request, Stream)):
    r.routes.push(Route("GET", path, http.sse_open, http.no_ws, h, len(r.layers), false))

fn fallback(r: mut Router, h: fn(Request) Response):
    r.fallback_handler = h
    r.fallback_layers = len(r.layers)
    r.has_fallback = true

fn layer(r: mut Router, mw: fn(Request, fn(Request) Response) Response):
    r.layers.push(copy(mw))

fn wrap(r: mut Router, mw: fn(Request, fn(Request) Response) Response):
    r.wraps.push(copy(mw))

# h inside mws[first], mws[first + 1], ... (the last one is outermost)
fn _compose(h: fn(Request) Response, mws: [fn(Request, fn(Request) Response) Response], first: int) fn(Request) Response:
    out = h
    i = first
    while i < len(mws):
        mw = mws[i]
        inner = out
        out = fn(req: Request) mw(req, inner)
        i += 1
    return out

fn _join_path(prefix: str, pattern: str) str:
    p = prefix
    if p.ends_with("/"):
        p = p[..len(p) - 1]
    if pattern == "/":
        if p == "":
            return "/"
        return p
    return p + pattern

fn nest(r: mut Router, prefix: str, sub: Router):
    for rt in sub.routes:
        h = _compose(_compose(rt.handler, sub.layers, rt.layers), sub.wraps, 0)
        r.routes.push(Route(rt.method, _join_path(prefix, rt.pattern), h, rt.ws, rt.sse, len(r.layers), rt.stream))
    if sub.has_fallback:
        fb = _compose(_compose(sub.fallback_handler, sub.layers, sub.fallback_layers), sub.wraps, 0)
        r.routes.push(Route("*", _join_path(prefix, "/{*rest}"), fb, http.no_ws, http.no_sse, len(r.layers), false))

fn _405(allow: str) Response:
    return Response(405, "text/plain; charset=utf-8", "method not allowed", "Allow: " + allow + "\r\n", 0)

fn _method_not_allowed(allow: str) fn(Request) Response:
    return fn(req: Request) _405(allow)

# the routes with their middleware applied, plus a 405 answer for each path
fn _finished_routes(r: Router) [Route]:
    out: [Route] = []
    allow: {str: str} = {}
    first: {str: int} = {}
    has_any: {str: bool} = {}
    for rt in r.routes:
        h = _compose(_compose(rt.handler, r.layers, rt.layers), r.wraps, 0)
        out.push(Route(rt.method, rt.pattern, h, rt.ws, rt.sse, rt.layers, rt.stream))
        if rt.method == "*":
            has_any[rt.pattern] = true
            continue
        m = rt.method
        if m == "GET":
            m = "GET, HEAD"
        if rt.pattern in allow:
            allow[rt.pattern] = allow[rt.pattern] + ", " + m
            first[rt.pattern] = min(first[rt.pattern], rt.layers)
        else:
            allow[rt.pattern] = m
            first[rt.pattern] = rt.layers
    for pat, methods in allow:
        if not (pat in has_any):
            h = _compose(_compose(_method_not_allowed(methods), r.layers, first[pat]), r.wraps, 0)
            out.push(Route("*", pat, h, http.no_ws, http.no_sse, 0, false))
    return out
```

## deps/roost/serve.tn

```tern
# Part of the roost package (see roost.tn for the overview): serving, on http's engine.

fn _start(r: Router, host: str, port: int, cert: str, key: str) Server:
    s = http.new_server()
    for rt in _finished_routes(r):
        s.add_route(rt.method, rt.pattern, rt.handler, rt.ws, rt.sse, rt.stream)
    fb = _compose(_compose(r.fallback_handler, r.layers, r.fallback_layers), r.wraps, 0)
    if r.max_conns > 0:
        s.limit_connections(r.max_conns)
    if cert != "":
        s.listen_tls(host, port, fb, cert, key)
    else:
        s.listen(host, port, fb)
    return s

fn start_on(r: Router, host: str, port: int) Server:
    return _start(r, host, port, "", "")

fn start_tls(r: Router, host: str, port: int, cert: str, key: str) Server:
    return _start(r, host, port, cert, key)

fn serve_tls(r: Router, port: int, cert: str, key: str):
    _start(r, "", port, cert, key).wait()

fn start(r: Router, port: int) Server:
    return start_on(r, "", port)

fn serve(r: Router, port: int):
    start_on(r, "", port).wait()

fn stop(s: Server):
    s.stop()
```

## deps/sentry/sentry.tn

```tern
# sentry: report errors and messages to Sentry (sentry.io or self-hosted) from any task.
#
#   import sentry
#   import tls                                   # for an https:// DSN
#
#   o = sentry.options()                         # defaults; change the fields you need
#   o.release = "shop@1.4.2"
#   c = sentry.init(os.env("SENTRY_DSN", ""), o) # an empty DSN: capturing does nothing
#   sentry.install(c)                            # runtime errors (crashes, failed tasks, 500s)
#   r.layer(sentry.middleware(c))                # ...with the request and route they happened in
#   c.capture_message("disk almost full", "warning")
#   c.capture_result(fs.try_read(path))          # an Err becomes an error event
#   c.close()                                    # before main returns: send what's queued
#
#   sentry.options() Options          release ($SENTRY_RELEASE), environment ($SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT
#                                     or "production"), server_name ($HOSTNAME), sample_rate 1.0,
#                                     max_queue 100, breadcrumbs 50, timeout_ms 10000, scrub [...]
#   sentry.init(dsn str, o Options) Client
#   c.ok() bool                       false for an empty or bad DSN; c.error() says which
#   c.capture_message(msg str, level str) str     "fatal" "error" "warning" "info" "debug"
```
